# Upload an image creative

## Image creative overview

Advertisers rely on image creatives to deliver a clear and concise message. You can add image creatives to your creative library in the IQM platform one by one or in bulk, and from the following locations:

- From the Creatives app
- From the Campaigns app

You can also choose between a static (PNG, JPG) or moving (GIF) image to accompany the ad’s call to action. Refer to [Creative ad specs and requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements) to confirm that your creatives follow IQM and industry requirements before you add them.

## Video tutorial: Upload an image creative

## Add an image creative

### Add an image creative from the Creatives app

Follow these steps to add a static or moving image creative from the Creatives app:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Image**.
3. Click **+ Add New**. This will open the **Image Creative** pop-up window.
4. Choose which method you’d like to follow to add the image creatives:
   1. Upload them from your computer’s local files.
   2. Drag-and-drop them from your computer’s local files.
   3. Upload them from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account.
5. To upload creatives from your computer’s local files, select **Upload Image,** choose one or more image files, and click **Open**.
6. To drag-and-drop creatives, open your computer’s local files, choose one or more image files, and drag your cursor from those files to the **or Drag & Drop** section.
7. To upload a creative from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired files from your online drive.
8. Review the creative preview(s) to confirm that each image renders as expected.
9. Type a name for the creative into the **Name** field.
   1. By default, the file’s name will populate. If you change the creative’s name, choose a unique one to differentiate the image from others that you may add.
10. In the **Click URL** field, enter the full URL address where users will be directed to when they click on the creative.
    1. To apply the same click URL to each of the creatives you’re uploading, use the **Click URL** field found in the **Apply to all** section instead.
11. Complete the **3rd Party ID** or **Pixel URL** fields, if desired.
    1. Refer to Add custom tracking to an image creative for more details and instructions.
12. Select **Add Creative** to save the image(s) to the **Creatives** app.

### Add an image creative from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to add a static or moving image creative from the Campaigns app:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a new creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. This will redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.
4. Locate the **Image Creatives** section.
5. Select **+ New Creative**.
6. Follow steps 4 through 12 of the Add an image creative from the Creatives app workflow. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Add Creative** button.
7. Save the creative(s) to the campaign.
   1. If this is an existing campaign, click **Save** on the campaign’s landing page.
   2. If this is a new campaign, click **Save as Draft** on the campaign’s landing page, or click **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections for this campaign.

## Add custom tracking to an image creative

### Custom tracking overview

If desired, you can specify external tags, pixels, or tracking URLs and add them to creatives in the IQM platform:

- **Pixel URL:** Verify ad serving using a third-party system. External tracking pixel URLs allow you to track impressions, clicks, and conversions independently, and serve as an external measurement verification source. Up to five Pixel URLs are supported per creative.
- **3rd Party ID:** Reconcile performance data with IQM using the ID that you assigned to a creative on an external, third-party platform. This field is optional with the following use cases:
  - Keep track of your uploaded ads.
  - Reconcile data and compare delivery information.
  - Apply the identifier for your own reporting purposes such as for use in an external data visualization tool.

### Add a Pixel URL or 3rd Party ID to an image creative

1. Go to the desired third-party system to create the tracking event and obtain a URL or ID.
2. After opening the creative in the Creatives app, use the scroll bar to reveal the **3rd Party ID** and **Pixel URL** fields.
3. If desired, enter the applicable ID in the **3rd Party ID** field of each creative.
4. If desired, add unique Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Expand the **Pixel URLs** section.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
5. If desired, add the same Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Select **Add**.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
   4. Click **Update**.
6. Once you’ve completed all other required and applicable fields, click **Add Creative** to finish.

- [Creative formats overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview)
- [Creative ad specs and requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements)
- [Manage creatives and creative groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651463-manage-creatives-and-creative-groups)
- [Assign a creative to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10552784-assign-a-creative-to-a-campaign)

# Upload a video creative

## Video creative overview

Advertisers rely on video creatives to encourage brand recall with rich storytelling content that leaves a lasting impression. You can add video creatives to your creative library in the IQM platform one by one or in bulk, and from the following locations:

- From the Creatives app
- From the Campaigns app

You can also choose between video creatives and VAST extensible markup language (XML)/URLs, or use a combination of the two in your video campaigns. Refer to [Creative ad specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs) to confirm that your creatives follow IQM and industry requirements before you add them.

## Video tutorial: Upload a video creative

## Add a standard video creative

### Add video creatives from the Creatives app

Follow these steps to add video creatives from the Creatives app:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Video**.
3. Click **+ Add new**. This will open the **Video Creative** pop-up window.
4. Choose which method you’d like to follow to add the video creatives:
   1. Upload them from your computer’s local files.
   2. Drag-and-drop them from your computer’s local files.
   3. Upload them from a Google Drive or Dropbox account.
5. To upload a creative from your computer’s local files, select **Upload Video**, choose one or more video files, and click **Open**.
6. To drag-and-drop a creative, open your computer’s local files, choose one or more video files, and drag your cursor from those files to the **or Drag and Drop** section of the **Video** pop-up window.
7. To upload a creative from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the files from the online drive.
8. Play the video to confirm that it renders and plays as expected.
9. Enter a name for the creative.
10. In the **Click URL** field, enter the full URL address where users will be directed to when they click on the creative.
    1. To apply the same click URL to each of the creatives you’re uploading, use the **Click URL** field found in the **Apply to all** section instead.
11. Complete the **3rd Party ID**, **Custom Tracking**, and/or **Pixel URL** fields, if desired.
    1. Refer to Add custom tracking to a video creative for more details and instructions.
12. Select **Add Creative** to save the creative(s) to the Creatives app.

### Add video creatives from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to add video creatives from the Campaigns app:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a new creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.
4. Locate and expand the **Video Creatives** section.
5. Select **+ New Creative**.
6. Follow steps 4 through 12 of the Add video creatives from the Creatives app workflow.
7. Save the creative(s) to the campaign.
   1. If this is an existing campaign, click **Save** on the campaign’s landing page.
   2. If this is a new campaign, click **Save as Draft** on the campaign’s landing page, or click **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections of the campaign.

## Add a VAST XML/URL

### Add VAST XML/URLs from the Creatives app

> **VAST XML/URL template:** Select **Sample File** in the **Video** pop-up window to download a spreadsheet template if you plan to add one or more VAST XML/URLs via a spreadsheet upload. Follow its formatting guidelines: Add the **Creative Name** to Column A.; Add the XML or URL code to Column B.; Add each additional creative via a separate row. You can save and reupload the spreadsheet to easily add your video creatives individually or in bulk.

Follow these steps to add VAST XML/URLs from the **Creatives** app:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Video**.
3. Click **+ Add new**. This will open the **Video Creative** pop-up window.
4. Choose which method you’d like to follow to add VAST code:
   1. Manually paste the code.
   2. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the code from your computer’s local files
   3. Drag-and-drop a spreadsheet that contains the code from your computer’s local files.
   4. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the code from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account.
5. To manually paste the code, select **+ Add VAST XML/URL** and enter the code into the **VAST XML/URL** field. Complete this process for each additional creative, if applicable.
6. To upload a spreadsheet from your computer’s local files, select **Upload Video**, choose one or more files, and click **Open**.
7. To drag-and-drop a spreadsheet, open your computer’s local files, choose one or more files, and drag your cursor from those files to the **or** **Drag and Drop** section of the **Video** pop-up window.
8. To upload a spreadsheet from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the files from the online drive.
9. Play the video to confirm that it renders and plays as expected.
10. Enter a name for the creative.
    1. The **Creative Name** field will auto-populate if you added the VAST XML/URL via spreadsheet upload and indicated a creative name in column A.

3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.

## Add custom tracking to a video creative

### Tracking URL overview

Tracking URLs are strings of HTML code that load when a user visits a particular webpage, completes an action, or converts.

Depending on the creative format, you can add the following tracking URLs to a creative in the IQM platform:

- **Impression URL:** Calculate the number of times the ad displays, and measure post-view attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define.
- **Click URL:** Calculate the number of times a user clicked on the ad, and complete post-click attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define.
- **Conversion URL:** Calculate the number of times a user completed a particular action after clicking on the ad, such as purchasing a product or service, or completing a contact form on the website.
- **Pixel URL:** Calculate the number of times a one-pixel-by-one-pixel image loads. Advertisers typically embed the code into their website’s header to measure page visits, or in an email marketing message to measure its open rate. Up to five Pixel URLs are supported per creative.

### Add a 3rd Party ID, Custom Tracking URL, or Pixel URL

1. Go to the desired third-party system to create the tracking event and obtain a URL or ID.
2. After opening the creative in the Creatives app, use the scroll bar to reveal the **3rd Party ID**, **Pixel URL**, and **Custom Tracking** fields.
3. If desired, enter the applicable ID in the **3rd Party ID** field of each creative.
4. If desired, expand the **Custom Tracking** section and enter the applicable ID to each respective field.
5. If desired, add unique Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Expand the **Pixel URLs** section.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
6. If desired, add the same Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Select **Add**.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
   4. Click **Update**.
7. Once you’ve completed all other required and applicable fields, click **Add Creative** to finish.

   3. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the code from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account.
5. To manually paste the code, select **+ Add DAAST XML/URL** and enter the code into the **DAAST XML/URL** field. Complete this process for each additional creative, if applicable.
6. To drag-and-drop a spreadsheet, open your computer’s local files, choose one or more files, and drag your cursor from those files to the **or Drag & Drop** section.
7. To upload a spreadsheet from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the files from the online drive.
8. Play the audio clip to confirm that it renders as expected.
9. Enter a name for the creative.
10. Complete the **3rd Party ID** and/or **Pixel URL** fields, if desired.
    1. Refer to Add custom tracking to an audio creative for more details and instructions.
11. Select **Add Creative** to save the audio ad(s) to the Creatives app.

You’ll notice that, unlike audio file uploads, DAAST XML/URL embeds don’t include the option to add URLs to a **Click URL** or **Custom Tracking** field. That’s because those tracking elements can be embedded directly into the DAAST code.

### Embed an audio file from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to embed a DAAST audio creative from the Campaigns app:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a new creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.
4. Locate the **Audio Creatives** section.
5. Select **+ New Creative**.
6. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Embed an audio file from the Creatives app workflow. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Add Creative** button.
7. Save the creative(s) to the campaign.
   1. If this is an existing campaign, click **Save** on the campaign’s landing page.
   2. If this is a new campaign, click **Save as Draft** on the campaign’s landing page, or click **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections for this campaign.

## Add custom tracking to an audio creative

### Custom tracking overview

If desired, you can specify external tags, pixels, or tracking URLs and add them to your audio creatives in the IQM platform to measure performance independently:

- **3rd Party ID:** Reconcile performance data with IQM using the ID that you assigned to a creative on an external, third-party platform. This field is optional with the following use cases:
  - Keep track of your uploaded ads.
  - Reconcile data and compare delivery information.
  - Apply the identifier for your own reporting purposes such as for use in an external data visualization tool.
- **Impression Tracking URL:** Calculate the number of times the ad displays, and measure post-view attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define.
- **Duration Tracking URLs (Start, 1st Quartile, Midpoint, 3rd Quartile, Complete):** Measure how much of the audio ad was played and determine whether it was started or reached 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% of its total duration.
- **Pixel URL:** Calculate the number of times a one-pixel-by-one-pixel image loads. Advertisers typically embed the code into their website’s header to measure page visits, or in an email marketing message to measure its open rate. Up to five Pixel URLs are supported per creative.

### Add a 3rd Party ID, tracking URL, or Pixel URL to an audio creative

1. Go to the desired third-party system to create the tracking event and obtain a URL or ID.
2. If desired, enter the applicable ID in the **3rd Party ID** field of each creative.
3. If desired, add custom tracking URLs.
   1. Include URLs directly in the code that you manually paste or upload via a spreadsheet.
   2. Expand the **Custom Tracking** section to add URLs to creatives that you add via audio files.
4. If desired, add unique Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Expand the **Pixel URLs** section.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
5. If desired, add the same Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Select **Add**.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
   4. Click **Update**.
6. Once you’ve completed all other required and applicable fields, click **Add Creative** to finish.

# Manage creatives and creative groups

## Managing creatives overview

Review, duplicate, group, or make changes to the creatives that you’ve previously added to your creative library in the Creatives app.

Refer to these resources if you want to add a new creative instead:

- [Upload an image creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651450-upload-an-image-creative)
- [Upload an HTML creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651452-upload-an-html-creative)

## Video tutorial: Manage creatives and creative groups

## Bulk actions

Certain bulk actions are available depending on formats and statuses of the creatives that you select. Review the tables below to determine which creatives are eligible for bulk actions, then locate the relevant section in this article to complete the desired action.

### Image creatives

## Search and filter creatives

Customize your **Creatives** page in any of the following ways to determine which creatives and details appear:

1. View all creatives regardless of their format, or limit the page to include only a certain creative format.
2. Choose whether to view all creatives, only creatives that are included in a creative group, or only creatives that aren’t included in a creative group.
3. Choose whether to view the creatives in a table or grid.
4. Use the **Search By** field to search using a creative ID, creative name, or 3rd party ID.
5. View only the creatives that feature a particular status.
6. Open the column selector to choose which fields appear in the table view.
7. Sort by the **ID**, **Creative Name**, **3rd Party ID**, or **Created** columns by selecting the arrows next to the desired column’s title.
   1. You must hover your cursor over the column’s title for the arrows to appear.

## Preview creatives

> **Pixel URL notice:** The tracking (pixel) URLs of all creatives are eligible for edits with the exception of Video, Native Video, and Audio creatives added manually via VAST/DAAST XML or VAST/DAAST XML URL. Video, Native Video, and Audio creatives added via VAST/DAAST file upload are eligible.

Follow these steps to review a creative’s details and preview it on different device types:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Search or filter the table to locate the creative you’d like to preview.
3. Select the ad’s creative ID in the **ID** column or the thumbnail in the **Preview** column. This will open a pop-up window where you can preview the creative.
4. Review who added the creative, when it was added, and its current status.
5. Preview an ad mockup on different device types.
6. Review the creative’s size and any tracking solutions associated with it.
   1. Select **Edit** to change and save these details.

## Group creatives

Save time on managing your creative assets by grouping them together. Note that each creative must share the same format (image, video, audio, native, HTML) to belong to the same group.

Follow these steps to add creatives to a new or existing group:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkboxes next to the creatives you’d like to assign to a new or existing group. These creatives must feature the same creative format.
3. Click **Save To Group**. This will open the **Group Creatives** pop-up window.
4. To save the creative(s) to an existing group, select **Existing Group**, open the **Creative Group** menu and choose the desired group, and click **Save**.
5. To save the creative(s) to a new group, select **New Group**, use the **Group Name** field to enter a unique name, and select **Save**.

Each group and its creatives will appear in the **Grouped Creatives** tab of the **Creatives** app.

You can also add creatives to a new or existing group when you first upload them to the IQM platform. This process ends by offering the option to group them via the **Group Creatives** pop-up window. Refer to the [Upload an image creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651450-upload-an-image-creative), [Upload an HTML creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651452-upload-an-html-creative), [Upload a video creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651461-upload-a-video-creative), [Upload an audio creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651462-upload-an-audio-creative), or [Upload a native creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8706031-upload-a-native-creative) to add a new creative, then return to Group creatives to add them to a new or existing group.

## Duplicate

Follow these steps to duplicate creatives individually or in bulk:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) you’d like to duplicate.
3. Open the **Actions** menu and click **Duplicate**.

The duplicated creative(s) will appear in the table and feature a **Pending** status. Its **Creative Name** is, by default, the original creative’s name followed by “copy.” You can Edit the name and apply any other changes outlined in this article.

## Delete

> **Deletion warning:** Note that deleted creatives and creative groups are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and editing them instead.

Follow these steps to delete creatives individually or in bulk:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) you’d like to delete.
3. Open the **Actions** menu and click **Delete**. This will open a **Delete Creative?** pop-up window.
4. Review any warnings, and select **Delete** to confirm your selection.

## Edit Click URLs, Pixel URLs, or 3rd Party IDs

> **Pixel URL notice:** The tracking (pixel) URLs of all creatives are eligible for edits with the exception of Video, Native Video, and Audio creatives added manually via VAST/DAAST XML or VAST/DAAST XML URL. Video, Native Video, and Audio creatives added via VAST/DAAST file upload are eligible.

You can edit a click URL, pixel URL, or 3rd party ID in one of two ways:

- From the table view on the **Creatives** page.
- From the **Creative Details** panel in the Preview creatives workflow.

In cases when any of the creatives are assigned to a campaign, you’ll be prompted to choose to apply the updated creatives to those campaigns or duplicate the creatives instead. Note that if you change the **Click URL** or **Pixel URL** fields and choose to apply the updated creatives to the campaigns, note that they’ll get submitted for re-approval.

### Edit URLs or IDs from a table

Follow these steps to apply an individual click URL, pixel URL, or 3rd party ID from a table:

1. Locate the **3rd Party ID**, **Click URL**, or **Pixel URL** columns, depending on the item you’d like to add or update.
   1. Note that you may need to open the column selector to add a particular column to the table.
2. Click the **3rd Party ID**, **Click URL**, or **Pixel URL** field next to the desired creative and enter the ID or URL. Select the checkbox next to the field to apply your changes.

Follow these steps to apply the same click URL or pixel URL to more than one creative from a table:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkboxes next to the creatives you’d like to update with the new click URL or pixel URL.
3. Open the **Actions** menu and click **Edit Click URL** or **Edit Pixel URL**. This will open the **Edit Click URL** or **Edit Pixel URL** pop-up window, depending on your selection.
4. Enter the new URL(s) into the available field(s).
5. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

### Edit URLs or IDs from a creative preview

Follow these steps to add or change an individual click URL, pixel URL, or 3rd party ID from a creative preview:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Preview creatives workflow.
2. Locate the **Creative Details** panel.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Update the desired field(s).
5. Select **Save** to apply your changes.

## Edit an HTML Code

You can edit one existing HTML creative’s HTML Code at a time, and only when its status is Pending, Running, or Paused.

Follow these steps to edit an HTML Code:

1. Select the preview image of the desired HTML creative. This will open a pop-up window, where you can review and manage the creative’s details.
2. Locate and expand the **HTML Code** section.
3. Click **Edit**.
4. Enter your desired HTML Code edits into the available field.
5. Select **Save** to apply your changes. The creative’s status will revert to Pending until the creative is approved.

## Edit a name

Select a creative’s **Creative Name** field to change its name. Enter the new name and select the checkmark icon to apply your changes.

## Run or pause

Follow these steps to pause **Running** creatives or run **Paused** creatives:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) you’d like to run or pause.
3. Open the **Actions** menu and click **Run** or **Pause**, depending on the creative’s current status.

## Identify assigned campaigns

Each creative’s **Campaigns** column includes the number of campaigns that the creative is currently assigned to. If you’ve assigned the creative to at least one campaign, select the number to review a list of those campaigns, along with other key details such as each campaign’s ID and status.

blocks.text: **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing campaigns in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Campaigns are the individual marketing strategies that define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. They contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify. Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more details, or continue reading to create a new campaign or manage an existing one.
Note that you’ll need to assign the new campaign to an existing insertion order (IO) at the time of campaign creation. Refer to these resources to create an IO if you haven’t yet completed this step:
[Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview)
[Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io)
[Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)

**More on running a campaign:** Note that a campaign doesn’t immediately begin spending and serving when you choose to **Run** it. First, the campaign will undergo a review process to confirm that it meets certain requirements. You’ll know when a campaign is approved when its status changes from **Pending** to **Running**. We’ll also notify you via email.

Refer to [Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQs)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498457-campaigns-frequently-asked-questions-faq) for campaign-status definitions, and go to Review campaigns to learn how to check a campaign’s current status.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: You can create a new campaign in the following ways:
From the Campaigns app
From the Dashboard app

Note that you’ll be prompted to select an IO when you enter your campaign’s details. You must select a budget-based insertion order (IO) if the campaign will have a monetary budget, or an impression-based IO if the campaign will have an impression budget. Refer to [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview)for more information on the differences between them.

sections.heading: Create a new campaign from the Campaigns app
heading_path: Create a new campaign from the Campaigns app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to create a new campaign in the Campaigns app:
Open the Campaigns app.
Choose the insertion order that will serve as the parent hierarchy for the new campaign. You’ll arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
Select **+ Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window.
Enter a name for the campaign.
Choose an [Advanced](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) or [PG](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) **Campaign Type**.
Select a **Campaign Creation Method**.
Click **From Scratch** to open an empty campaign creation form.
Click **From Template** to open a campaign creation form that includes the settings you previously saved as a template.
If you select **From Template**, open the **Template** menu to search and select the desired template.
Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign’s details page, where you can specify campaign settings and targeting rules.
Enter the maximum budget or maximum impressions that the campaign should spend.
Enter the maximum amount you’re willing to bid for 1,000 ad impressions.
If you specify a Min Bid Price, the Max Bid Price must be greater than that value.
Select **Show CPM Breakdown** to review which campaign elements are contributing to the campaign’s **Total CPM**, and those elements’ individual CPMs.

Refer to [Spending reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview) for more information on each of the metrics included in the campaign’s **Total CPM**.
If desired, enter the minimum amount you’re willing to bid for 1K ad impressions.
The Min Bid Price must be less than the campaign’s Max Bid Price.
Choose the campaign’s Start Date and, if desired, End Date.
Complete all other required fields and specify any additional, optional targeting settings.

Refer to the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) to review each required and optional campaign targeting element, and for additional support with applying your desired settings.
If desired, save your campaign’s targeting settings as a new campaign template.
Select **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format, or click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

sections.heading: Create a new campaign from the Dashboard app
heading_path: Create a new campaign from the Dashboard app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to create a new campaign from the Dashboard app:
Open the Dashboard app.
Select **Create New** and click **Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window, which you’ll use to specify certain campaign details.
Open the **Insertion Order** menu and choose an existing IO.
Enter a name for the campaign.
Choose an [Advanced](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) or [PG](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) **Campaign Type**.
Select a **Campaign Creation Method**.
Click **From Scratch** to open an empty campaign creation form.
Click **From Template** to open a campaign creation form that includes the settings you previously saved as a template.
If you select **From Template**, open the **Template** menu to search and select the desired template.
Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign’s details page, where you can specify campaign settings and targeting rules.
Follow steps 8 through 15 of the Create a new campaign from the Campaigns app workflow to finish campaign setup.
**Campaign template notice:** Items included in the **Campaign Info** section, such as budget, bid price, and date details, are excluded from campaign templates.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Follow these steps to save a campaign’s settings as a template:
Create a new campaign or open an existing campaign.
Apply your desired settings to the campaign.
Refer to [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for additional support.
Click **Save As Template**. This will open the **Save As Template** pop-up window.
Enter a name for the template.
Choose which campaign settings to include in the template.
Click **Select All** to include all applicable settings.
Select individual sections to include.
Select **Save Template** to apply the selected settings to the template.

**More on campaign management:** This article outlines the ways that you can manage existing campaigns from the Campaigns app. You can also adjust certain campaign elements–like budgets and bid prices–directly from a dashboard. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for step-by-step instructions.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Follow these steps to review a campaign from the Campaigns app:
Open the Campaigns app.
Search or filter the table to locate the desired insertion order (IO).
Click the name of the IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
Review the **Insertion Order Info** table for campaign-level details such as statuses, spend and pacing information, performance metrics, and more.
Open the column selector to add additional metric columns to the table, if desired.
Search or filter to locate a specific campaign.
Select the campaign’s name to review and manage the individual campaign’s settings, details, and targeting rules.
You can also review key campaign details from the Dashboard app. Refer to our [Data dashboards](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11510700-data-dashboards) resources for more information.
Complete the Review campaigns workflow to open an existing campaign and manage any of its details, including its **Total Budget**, **Daily Budget**, **Max Bid Price**, and **Min Bid Price**.
You can also change your campaigns’ total and daily budgets directly from the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app. The steps you’ll take to apply these changes are outlined below.

**Set, Add, or Split:** When you change a campaign’s total budget, you’ll choose whether to **Set**, **Add**, or **Split** the new value. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Set, Add, Split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_446aae6bbb) for more information on these options.
Note that budgets are editable for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Follow these steps to change your campaigns’ total budgets individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to update with a new budget.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Total Budget**. This will open the **Set/Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
Enter the new value in the **Total Budget** field.
Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split** depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
Select **Set** to add a total budget for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to an existing total budget.
Follow these steps to change your campaigns’ daily budgets individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to update with a new budget.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Daily Budget**. This will open the **Set/Change Daily Budget** pop-up window.
Enter the desired value in the **Daily Budget** field.
Select **Set** to add a daily budget for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to an existing daily budget.

sections.heading: Manage Max Bid Prices and Min Bid Prices
heading_path: Manage Max Bid Prices and Min Bid Prices

blocks.text: Follow these steps to set or update your campaigns’ Max Bid Prices or Min Bid Prices individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to update with a Max Bid Price or Min Bid Price.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).

Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Max Bid Price** or **Min Bid Price**. This will open the **Set/Change Max Bid Price** or **Set/Change Min Bid Price** pop-up window, depending on your selection.
Enter the new value in the **Max Bid Price** or **Min Bid Price** field.
Select **Set** to add a Max or Min Bid Price for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to an existing Max or Min Bid Price.
Follow these steps to pause **Running** campaigns individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to temporarily stop from serving impressions.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
Click **Pause** to temporarily stop ad serving for the selected campaign(s).

**More on CampaignPulse:** Refer to [Campaigns overview: AI Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_b80f13a4bb) for more information on CampaignPulse, including which campaigns are eligible and which campaign-performance elements it checks.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical blockers to a running campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for [eligible](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55)campaigns in the following ways:
From the **Insertion Order Info** page
From the **Campaign details** page
From the Dashboard app

sections.heading: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Insertion Order Info page
heading_path: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Insertion Order Info page

blocks.text: Follow these steps to access CampaignPulse and review its insights from the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app:
Open the Campaigns app.
Select an insertion order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
Locate the **AI Insights** column.
Select **Run Now**.
Select the **AI Insights** icon next to the desired campaign. This will open the **AI Insights** panel.
A number indicates that CampaignPulse identified risks to campaign delivery.
An enabled **AI Insights** icon with no number indicates that the campaign is currently eligible for CampaignPulse, but no critical underdelivery risks were identified.
A disabled **AI Insights** icon indicates that the campaign is currently ineligible for CampaignPulse.
If desired, filter the insights by type.

For more support with taking action on the CampaignPulse insights, refer to [Campaigns overview: CampaignPulse delivery insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_595b0bbe29).

sections.heading: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Campaign details page
heading_path: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Campaign details page

blocks.text: Follow these steps to access CampaignPulse and review its insights from the **Campaign Details** page of the Campaigns app:
Open the Campaigns app.
Select an insertion order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
Locate the **Actions** column.
Select the pencil icon next to the desired campaign. This will open the **Campaign details** page, where you can edit the campaign’s details and/or run CampaignPulse insights.
Select the **AI Insights** icon at the top of the page. This will open the **AI Insights** panel.
A number indicates that CampaignPulse identified risks to campaign delivery.
An enabled **AI Insights** icon with number indicates that the campaign is currently eligible for CampaignPulse, but no critical underdelivery risks were identified.
A disabled **AI Insights** icon indicates that the campaign is currently ineligible for CampaignPulse.
Click **Run Now**.
If desired, filter the insights by type.

sections.heading: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Dashboard app
heading_path: Run and review CampaignPulse insights from the Dashboard app

blocks.text: Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for step-by-step instructions on running and reviewing CampaignPulse insights from the Dashboard app.
You can edit one campaign at a time. Follow these steps to edit a campaign:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign that you’d like to edit.
Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
Open the **Change** menu and select **Edit**. This will open the campaign’s details page, where you can update key campaign settings and targeting rules.
Apply and save your desired changes.
Follow these steps to duplicate a campaign:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign that you’d like to duplicate.
Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
Open the **Change** menu and select **Duplicate**. This will open the **Duplicate Campaign** pop-up window.
Choose which IO should be associated with the duplicated campaign.
Select a start date and, if desired, an end date for the campaign.
Click **Duplicate**. This will create a new draft campaign based on the existing campaign that you duplicated.
Edit the campaign to apply your desired changes and run it.

**Campaign deletion notice:** Note that deleted campaigns are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating a campaign and updating it to reflect any desired changes. You can also pause a campaign at any time.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Follow these steps to delete campaigns individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to delete.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
Open the **Change** menu and select **Delete**. You’ll be prompted to confirm your selection.

sections.heading: Apply Bid Model settings to a campaign
heading_path: Apply Bid Model settings to a campaign

blocks.text: **More on advanced modeling:** A Bid Model is a high-performance machine that you can steer to optimize your campaigns. You create a set of rules that the Bid Model deploys as the campaign runs. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview), allocate budgets with [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), and define priorities with [Dimension Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) to optimize performance in real time. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more information.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Follow these steps to apply Bid Model settings to one campaign at a time:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign that you’d like to model.
Select the checkbox next to the campaign.

Open the **More** menu and select **Optimize Campaign**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app, where you can apply your desired Bid Model settings to any [supported campaign dimensions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177).
Follow these steps to apply or change end dates individually or in bulk:
Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
Locate the campaign that you’d like to update with a new End Date.
Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
Click **Set End Date**. This will open the **Set/Change End Date** pop-up window.
Choose the desired End Date.
Select **Set** to add an End Date for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to a campaign’s existing End Date settings.
You can restore an expired campaign by extending its End Date. This will reactivate the campaign, which will resume serving ads as long as its budget hasn’t been depleted.

Note that an insertion order’s (IO) status outweighs the statuses of its individual campaigns. You can restore an expired IO by extending its End Date from the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app.

# Create or manage a campaign

## Campaigns overview

> **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing campaigns in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

Campaigns are the individual marketing strategies that define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. They contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify. Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more details, or continue reading to create a new campaign or manage an existing one.

Note that you’ll need to assign the new campaign to an existing insertion order (IO) at the time of campaign creation. Refer to these resources to create an IO if you haven’t yet completed this step:

- [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview)
- [Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io)
- [Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)

## Create a new campaign

> **More on running a campaign:** Note that a campaign doesn’t immediately begin spending and serving when you choose to **Run** it. First, the campaign will undergo a review process to confirm that it meets certain requirements. You’ll know when a campaign is approved when its status changes from **Pending** to **Running**. We’ll also notify you via email. Refer to [Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQs)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498457-campaigns-frequently-asked-questions-faq) for campaign-status definitions, and go to Review campaigns to learn how to check a campaign’s current status.

You can create a new campaign in the following ways:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

Note that you’ll be prompted to select an IO when you enter your campaign’s details. You must select a budget-based insertion order (IO) if the campaign will have a monetary budget, or an impression-based IO if the campaign will have an impression budget. Refer to [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview)for more information on the differences between them.

### Create a new campaign from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to create a new campaign in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose the insertion order that will serve as the parent hierarchy for the new campaign. You’ll arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the campaign.
5. Choose an [Advanced](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) or [PG](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) **Campaign Type**.
6. Select a **Campaign Creation Method**.
   1. Click **From Scratch** to open an empty campaign creation form.
   2. Click **From Template** to open a campaign creation form that includes the settings you previously saved as a template.
   3. If you select **From Template**, open the **Template** menu to search and select the desired template.
7. Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign’s details page, where you can specify campaign settings and targeting rules.
8. Enter the maximum budget or maximum impressions that the campaign should spend.
9. Enter the maximum amount you’re willing to bid for 1,000 ad impressions.
   1. If you specify a Min Bid Price, the Max Bid Price must be greater than that value.
10. Select **Show CPM Breakdown** to review which campaign elements are contributing to the campaign’s **Total CPM**, and those elements’ individual CPMs.
    1. Refer to [Spending reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview) for more information on each of the metrics included in the campaign’s **Total CPM**.
11. If desired, enter the minimum amount you’re willing to bid for 1K ad impressions.
    1. The Min Bid Price must be less than the campaign’s Max Bid Price.
12. Choose the campaign’s Start Date and, if desired, End Date.
13. Complete all other required fields and specify any additional, optional targeting settings.
    1. Refer to the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) to review each required and optional campaign targeting element, and for additional support with applying your desired settings.
14. If desired, save your campaign’s targeting settings as a new campaign template.
15. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format, or click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

### Create a new campaign from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to create a new campaign from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Select **Create New** and click **Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window, which you’ll use to specify certain campaign details.
3. Open the **Insertion Order** menu and choose an existing IO.
4. Enter a name for the campaign.
5. Choose an [Advanced](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) or [PG](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) **Campaign Type**.
6. Select a **Campaign Creation Method**.
   1. Click **From Scratch** to open an empty campaign creation form.
   2. Click **From Template** to open a campaign creation form that includes the settings you previously saved as a template.
   3. If you select **From Template**, open the **Template** menu to search and select the desired template.
7. Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign’s details page, where you can specify campaign settings and targeting rules.
8. Follow steps 8 through 15 of the Create a new campaign from the Campaigns app workflow to finish campaign setup.

## Create a campaign template

> **Campaign template notice:** Items included in the **Campaign Info** section, such as budget, bid price, and date details, are excluded from campaign templates.

Follow these steps to save a campaign’s settings as a template:

1. Create a new campaign or open an existing campaign.
2. Apply your desired settings to the campaign.
   1. Refer to [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for additional support.
3. Click **Save As Template**. This will open the **Save As Template** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the template.
5. Choose which campaign settings to include in the template.
   1. Click **Select All** to include all applicable settings.
   2. Select individual sections to include.
6. Select **Save Template** to apply the selected settings to the template.

## Manage existing campaigns

> **More on campaign management:** This article outlines the ways that you can manage existing campaigns from the Campaigns app. You can also adjust certain campaign elements–like budgets and bid prices–directly from a dashboard. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for step-by-step instructions.

### Review campaigns

Follow these steps to review a campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or filter the table to locate the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Click the name of the IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
4. Review the **Insertion Order Info** table for campaign-level details such as statuses, spend and pacing information, performance metrics, and more.
   1. Open the column selector to add additional metric columns to the table, if desired.
5. Search or filter to locate a specific campaign.
6. Select the campaign’s name to review and manage the individual campaign’s settings, details, and targeting rules.

You can also review key campaign details from the Dashboard app. Refer to our [Data dashboards](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11510700-data-dashboards) resources for more information.

### Manage campaign budgets

Complete the Review campaigns workflow to open an existing campaign and manage any of its details, including its **Total Budget**, **Daily Budget**, **Max Bid Price**, and **Min Bid Price**.

You can also change your campaigns’ total and daily budgets directly from the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app. The steps you’ll take to apply these changes are outlined below.

### Change a campaign’s total budget

> **Set, Add, or Split:** When you change a campaign’s total budget, you’ll choose whether to **Set**, **Add**, or **Split** the new value. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Set, Add, Split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_446aae6bbb) for more information on these options. Note that budgets are editable for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

Follow these steps to change your campaigns’ total budgets individually or in bulk:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
2. Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to update with a new budget.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Total Budget**. This will open the **Set/Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
5. Enter the new value in the **Total Budget** field.
6. Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split** depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
   1. You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
7. Select **Set** to add a total budget for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to an existing total budget.

### Change a campaign’s daily budget

Follow these steps to change your campaigns’ daily budgets individually or in bulk:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review campaigns workflow.
2. Locate the campaign(s) that you’d like to update with a new budget.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Daily Budget**. This will open the **Set/Change Daily Budget** pop-up window.

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical blockers to a running campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for [eligible](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55)campaigns in the following ways:

# Retargeted audience overview

## Retargeted audience overview

Retargeted audiences help your brand stay connected with your past website visitors.

When you create a Retargeted audience, you’ll choose a data-collection period, and add a unique Pixel Script Code–also known as a retargeting tag–to your website’s header. Once that retargeting tag is installed, the Retargeted audience will capture any unique users who visit your website. You can target the Retargeted audience to help increase engagement by bringing past visitors back to your website, or block it to ensure that every dollar of your upper-funnel awareness campaigns goes toward driving new interest for your brand.

Refer to [Create or manage a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience) for more information on how to create a Retargeted audience and obtain a Pixel Script Code.

## Retargeted audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Retargeted audiences. The following conditions must also be met before an advertiser or campaign becomes eligible for Retargeted audience targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Data collection period** | Up to 12 months |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type*** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience creation date**** | 1 year (recommended) |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. Healthcare advertisers should note that a single campaign, however, can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target a Retargeted audience consisting of your website’s past visitors if it’s already targeting an HCP Geofarmed audience.

** **Audience creation date:** While you can target or block a Retargeted audience that you created more than one year ago, we recommend creating a new one to ensure it includes the latest Reach data.

## Retargeted audience statuses

You can review a Retargeted audience’s status on the **Retargeted Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience#h_14404f5078) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience#h_18c8a49f33). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Retargeted audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Data Collection Period

The data collection period will add users to the Retargeted audience during a set timeframe. For example, if you select “30 Days” on June 30th, we’ll add users who visit your website between July 1st and July 30th. If you run a campaign with this audience on August 30th, it’ll still contain users from the July 1st-30th timeframe. In other words, the Retargeted audience’s data collection period represents a snapshot of data over a fixed set of dates.

Refer to [Create or manage a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience) for step-by-step instructions on choosing a data collection period.

### Reach

In campaign reporting, **Reach** represents the number of unique individuals who were exposed to your ad. In Retargeted audiences, however, this metric represents the total targetable audience that you can potentially reach by targeting that particular audience. These are the users who visited your campaign’s website during the data collection period you chose and where a Pixel Script Code was installed.

Depending on a Retargeted audience’s **Reach**, you may need to target additional audiences to a campaign to help ensure that it has enough data to [pace](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) appropriately. Note that the actual addressable audience will also become smaller as you apply additional targeting rules and other settings to your campaign.

We recommend applying forecasting and reporting methods to determine whether a Retargeted campaign is expected to spend its budget in full. Refer to [Other campaign targeting considerations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide#h_8b32ef79d4) to leverage your preferred tools in the Campaigns, Planner, Reports, and Insights app and right-size your Retargeted campaign strategy.

### Pixel Script Code installation

When you create a Retargeted audience, we’ll provide a unique Pixel Script Code–also known as a retargeting tag. You’ll need to integrate this code into your website’s header to begin capturing users for the audience. If another user will integrate the tag on your behalf, you can send the Pixel Script Code and step-by-step instructions to them directly from the IQM platform.

Refer to [Create or manage a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience) for more information on how to complete this process.

## Locate additional Retargeted audience resources

- [Create or manage a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750312-create-or-manage-a-retargeted-audience)
- [Troubleshoot a Retargeted audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750322-troubleshoot-a-retargeted-audience)

title: Segmented audience overview

blocks.text: Segmented audiences include groups of users who share similar traits. You’ll add segments or groups of segments to the audience to reach that unique group of users. These audiences can be highly specific or more broad, depending on your campaign’s goals and your scale considerations. For example, you might include empty nesters who love hiking, or doctors specializing in pediatrics.

Review IQM Healthcare audience segments and IQM Political audience segments for more details on these Segmented audience types, and refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to choose curated audience segments or create your own from thousands of customer attributes.

We also offer targeting for custom audiences, which allows you to onboard your own custom segments and add them to your campaigns. Review [Custom advertiser segments overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11844263-custom-advertiser-segments-overview) for more information.

**More on Healthcare audiences:** Healthcare advertisers can create another audience type, ABM audiences, to maximize relevance, engagement, and value. These ABM audiences leverage comprehensive hospital data from providers such as HealthLink Dimensions (HLD) or RevOptimal to pass personalized messages to healthcare professionals at scale, and with a privacy-safe approach.

With ABM audiences, you can craft highly specific healthcare audiences using custom and pre-defined segments based on [account-based attributes](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview#h_70d7a117e3) such as health systems, specialty practices, and [NPI reach](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview#h_cd1bd07d38). Refer to [Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview) for more information.

blocks.text: Healthcare advertisers can create Segmented audiences for precise outreach to healthcare professionals across a number of audience categories. These segments vary by data provider and include NPI-based targeting.

For ready-to-use targeting, you can also add PurpleLab’s off-the-shelf (OTS) segments for healthcare professionals (HCP) and patients. When you add segments, you’ll find them under **IQM Healthcare** › **PurpleLab** › **HCP** › **OTS** and **IQM Healthcare** › **PurpleLab** › **Patient** › **OTS**.

Targeting strategies for Healthcare campaigns can be especially challenging as certain industry professionals don’t have NPI numbers associated with them. For example, you may want to reach nurses who play a major role in educating patients about their treatments and medications. In these instances, you can target nurse audience segments powered by Data360 to reach these healthcare professionals by specialty rather than NPI number. These segments span specialty categories including Diagnosis, Diagnosis Test, Imaging Test, Lab Test, Prescription, Procedure, and Treatment.
Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to start building Segmented audiences for Healthcare campaigns.

Political advertisers can create Segmented audiences to reach voter audiences based on a number of audience categories such as demographics, donor status, income, propensity to vote, and more. These segments vary by data provider.

You can also add StatSocial’s political audience segments, which group voters by the news outlets, political accounts, and voices they follow and engage with on social media. When you add segments, you’ll find them under **IQM Political** › **StatSocial**.

Public affairs advertisers can create Segmented audiences for campaigns aiming to influence policy and decision-makers in government. The opinions of these individuals’ aides, staffers, family, friends, and more all play a role in influencing how they vote. When you create a Segmented audience from Power Segments, you cross-reference geographic proximity and other signals to identify and reach users in these individuals’ networks. You’ll choose whether to target their “sphere” (closest contacts via PowerSphere segments) and/or “orbit” (second-degree connections via PowerOrbit segments) to achieve your campaign goals.
Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to start building Segmented audiences for Political campaigns.

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Segmented audiences. The types of Segmented audience segments you can use, however, depend on the brand’s vertical. For example, only Healthcare advertisers are eligible to target Nurse and Healthcare Practitioner audience segments. Similarly, only Political advertisers are eligible to target Voter and Constituent audience segments.

Segmented audiences and their individual audience segments each display a CPM price.

A Segmented audience’s CPM price isn’t the total price of each of its individual audience segments. Instead, its CPM price is the cost of the highest-priced segment. For example, if one audience includes 100 Segmented audience segments, and each of those segments is priced at a $0.10 CPM price, then the audience’s total CPM price is $0.10. In instances where the audience includes differently priced segments, its total CPM price is the cost of the highest-priced segment.
Note that there’s no cost associated with adding segments to a Segmented audience. The listed CPM prices will apply once you run a campaign that’s targeting the Segmented audience.

blocks.text: An “OR” relationship means that a user must meet at least one condition, while an “AND” relationship means that a user must meet all of the conditions.

A Segment Group applies an “OR” relationship to each audience segment within it. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the Segmented audience segments that you added to the group, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

A single Segmented audience can include multiple Segment Groups, which allows you to get more specific with your audience requirements. You can choose an “AND” or an “OR” relationship between each Segment Group. For example, an advertiser creates a Segmented audience with two Segment Groups. An “OR” relationship would allow their campaign to target a user if they’re included in any of the Segmented audience segments that they added to either Segment Group. However, an “AND” relationship would only allow their campaign to target a user if they’re included in at least one audience segment from each Segment Group.

Note that “AND” relationships can impact an audience’s scale because they’re more restrictive than “OR” relationships. To help avoid interruptions to your campaign’s ability to spend, review an audience’s estimated **Reach** prior to targeting it.
