# Segmented audience overview

## Segmented audience overview

Segmented audiences include groups of users who share similar traits. You’ll add segments or groups of segments to the audience to reach that unique group of users. These audiences can be highly specific or more broad, depending on your campaign’s goals and your scale considerations. For example, you might include empty nesters who love hiking, or doctors specializing in pediatrics.

Review IQM Healthcare audience segments and IQM Political audience segments for more details on these Segmented audience types, and refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to choose curated audience segments or create your own from thousands of customer attributes.

We also offer targeting for custom audiences, which allows you to onboard your own custom segments and add them to your campaigns. Review [Custom advertiser segments overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11844263-custom-advertiser-segments-overview) for more information.

### IQM Healthcare audience segments

> **More on Healthcare audiences:** Healthcare advertisers can create another audience type, ABM audiences, to maximize relevance, engagement, and value. These ABM audiences leverage comprehensive hospital data from providers such as HealthLink Dimensions (HLD) or RevOptimal to pass personalized messages to healthcare professionals at scale, and with a privacy-safe approach. With ABM audiences, you can craft highly specific healthcare audiences using custom and pre-defined segments based on [account-based attributes](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview#h_70d7a117e3) such as health systems, specialty practices, and [NPI reach](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview#h_cd1bd07d38). Refer to [Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview) for more information.

Healthcare advertisers can create Segmented audiences for precise outreach to healthcare professionals across a number of audience categories. These segments vary by data provider and include NPI-based targeting.

For ready-to-use targeting, you can also add PurpleLab’s off-the-shelf (OTS) segments for healthcare professionals (HCP) and patients. When you add segments, you’ll find them under **IQM Healthcare** › **PurpleLab** › **HCP** › **OTS** and **IQM Healthcare** › **PurpleLab** › **Patient** › **OTS**.

Targeting strategies for Healthcare campaigns can be especially challenging as certain industry professionals don’t have NPI numbers associated with them. For example, you may want to reach nurses who play a major role in educating patients about their treatments and medications. In these instances, you can target nurse audience segments powered by Data360 to reach these healthcare professionals by specialty rather than NPI number. These segments span specialty categories including Diagnosis, Diagnosis Test, Imaging Test, Lab Test, Prescription, Procedure, and Treatment.

Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to start building Segmented audiences for Healthcare campaigns.

### IQM Political audience segments

Political advertisers can create Segmented audiences to reach voter audiences based on a number of audience categories such as demographics, donor status, income, propensity to vote, and more. These segments vary by data provider.

You can also add StatSocial’s political audience segments, which group voters by the news outlets, political accounts, and voices they follow and engage with on social media. When you add segments, you’ll find them under **IQM Political** › **StatSocial**.

Public affairs advertisers can create Segmented audiences for campaigns aiming to influence policy and decision-makers in government. The opinions of these individuals’ aides, staffers, family, friends, and more all play a role in influencing how they vote. When you create a Segmented audience from Power Segments, you cross-reference geographic proximity and other signals to identify and reach users in these individuals’ networks. You’ll choose whether to target their “sphere” (closest contacts via PowerSphere segments) and/or “orbit” (second-degree connections via PowerOrbit segments) to achieve your campaign goals.

Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to start building Segmented audiences for Political campaigns.

## Segmented audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Segmented audiences. The types of Segmented audience segments you can use, however, depend on the brand’s vertical. For example, only Healthcare advertisers are eligible to target Nurse and Healthcare Practitioner audience segments. Similarly, only Political advertisers are eligible to target Voter and Constituent audience segments.

A campaign must also meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for Segmented audience targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical*** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type**** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience data provider** | One data provider per audience |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Advertiser vertical: Specialty** advertisers are eligible to create and target Segmented audiences that include only non-Healthcare and non-Political audience segments. **Healthcare** advertisers may be eligible to create and target Segmented audiences that include Specialty and/or Healthcare audience segments. **Political** advertisers may be eligible to create and target Segmented audiences that include Specialty and/or Political audience segments.

****Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A campaign targeting an ABM audience, however, must only include one or more ABM audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target an ABM audience if it’s already targeting a Segmented audience. Refer to [ABM audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview) for more information.

## Segmented audience pricing

Segmented audiences and their individual audience segments each display a CPM price.

A Segmented audience’s CPM price isn’t the total price of each of its individual audience segments. Instead, its CPM price is the cost of the highest-priced segment. For example, if one audience includes 100 Segmented audience segments, and each of those segments is priced at a $0.10 CPM price, then the audience’s total CPM price is $0.10. In instances where the audience includes differently priced segments, its total CPM price is the cost of the highest-priced segment.

Note that there’s no cost associated with adding segments to a Segmented audience. The listed CPM prices will apply once you run a campaign that’s targeting the Segmented audience.

### Example: Segmented audience pricing

> **Segmented audience price notice:** The prices listed in this example are for illustrative purposes only. Refer to the IQM platform for the current price of each audience segment.

| **Example scenario of Segmented audience segment selections** | **Example Segmented audience cost (CPM)** |
| --- | --- |
| 1 $1.50 CPM segment selected 1 $1.25 CPM segment selected | $1.50 |
| 10 $1.50 CPM segments selected 1 $1.25 CPM segment selected | $1.50 |
| 10 $1.50 CPM segments selected 5 $1.25 CPM segments selected 3 $1.75 CPM segments selected | $1.75 |

## Segmented audience statuses

You can review a Segmented audience’s status on the **Segmented Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience#h_ba9078afb7) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Segmented audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Segment Groups and relationships

An “OR” relationship means that a user must meet at least one condition, while an “AND” relationship means that a user must meet all of the conditions.

A Segment Group applies an “OR” relationship to each audience segment within it. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the Segmented audience segments that you added to the group, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

A single Segmented audience can include multiple Segment Groups, which allows you to get more specific with your audience requirements. You can choose an “AND” or an “OR” relationship between each Segment Group. For example, an advertiser creates a Segmented audience with two Segment Groups. An “OR” relationship would allow their campaign to target a user if they’re included in any of the Segmented audience segments that they added to either Segment Group. However, an “AND” relationship would only allow their campaign to target a user if they’re included in at least one audience segment from each Segment Group.

Note that “AND” relationships can impact an audience’s scale because they’re more restrictive than “OR” relationships. To help avoid interruptions to your campaign’s ability to spend, review an audience’s estimated **Reach** prior to targeting it.

#### Example: Segment Groups and relationships

| **Segmented audience targeting scenario** | **Segment Group strategy** |
| --- | --- |
| Target nurses who work in the anesthesiology or pediatric anesthesiology specialties, and are located in Florida. | **Group 1 (OR)** - Nurse segment(s) ***AND*** **Group 2 (OR)** - Geography segment(s) |
| Target donors who support Animal Welfare causes, or have been in the vicinity of a given Cabinet Member in recent months. | **Group 1 (OR) -** Donor segment(s) ***OR*** **Group 2 (OR)** - Advocacy segment(s) |
| Target empty nesters in their late 60s who donate to medical-related causes, own their home, and show interest in outdoor activities. | **Group 1 (OR) -** Age segment(s) ***AND*** **Group 2 (OR)** - Home-ownership-status segment(s) ***AND*** **Group 3 (OR)** - Outdoor interest segment(s) |

### Segmented Audience Breakdown

Once a Segmented audience features a **Ready** status, its **Audience Breakdown** will populate with audience insights across genders, age groups, devices, and geographies. You can review these insights and apply them to your campaign to craft a personalized strategy based on the audience’s key characteristics.

Refer to [Review a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience#h_ba9078afb7) for instructions on how to locate these insights for a given audience.

## Locate additional Segmented audience resources

- [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience)
- [Troubleshoot a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749141-troubleshoot-a-segmented-audience)

# Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings

## Optimization & Delivery overview

**Optimization**, **Budget Capping**, **Bid Pacing**, and **Frequency Capping** are the four elements that form a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings. How you manage them can impact the campaign’s ability to pace on track and achieve its performance goals.

Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on these elements, or continue reading to manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings.

## Video tutorial: Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings

## Locate a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery section

Follow these steps to locate a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery section, which you’ll use to manage its **Optimization**, **Budget Capping**, **Bid Pacing**, and **Frequency Capping** settings.

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select the desired campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
   1. Click **+ Create Campaign** if you’d like to add Optimization & Delivery settings to a new campaign instead.
4. Locate and expand the **Optimization & Delivery** section.

## Manage Optimization

You can choose one **Optimization** method per campaign:

- Set Rule Based Optimization (Manual)
- Set AI Based Optimization (Automated)

Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on each of these options, including their requirements.

### Set Rule Based Optimization (Manual)

> **More on manual optimizations:** Refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview) for more information on how to approach manual optimization and which tools and features you can leverage to improve a campaign’s performance.

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s manual optimization settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. Click **Rule Based**.
3. A summary of the campaign’s **Advanced Modeling** settings will display after you apply any [Bid Model settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) to the campaign.
   1. **Advanced Modeling** settings can be applied if the campaign’s daily budget equals or exceeds $100 and has a duration of 3 or more days. At least one supported dimension (Creatives, Location, Inventory, Device) must also be added to the campaign.

### Set AI Based Optimization (Automated)

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s AI-based optimization settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. Click **AI Based**.
3. Choose one **Campaign Objective**: **Awareness**, **Consideration**, or **Conversion**.
4. Select one **Campaign Goal**.
   1. The Increase goals and Reduction goals available in the **Campaign Goal** menu are dependent on the selected **Campaign Objective**. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) to review goal options by objective.
5. If desired, enter a target KPI value related to the selected **Campaign Goal**.
   1. The IQM platform’s AI engine will aim to achieve this performance metric.
   2. Refer to [AI Based Optimization - Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_6b15684c1c) for more details.

## Manage Bid Shading

Bid Shading is available for campaigns with either **Rule Based Optimization** or **AI Based Optimization** settings applied.

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s **Bid Shading** settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. The **Bid Shading** feature is enabled by default. Select the toggle switch at any time to disable it, if desired.
3. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections to the new campaign in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the new campaign.
   3. Select **Save** to apply your selections to an existing campaign.

## Manage Budget Capping

Budget Capping is available for campaigns with either **Rule Based Optimization** or **AI Based Optimization** settings applied.

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s **Budget Capping** settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. The **Budget Capping** feature is disabled by default. Select the toggle switch at any time to enable it, if desired.
3. Define a budget cap for impressions, clicks, and/or conversions.
   1. Enter a **Maximum Daily** and/or **Maximum Total** spending limit for **Impressions**.
   2. Enter a **Maximum Daily** and/or **Maximum Total** spending limit for **Clicks**.
   3. Enter a **Maximum Daily** and/or **Maximum Total** spending limit for **Conversions**.
4. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections to the new campaign in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the new campaign.
   3. Select **Save** to apply your selections to an existing campaign.

## Manage Frequency Capping

> **More on Frequency Capping:** Frequency capping is a campaign-level setting that limits the number of times you’ll serve your ad to the same user within specific timeframe(s). A maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. Review [Optimization & Delivery overview - Frequency Capping](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_a623e383be) for more information and requirements. Note that your campaign may serve more impressions to a device identifier if the corresponding IQM ID or Ramp ID is not associated during bidding. Refer to [Frequency Capping overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8480958-frequency-capping-overview) for more details.

Frequency Capping is available for campaigns with either **Rule Based Optimization** or **AI Based Optimization** settings applied.

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s **Frequency Capping** settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. The **Frequency Capping** feature is disabled by default. Select the toggle switch at any time to enable it, if desired.
3. Add the campaign’s frequency capping rules.
   1. Enter the desired number of impressions.
   2. Enter a duration and select the duration type from the dropdown menu.
   3. Repeat the process to add up to four frequency rules per campaign: One for each [duration type](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_3988196011).
4. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections to the new campaign in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the new campaign.
   3. Select **Save** to apply your selections to an existing campaign.

## Manage Bid Pacing

Bid Pacing is available for campaigns with either **Rule Based Optimization** or **AI Based Optimization** settings applied.

Follow these steps to manage a campaign’s **Bid Pacing** settings:

1. Locate and expand the Optimization & Delivery section.
2. The **Bid Pacing** feature is enabled by default. Select the toggle switch at any time to disable it, if desired.
3. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections to the new campaign in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the new campaign.
   3. Select **Save** to apply your selections to an existing campaign.

## Review KPI performance details

Your reporting method will differ based on whether you chose **Rule Based** or **AI Based Optimization** settings for the campaign.

### Review performance details for Rule Based campaigns

Refer to the [“Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) article to review each of the reports, dashboards, and data insights that you can leverage to uncover and interpret campaign performance details.

### Review performance details for AI Based campaigns

Follow these steps to review daily **AI Based Optimization** performance details:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select the insertion order to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Select **AI Based** from the desired campaign’s **Optimization Method** column. This will open the **AI Based Optimization** pop-up window.
   1. You may need to select **Optimization Method** from the **Columns** menu to add it to the table.
4. Review the original objective, goal, and KPI details you entered when you set up the campaign’s optimization settings.
5. Review the campaign’s performance details for the selected campaign goal.
   1. Refer to [AI Based Optimization - KPI Performance Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_9b5c185bf6) for more information on interpreting the performance data.

# Add and manage funds

## Adding funds overview

All agencies with Workspace-level ownership can access the Organization app and use it to manage funds. The **Bill & Payment** tab of the Organization app is where you’ll add your payment details.

### Balance management

Agencies need their own balance, and each of their seats also requires its own separate balance. However, note that a customer’s spending is restricted by the balance in the agency’s account, even if the customer’s seat has a higher balance.

Since funds are maintained separately, there’s no way for agencies to distribute funds they’ve already added to the Workspace to individual advertisers. Instead, agencies are able to add new payments to their customers’ accounts at any time via a ledger entry.

## Add a ledger entry

A ledger entry allows you to confirm you received a payment outside of the IQM system, and offer that paid balance to the advertiser.

Follow these steps to add payments as a ledger entry:

1. Open the Customers app.
2. Select the Finance tab.
3. Choose the desired advertiser.
4. Click **+ Add Payment.** This will open the **Add Payment** pop-up window.
5. Select **Add As Fund**.
6. Enter the details of the payment you received from the customer:
   1. Add the payment amount, which will be added to the customer’s account.
   2. Select the date that the payment was received.
   3. Open the **Mode of Transfer** menu to choose how the payment was sent to you (e.g., Wire Transfer, Check, etc.)
   4. Add the ID of the transaction.
   5. If desired, select **Browse** to upload proof of the payment you received outside of the IQM system.
7. Select **Add Payment**.

This payment will be added to the customer’s funds and reflected as a balance once the payment is completed and approved.

## Add a ledger entry against an invoice

You can add a ledger entry against an invoice when you received payment outside of the IQM system.

Follow these steps to make a payment against a generated invoice:

1. Open the Customers app.
2. Select the Finance tab.
3. Choose the desired advertiser.
4. Click **+ Add Payment.** This will open the **Add Payment** pop-up window.
5. Select **Against Invoice**.
6. Open the **Select Invoice** menu to choose the desired invoice.
7. Enter the details of the payment you received from the customer:
   1. Add the payment amount, which will be added to the customer’s account.
   2. Select the date that the payment was received.
   3. Open the **Mode of Transfer** menu to choose how the payment was sent to you (e.g., Wire Transfer, Check, etc.)
   4. Add the ID of the transaction.
   5. If desired, select **Browse** to upload proof of the payment you received outside of the IQM system.
8. Select **Add Payment**.

The selected invoice will automatically be marked as paid once the payment is completed.

## Offer credit

> **More on credit:** Agencies can offer credit to their respective customers in instances when you’d like to maintain a post-paid relationship. As the credited amount immediately becomes directly available to the seat, we recommend completing a credit check prior to offering a credit.

Follow these steps to offer a credit to a customer:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Add a ledger entry workflow.
2. Scroll to the **Credit Management** section.
3. Click **Offer Credits**. This will open the **Offer Credits** pop-up window.
4. Add the amount you’d like to credit to the customer.
5. If desired, select or deselect **Direct Credit**.
6. Click **Offer Credits**.

The offered credit will appear in the customer’s Organization app in the **Bill & Payment** section, where they can claim the credit and use it as available funds.

## Add funds

> **Agency payment notice:** Agencies with Workspace-level ownership can manage white label settings to receive customer payments directly via PayPal. Refer to [Manage an Organization Profile](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003211-manage-an-organization-profile) for more information on managing white label, invoice, and margin settings.

The **Add Funds** feature allows both agencies and advertisers to make prepayments via PayPal or a financial institution directly into their seat balance.

Follow these steps to add funds to your account:

1. Select the **Bill & Payment** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Payments**.
3. Select **Add Funds**. This will open the **Add Funds** pop-up panel.
4. Enter the dollar amount that you want to add.
   1. The amount you enter is inclusive of fees. For example, if you enter “$1,000” and are charged a 3.5% transaction fee, you will pay $1,000 and the $965 net funds will be added to your account.
5. Choose how you’d like to make the payment: **Credit Card**, **Debit Card**, or **PayPal**.
6. Select **Pay**. You’ll be prompted to enter your payment information (**Credit Card**, **Debit Card**) or log in and make your payment selections (**PayPal**).

Once processed, the funds will be added to your account. For example, when advertisers add funds, their account balance won’t be added to the Workspace’s balance. We recommend locating the payment in the **Payments** table and adding a comment of up to 250 characters to the **Comment** column with any relevant details.

## Review previous payments

Follow these steps to review the details of previous payment transactions:

1. Select the **Bill & Payment** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Payments**.
3. Open the filter menu to choose which types of payments will appear in the **Payments** table.
4. Review the desired details in the **Payments** table:
   1. **Payment No.**: Review the payment’s transaction number.
   2. **Initiated By:** Review the user who initiated the transaction.
   3. **Transaction On:** Review the date in which the transaction was initiated.
   4. **Net Funds:** Review the total dollar amount added to the account once fees were accounted for.
   5. **Status:** Review whether the funds were successfully added (**Paid**), are still being processed (**Pending**), were cancelled (**Cancelled**), or were unable to be added (**Rejected**).
   6. **Mode of Payment:** Review whether the funds were added via a credit card, debit card, wire transfer, or PayPal transaction.
   7. **Payment Type:** Review whether the payment was added as funds or against an invoice balance.
   8. **Comment:** Review any comments associated with the payment.

## Pay or download an invoice

### Pay an invoice

Follow these steps to pay an invoice:

1. Select the **Bill & Payment** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Invoice**.
3. Select **Pay Now** in the **Actions** column of the invoice you’d like to pay. This will open the **Proceed to Pay** pop-up window.
4. Enter the payment amount.
   1. The amount you enter is inclusive of fees. For example, if you enter “$1,000” and are charged a 3.5% transaction fee, you will pay $1,000 and the $965 net funds will be applied to the invoice.
5. Choose the payment type (**Credit Card**, **Debit Card**, or **PayPal**).
6. Select **Pay**.

### Download an invoice

Follow these steps to review and download existing invoices:

1. Select the **Bill & Payment** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Invoice**.
3. Select the download icon in the **Actions** column of the invoice you’d like to pay.

The invoice will immediately begin downloading to your device.

## Determine your available balance

Open the Dashboard app and refer to the top of the page to review your available balance.

# Conversions overview

## Conversion overview

In a campaign’s **Conversion** section, you’ll associate tracking pixels with your campaign to assign credit for a conversion. Choose a tracking pixel that you’re previously added in the Conversion app, and/or create a new pixel directly from the campaign. Depending on how you set up the conversion, this attribution may be view based (the ad that was last viewed), click based (the ad that was last clicked), or a combination of the two.

## Pixel Conversions

Pixel conversion tracking is a cost-effective way to gain valuable insights into users’ actions. When you track conversions using a tracking pixel, you’ll place a small pixel on your website to allow IQM to measure user actions such as page visits, purchases, or signups. We attribute those conversions to specific ads or campaigns to provide insights into user behavior and preferences, as well as campaign performance.

Refer to [Create a Pixel conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_0c486fbc4a) for more information.

## Postback Conversions

> **Mobile app conversion notice:** Mobile app-based conversions use Postback conversions only.

Postback conversions allow for server-to-server communication with measurement partners such as Kochava, Appsflyer, Singular, and Adjust. You’ll set up the postback on your preferred measurement partner’s platform and copy a impression URL, then return to the IQM platform to add the impression URL to a new postback conversion and assign it to your campaign.

Since postback conversion tracking involves real-time tracking and attribution, this method helps advertisers measure and optimize their mobile ad campaigns more effectively.

Refer to [Create a Postback conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_80ad3405c6) for more information.

## Universal Pixel Conversions

Universal Pixels modernize the standard approach to conversion tracking. While traditional methods often require individual pixels on specific conversion pages, this unified solution fires across your entire website via a single JavaScript tag.

Implementing a Universal Pixel allows you to efficiently capture insights into various user behaviors, including signups, page visits, and purchases. This data is then attributed to individual ads or campaigns, helping you better understand performance trends and customer preferences. Because it supports multiple event types—such as tracking when a purchase is completed or a signup is initiated—this site-wide tag is the recommended way to simplify your measurement and attribution strategy.

Refer to [Create a Universal Pixel conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_3f9ebb7e61) for more information.

## Eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create a Pixel or Postback conversion in the Conversion app. Note, however, that app-level permissions are managed by your Workspace admin.

Certain advertisers are eligible to create a Universal Pixel conversion in the Conversion app if an IQM Super Admin has enabled this feature for your account.

A campaign must also meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for conversions.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced PG |
| **Campaign status*** | Draft Pending Running - No ad impressions served |
| **Conversion type**** | Pixel *or* Postback *or* Universal Pixel |
| **URL formatting** | Begins with “[http://www](http://www).” or “[https://www](https://www).” Ends with the site’s top-level domain (e.g., “.com” or “.org”) |

***Campaign status:** Conversions can be added, edited, or removed from a campaign *only* before the campaign begins serving ad impressions. We recommend confirming that the intended conversion details are applied to the campaign prior to running it.

****Conversion type:** One type of conversion–Pixel or Postback or Universal Pixel–is supported per campaign.

## Key terms and concepts

### Conversion metrics

The Conversion app surfaces a number of conversion reporting metrics. These metrics are critical in assessing whether an ad is performing as expected. They measure the effectiveness of a campaign by tracking the number of users who completed a desired action after interacting with the ad.

Refer to [Conversion reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343706-conversion-reporting-metrics) for a full list of these metrics and their definitions.

### Impression URL and Click URL

The Postback conversion creation process includes adding a Tracking Pixel URL and a Click URL after you select the attribution measurement partner of your choice.

The impression URL will be automatically appended to all creatives to monitor ad impressions across users’ devices. You’ll obtain this URL directly from the measurement partner you chose, then paste it in the available field during conversion creation in the IQM platform.

The Click URL is the destination where users will be directed to when they click on your ad. While this URL is likely a particular page of your brand’s website, you’ll also obtain this URL from the measurement partner you chose.

### Conversion attribution: Hybrid, View Based, Click Based

When you create a new Pixel or Universal Pixel conversion, you’ll choose how we should assign credit for a conversion. Your options include **Hybrid**, **View Based**, or **Click Based** attribution.

**View Based** attribution assigns credit for a conversion to an ad that was last viewed and never clicked, while **Click Based** attribution assigns credit to an ad that was last clicked. **Hybrid** attribution combines both the click-based and view-based methods to assign credit for a conversion either to an ad that was last clicked or an ad that was last viewed but not clicked.

### Advanced pixel customization options

When you create a new Pixel conversion, you’ll have the option to add up to three advanced customization options to it, if desired.

| **Advanced pixel customization option** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Piggyback Pixel URL | An additional URL that can be added to a conversion pixel to send conversion information to a third-party platform. Both Image Pixel and JavaScript Pixel Piggyback URLs are supported. |
| Custom Field | A field used to pass additional data of your choice along with the conversion details, which can then be used in reporting for more detailed insights. |
| Financial Metric | A field used to pass additional financial data along with conversion details, which you can use to calculate [ROAS](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343706-conversion-reporting-metrics#h_ee24234810)performance. |

### Advanced settings

When you create a new Pixel or Universal Pixel conversion, you’ll have the option to add advanced settings that determine exactly how conversion events are attributed to your ad.

| **Advanced setting** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Conversion Duration Settings | Determine the length of time after a user clicks or views an ad after which a conversion can be attributed to that ad. The **Post View Interval** option is available when you select a **View Based** conversion attribution method, the **Post Click Interval** option is available when you select a **Click Based** conversion attribution method, and both are available when you select a **Hybrid** conversion attribution method. |
| Repeat Conversions | Allow for multiple conversions from the same user to be tracked and attributed to the same ad or campaign. Choose whether to count all conversions per user, count only one conversion per user, or count one conversion per user at a time interval that you specify. For example, you might choose to count one conversion per user every day, or once every five hours. Whole numbers between 1 and 6 are accepted for **Days**, and whole numbers between 1 and 23 are accepted for **Hours**. |
| Conversion Modelling | Enable a machine learning technique to attribute conversions to ads that may not have received direct clicks or views from the same device, but from another device used by the same user. Also known as cross-device modelling, this feature is powered by the [IQM Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview). |

# Create or manage a conversion

## Conversions overview

> **Conversion notice:** We recommend confirming that the intended conversion details are applied to the campaign prior to running it. Conversions can be added, edited, or removed from a campaign only before the campaign begins serving.

You can create a Pixel, Postback, or Universal Pixel conversion in the Conversions app. When you track conversions using a tracking pixel, you’ll place a small image pixel on your website to allow IQM to measure user actions such as page visits, purchases, or signups. Postback conversions allow for server-to-server communication with measurement partners, which you’ll use to measure and optimize your mobile ad campaigns more effectively through real-time tracking and attribution.

Refer to [Conversions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview) for more information on the differences between conversion types, or continue reading to create one in the IQM platform.

## Create a conversion

Open the Conversion app to create the following conversions:

- Pixel
- Postback
- Universal Pixel

### Create a Pixel conversion

Follow these steps to create a new Pixel conversion event:

1. Select **Pixel**.
2. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Pixel Details** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name for the pixel.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this conversion event from others that you may create.
4. Select a **Conversion Attribution** method.
   1. Refer to [Conversion attribution: Hybrid, View Based, Click Based](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_66cf3157a9) for more details on each option.
5. If desired, select the toggle to enable one or more advanced settings.
   1. Refer to [Conversions overview: Advanced settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_b51681b662) for more details on each option, and complete each applicable field.
6. Click **Next**.
7. If desired, select **+ Add** in the relevant section(s) to apply up to five advanced pixel customizations.
   1. Refer to [Conversions overview: Advanced pixel customization options](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_7d1234977b) for more details on each option.
8. Select **Create Pixel**.

Your Pixel Script Code will generate immediately and include any [Advanced Pixel Customizations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_7d1234977b) if you added them during conversion creation. We’ll automatically redirect you to a **Pixel Integration** page that includes the code and the steps you’ll follow to integrate it.

### Create a Postback conversion

Follow these steps to create a new Postback conversion event using the Media Measurement Partner (MMP) of your choice:

1. Select **Postback**.
2. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Postback Details** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this conversion event from others that you may create.
4. Select the attribution measurement partner who provided you with the Impression Pixel URL and Click URL.
   1. Refer to [Conversions overview: Impression Pixel URL and Click URL](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_62b6805eea) for more details on these items.
5. Paste the Impression Pixel URL and Click URL into their respective fields.
6. Click **Create**.

### Create a Universal Pixel conversion

Follow these steps to create a Universal Pixel:

1. Select **Universal Pixel**.
2. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Universal** **Pixel Details** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name for the Universal Pixel.
4. Select a **Conversion Attribution** method.
   1. Refer to [Conversion attribution: Hybrid, View Based, Click Based](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_66cf3157a9) for more details on each option.
5. If desired, select the toggle to enable one or more advanced settings.
   1. Refer to [Conversions overview: Advanced settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_b51681b662) for more details on each option, and complete each applicable field.
6. Click **Create Pixel**.

Your Universal Pixel Code will generate immediately. We’ll automatically redirect you to a **Universal Pixel Details** page that includes the code and the steps you’ll follow to integrate it.

## Manage a conversion

Review, search, sort, or filter your existing conversions in the Conversion app. You can also obtain or send conversion details, and edit or delete a conversion.

### Review a conversion

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing conversion:

1. Select **All**, **Pixel**, **Postback**, or **Universal Pixel**.
2. Search or filter the table to locate the conversion you’d like to review.
   1. Open the column selector, if desired, to add or remove a table column.
3. Select the conversion’s name in the **Conversion Name** column. This will open the conversion’s details.

### Obtain the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code

When you create a new Pixel conversion or Universal Pixel conversion, you’ll automatically be directed to the newly generated Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code.

Follow these steps to obtain the code for an existing conversion:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review a conversion workflow.
2. Select the **Copy Pixel Code** tab or **Copy Universal Pixel Code** tab, depending on the type of conversion you selected.
3. Copy the code to your clipboard.
4. Select **Done** to return to the conversions list.

### Send the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code

Follow these steps to send a Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code, and integration instructions, to yourself or others:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review a conversion workflow.
2. Select the **Email Pixel Code** tab or **Copy Universal Pixel Code** tab, depending on the type of conversion you selected.
3. Enter up to 15 email aliases into the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
4. If desired, apply changes to the **Email subject** and/or **Email Text** fields.
   1. The code and integration instructions are uneditable.
5. Select **Done** to send the email and return to the conversions list.

### Edit a conversion

You can edit one conversion at a time. Note that only edits to each conversion’s name are supported.

Follow these steps to edit a conversion:

1. Select **All**, **Pixel**,**Postback**, or **Universal Pixel**, depending on the conversion event that you’d like to edit.
2. Select the pencil icon in the **Actions** column of the desired conversion.
3. Click **Edit Conversion**. This will open the **Edit Pixel Details**, **Edit Postback Details**, or **Edit Universal Pixel Details** pop-up window.
4. Enter your edits to the conversion’s name.
5. Select **Next** to apply your changes.

### Duplicate a conversion

While you can edit or delete existing conversions, duplication isn’t supported because each conversion event includes a unique code or unique URLs.

Follow the steps outlined in Create a conversion to create a new Pixel, Postback, or Universal Pixel conversion instead.

### Delete a conversion

> **Conversion deletion notice:** Note that deleted conversions are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent.

You can delete certain conversion events individually or in bulk. Each conversion must feature an **Active** or **Pending** status—and must not be assigned to a campaign—to be eligible for deletion.

Follow these steps to delete a conversion:

1. Select **All**, **Pixel**,**Postback**, or **Universal Pixel**, depending on the conversion event that you’d like to delete.
2. Select the trashcan icon in the **Actions** column of the desired conversion.
3. Review any warnings and confirm your selection.

Any deleted conversions will no longer appear in the Conversion app.

## Integrate the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code

> **More on a website’s header section:** The header section immediately follows “<head>” in a website’s code. The “<head>” element is a container that stores information that isn’t directly displayed to the end user. For example, it can include a tracking pixel, define webpage styles and scripts, and determine other metadata. You can locate the “<head>” element by reviewing the code placed between the “<html>” tag and the “<body>” tag.

Follow these steps to integrate the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code, and refer to the simplified representation of what your header might look like in the code snippet shown above.

1. Obtain the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code and copy it to your clipboard.
2. Locate the header section of the website’s code. If you’re using a CMS or web platform to manage the site, locate the header template instead.
3. Locate the section’s closing tag, “</head>”.
4. Paste the code directly above “</head>”.
   1. By placing the code here, you’ll ensure that the script loads early in the page’s overall rendering process. This allows the pixel to collect data efficiently.

If installed correctly, the pixel will immediately begin firing and collecting user-visit data. However, note that it may take up to two hours for pixel fires to reflect in the IQM platform.

## Test the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code

Test the pixel after you add it to your website to confirm that it’s capturing events as expected.

Follow these steps to test a Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code that you’ve installed:

1. Open the Conversions app.
2. Locate the Pixel conversion or Universal Pixel conversion that you’d like to test.
3. Select **Test** from the **Status** column. This will open a **Test Pixel Conversion** or **Test Universal Pixel Conversion** pop-up window.
4. Use the **Integration page URL** field to add the URL of the webpage where you installed the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code.
5. Select **Test Pixel**. A new tab will open and redirect you to the webpage that you entered in step 4.
6. Complete the conversion action on the webpage to determine whether or not the pixel is capturing events.

Note that you’ll need to complete steps 5 and 6 in the new browser tab to register the conversion and confirm that you installed the pixel correctly.

Once a successful conversion is recorded, the conversion’s status will change from **Pending** to **Active** in the **Status** column. Status changes may be delayed for up to two hours following the conversion.

## Assign a conversion to a campaign

Assign conversions to new or existing campaigns in the Conversion app or Campaigns app. Note that any conversions must be associated with a campaign before that campaign begins serving ad impressions.

### Add a conversion to a new campaign - Conversion app

Follow these steps to assign a conversion to a new campaign in the Conversion app:

1. Select the checkbox next to the desired conversion(s).
2. Click **Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window.
3. Search or browse and select an insertion order from the **Insertion Order** menu.
4. Enter the new campaign’s name into the **Campaign Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this campaign from others that you may create.
5. Select **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign creation page of the **Campaigns** app.

### Add a conversion to a new campaign - Campaigns app

Follow these steps to assign a conversion a new campaign in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO). This will direct you to the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the new campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Locate and expand the **Conversion** section.
5. Choose a conversion type.
6. Click **Select Pixel** or **Select Postback**. This will open the **Select Pixel**, **Select Universal Pixel**, or **Select Postback** pop-up window, depending on the conversion type you chose.
7. Select the radio button(s) next to the desired conversion(s).
8. Click **Select**.

### Add a conversion to an existing campaign - Conversion app

Follow these steps to assign a conversion to an existing campaign in the Conversion app:

1. Select the checkbox next to the desired conversion.
2. Click **Add To Campaign**. This will open the **Add to Campaign** pop-up window.
3. Choose the desired campaign(s) from the **Campaigns** menu.
4. Select **Update** to add the conversion to the listed campaign(s).

### Add a conversion to an existing campaign - Campaigns app

Follow these steps to assign a conversion to an existing campaign in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you’d like to add the Retargeted audience(s).
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. This will redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Follow steps 4 through 8 of the Add a conversion to a new campaign - Campaigns app workflow.

## Unassign a conversion from a campaign

> **Unassign campaigns notice:** You can unassign conversions from campaigns featuring a **Running** or **Pending** status that haven’t begun serving. Campaigns that are **Expired**, **Deleted**, and/or have begun serving aren’t eligible.

Follow these steps to unassign a conversion from one or more campaigns:

1. Select the checkbox next to the desired conversion.
2. Click **Assign To Campaign**. This will open the **Add To Campaign** pop-up window.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaigns.
   1. Select the checkbox in the header row of the table to select all assigned campaigns instead.
4. Click **Unassign**.
5. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

title: Create or manage a Geofarmed audience

blocks.text: Geofarmed audiences consist of individuals who have visited a specific geographic location or set of geographic locations. These locations can be on-premises or in the vicinity of a point of interest. Users are added to the audience based on visits within a specified date range and frequency.

Specialty and Political advertisers can Create a Geofarmed audience; and Healthcare advertisers have the option to also Create an NPI-based HCP or Nurse Geofarmed audience, Create a non-NPI-based Nurse Geofarmed audience, or Create a Generic Geofarmed audience.

Refer to [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Geofarmed audience in the IQM platform.
You can create a Geofarmed audience for Specialty or Political campaigns in the following ways
By Custom Areas
By ZIP Codes
By File Upload
You can also use a combination of these options; for example, you might select certain custom areas and upload a spreadsheet of ZIP Codes to create your Geofarmed audience.
Follow these steps to access the access the **+ Create Audience** workflow:
Open the Audiences app.
Select **Geofarmed Audience**.
Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Geofarmed Audience** pop-up window.
Follow these steps to create a new Geofarmed audience by choosing custom areas:
Select a country from the **Country** menu.
Click the **Custom Area** tab.
Choose a **Circle**, **Polygon**, or **Rectangle** shape, depending on your preference.
Select the **+** or **-** icon to set the mile radius that your shape should represent.
If desired, search by a location to move the map view to that area.
Draw the desired custom area on the map.
Review your selection(s) in the **Targeted Locations** panel.
Select the arrow icon to expand the list.
Repeat steps 3 through 7 to add additional custom areas, which will be assigned an “OR” relationship.
Click **Next**.
Enter a name for the audience.
Choose the audience’s **Time Range** settings.
Select the **Timezone**.
Select a **Start Date** and, if desired, **End Date**.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Start Date and End Date](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_9f405e2c98) for more information on how these settings determine which users get added to the Geofarmed audience.
If desired, expand the **Advanced** section to apply frequency and time range settings to this audience.

# Create or manage a Geofarmed audience

## Geofarmed audience overview

Geofarmed audiences consist of individuals who have visited a specific geographic location or set of geographic locations. These locations can be on-premises or in the vicinity of a point of interest. Users are added to the audience based on visits within a specified date range and frequency.

Specialty and Political advertisers can Create a Geofarmed audience; and Healthcare advertisers have the option to also Create an NPI-based HCP or Nurse Geofarmed audience, Create a non-NPI-based Nurse Geofarmed audience, or Create a Generic Geofarmed audience.

Refer to [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Geofarmed audience in the IQM platform.

## Create a Geofarmed audience (Specialty, Political)

You can create a Geofarmed audience for Specialty or Political campaigns in the following ways

- By Custom Areas
- By ZIP Codes
- By File Upload

You can also use a combination of these options; for example, you might select certain custom areas and upload a spreadsheet of ZIP Codes to create your Geofarmed audience.

Follow these steps to access the access the **+ Create Audience** workflow:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Geofarmed Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Geofarmed Audience** pop-up window.

### By Custom Areas (Specialty, Political)

Follow these steps to create a new Geofarmed audience by choosing custom areas:

1. Select a country from the **Country** menu.
2. Click the **Custom Area** tab.
3. Choose a **Circle**, **Polygon**, or **Rectangle** shape, depending on your preference.
4. Select the **+** or **-** icon to set the mile radius that your shape should represent.
5. If desired, search by a location to move the map view to that area.
6. Draw the desired custom area on the map.
7. Review your selection(s) in the **Targeted Locations** panel.
   1. Select the arrow icon to expand the list.
8. Repeat steps 3 through 7 to add additional custom areas, which will be assigned an “OR” relationship.
9. Click **Next**.
10. Enter a name for the audience.
11. Choose the audience’s **Time Range** settings.
    1. Select the **Timezone**.
    2. Select a **Start Date** and, if desired, **End Date**.
    3. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Start Date and End Date](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_9f405e2c98) for more information on how these settings determine which users get added to the Geofarmed audience.
12. If desired, expand the **Advanced** section to apply frequency and time range settings to this audience.
    1. Enter the number of times the user must have visited a target location, and during what interval (**Total**, **Weekly**, **Monthly**), before they can be added to the audience.
       1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Frequency](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_62d44a3f45) for more information on how the audience’s **Advanced** settings work.
    2. Choose specific days of the week and times of the day during which users should be added to the audience.
       1. All days and times are selected by default. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Customize Time Range](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_8f980ca032) for more information on how these settings are executed.
       2. Any **Frequency** settings will apply during the selected times.
13. Select **Create.**

Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Geofarmed audience.

### By ZIP Codes (Specialty, Political)

Follow these steps to create a new Geofarmed audience by adding ZIP Codes:

1. Select a country from the **Country** menu.
2. Click the **ZIP Codes** tab.
3. Type or paste a list of ZIP codes into the available field, separated by commas.
4. Select **Add**.
5. Review your selection(s) in the **Targeted Locations** panel.
   1. Select the arrow icon to expand the list.
6. Click **Next**.
7. Follow steps 10 through 13 of By Custom Areas (Specialty, Political).

Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Geofarmed audience.

### By File Upload (Specialty, Political)

> **File upload notice:** CSV files are supported, and may contain a maximum of 1K records per file.

Follow these steps to create a new Geofarmed audience by uploading a file containing locations, addresses, or polygons:

1. To upload a list of ZIP codes:
   1. Download the **Sample File** to ensure your file is formatted correctly.
   2. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files, click **Upload File** and select it.
   3. If the desired file is stored in an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company's icon.
      1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired file from the online drive.
2. To upload a custom area:
   1. Select **Locations**, **Addresses**, or **Polygons** in the **File Type** section.
   2. Download the **Sample File** to ensure your file is formatted correctly.
   3. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files, click **Upload File** and it.
   4. If the desired file is stored in an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company's icon.
      1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired file from the online drive.
3. Review your selection(s) in the **Targeted Locations** panel.
   1. Select the arrow icon to expand the list.
4. Select **Next**.
5. Follow steps 10 through 13 By Custom Areas (Specialty, Political).

Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Geofarmed audience.

## Create a Geofarmed audience (Healthcare)

> **Healthcare Geofarmed audience notice:** A single Healthcare Geofarmed audience must include only one type: **NPI-based (HCP, Nurse)**, **Non-NPI-based (Nurse)**, or **Generic**.

You can create an NPI-based, non-NPI-based, or generic Geofarmed audience for Healthcare campaigns in the following ways

- By Custom Areas
- By ZIP Codes
- By File Upload

You can also use a combination of these options; for example, you might select certain custom areas and upload a spreadsheet of ZIP Codes to create your Geofarmed audience.

Follow these steps to access the access the **+ Create Audience** workflow:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Geofarmed Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Geofarmed Audience** pop-up window.

### NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) (Healthcare)

Follow these steps to create a new NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) Geofarmed audience:

1. Use your preferred method(s) to specify the audience’s locations:
   1. By Custom Areas
   2. By ZIP Codes
   3. By File Upload
2. On the **2 out of 2 steps** page, choose the NPI-based audience’s type: **HCP** and/or **Nurse**.
   1. Selecting both types will result in the creation of two Geofarmed audiences.
   2. If desired, proceed without selecting a checkbox to create a “generic” Geofarmed audience, which will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.
3. Follow steps 10 through 13 of By Custom Areas to specify the audience’s time range and advanced settings, and create the audience.

> **NPI-based Geofarmed audience notice:** Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin fetching data after you select **Create Audience**. Once this process is complete and the audience reaches a **Data Fetched** status, you’ll need to return to the audience and Select a data partner to continue the audience-generation process. Refer to [Geofarmed audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_56b6dde468) for more information on each status.

### Non-NPI-based (Nurse) (Healthcare)

Follow these steps to create a new non-NPI-based (Nurse) Geofarmed audience:

1. Use your preferred method(s) to specify the audience’s locations:
   1. By Custom Areas
   2. By ZIP Codes
   3. By File Upload
2. On the **2 out of 2 steps** page, choose the audience’s type: **Non-NPI Nurse**.
   1. If desired, proceed without selecting a checkbox to create a “generic” Geofarmed audience, which will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.
3. Follow steps 10 through 13 of By Custom Areas to specify the audience’s time range and advanced settings, and create the audience.

Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Geofarmed audience.

### Generic (Healthcare)

Follow these steps to create a generic Geofarmed audience for healthcare campaigns:

1. Use your preferred method(s) to specify the audience’s locations:
   1. By Custom Areas
   2. By ZIP Codes
   3. By File Upload
2. On the **2 out of 2 steps** page, proceed without clicking a checkbox in the **Select Type** section.
   1. The audience will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.
3. Follow steps 10 through 13 of By Custom Areas to specify the audience’s time range and advanced settings, and create the audience.

Your Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Geofarmed audience.

### Select a data partner (Healthcare)

Advertisers who create an NPI-based Geofarmed audience (HCP, Nurse) must return to the audience and select a data partner before we can finish processing it. You’ll complete this step when the audience’s status changes from **Fetching Data** to **Data Fetched**.

Refer to [Geofarmed audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_56b6dde468) or more information on each status, and follow these steps to select a data partner for an NPI-based Geofarmed audience featuring a **Data Fetched** status:

1. In the **Actions** column, click **Select Partner** for the desired audience. This will open the **Data Partner** pop-up window.
2. Review each data provider’s reach and cost details.
3. Choose your preferred partner.
   1. Any data partner with a **Reach** of 100 or greater can be selected.
4. Click **Select Data Partner** to apply your selection to the audience.

The NPI-based Geofarmed audience will immediately begin processing.

## Manage a Geofarmed audience

Use the **Geofarmed Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, to filter your existing Geofarmed audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them; and to assign them to campaigns.

### Review a Geofarmed audience

Follow these steps to review an existing Geofarmed audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status** for all audiences and by **Type** for Healthcare audiences.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the audience features a **Ready** status, you can also review additional data and insights.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. If you created a Healthcare audience, review the **Type** and **Data Partner** in the summary panel.
   3. Review the details you entered when you created the audience such as the audience’s target locations.
4. On the **2 out of 2 Steps** page, select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Geofarmed Audience** page.

### Edit a Geofarmed audience

> **More on editing Geofarmed audiences:** Only an existing Geofarmed audience’s name can be edited. If you’d like to apply changes to the audience’s other settings—such as its target locations or frequency settings—we recommend duplicating the audience or creating a new one instead.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Geofarmed audience’s name:

1. Select the existing name from the table’s **Audience Name** column, and type the new audience name directly in the cell.
2. Click the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

### Duplicate a Geofarmed audience

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Geofarmed audience:

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column.
2. Follow the steps outlined in Create a Geofarmed audience (Specialty, Political) or Create a Geofarmed Audience (Healthcare) to name the audience and apply your preferred settings.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same locations and settings as the existing audience; and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Geofarmed Audience** table of the Audiences app. The original audience will remain unchanged.

### Delete a Geofarmed audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the existing audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Geofarmed audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Geofarmed audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

## Assign a Geofarmed audience to a campaign

A single campaign can target up to 20 audiences. You can assign Geofarmed audiences to new and existing campaigns, and from the Audiences and Campaigns apps. Refer to [Assign an audience to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

## Review data costs

The **Data Cost** metric represents a campaign’s total spend or targeting and/or blocking data segments. This includes the total amount spent on audience targeting.

You can review a campaigns’ data costs in the following ways:

- From the Dashboard app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Reports app

### Review a campaign’s data costs from the Dashboard app

Follow the steps outlined in [Customize a dashboard table - Add or remove a column](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_35346e0a69) to choose which metrics are displayed on your dashboard. Select the **Data Cost** metric from the **Spending** category to add it.

### Review a campaign’s data costs from the Campaigns app

In the Campaigns app, open the column selector to choose which metrics are displayed in the table. Select the **Data Cost** metric from the **Spending** category to add it.

### Review a campaign’s data costs from the Reports app

Follow the steps outlined in [Generate a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report#h_6d07656e4b) to create a custom report. Select the **Data Cost** metric from the **Spending** category to add it to the report.

## Locate additional Geofarmed audience resources

- [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview)
- [Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750433-troubleshoot-a-geofarmed-audience)

title: Geofarmed audience overview

blocks.text: Geofarmed audiences include people who’ve visited a specific geographic location that you define, whether on-premises or in proximity of the point of interest. You’ll define a geographic area by searching an address, creating a virtual boundary on a map, or uploading files of the desired locations. Users will get added to the audience based on their proximity to those locations within a specified date range and frequency.

Use cases for Geofarmed audiences are vast and vary based on your campaign goals. A Specialty advertiser running an upper-funnel awareness campaign, for example, might wish to exclude users who were in proximity of their brick-and-mortar storefronts in the past 30 days. Depending on their vertical, advertisers may also create NPI-based and non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences for healthcare campaigns or Political Geofarmed audiences for political campaigns.

Refer to [Create or manage a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience) to select a geographical area and start capturing users for campaign targeting and blocking.

**More on NPI-based Geofarmed audiences:** Gain deeper insights into your NPI-based Geofarmed audiences with two compatible measurement solutions: Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports and Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports.

PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your NPI-based healthcare audiences; while SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and your competitors’ prescription patterns.

Refer to [PLD Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) and [SLS Insights overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on these measurement products.
