# Geofarmed audience overview

## Geofarmed audience overview

Geofarmed audiences include people who’ve visited a specific geographic location that you define, whether on-premises or in proximity of the point of interest. You’ll define a geographic area by searching an address, creating a virtual boundary on a map, or uploading files of the desired locations. Users will get added to the audience based on their proximity to those locations within a specified date range and frequency.

Use cases for Geofarmed audiences are vast and vary based on your campaign goals. A Specialty advertiser running an upper-funnel awareness campaign, for example, might wish to exclude users who were in proximity of their brick-and-mortar storefronts in the past 30 days. Depending on their vertical, advertisers may also create NPI-based and non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences for healthcare campaigns or Political Geofarmed audiences for political campaigns.

Refer to [Create or manage a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience) to select a geographical area and start capturing users for campaign targeting and blocking.

### NPI-based and non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences (Healthcare)

> **More on NPI-based Geofarmed audiences:** Gain deeper insights into your NPI-based Geofarmed audiences with two compatible measurement solutions: Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports and Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports. PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your NPI-based healthcare audiences; while SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and your competitors’ prescription patterns. Refer to [PLD Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) and [SLS Insights overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on these measurement products.

Geofarmed audiences help ensure maximum unique reach to healthcare professionals (HCPs) and nurses based on their proximity to a set of physical locations. These locations may include, for example, hospitals, clinics, and healthcare events that move the needle for your brand.

Healthcare advertisers can leverage two types of Geofarmed audiences: NPI-based (HCPs, Nurses) and non-NPI-based (Nurses) Geofarmed audiences. Depending on your audience type, you’ll leverage our in-house and integrated data sources to compliantly extract the precise device IDs, location details, and NPI data needed to reach high-value healthcare professionals across their connected devices.

**We directly ingest NPI numbers from leading industry sources, which power our identity graph with over 80% coverage of the HCP universe and result in maximum unique campaign reach.*

Refer to [Create or manage a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience) to generate NPI-based or non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences.

### Political Geofarmed audiences

Geofarmed audiences help ensure maximum unique reach to constituents based on their proximity to a set of physical locations. For example, a Political advertiser running a lower-funnel conversion campaign might wish to target users who visited political rallies in New York at least twice in October. Another Political advertiser creates a Geofarmed audience based on DMAs and Congressional Districts.

Political advertisers can leverage standard Geofarmed audiences to reach their target voter audience. Follow the steps outlined in [Create a Geofarmed audience (Specialty, Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_34286e52a9) to generate an audience that includes users based on the States, Cities, Counties; and DMAs, Congressional Districts, State Senates, and/or State Houses of your choice.

## Geofarmed audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Geofarmed audiences. A campaign must also meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for Geofarmed audience targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical*** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience dates** | 1 day (minimum) to 60 days (maximum) |
| **Audience frequency** | 1 (minimum) to 10 (maximum) |
| **Audience type**** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Advertiser vertical: Specialty** and **Political** advertisers are eligible to create and target Geofarmed audiences. **Healthcare** advertisers may be eligible to also create and target NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) and non-NPI-based (Nurse) Geofarmed audiences.

****Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A single campaign, however, can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target an HCP Geofarmed audience if it’s already targeting a Non-NPI Nurse Geofarmed audience. Refer to [Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11750433-troubleshoot-a-geofarmed-audience) for additional support.

## Geofarmed audience pricing

Geofarmed audiences each display a CPM price. Note that there’s no cost associated with generating a Geofarmed audience. Instead, the listed CPM price will apply once you run a campaign that’s targeting the Geofarmed audience.

You can review the CPM cost of targeting a given Geofarmed audience once it finishes generating and features a **Ready** status. In the case of NPI-based Geofarmed audiences (Healthcare), you’ll also review pricing details when you choose your preferred data provider(s).

Refer to [Review a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_3eb1894436) to learn how to locate an audience’s cost details.

## Geofarmed audience statuses

You can review a Geofarmed audience’s status on the **Geofarmed Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_3eb1894436) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Data Fetched (Select Partner)*** | We’ve fetched the relevant data for your audience. Now you can review the audience’s reach and cost details by data partner and choose your preferred provider to continue generating the audience. |
| **Fetching Data*** | We’re working on fetching data from Veraset or non-NPI Nurse data from Data360, and leveraging the IQM HCP Graph to match NPI data. This process also includes gathering Reach data across data partners. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Geofarmed audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

*This audience status is applicable only to NPI-based Geofarmed audiences (HCP, Nurse), and non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences (Nurse).

## Key terms and concepts

### Frequency

Frequency refers to the number of times a user visits the relevant geolocation(s). You can choose a frequency ranging from 1 to 10, and this selection determines which users will get added to your Geofarmed audience.

A single Geofarmed audience can feature one of three **Frequency Type** settings: Total, Weekly, or Monthly.

| **Frequency setting** | **Frequency setting description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Total** | The sum of times that a given user visits the relevant geolocation(s) across the entire chosen date range. For example, with a **Total Frequency** of 3, the user must visit any combination of the relevant geolocation(s) at least 3 times during the chosen date range to be added to the Geofarmed audience. |
| **Weekly** | The sum of times that a given user visits the relevant geolocation(s) per week at any point during the chosen date range. For example, with a **Weekly Frequency** of 3, the user must visit any combination of the relevant geolocation(s) at least 3 times in the same week during the chosen date range to be added to the Geofarmed audience. |
| **Monthly** | The sum of times that a given user visits the relevant geolocation(s) per month at any point during the chosen date range. For example, with a **Monthly Frequency** of 3, the user must visit any combination of the relevant geolocation(s) at least 3 times in the same month during the chosen date range to be added to the Geofarmed audience. |

### Start Date and End Date

When you create a Geofarmed audience, we’ll prompt you to choose a **Start Date** and an optional **End Date**.

This data collection period is static and determines which users will be added to the Geofarmed audience. For example, if you choose June 1st-June 30th, we’ll add users who visited the relevant geolocations during those dates as long as they visited them at the frequency you defined for this audience.

#### Example: Frequency, Start Date, and End Date

You create a Geofarmed audience and indicate these requirements during audience setup:

**ZIP Codes:** 10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006, 10007, 10009, 10010, and 10011

**Frequency:** 3

**Frequency Type:** Total

**Start Date:** June 1

**End Date:** June 30

Refer to the table below to review a list of scenarios, and whether or not a particular user will be added to this Geofarmed audience based on your selections.

| **Example scenario** | **User added to the Geofarmed audience** |
| --- | --- |
| Visited 10009 four times between June 29 and June 30 | Yes |
| Visited both 10010 and 10011 two times between June 1 and June 30 | Yes |
| Visited 10001 once on June 3, 10002 once on June 5, and 10003 once on June 19 | Yes |
| Visited 10009 twice between June 29 and June 30 | No |
| Visited both 10010 and 10011 one time between June 1 and June 30 | No |
| Visited 10001 once on June 3 and 10002 once on June 5 | No |

### Location relationship logic

Geofarmed audiences apply an “OR” relationship to your location targeting selections. This means that your campaign will include a user in the audience if they’re located in any of the locations you choose, as long as all other audience criteria (e.g., Frequency, Start Date, End Date) and campaign targeting criteria are met.

### National Provider Identifier (NPI)

A National Provider Identifier (NPI) is a 10-digit numeric identifier. It’s a component of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) that serves as a unique identification number for covered healthcare providers.

Note that certain healthcare professionals, such as nurses who don’t bill for services, aren’t assigned an NPI number. You can still reach these individuals by generating and targeting Non-NPI-based Nurse Geofarmed audiences.

Advertisers who’d like to leverage our integrated data sources to generate NPI-Based (HCP, Nurse) Geofarmed audiences, or create Non-NPI-based Nurse audiences or Generic healthcare audiences, can refer to [Create a Geofarmed audience (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_8fbd30587c) for more details.

### Customize Time Range

When you create a Geofarmed audience, you have the option to specify time range settings in the **Customize Time Range** section. This allows you to get more specific with your audience requirements than solely choosing the Start Date and End Date during which users should be captured. For example, you might wish to include only the users who visited a point of interest on Monday through Friday during business hours.

#### Customize Time Range cell colors

The audience will only include users during the days and times that are selected:

- **White cells:** The audience is blocked from including users who visited the target location(s) during this time period.
- **Blue cells:** The audience is permitted to include users who visited the target location(s) during this time period. By default, all days and times are selected for all Geofarmed audiences, meaning that any users who visited the target location(s) during the date range you selected will be included.

##### Cell colors example – Customize Time Range settings are not applied

An advertiser creates a new Geofarmed audience with no **Customize Time Range** settings applied to it. This audience is permitted to include users who visit the target location(s) on any day of the week, and at any time, as long as the visit took place during the selected date range.

If the advertiser changes their mind and selects one or more time ranges to target, then any days and times that aren’t selected (**White cells**) will be blocked from including users.

##### Cell colors example – Customize Time Range settings are applied

An advertiser creates a new Geofarmed audience and wants to apply **Customize Time Range** settings to it. The advertiser chooses which days and times to block (**White cells**) and which days and times to allow (**Blue cells**) adding users to the audience.

In this example, users who visit the target location(s) during the selected date range at any time except 6-7am on Wednesdays, and/or from 6-7am on Thursday through Monday, can be added to the audience.

title: Create or manage a Global Blocklist

blocks.text: **More on inventory targeting and blocking:** No ads from any campaign will be served on inventory that you’ve included in your Global Blocklist. There may be instances when you want to target or block the same set of inventory across multiple campaigns–but not every campaign.

We recommend creating inventory groups instead for this use case. They allow you to select multiple inventory items and group them together into a single collection. You can add the relevant group(s) on a campaign-by-campaign instead of manually selecting and adding individual Open Exchange, Private Marketplace (PMP), or Contextual inventory for each campaign.
Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information.

blocks.text: Most advertisers identify one or more types of digital media placements or websites that they’d like to exclude from all of their ad campaigns. # Create or manage a Global Blocklist

## Global Blocklist overview

> **More on inventory targeting and blocking:** No ads from any campaign will be served on inventory that you’ve included in your Global Blocklist. There may be instances when you want to target or block the same set of inventory across multiple campaigns–but not every campaign. We recommend creating inventory groups instead for this use case. They allow you to select multiple inventory items and group them together into a single collection. You can add the relevant group(s) on a campaign-by-campaign instead of manually selecting and adding individual Open Exchange, Private Marketplace (PMP), or Contextual inventory for each campaign. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information.

Most advertisers identify one or more types of digital media placements or websites that they’d like to exclude from all of their ad campaigns. This inventory is typically deemed inappropriate due to adult content, hate speech, or misleading information; or feature low engagement or create a poor user experience.

You can add this inventory to a Global Blocklist to automatically exclude the same set of inventory across each of your campaigns. The platform will immediately stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked to help ensure that your ads are only displayed on high-quality websites that align with the brand’s image and target audience.

## Eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to add Open Exchange inventory to, and remove it from, a Global Blocklist.

Note that your Workspace admin may block certain inventory at the Workspace level. This means that your advertiser account will block that inventory by default, and you won’t be able to remove those items from the Global Blocklist. Contact your Workspace admin with any questions related to inventory that is blocked at the Workspace level.

## Add inventory to a Global Blocklist

> **Inventory app data notice:** The data down in the Inventory app (e.g., Impressions, Reach, etc.) is based on bidder traffic from the past 7 days, and may not reflect real-time availability or performance.

You can take any of the following approaches to add Open Exchange inventory to your advertiser account’s Global Blocklist:

- Inventory app - Upload a file to block inventory in bulk
- Inventory app - Select individual inventory to block
- Bid Model app - Select individual inventory that you chose to add to your campaign or that appeared in the campaign’s ad-serving data

### Upload a file - Inventory app

> **More on bundles and domains:** Both bundles and domains are supported for CSV-file uploads. **Bundles:** Block an app using its bundle ID or package name, like “G15147002586” or “com.spectrumtv”.; **Domains:** Block an exact website domain such as “example.com”. Place a “*.” prefix before the website domain (e.g., “*.example.com”) to block that domain and all of its first-level subdomains such as “blog.example.com” and “ads.example.com”.

You can upload a CSV file to block inventory in bulk. A single file can contain up to 50K records and must follow the formatting guidelines outlined in the provided sample file.

Follow these steps to obtain the sample file and upload a Global Blocklist:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **Global Blocklist** tab.
3. Click the **Sample File** link to download a CSV file containing formatting guidelines.
4. Prepare your file on your local device to include each of the inventory items you’d like to add to the Global Blocklist.
5. Select **Upload** to browse your local files and select the Global Blocklist CSV.
   1. If desired, drag the file into the provided space instead.
6. Blocked inventory will appear in a list format on the Global Blocklist page.
7. If desired, add a comment next to any of the blocked inventory for future reference.

The inventory that was successfully added will immediately appear in your Global Blocklist, and the platform will stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked.

### Select individual inventory - Inventory app

Follow these steps to manually add inventory to a Global Blocklist from the Inventory app:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **Open Exchange** tab.
3. Apply search criteria or filters to determine which sites or apps appear in the inventory list.
4. Select the checkbox(es) next to the inventory that you want to add to the Global Blocklist.
5. Click **Block** to add those items to the list.

The inventory will immediately appear in your Global Blocklist, and the platform will stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked.

### Select individual inventory items - Bid Model app

> **More on advanced modelling:** A Bid Model is a high-performance machine that you can steer to optimize your campaigns. You create a set of rules that the Bid Model deploys as the campaign runs. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with Bid Modifiers, allocate budgets with Spend Ratios, and define priorities with Dimension Priorities to optimize performance in real time across inventory and other supported campaign dimensions. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more information.

You can add inventory to your Global Blocklist directly from the Bid Model app. Unlike the Inventory app, which includes all inventory, the Bid Model app includes two types of inventory: inventory you chose to add to your campaign’s targeting rules, and inventory that appeared in the campaign’s ad-serving data.

Follow these steps to add inventory to your Global Blocklist from the Bid Model app:

1. Open the Bid Model app.
2. Expand the **Inventory** menu and select the type of inventory that you’d like to add to your Global Blocklist.
3. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory or upload a file containing up to 50K records.
   1. Larger inventory files may be added on an ad-hoc basis. Contact us at [support@IQM.com](mailto:support@IQM.com) for additional support.
4. Select **Block**.

The inventory will immediately appear in your Global Blocklist, and the platform will stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked.

## Manage a Global Blocklist

Each advertiser account can include one Global Blocklist. You can manage an existing Global Blocklist adding more inventory to it, or removing previously added inventory from it.

### Remove inventory from a Global Blocklist

Follow these steps to remove inventory from a Global Blocklist:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **Global Blocklist** tab.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the inventory you’d like to remove from the Global Blocklist.
4. Click **Unblock**.
5. Review any warnings, and confirm your selection.

Your changes will reflect in the Global Blocklist immediately, and the inventory you removed will be unblocked at once.

### Assign a Global Blocklist to a campaign

Your Global Blocklist applies automatically to each of your campaigns. The platform will immediately stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked. This means no additional action is required, and you won’t need to add the Global Blocklist to any individual campaign.

### Remove a Global Blocklist from a campaign

Your Global Blocklist applies automatically to each of your campaigns. The platform will immediately stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked. This means you won’t be able to remove a Global Blocklist from any individual campaign.

You can remove inventory from a Global Blocklist instead, if necessary, but note that each of your other campaigns will also be impacted by this change.

## Locate additional inventory resources

- [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview)
- [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group)
- [Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9613510-create-or-manage-a-private-marketplace-pmp-inventory-deal)
- [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign)

# Lookalike audience overview

## Lookalike audience overview

Lookalike audiences are made up of users with similar characteristics to an existing [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). When you target a Lookalike audience, you reach new, qualified prospects with high conversion potential. You’ll select the source audience, choose how similar the new audience should be to the existing one, and specify the desired audience size to generate the Lookalike audience.

Lookalike audiences are highly efficient. We recommend this audience type when your goal is to reduce waste and improve campaign performance. Certain advertisers may wish to create Lookalike audiences when they’re aiming to lower their [data costs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview#h_75ff53192b). It’s also especially valuable for campaigns with smaller budgets that have less room for test-and-learn spending.

Review this article for more details and requirements, then refer to [Create or manage a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019248-create-or-manage-a-lookalike-audience) to get started.

## Lookalike audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Lookalike audiences. The following conditions must also be met before an advertiser or campaign becomes eligible for Lookalike audience creation and targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical*** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Source audience type** | Matched |
| **Compatible audience type**** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience creation date***** | 1 year (recommended) |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Advertiser vertical: Specialty** advertisers are eligible to create and target Lookalike audiences based on audiences that include only non-Healthcare and non-Political data. **Healthcare** advertisers may be eligible to create and target them based on audiences that include Specialty and/or NPI data. **Political** advertisers may be eligible to create and target them based on audiences that include Specialty and/or voter audience data.

****Compatible audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. Healthcare advertisers should note that a single campaign, however, can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences.

*****Audience creation date:** While you can target or block a Lookalike audience that you created more than one year ago, we recommend creating a new one to ensure it includes the latest Reach data.

## Lookalike audience statuses

You can review a Lookalike audience’s status on the **Lookalike Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019248-create-or-manage-a-lookalike-audience#h_7ab8c81b82) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019248-create-or-manage-a-lookalike-audience#h_dffe99b850). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Lookalike audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Match Rate

When you select one or more Matched audiences to base a new Lookalike audience on, we’ll remind you of those audiences’ **Match Rates**. A **Match Rate** represents the percentage of users whose digital identities we were able to correlate to the identifiers that you included in your Matched audience’s source file(s). The average match rate on the IQM platform is 80%.

Refer to [Matched audience key terms and concepts: Records, Match Rate, and Reach](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_d4f8225cc8) for more information.

### Reach

In campaign reporting, **Reach** represents the number of unique individuals who were exposed to your ad. In Lookalike audiences, however, this metric represents the total targetable audience (unique users) that you can potentially reach by targeting it. Note that the actual addressable audience will become smaller as you apply additional targeting rules and other settings to your campaign.

### Audience Size and Similarity

When you create a new Lookalike audience, we’ll prompt you to let us know how similar the new audience should be to the existing Matched audience you selected, and to specify the desired audience size.

The relationship between these two settings is inversely proportional. This means that a highly similar audience will be smaller in size, and a less similar audience will be larger in size. Keep this relationship in mind when you choose your Lookalike audience settings to help ensure you strike your preferred balance between scale and value.

## Locate additional Lookalike audience resources

- [Create or manage a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019248-create-or-manage-a-lookalike-audience)
- [Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749823-troubleshoot-a-lookalike-audience)

title: Contextual audience overview

blocks.text: When you engage users based on their actual browsing behaviors, you can anticipate how they might interact with your ads. Contextual audiences are formed by grouping users together based on their online activity. You determine these groups by indicating a list of relevant keywords and/or URLs and a timeframe. We add a user to the Contextual audience when they visit sites that feature those keywords or URLs, browse them during the time period you select, and meet any other parameters that you specify during audience setup. You can target the Contextual audience to advertise to that group of users across the open internet.

Aside from keywords and URLs, your **Frequency** and **Data Collection Period** choices determine which users we will add to your contextual audience. Refer to the Key terms and concepts section for more details on how these audience qualifiers work.

**More on NPI-based Contextual audiences:** Gain deeper insights into your NPI-based Contextual audiences with two compatible measurement solutions: Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports and Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports.

PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your NPI-based healthcare audiences; while SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and your competitors’ prescription patterns.

Refer to [PLD Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) and [SLS Insights overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on these measurement products.

blocks.text: Contextual audiences help ensure maximum unique reach to healthcare professionals (HCPs) and nurses based on their browsing behaviors.

Healthcare advertisers can leverage two types of Contextual audiences: NPI-based (HCPs, Nurses) and non-NPI based (Nurses) Contextual audiences. Depending on your audience type, you’ll leverage our in-house and integrated data sources to compliantly extract the precise data needed to reach high-value healthcare professionals across their connected devices.
**We directly ingest NPI numbers from leading industry sources, which power our identity graph with over 80% coverage of the HCP universe and result in maximum unique campaign reach.*
The option to create an NPI-based or non-NPI-based Contextual audience is optional: Healthcare advertisers can choose to create a standard Contextual audience, if desired.

Advertisers who’d like to create a standard Contextual audience or leverage our integrated data sources to generate NPI-based or non-NPI-based Contextual audiences can refer to [Create or manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience) for more details.

You can review a Contextual audience’s status on the **Contextual Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_f54df4cbcc) for more information on how to access this page.
**Status**
**Definition**
**Ready**
Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign).
**Processing**
We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours.
**Data Fetched (Select Partner)***
We’ve fetched the relevant data for your audience. Now you can review the audience’s reach and cost details by data partner and choose your preferred provider to continue generating the audience.
**Fetching Data***

The audience’s keywords and URLs are being matched for their presence in the IQM Database. The system is identifying the users or NPIs–depending on the audience subtype–who visited sites that featured your audience’s keywords and/or URLs. This process also includes gathering Reach data across data partners.
**Failed**
You encountered a technical error during audience creation. You can attempt to regenerate the audience by selecting **Generate Again** from the **Actions** column.
**Deleted**

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Contextual audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time.

blocks.text: *This audience status is applicable only to NPI-based Contextual audiences (HCP, Nurse), and non-NPI-based Contextual audiences (Nurse).

Frequency refers to the number of times a user visits the publisher(s) relevant to one or more keywords or URLs that you added to the Contextual audience. You can choose a frequency ranging from 1 to 10. The frequency you select determines which users will get added to your Contextual audience.
A frequency of “5” will add a user to the Contextual audience when all three of these conditions are met:
The user visited any number of sites that featured any combination of your keywords.
The user encountered any combination of those keywords five times.
The user's browsing activity took place during the time period you defined.

Consider a healthcare advertiser who chose "asthma" and "wheezing" as their keywords, and "Last 30 days" as their timeframe. We will add a user to your Contextual audience whether they visited one site containing the word "asthma" five times during the last 30 days; or visited two sites containing the keyword "asthma" and three sites containing the keyword "wheezing" during the last 30 days, for example.

# Contextual audience overview

## Contextual audience overview

When you engage users based on their actual browsing behaviors, you can anticipate how they might interact with your ads. Contextual audiences are formed by grouping users together based on their online activity. You determine these groups by indicating a list of relevant keywords and/or URLs and a timeframe. We add a user to the Contextual audience when they visit sites that feature those keywords or URLs, browse them during the time period you select, and meet any other parameters that you specify during audience setup. You can target the Contextual audience to advertise to that group of users across the open internet.

Aside from keywords and URLs, your **Frequency** and **Data Collection Period** choices determine which users we will add to your contextual audience. Refer to the Key terms and concepts section for more details on how these audience qualifiers work.

### NPI-based and non-NPI-based Contextual audiences (Healthcare)

> **More on NPI-based Contextual audiences:** Gain deeper insights into your NPI-based Contextual audiences with two compatible measurement solutions: Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports and Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports. PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your NPI-based healthcare audiences; while SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and your competitors’ prescription patterns. Refer to [PLD Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) and [SLS Insights overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on these measurement products.

Contextual audiences help ensure maximum unique reach to healthcare professionals (HCPs) and nurses based on their browsing behaviors.

Healthcare advertisers can leverage two types of Contextual audiences: NPI-based (HCPs, Nurses) and non-NPI based (Nurses) Contextual audiences. Depending on your audience type, you’ll leverage our in-house and integrated data sources to compliantly extract the precise data needed to reach high-value healthcare professionals across their connected devices.

**We directly ingest NPI numbers from leading industry sources, which power our identity graph with over 80% coverage of the HCP universe and result in maximum unique campaign reach.*

The option to create an NPI-based or non-NPI-based Contextual audience is optional: Healthcare advertisers can choose to create a standard Contextual audience, if desired.

Advertisers who’d like to create a standard Contextual audience or leverage our integrated data sources to generate NPI-based or non-NPI-based Contextual audiences can refer to [Create or manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience) for more details.

## Contextual audience statuses

You can review a Contextual audience’s status on the **Contextual Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_f54df4cbcc) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Data Fetched (Select Partner)*** | We’ve fetched the relevant data for your audience. Now you can review the audience’s reach and cost details by data partner and choose your preferred provider to continue generating the audience. |
| **Fetching Data*** | The audience’s keywords and URLs are being matched for their presence in the IQM Database. The system is identifying the users or NPIs–depending on the audience subtype–who visited sites that featured your audience’s keywords and/or URLs. This process also includes gathering Reach data across data partners. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. You can attempt to regenerate the audience by selecting **Generate Again** from the **Actions** column. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Contextual audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

*This audience status is applicable only to NPI-based Contextual audiences (HCP, Nurse), and non-NPI-based Contextual audiences (Nurse).

## Key terms and concepts

### Frequency

Frequency refers to the number of times a user visits the publisher(s) relevant to one or more keywords or URLs that you added to the Contextual audience. You can choose a frequency ranging from 1 to 10. The frequency you select determines which users will get added to your Contextual audience.

##### Example: Frequency

A frequency of “5” will add a user to the Contextual audience when all three of these conditions are met:

- The user visited any number of sites that featured any combination of your keywords.
- The user encountered any combination of those keywords five times.
- The user's browsing activity took place during the time period you defined.

Consider a healthcare advertiser who chose "asthma" and "wheezing" as their keywords, and "Last 30 days" as their timeframe. We will add a user to your Contextual audience whether they visited one site containing the word "asthma" five times during the last 30 days; or visited two sites containing the keyword "asthma" and three sites containing the keyword "wheezing" during the last 30 days, for example.

### Data Collection Period

A data collection period is the timeframe during which a user visits the publisher(s) relevant to one or more keywords or URLs that you added to the Contextual audience. You can choose a **Static** data collection period of up to 60 days over the past six-month period or future three-month period, or you can choose a **Dynamic** data collection period of up to 60 days that moves forward each day.

#### Static and Dynamic data collection periods

A **Static** data collection period will add users to the audience during a set timeframe. For example, if you select “Last 30 days” on June 30th, we’ll add users who visited contextually relevant sites between June 1st-30th to the Contextual audience. If you run a campaign with this audience on August 30th, it’ll still contain users from the June 1st-30th timeframe. In other words, a **Static** data collection period represents a snapshot of data over a fixed set of dates.

A **Dynamic** data collection period will continually add users to the audience while that audience is active. For example, if you enter “30 Days” on June 30th, we’ll add users who visited contextually relevant sites between June 1st-30th to the Contextual audience. On July 1st, the audience will include users who visited contextually relevant sites between June 2nd-July 1st. On July 2nd, this timeframe shifts from June 3rd-July 2nd. In other words, a **Dynamic** data collection period takes place over a rolling timeframe, with data refreshes taking place once every 24 hours.

##### Example: Data Collection Period - Static

You create a Contextual audience made up of users who are interested in Asthma and its treatments. You indicated these requirements during audience setup:

- **Keywords:** Asthma, wheezing, shortness of breath, inhaler, albuterol
- **URLs:** [https://www.drugs.com/drug-class/adrenergic-bronchodilators.html](https://www.drugs.com/drug-class/adrenergic-bronchodilators.html),
  [https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma)
- **Frequency:** 5
- **Data Collection Period**: Last 30 Days

Refer to the table below to review a list of scenarios, and whether or not we will add a user to this Contextual audience based on your selections.

| **Example scenario of user's browsing behavior** | **User added to Contextual audience** |
| --- | --- |
| Visited one site containing the keyword "asthma" five times during the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited five sites containing any of the five keywords one time each during the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited two sites containing the keyword "wheezing" and three sites containing the keyword "inhaler" during the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited [https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma) five times in the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited each URL a total of five times in the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited one site containing the keywords "shortness of breath," "inhaler," "wheezing," and "albuterol," and visited [https://www.drugs.com/drug-class/adrenergic-bronchodilators.html](https://www.drugs.com/drug-class/adrenergic-bronchodilators.html) one time, in the last 30 days | Yes |
| Visited one site containing the keyword "inhaler" four times during the last 30 days | No |
| Visited four sites containing any one keyword during the last 30 days | No |
| Visited two sites containing the keyword "albuterol" and two sites containing the keyword "shortness of breath" during the last 30 days | No |
| Visited [https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma) twice in the last 30 days | No |

##### Example: Data Collection Period - Dynamic

You create a Contextual audience made up of users who are interested in Asthma and its treatments. During audience setup, you indicate the same requirements outlined in Example: Data Collection Period - Static, but choose a **Dynamic** data collection period instead of a **Static** one.

The Example: Data Collection Period - Static example scenarios detailing whether or not a user will get added to the Contextual audience will still apply when the data collection period is **Dynamic**. We add a user to the Contextual audience when they visit sites that feature the keywords or URLs you specified, and browse them during the time period and at the frequency you selected. However, the way this Contextual audience evolves over time differs from audiences with a **Static** data collection period.

Refer to the graphic below for an illustration of a data collection period that covers the last 10 days. Since you select a **Dynamic** timeframe, the 10-day date range you chose continues to move forward with the campaign’s flight, refreshing daily and capitalizing on new data each day that the campaign runs.

### AI-powered keyword generation

When you create a keyword-based Contextual audience, we’ll prompt you to manually enter your desired keywords or upload a file that contains them.

There may be instances when you know the themes or types of keywords you’d like to add, but you haven’t determined a preferred list of keywords. You have the option to enter a description of your Contextual audience rather than specific terms. This will generate keyword recommendations for you that are powered by AI.

You’ll have an opportunity to review the AI-generated keywords list and select which ones will be used to create the Contextual audience. Refer to [Create or manage a Contextual](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience) audience to get started with AI-powered keyword generation.

### National Provider Identifier (NPI)

A National Provider Identifier (NPI) is a 10-digit numeric identifier. It’s a component of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) that serves as a unique identification number for covered healthcare providers.

Advertisers who’d like to leverage our integrated data sources to generate NPI-based Contextual audiences can refer to [Create an NPI-based Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_0b85ddb256) for more details.

Note that certain healthcare professionals, such as nurses who don’t bill for services, aren’t assigned an NPI number. You can still reach these individuals by generating and targeting Nurse Contextual audiences. Refer to [Create a non-NPI-based Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_e57c493b83) for more details.

## FAQ

Expand the drop-down arrow next to a question to reveal the answer.

### Error messages

##### Q: What is the meaning of the “URL is outside the programmatic universe” error?

**A:** The site is not authorized for digital ads by the IAB Tech Lab’s “Ads.txt” initiative. It aims to tackle domain spoofing, arbitrage, and other forms of ad fraud by indicating the authorized resellers of a publisher’s ad inventory.

##### Q: What is the meaning of the “URL can not be validated” error?

**A:** The URL does not correspond to an active site. Confirm that your URLs do not contain errors such as typos or missing punctuation, and check that the site is active.

### Data collection periods

##### Q: What data collection length can I choose for my Contextual audience?

**A:** For audiences with a **Static** data collection period, you can choose a date range of up to 60 days over the past six-month period or future three-month period. For audiences with a **Dynamic** data collection period, you can choose a rolling lookback period of up to 60 days from today.

##### Q: Can I create a custom data collection period that is longer than 60 days?

**A:** We recommend a data collection period of 30 days or less for most Contextual audiences.

In certain cases, you might want to select a wider data collection period. For example, products and services within the automotive market typically have a longer purchase cycle than those of lower-cost retail businesses. You can choose a data collection period of up to 60 days directly from the platform to address those use cases.

Submit a support request to create a Contextual audience with a data collection period exceeding the IQM platform’s 60-day limit.

### Users in a Contextual audience

##### Q: Will a data collection period of “Last 30 days” collect users during that time frame from the time the audience was created, or will it continually add users from the last 30 days when the audience is active?

**A:** We offer the “Last 30 days” options as a preset to help you quickly select a data collection period of 30 days ago through today. For example, if you choose “Last 30 days” on June 30th, we will add users who visited contextually relevant sites between June 1st-30th to the Contextual audience. If you run a campaign with this audience on August 30th, it will still contain users from June 1st-30th.

### Create a Contextual audience

##### Q: What steps should I follow to create a Contextual audience?

**A:** Refer to the how-to instructions listed in [Create a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_8ce6332d08). It includes steps to create the audience by keyword or URL, and individually or in bulk.

##### Q: Can healthcare advertisers choose both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audience types in a single Contextual audience?

**A:** No, healthcare advertisers have the following options for a single Contextual audience:

- Select both the **HCP** and **Nurse** NPI-based audience types *OR*
- Select the **Non-NPI Nurse** non-NPI-based audience type *OR*
- Make no audience-type selections to create a standard Contextual audience for their healthcare campaigns

##### Q: What happens if I choose both the HCP and Nurse NPI-based audience types in a single Contextual audience?

**A:** When you select both audience types, two audiences will be generated for you: one NPI-based HCP Contextual audience, and one NPI-based Nurse Contextual audience.

##### Q: What happens if, as a Healthcare advertiser, I don’t choose either an HCP or Nurse NPI-based audience or a Nurse non-NPI-based Contextual audience?

**A:** You can proceed with Contextual audience creation for your healthcare campaigns without selecting an audience subtype. This will create a “Generic” Contextual audience, which will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.

### Manage or target a Contextual audience

##### Q: How can I edit, duplicate, or delete a Contextual audience?

**A:** Refer to the how-to instructions listed in [Manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience#h_f54df4cbcc) to complete these actions.

##### Q: Can a single campaign target mixed audience types (e.g., NPI-based HCP, Non-NPI-based Nurse)?

**A:** No; healthcare advertisers should note that a campaign must only target the same audience subtype. For example, if you create an NPI-based Contextual audience and select both **Nurse** and **HCP** subtypes, then two audiences will be created.

Although both of these audiences are NPI-based, a single campaign can’t target both of them since they feature different subtypes. Refer to the table below for audience-compatibility examples.

| **Audience subtype(s)** | **Allowed combination (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| NPI-based HCP only | Y |
| NPI-based HCP + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| NPI-based Nurse only | Y |
| NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| Non-NPI-based Nurse only | Y |
| Non-NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| NPI-based HCP + NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based HCP + Non-NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based Nurse + Non-NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based HCP + NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | N |

# Create or manage a Contextual audience

## Contextual audience overview

When you engage users based on their actual browsing behaviors, you can anticipate how they might interact with your ads. Contextual audiences are formed by grouping users together based on their online activity. You determine these groups by indicating a list of relevant keywords and/or URLs and a timeframe. We add a user to the contextual audience when they visit sites that feature those keywords or URLs, browse them during the time period you select, and meet any other parameters that you specify during audience setup. You can target the Contextual audience to advertise to that group of users across the open internet.

Review [Contextual audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) for more information on Contextual audiences and to review scenario-based examples.

## Create a Contextual audience (Specialty, Political)

> **Maximum keywords or URLs:** There's no limit to the number of keywords or URLs that you can add to a single Contextual audience. We recommend a maximum of 100 per audience.

You can create a Contextual audience in the following ways:

- By keyword, one by one
- By keyword, in bulk
- By keyword, using AI
- By URL, one by one
- By URL, in bulk

You can also use a combination of these options; for example, you might add a list of keywords and upload a spreadsheet of URLs to create your Contextual audience.

Follow these steps to access the **+ Create Audience** workflow:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Contextual Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Contextual Audience** pop-up window.

### By keyword, one by one

Follow these steps to create a Contextual audience from keywords one by one:

1. Enter a name for the audience.
2. Type a keyword into the **Keyword** field and select **Enter** on your device’s keyboard.
3. Additional, optional keyword recommendations will appear. Browse the list and select one or more keywords, if desired.
4. Repeat steps 2-3 for each additional keyword.
5. Locate the **Contextual Criteria Summary** section to review each term you’ve added.
   1. If desired, select the **X** icon next to any terms to remove them.
   2. If desired, click the wand icon to prompt AI to generate more keywords that are similar to the ones you’ve added to the **Added Keywords section**.
6. Select **Next**.
7. Choose a **Static** or **Dynamic** data collection period.
   1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Static and Dynamic data collection periods](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_69114daaf7) for more information on the differences between these options.
8. For **Static**, select a date range and frequency.
   1. Choose a date range of up to 60 days over the past six-month period or future three-month period.
   2. Choose a frequency between 1 and 10.
   3. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Frequency](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_fa4ee965fc) for more information on how frequency determines which users will be added to this audience.
9. For **Dynamic**, enter a timeframe and frequency.
   1. Choose a timeframe of up to 60 days.
   2. Choose a frequency between 1 and 10.
   3. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Frequency](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_fa4ee965fc) for more information on how frequency determines which users will be added to this audience.
10. Select **Create**.

### By keyword, in bulk

Follow these steps to create a Contextual audience from keywords in bulk:

1. Use a spreadsheet application to prepare an XLSX or CSV file with a list of keywords.
   1. Download the sample file to ensure that your file is formatted correctly.
   2. List each keyword as its own, separate row in Column A of the spreadsheet.
2. Click **Upload** and select the desired file.
3. Locate the **Contextual Criteria Summary** section to review each term you’ve added.
   1. If desired, select the **X** icon next to any terms to remove them.
   2. If desired, click the wand icon to prompt AI to generate more keywords that are similar to the ones you’ve added to the **Added Keywords section**.
   3. Click **+** next to a **Recommended Keyword** to add it to the audience.
4. Select **Next**.
5. Follow steps 7 through 10 of the By keyword, one by one workflow to finish creating this audience.

### By keyword, using AI

Follow these steps to use AI to generate a list of keywords and add them to a Contextual audience:

1. Click **Try AI**.
2. Enter information such as content themes and keyword requirements into the provided field.
3. Select **Enter** on your device’s keyboard or click the arrow icon next to your description.
4. Browse the list of generated keywords and select the ones you’d like to add to the audience.
   1. Up to 15 AI-generated keywords will display for each search.
5. Repeat steps 2 through 4 to enter additional requirements and add more keywords.
6. Locate the **Contextual Criteria Summary** section to review each term you’ve added.
   1. If desired, select the **X** icon next to any terms to remove them.
   2. If desired, click the wand icon to prompt AI to generate more keywords that are similar to the ones you’ve added to the **Added Keywords section**. Up to 20 additional keywords will display each time you click the wand icon.
7. Select **Next**.
8. Follow steps 7 through 10 of the By keyword, one by one workflow to finish creating this audience.

### By URL, one by one

> **More on URLs:** Whether you add URLs individually or in bulk, the Contextual audience will consider all child URLs (e.g., [https://iqm.com/company/about-us](https://iqm.com/company/about-us)) when you enter a parent URL (e.g., [https://iqm.com](https://iqm.com)).

Follow these steps to create a Contextual audience from URLs one by one:

1. Enter a name for the audience.
2. Select the **URLs** tab.
3. Type a URL into the **URL** field.
4. Click **Add**.
5. A preview will populate. Confirm it matches the site you intended to enter.
6. Repeat steps 3 through 5 for each additional URL.
7. Locate the **Contextual Criteria Summary** section to review each URL you’ve added.
   1. If desired, select the **X** icon next to any URLs to remove them.
8. Select **Next**.
9. Follow steps 7 through 10 of the By keyword, one by one workflow to finish creating this audience.

### By URL, in bulk

Follow these steps to create a Contextual audience from URLs in bulk:

1. Enter a name for the audience.
2. Select the **URLs** tab.
3. Use a spreadsheet application to prepare an XLSX or CSV file with a list of URLs.
   1. Download the sample file to ensure that your file is formatted correctly.
   2. List each URL as its own, separate row in Column A of the spreadsheet.
4. Click **Upload** and select the desired file.
5. Locate the **Contextual Criteria Summary** section to review each URL you’ve added.
   1. If desired, select the **X** icon next to any URLs to remove them.
6. Select **Next**.
7. Follow steps 7 through 10 of the By keyword, one by one workflow to finish creating this audience.

## Create a Contextual audience (Healthcare)

> **Maximum keywords or URLs:** There’s no limit to the number of keywords or URLs that you can add to a single Contextual audience. We recommend a maximum of 100 per audience.

You can create the following Contextual audiences for your Healthcare campaigns:

- NPI-based (HCP, Nurse)
- Non-NPI-based (Nurse)
- Generic

### NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) (Healthcare)

Follow these steps to create a new NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) Contextual audience for a healthcare campaign:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Contextual Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Contextual Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Choose the NPI-based audience’s type: **HCP** and/or **Nurse**.
   1. Selecting both types will result in the creation of two Contextual audiences.
   2. If desired, proceed without selecting a checkbox to create a “generic” Contextual audience, which will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.
6. Use your preferred method(s) to add keywords and/or URLs to the audience, choose its data collection period and frequency settings, and create it.
   1. By keyword, one by one
   2. By keyword, in bulk
   3. By keyword, using AI
   4. By URL, one by one
   5. By URL, in bulk

> **NPI-based Contextual audience notice:** Your Contextual audience will immediately begin fetching data after you select **Create Audience**. Once this process is complete and the audience reaches a **Data Fetched** status, you’ll need to return to the audience and Select a data partner to continue the audience-generation process. Refer to [Contextual audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_5a411c85a1) for more information on each status.

### Non-NPI-based (Nurse) (Healthcare)

Follow these steps to create a new non-NPI-based (Nurse) Contextual audience for a healthcare campaign:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Contextual Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Contextual Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Choose the **Non-NPI Nurse** audience type.
   1. If desired, proceed without selecting a checkbox to create a “generic” Contextual audience, which will be listed as a “-” **Type** audience in the Audiences app.
6. Use your preferred method(s) to add keywords and/or URLs to the audience, choose its data collection period and frequency settings, and create it.
   1. By keyword, one by one
   2. By keyword, in bulk
   3. By keyword, using AI
   4. By URL, one by one
   5. By URL, in bulk

### Generic (Healthcare)

You can create a generic Contextual audience for healthcare campaigns by not making an audience **Type** selection.

Use your preferred method(s) to add keywords and/or URLs to the audience, choose its data collection period and frequency settings, and create it:

- By keyword, one by one
- By keyword, in bulk
- By keyword, using AI
- By URL, one by one
- By URL, in bulk

### Select a data partner (Healthcare)

Healthcare advertisers who create an NPI-based Contextual audience must return to the audience and select a data partner before we can finish processing it. You’ll complete this step when the audience’s status changes from **Fetching Data** to **Data Fetched.**

Refer to [Contextual audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_5a411c85a1) for more information on each status, and follow these steps to select a data partner for an NPI-based Contextual audience featuring a **Data Fetched** status:

1. In the **Actions** column, click **Select Partner** for the desired audience. This will open the **Data Partner** pop-up window.
2. Review each data provider’s reach and cost details.
3. Choose your preferred partner.
   1. Any data partner with a **Reach** of 100 or greater can be selected.
4. Click **Select Data Partner** to apply your selection to the audience.

The NPI-based Contextual audience will immediately begin processing.

## Manage a Contextual audience

Use the **Contextual Audiences** page in the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing Contextual audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them.

### Review a Contextual audience

Follow these steps to review an existing Contextual audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status** for all audiences and by **Type** for Healthcare audiences.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the audience features a **Ready** status, you can also review additional data and insights.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. If you created a Healthcare audience, review the **Type** and **Data Partner** in the summary panel.
   3. Review the details you entered when you created the audience such as the **Data Collection Details** and a list of individual keywords and/or URLs.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Contextual Audience** page.

### Edit a Contextual audience

> **More on editing Contextual audiences:** Only an existing Contextual audience’s name can be edited. If you’d like to apply changes to the audience’s other settings—such as its keywords, URLs, and data collection period—we recommend duplicating the audience or creating a new one instead.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Contextual audience’s name:

1. Select the existing name from the table’s **Audience Name** column, and type the new audience name directly in the cell.
2. Click the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

### Duplicate a Contextual audience

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Contextual audience:

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column.
2. Follow the steps outlined in Create a Contextual audience (Specialty, Political) or Create a Contextual audience (Healthcare) to name the audience and apply your preferred settings.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same keywords, URLs, and settings as the existing audience; and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Contextual Audience** table of the Audiences app. The original audience will remain unchanged.

### Delete a Contextual audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the existing audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Contextual audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Contextual audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete.
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

## Assign a Contextual audience to a campaign

Contextual audiences can be assigned to new and existing campaigns, and from the Audiences and Campaigns apps. Refer to [Assign an audience to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

- [Contextual audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview)

blocks.text: Creative specifications (specs) are the guidelines that you’ll follow when you add a new creative to the IQM platform. These specs relate to factors ranging from dimensions to text-character lengths, for example, with the ultimate goal of helping you achieve two outcomes:

**Inventory:** When a site or app loads, a publisher fills a set of reserved ad-inventory slots with creatives. Each time an ad opportunity appears in the bid stream, creatives must match the dimensions of these sections to be eligible for placement.

**Appearance:** Users’ ability to clearly decipher your brand’s message is critical to the success of your campaigns. Following specs that are specific to individual creative formats and/or publishers help ensure that every ad renders as expected.
Refer to this guide and any in-platform text when setting up your campaigns to follow IQM and industry standards for creatives.

**Supported sizes:** The tables included throughout this article highlight recommended creative sizes. There are no restrictions to the creative sizes you can upload to the IQM platform as all are supported. Note, however, that less common sizes may limit your access to inventory and impact a campaign’s ability to scale.

title: Create or manage a Lookalike audience

blocks.text: Lookalike audiences are made up of users with similar characteristics to an existing [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). You’ll select the high-value source audience, choose how similar the new audience should be to the existing one, and specify its ideal audience size.

Refer to [Lookalike audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Lookalike audience in the IQM platform.
You can create one Lookalike audience at a time in the Audiences app. Follow these steps to create a new Lookalike audience:
Open the Audiences app.
Select **Lookalike Audience**.
Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Lookalike Audience** pop-up window.
Enter a name for the audience.
Open the **Matched Audience** menu and select the existing audience(s) that your new audience should use as source data.
Review the selected audiences’ **Match Rate** and **Reach** details.
Since the Lookalike audience will share characteristics with these audiences, we recommend choosing ones with similar objectives and performance.
Click **Next**.
Slide the **Audience Similarity & Size** toggle to the left or right to define how the audience should prioritize these settings.

# Create or manage a Lookalike audience

## Lookalike audience overview

Lookalike audiences are made up of users with similar characteristics to an existing [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). You’ll select the high-value source audience, choose how similar the new audience should be to the existing one, and specify its ideal audience size.

Refer to [Lookalike audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Lookalike audience in the IQM platform.

## Create a Lookalike audience

You can create one Lookalike audience at a time in the Audiences app. Follow these steps to create a new Lookalike audience:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Lookalike Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Lookalike Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Open the **Matched Audience** menu and select the existing audience(s) that your new audience should use as source data.
   1. Review the selected audiences’ **Match Rate** and **Reach** details.
   2. Since the Lookalike audience will share characteristics with these audiences, we recommend choosing ones with similar objectives and performance.
6. Click **Next**.
7. Slide the **Audience Similarity & Size** toggle to the left or right to define how the audience should prioritize these settings.
   1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts:](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview#h_713ea3f391)[Audience Size and Similarity](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview#h_713ea3f391) for more details on the relationship between these two values.
8. Apply the audience’s **Geo Expansion Settings**.
   1. At least one **State** is required, while **Cities** and **Countries** are optional.
9. If you’re a Political advertiser, target particular **Senates**, **Congressional Districts**, and/or **State Houses**, if desired.
10. Select **Create**.

Your Lookalike audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Lookalike audience.

## Manage a Lookalike audience

Use the **Lookalike Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing Lookalike audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them; and to assign them to campaigns.

### Review a Lookalike audience

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing Lookalike audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status**.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the Lookalike audience features a **Ready** status, you can review additional details.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. Review the details you entered when you created the audience such as its source Matched audience(s) and **Geo Expansion Settings**.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Lookalike Audience** page.

### Edit a Lookalike audience

> **More on editing Lookalike audiences:** Only an existing Lookalike audience’s name can be edited. If you’d like to apply changes to the audience’s other settings—such as its source Matched audiences and Geo Expansion Settings—we recommend duplicating the audience or creating a new one instead.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Lookalike audience’s name:

1. Select the existing name from the table’s **Audience Name** column, and type the new audience name directly in the cell.
2. Click the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

### Duplicate a Lookalike audience

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Lookalike audience:

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column.
2. Follow the steps outlined in the Create a Lookalike audience workflow to name the audience and apply your preferred settings.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same Matched audience(s) and settings as the existing audience; and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Lookalike Audience** table of the Audiences app and feature a **Processing** status. The original audience will remain unchanged.

### Delete a Lookalike audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the existing audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Lookalike audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Lookalike audience:

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

## Assign a Lookalike audience to a campaign

A single campaign can target up to 20 audiences. Lookalike audiences can be assigned to new and existing campaigns, and from the Audiences and Campaigns apps. Refer to [Assign an audience to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

- [Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749823-troubleshoot-a-lookalike-audience)
