# Campaign audience overview

## Campaign audience overview

Campaign audiences are made up of users that you’ve reached in past or current campaigns. With this high-value group of users, you can re-engage audiences who are already familiar with your brand, or offer new products and services to existing customers. You can also add a Campaign audience to an awareness campaign’s Blocklist to help ensure that budgets are allocated to exposing new users to the brand.

Refer to [Create or manage a Campaign audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033837-create-or-manage-a-campaign-audience) to get started, or continue reading to learn more about this audience type and its requirements.

### Healthcare Campaign audiences

Healthcare advertisers can create Campaign audiences by selecting campaigns that have targeted at least one HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, or Patient type audience. The option to create an HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, or Patient Campaign audience is optional: Healthcare advertisers can choose to create a Generic Campaign audience instead, if desired.

The generated Campaign audience will take the same type as the selected campaign(s). For example, choosing an **HCP** type—and selecting campaigns that targeted at least one HCP audience—will result in an HCP-type Campaign audience.

Refer to [Create or manage a Campaign audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033837-create-or-manage-a-campaign-audience) to get started, or continue reading to learn more about Campaign audiences and requirements.

## Campaign audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Campaign audiences. The following conditions must also be met before an advertiser or campaign becomes eligible for Campaign audience targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Data collection period** | Up to 12 months |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type*** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. Healthcare advertisers should note that a single campaign, however, can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target a Campaign audience consisting of your Non-NPI Nurses you’ve reached in previous campaigns if it’s already targeting an NPI-based [Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview).

## Key terms and concepts

### Impressions, Clicks, and Conversions

When you create a new Campaign audience, you’ll choose one or more source campaigns from which the audience should pull users who you reached with your ad. You’ll also define the criteria that the Campaign audience will use to determine which users should be added: users who saw your ad, users who clicked on your ad, or users who converted.

The criteria you choose depends on the goals of the campaigns that will target the Campaign audience you create. Keep the audience’s potential [Reach](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview#h_59b2d231e4) in mind when making your selection.

#### Impressions

Choose **Impressions** as the audience’s criteria to include users who were served your ad. Note that those campaigns’ impressions were measured when the ad server sent your ad to a webpage. This means that–while impressions provide critical insight into potential exposure—they aren’t a measure of user interest or engagement.

#### Clicks

Choose **Clicks** as the audience’s criteria to include users who clicked on the ads you served. These users’ clicks can indicate engagement and interest in the products or services you advertised, or overall ad appeal.

#### Conversions

Choose **Conversions** as the audience’s criteria to include users who completed a conversion event after being exposed to your ad, and credit for that conversion was able to be attributed to the selected campaign(s) because it took place during a particular conversion window.

## Locate additional Campaign audience resources

- [Create or manage a Campaign audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033837-create-or-manage-a-campaign-audience)
- [Troubleshoot a Campaign audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11996047-troubleshoot-a-campaign-audience)

## Manage a Campaign audience

Use the **Campaign Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing Campaign audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them; and to assign them to campaigns.

### Review a Campaign audience

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing Campaign audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status**.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the Campaign audience features a **Ready** status, you can review additional details.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. Review each campaign and its details in the table.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Campaign Audience** page.

### Edit a Campaign audience

> **More on editing Campaign audiences:** Only an existing Campaign audience’s name can be edited. If you’d like to apply changes to the audience’s other settings—such as its source campaigns and data collection period—we recommend duplicating the audience or creating a new one instead.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Campaign audience’s name:

1. Select the existing name from the table’s **Audience Name** column, and type the new audience name directly in the cell.
2. Click the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

### Duplicate a Campaign audience

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Campaign audience:

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column.
2. Follow steps 4 through 8 of the Create a Campaign audience workflow to name the audience and apply your preferred settings.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same source campaigns and settings as the existing audience, and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.
3. Select **Duplicate** to create the duplicated audience.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Campaign Audience** table of the Audiences app and feature a **Processing** status. The original audience will remain unchanged.

### Delete a Campaign audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the existing audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Campaign audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Campaign audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

## Assign a Campaign audience to a campaign

Assign Campaign audiences to new or existing campaigns in the Audiences app or Campaigns app. A single campaign can target up to 20 audiences.

Refer to [Assign an audience to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

# Activity Log overview

## Activity Log overview

The Activity Log is a record of events and actions that took place on the IQM platform. This detailed timeline tracks various activities performed by individual users. Monitor these activities to refine and optimize your campaigns and operations.

We recommend using the Activity Log in combination with the insights you generate in the **Reports** app to help identify patterns that contributed to changes in campaign performance.

## Activity Log eligibility requirements

All agencies with workspace-level ownership can access the **Activity Log** portion of the **Organization** app. Advertisers can also access it from the **Organization** app.

## Activity Log components

You can review each of the following components in your Activity Log, regardless of the activity category or filters that you apply:

- **Date:** Either Today or the day of the week; followed by the month, date, and year that the logged action was performed.
- **Timestamp:** The exact time of day that the logged action was performed.
- **Activity:** The logged action that was performed, including the specific element that was added or updated. For example, changes applied to a campaign will include the campaign ID in the Activity description.
- **App:** The app that was used to perform the logged action.
- **User:** The specific user that performed the logged action.
- **Bookmark:** A bookmark icon that you can select, if desired, to flag an activity for future reference.

## Included activities and filters

Review a record of all applicable in-platform activities, or add precision by monitoring the Activity Log by a specific activity category or filter.

| **Activity or filter category** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **All Activities** | List actions that took place across any app and were performed by any user across the **Account Level**, **Financial**, **Campaign**, and **Flagged** activity categories. |
| **Account Level Activities** | Review all activities completed by a particular advertiser account, and confirm which users completed those actions. |
| **Financial Activities** | Display only finance- and payment- related activities. |
| **Campaign Activities** | Show only campaign-related activities that include adding, editing, deleting, and duplicating campaigns. |
| **Flagged Activities** | Retrieve important actions that you bookmarked for future reference. |
| **Apps** | Filter by one or more **Apps** to monitor all in-platform actions that were completed in those apps. |
| **Users** | Filter by **Users** to monitor all in-platform actions completed by a particular user or set of users. Select **All Activities** or a specific activity category for a more granular review of those users’ actions. |

Refer to [Filter an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log#h_c4a4a4efb8) for details on how to apply an activity category or filter to your Activity Log.

## Locate additional Activity Log resources

- [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log)

title: How IQM attributes conversions

blocks.text: Conversion modeling, powered by data and machine learning, plays a crucial role in accurately attributing conversions to ad exposures. In this article, we'll explore IQM’s methodology for measuring conversions.

In response to evolving privacy regulations and the increasing limitations on cookie tracking, IQM has developed strategies for both cookieless and cross-device conversion attribution. Presently, IQM utilizes IP addresses as alternative identifiers to attribute conversions accurately in cookieless environments. IQM is actively advancing its capabilities and plans to introduce a cross-device ID graph in the near future. This improvement will significantly boost the precision and dependability of cross-device conversion attribution, enabling marketers to better understand which ad exposure directly led to a conversion.
Please see the below examples to understand how conversions are attributed.

Consider a scenario where a user clicks on a brand's advertisement on their mobile device and later completes the purchase on a desktop computer. The credit for the conversion is applied to the mobile ad they clicked on.

A user is served multiple brand ads across devices. First, they were served an ad on CTV. Then they were exposed on desktop, followed by mobile. Later in the day, the user makes a conversion on the brand’s website. In this case, the credit for the conversion goes to the mobile ad, as it was the last exposure before converting.

Traditionally, this cross-device conversion might be challenging to attribute accurately due to the absence of cookies across devices. However, with IQM's advanced conversion modeling capabilities, it is attributed to the last ad exposure or click-through before conversion, providing marketers with insights into the effectiveness of their cross-channel efforts.

cleaned_markdown:
# How IQM attributes conversions

Conversion modeling, powered by data and machine learning, plays a crucial role in accurately attributing conversions to ad exposures. In this article, we'll explore IQM’s methodology for measuring conversions.

#### Cookieless and Cross-Device Conversion Attribution

In response to evolving privacy regulations and the increasing limitations on cookie tracking, IQM has developed strategies for both cookieless and cross-device conversion attribution. Presently, IQM utilizes IP addresses as alternative identifiers to attribute conversions accurately in cookieless environments. IQM is actively advancing its capabilities and plans to introduce a cross-device ID graph in the near future. This improvement will significantly boost the precision and dependability of cross-device conversion attribution, enabling marketers to better understand which ad exposure directly led to a conversion.

Please see the below examples to understand how conversions are attributed.

##### Example 1:

Consider a scenario where a user clicks on a brand's advertisement on their mobile device and later completes the purchase on a desktop computer. The credit for the conversion is applied to the mobile ad they clicked on.

##### Example 2:

A user is served multiple brand ads across devices. First, they were served an ad on CTV. Then they were exposed on desktop, followed by mobile. Later in the day, the user makes a conversion on the brand’s website. In this case, the credit for the conversion goes to the mobile ad, as it was the last exposure before converting.

Traditionally, this cross-device conversion might be challenging to attribute accurately due to the absence of cookies across devices. However, with IQM's advanced conversion modeling capabilities, it is attributed to the last ad exposure or click-through before conversion, providing marketers with insights into the effectiveness of their cross-channel efforts.

# Run Campaign Estimations

## Campaign Estimations overview

The Campaign Estimations forecasting feature takes place directly from a campaign. This tool generates projections for the campaign’s Reach, Impressions, and Audience Size based on the targeting parameters that you add to it.

Refer to [Campaign Estimations overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11997149-campaign-estimations-overview) to reference the minimum required fields for each forecasting metric to generate, and follow the instructions below to use the Campaign Estimations tool.

## Run Campaign Estimations

> **Campaign creation resources:** If this is your first time creating a campaign, we recommend reviewing the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) and the [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) resource. They provide an overview of each required and optional campaign targeting element, and step-by-step instructions to help you apply the settings that make the most sense for your campaign while following campaign requirements.

Generate forecasts for new campaigns as you build them, or return to in-flight campaigns and generate these insights before you apply changes.

### Run Campaign Estimations from a new campaign

Follow these steps to run Campaign Estimations while you add your targeting parameters to a new campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose the insertion order that will serve as the parent hierarchy for the new campaign. You’ll arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the campaign.
5. Choose an [Advanced or PG](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) **Campaign Type**.
6. Select a **Campaign Creation Method**.
   1. Click **From Scratch** to open an empty campaign creation form.
   2. Click **From Template** to open a campaign creation form that includes the settings you previously saved as a template.
   3. If you select **From Template**, open the **Template** menu to search and select the desired template.
7. Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the campaign’s details page, where you can specify campaign settings and targeting rules.
8. Complete the minimum required fields to generate your desired Campaign Estimation(s).
   1. Refer to [Forecasts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11997149-campaign-estimations-overview#h_126ba9da5e) for a breakout of minimum required fields by metric.
9. Locate the left-side panel and select **Run Campaign Estimations**.
10. Complete the campaign’s other required and applicable fields.
    1. Refer to [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for additional support with applying your desired campaign settings

The **Campaign Estimations** panel will refresh after you add or update any Campaign [parameters that affect Campaign Estimation metric calculations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11997149-campaign-estimations-overview#h_16454395aa).

### Run Campaign Estimations from an existing campaign

Follow these steps to run Campaign Estimations while you apply changes to an existing campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or filter the table to locate the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Click the name of the IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
4. Select the campaign’s name to open its details page.
5. Follow steps 7 through 10 of the Run Campaign Estimations from a new campaign workflow.

## Generate Required Total Budget and Required Total Max Bid

There may be instances where you’d like for the campaign to reach more unique users and/or serve more impressions than what was forecasted in the **Reach & Impressions** section of your Campaign Estimations.

Follow these steps to generate insights into the **Required Total Budget** and/or **Required Total Max Bid** that you’ll need to set to achieve those desired values:

1. Slide the **Unique Reach** and/or **Total Impression** slide buttons to the right until your desired values are shown.
2. Review the **Required Total Budget** and **Required Total Max Bid** fields.
3. If desired, select **Update** to apply the required values to the campaign.

title: Add macros to tracking links

blocks.text: Tracking links are URLs designed to monitor and measure campaign performance. You can add specific macros to a tracking link to capture and analyze campaign-specific information, creative identifiers, device identifiers, and more. This information helps provide valuable insights into performance and engagement, targeting details, and overall user behavior.
Macros serve as command placeholders within a tracking link. These placeholders allow for the insertion or relevant data points like ad interactions, user devices, campaign details, and more.
Consider an example where an advertiser runs a mobile ad campaign with the following details:
**Campaign Name:** Summer Sale 2025

# Add macros to tracking links

## Macros and tracking links overview

Tracking links are URLs designed to monitor and measure campaign performance. You can add specific macros to a tracking link to capture and analyze campaign-specific information, creative identifiers, device identifiers, and more. This information helps provide valuable insights into performance and engagement, targeting details, and overall user behavior.

### Macro process example

Macros serve as command placeholders within a tracking link. These placeholders allow for the insertion or relevant data points like ad interactions, user devices, campaign details, and more.

Consider an example where an advertiser runs a mobile ad campaign with the following details:

- **Campaign Name:** Summer Sale 2025
- **Creative ID:** 123456
- **Device ID:** ABCDEF

The advertiser adds three macros in the tracking links: {IAA_CAMPAIGN}, {IAA_CREATIVE_ID}, and {IAA_DEVICE_ID}. Refer to the table below to reference how the respective macros would be populated with the relevant campaign details.

# Audience Insights report overview

## Audience Insights overview

The Audience Insights report surfaces insights about users that you add to a Matched audience. It includes data such as audience characteristics, interests, and behaviors. Generate and apply these insights to gain a holistic and in-depth view of user attributes and craft highly targeted and personalized campaigns.

You can generate an Audience Insights report if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to the Audience Insights report eligibility requirements section for more information.

## Audience Insights report eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to generate Audience Insights; however, an audience must meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for Audience Insights reporting.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Audience type*** | [Matched](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview) audience |
| **Audience status** | Ready |
| **Audience reach**** | 10,000+ |
| **Audience creation date (recommended)** | While not a requirement, we recommend generating insights for audiences created within the past year. Doing so helps ensure you develop strategies based on the most up-to-date reach data. |

* **Audience type:** Audience Insights reports are available for eligible Specialty, Political, and Healthcare (HCP, Nurse) Matched audiences. Patient Matched audiences are not supported.

** **Audience reach:** A matched audience’s **Reach** metric represents the total number of unique users who saw an ad at least once.

## Audience Insights report pricing

There is no cost associated with generating an Audience Insights report.

Note that, while you can generate insights for an unlimited number of audiences, you can only do so once per audience. An exception to this limit is when insights are deleted: you can regenerate them, and they will include the same data as the first report you generated if the audience remained unchanged.

Refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337876-generate-or-manage-an-audience-insights-report) for details on how to locate, download, and send insights that you’ve already generated.

## Audience Insights data visualizations

> **Data visualizations notice:** Data visualizations are available in Audience Insights reports that are downloaded or emailed as a PDF file.

All audience insights include a data table featuring **Absolute Audience Value (#)**, **Audience Value (%)**, **National Average (%)**, and **Delta (#)** details. They also include a data visualization, which differs depending on the Audience Insight category, and can include a bar graph, circle chart, or scatter plot.

## Audience Insights report metrics

Each audience insight category includes a series of metrics and values associated with that category, as well as a **National Average**, an **Audience Average**, and the difference between them. This delta highlights how much your audience deviates from the average population.

> **More on average values:** National averages are benchmarks that represent the average values for the demographic, geographic, interest, and political preferences of the entire population of a country. These averages are derived from the [US Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/decade/2020/2020-census-results.html).

Review the Audience Insights report metrics below, and refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337876-generate-or-manage-an-audience-insights-report) when you’re ready to create one.

### Audience Summary

Review Audience Summary insights to assess the total number of individuals and households in the audience, as well as a total count of available phone numbers and email aliases. These details can help you determine the potential reach for this audience.

Audience Summary insights include the following metrics:
- Total Household
- Total People
- Total Phones
- Total Emails

Assess the audience’s gender distribution with Gender Insights. These details can help you tailor your messaging and products to resonate specifically with male or female users.

Gender Insights metrics include the following genders:
- Male
- Female
- Unknown

### Ethnicity Group Insights

Review Ethnicity Group Insights to delve deeper into your customer base’s ethnic diversity. Use these details to foster inclusivity and cultural relevance, and deliver messages that resonate with diverse audiences.

Ethnicity Group Insights metrics include the following groups:
- African-American
- Hispanic
- European
- Other
- Unknown

### Marital Status Insights

Learn about the educational background of your audience with Education Insights. Create content that aligns with these users’ educational backgrounds and related experiences.

- Less than HS Diploma
- HS Diploma
- Vocational Technical Degree
- Some College
- Bach Degree
- Grad Degree
- Unknown

### Occupation Group Insights

Gain valuable insights into the employment status and professional profiles of the audience with Occupation Group Insights. Apply these details to address the specific needs and preferences of professionals in different industries.

Occupation Group Insights metrics include a range of job categories (e.g., Blue Collar), statuses (e.g., Retired), and professions (e.g., Farming/Fish/Forestry), which can differ widely by audience.

### Home Ownership Insights

Review Home Ownership insights to assess the total number of audience members who own homes versus rent. These details can help you tailor marketing messages to the distinct needs and interests of homeowners, and ensure ads resonate with the intended audience.

Home Ownership Insights metrics include the following ownership statuses:
- Homeowner
- Not Homeowner
- Unknown

### Home Value Insights

Access data on the estimated home values of your audience with Home Value Insights. Discover the products and services suitable for different property value segments, and promote offers that align with your customers’ financial capacities.

Home Value Insights metrics include the following value ranges:
- $1K-$50K
- $50K-$100K
- $100K-$150K
- $150K-$200K
- $200K-$250K
- $250K-$300K
- $300K-$400K
- $400K-$500K
- $500K-$775K
- $775K-$1M
- $1M-$2M
- $2M-$3M
- $3M-$5M
- Unknown

### State Income Decile Insights

Deciles segment users based on their usual weekly earnings in relation to each other. This segmentation can differ by state. According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, approximately 10% of all full-time wage and salary workers earn less than the upper limit of Decile 1, and 90% earn less than the upper limit of Decile 9.

Get more granular by categorizing your audience based on these income percentiles with State Income Decile Insights. Develop region-specific marketing strategies, and optimize promotions according to the income levels of the audience in different regions.

State Income Decile Insights metrics include the following deciles, which relate to each user’s respective state:
- 0
- 1

### Net Worth Insights

Assess the net worth of the audience with Net Worth Insights. Understanding the financial standing of these users allows you to tailor products and services that cater specifically to high-net-worth individuals. Identity your high-value customers and create premium offerings for them.

Net Worth Insights metrics include the following value ranges:
- $1-$4,999
- $5,000-$9,999
- $10,000-$24,999
- $25,000-$49,000
- $50,000-$99,999
- $100,000-$249,999

- $500,000+
- Unknown

### Contributions Insights

Understanding the charitable giving behavior of the audience with Contribution Insights. Align your corporate social responsibility initiatives with these customers’ values and connect with them through shared philanthropic interests. These efforts can enhance the brand’s reputation and foster a positive brand image.

Contributions Insights metrics include the following donor categories:
- Democratic Contributor
- Republican Contributor
- Unknown

## Audience Insights report statuses

You can review an Audience Insights report’s current status on the **Audience Insights** page of the **Insights** app.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your insights are generated. You can view, download, or email the Audience Insights report. |
| **Processing** | We are working on generating your insights. Check back in about 5 minutes. |
| **Failed** | You either encountered a technical error during report generation, or the audience you selected is no longer eligible for insights generation. Try again in a few minutes to rule out a technical error. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Delta

Each Audience Insights report category includes a **National Average** and **Audience Value**. The **Delta** represents the difference between these two percentages.

The **Delta** measures how much of the audience deviates from the average population in terms of demographic, geographic, interest, and political preferences. You can use this data to identify areas where the audience is unique, and tailor your marketing strategies and creatives accordingly.

# Generate or manage an Audience Insights report

## Audience Insights report overview

Audience Insights reports provide a holistic and in-depth view of an audience, including users’ audience characteristics, interests, and behaviors.

You can generate an Audience Insights report if your campaigns meet certain criteria. Refer to the [Audience Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview) page for more information on eligibility requirements, metrics, and more.

## Video tutorial: Generate an Audience Insights report

## Generate an Audience Insights report

You can generate an Audience Insights report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Audience app

### Generate from the Insights app

Follow these steps to generate a new Audience Insights report from the Insights app:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Click **Audience Insights**.
3. Select **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Audience Insights** pop-up window.
4. Search or browse the audience(s) for which you want to generate insights.
   1. An audience is available in the table when it’s [eligible for Audience Insights report generation](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview#h_b5765ae4d3) and hasn’t previously been used to generate an Audience Insights report.
5. Select the checkbox next to the desired audience(s).
6. Click **Generate Insight**.

Insights typically generate within a few minutes. You can review and manage them once they feature a **Ready** status.

### Generate from the Audiences app

Follow these steps to generate a new Audience Insights report from the Audiences app:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Matched Audience**.
3. In the **Insights** column of the desired audience, select **Generate.**

Note that the **Generate** option is enabled only for Matched audiences that are [eligible for Audience Insights report generation](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview#h_b5765ae4d3).

Insights typically generate within a few minutes. You can review and manage them once they feature a **Ready** status.

## Manage an Audience Insights report

Use the **Audience Insights** page of the Insights app or the **Matched Audience** page of the Audiences app to download, email, or delete a report; or generate it again. You can complete these actions once the report features a **Ready** status.

### Download an Audience Insights report

> **Custom logo notice:** You can add a custom logo to any Audience Insights report that you download as a PDF file. The logo must be 2 MB or less in size; and saved as a PNG, JPG, or BMP file.

You can download an Audience Insights report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Audience app

#### Download from the Insights app

Follow these steps to download an Audience Insights report from the Insights app:

1. Filter or search the Audience Insights reports to locate the one you want to download.
2. Open the **Download** dropdown menu in the **Actions** column.
3. Click **Download as PDF** or **Download as XLSX**, depending on your preference.
   1. **Download as PDF** will open the **Download as PDF** pop-up window, where you can choose whether the file should feature a default logo or a custom logo that you upload. Click **Download PDF** to finalize your selections and download the file to your device.
   2. **Download as XLSX** will immediately download the file to your device.

#### Download from the Audiences app

Follow these steps to download an Audience Insights report from the Audiences app:

1. Select **Matched Audience**.
2. In the **Insights** column of the desired audience, select the download icon.
3. Choose **Download as PDF** or **Download as XLSX**, depending on your preference.
   1. **Download as PDF** opens the **Download Audience Insight**s pop-up window, where you can choose whether the file should feature a default logo or a custom logo that you upload. Click **Download PDF** to finalize your selections and download the file to your device.
   2. **Download as XLSX** immediately downloads the file to your device.

### Email a report

You can send an Audience Insights report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Audience app

#### Email from the Insights app

Follow these steps to send a report once to a list of recipients from the Insights app:

1. Filter or search the Audience Insights reports to locate the one you want to download.
2. Select the envelope icon from the **Actions** column.
3. Click **Email as PDF** or **Email as XLSX**, depending on your preference. This will open the **Email Audience Insights** pop-up window.
4. Add up to email aliases to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
5. If you selected **Download as PDF**, choose whether the PDF file should feature a default logo or a custom logo that you upload.
6. Select **Send Email**.

The email will include a link that the recipients can use to download the report. This link expires 24 hours after you select **Send Email**.

#### Email from the Audiences app

Follow these steps to send a report once to a list of recipients from the Audiences app:

1. Select **Matched Audience**.
2. In the **Insights** column of the desired audience, select the envelope icon. This will open the **Email Audience Insights** pop-up window.
3. Choose **Email as PDF** or **Email as XLSX**, depending on your preference.
4. Add up to email aliases to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
5. If you selected **Download as PDF**, choose whether the PDF file should feature a default logo or a custom logo that you upload.
6. Select **Send Email**.

The email will include a link that the recipients can use to download the report. This link expires 24 hours after you select **Send Email**.

### Delete a report

You can delete an Audience Insights report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Audience app

You can delete any Audience Insights reports. While you can’t recover a deleted report, you can generate the same report again if the source audience was not altered and is still available in the **Audiences** app.

#### Delete from the Insights app

Follow these steps to delete an Audience Insights report from the Insights app:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to download.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the report(s) you want to delete.
3. Click **Delete**.

#### Delete from the Audiences app

Follow these steps to delete an Audiences Insights report from the Audiences app:

1. Select **Matched Audience**.
2. In the **Insights** column of the desired audience, select the trashcan icon.

title: Insertion orders (IO) overview

blocks.text: Insertion orders (IOs) function as an organizational framework. The primary function of an IO is to provide an effective means of organizing and managing campaigns that share similar traits. It’s also a means of managing the budgets of those campaigns.

Along with their campaign-management capabilities, IOs serve as a contractual agreement. They outline the terms and conditions for one or more advertising campaigns, and ensure that those campaigns adhere to the guidelines and criteria that you define.

Note that you may see IOs referred to as campaigns or campaign groups in other demand-side platforms (DSPs). Campaigns in the IQM platform, however, refer to the individual marketing strategies that you’ll create to define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more information on campaigns.
The criteria that you define for an IO can include the following elements:
**Scheduling:** Choose a Start Date and End Date. The IO will ensure that the campaigns you’ve assigned to it won’t extend beyond the IO’s End Date.

**Budget management:** Define a budget ([Spend](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io) or [Impressions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)) to manage the spending of funds or impressions across all campaigns within the IO. Campaigns can include individual spend or impression budgets, but these campaigns will stop service once their cumulative spend reaches the IO budget that you’ve set.

**Bid-price settings:** Choose a [Max Bid Price](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview#h_7d3abcd448), which is the most you’re willing to bid for an impression across any of the IO’s campaigns, and regardless of whether or not any [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) are applied.
**Campaigns:** Associate one or more campaigns to the IO to apply its settings to those strategies.

We also recommend reporting at the IO level to gain a comprehensive view of the performance and costs associated with each of the campaigns within the IO. This consolidated approach simplifies the process of tracking and assessing the effectiveness of your marketing strategies. Refer to [Reporting dimensions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343842-reporting-dimensions-overview) for more information.

While IOs function as an organizational framework, campaigns include your individual strategies and contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify.
The majority of your parameters and settings are defined at the campaign level. Certain settings–such as scheduling and budgets–can be set at the IO level.
Refer to the table below for more information on the individual functions that can be managed at the campaign level and/or IO level:
**Setting**
**Insertion Order (IO)**
**Campaign**
**Scheduling**
IO dates define the timeframe during which the IO’s campaigns can run.
Each campaign can feature varying flights that take place during the dates defined at the IO level.
**Budget**
IO budgets set the cumulative spend or cumulative impressions across the IO’s campaigns.

Campaign budgets allocate the IO budget across individual campaigns. The campaigns will stop serving once that campaign’s budget is reached or the IO budget has been reached–whichever takes place first.
**Targeting**
N/A - Set at campaign level

When you define the campaign’s targeting strategy, you choose which [campaign targeting elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) to apply in order to strike the balance between scale, efficiency, and performance.
**Optimization & Delivery**
N/A - Set at campaign level

A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad.
**Creatives**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Select one creative format per campaign, and add one creative or multiple creative versions.
**Inventory**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Specify where ads should be placed by targeting Open Exchange inventory, Contextual inventory, or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals.
**Optimization**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Adjust individual campaign strategies such as bid amounts, creative rotation, and targeting criteria for different target-audience segments to improve performance.
**Conversions**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Implement and test conversion and postback pixels to measure how ad exposure impacts how your target audience interacts with your brand or its products and services.
**Reporting**
Report at the IO level to consolidate each of its strategies and gain an overall view of cost and performance.
Report at the campaign level to track the performance of specific targeting strategies and inform optimization decisions for current and future campaigns.

# Insertion orders (IO) overview

## Insertion orders (IO) overview

Insertion orders (IOs) function as an organizational framework. The primary function of an IO is to provide an effective means of organizing and managing campaigns that share similar traits. It’s also a means of managing the budgets of those campaigns.

Along with their campaign-management capabilities, IOs serve as a contractual agreement. They outline the terms and conditions for one or more advertising campaigns, and ensure that those campaigns adhere to the guidelines and criteria that you define.

Note that you may see IOs referred to as campaigns or campaign groups in other demand-side platforms (DSPs). Campaigns in the IQM platform, however, refer to the individual marketing strategies that you’ll create to define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more information on campaigns.

## Insertion orders (IOs) elements

The criteria that you define for an IO can include the following elements:

- **Scheduling:** Choose a Start Date and End Date. The IO will ensure that the campaigns you’ve assigned to it won’t extend beyond the IO’s End Date.
- **Budget management:** Define a budget ([Spend](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io) or [Impressions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)) to manage the spending of funds or impressions across all campaigns within the IO. Campaigns can include individual spend or impression budgets, but these campaigns will stop service once their cumulative spend reaches the IO budget that you’ve set.
- **Bid-price settings:** Choose a [Max Bid Price](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview#h_7d3abcd448), which is the most you’re willing to bid for an impression across any of the IO’s campaigns, and regardless of whether or not any [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) are applied.
- **Campaigns:** Associate one or more campaigns to the IO to apply its settings to those strategies.

We also recommend reporting at the IO level to gain a comprehensive view of the performance and costs associated with each of the campaigns within the IO. This consolidated approach simplifies the process of tracking and assessing the effectiveness of your marketing strategies. Refer to [Reporting dimensions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343842-reporting-dimensions-overview) for more information.

## Insertion orders (IOs) versus campaigns

While IOs function as an organizational framework, campaigns include your individual strategies and contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify.

The majority of your parameters and settings are defined at the campaign level. Certain settings–such as scheduling and budgets–can be set at the IO level.

Refer to the table below for more information on the individual functions that can be managed at the campaign level and/or IO level:

| **Setting** | **Insertion Order (IO)** | **Campaign** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheduling** | IO dates define the timeframe during which the IO’s campaigns can run. | Each campaign can feature varying flights that take place during the dates defined at the IO level. |
| **Budget** | IO budgets set the cumulative spend or cumulative impressions across the IO’s campaigns. | Campaign budgets allocate the IO budget across individual campaigns. The campaigns will stop serving once that campaign’s budget is reached or the IO budget has been reached–whichever takes place first. |
| **Targeting** | N/A - Set at campaign level | When you define the campaign’s targeting strategy, you choose which [campaign targeting elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) to apply in order to strike the balance between scale, efficiency, and performance. |
| **Optimization & Delivery** | N/A - Set at campaign level | A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. |
| **Creatives** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Select one creative format per campaign, and add one creative or multiple creative versions. |
| **Inventory** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Specify where ads should be placed by targeting Open Exchange inventory, Contextual inventory, or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. |
| **Optimization** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Adjust individual campaign strategies such as bid amounts, creative rotation, and targeting criteria for different target-audience segments to improve performance. |
| **Conversions** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Implement and test conversion and postback pixels to measure how ad exposure impacts how your target audience interacts with your brand or its products and services. |
| **Reporting** | Report at the IO level to consolidate each of its strategies and gain an overall view of cost and performance. | Report at the campaign level to track the performance of specific targeting strategies and inform optimization decisions for current and future campaigns. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Budget-based and impression-based insertion orders (IOs)

You’ll choose between budget-based or impression-based settings when you create a new IO. With budget-based IOs, all assigned campaigns will stop serving once their cumulative spend reaches the monetary budget that you’ve defined. With impression-based IOs, all assigned campaigns will stop serving once their cumulative served impressions reach the impression budget that you’ve defined.

The choice between a budget-based or impression-based IO depends on your goals, budget preferences and flexibility, and desired outcomes. Refer to [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) to learn more about the differences between these IO types, then review [Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io) or [Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io) when you’re ready to set one up for your campaigns.

# Install and test a Pixel or Universal Pixel

## Pixel and Universal Pixel overview

Tracking user activities on your website is pivotal for harnessing the power of data for your campaigns. This measurement is made possible through pixel tags, which are strings of HTML code that you can place on your website to measure conversions. You may also see pixel tags referred to as pixels, tracking pixels, or pixel URLs.

Universal Pixels modernize the standard approach to conversion tracking. While traditional methods often require individual pixels on specific conversion pages, this unified solution fires across your entire website via a single JavaScript tag.

Implementing a Universal Pixel allows you to efficiently capture insights into various user behaviors, including signups, page visits, and purchases. This data is then attributed to individual ads or campaigns, helping you better understand performance trends and customer preferences. Because it supports multiple event types—such as tracking when a purchase is completed or a signup is initiated—this site-wide tag is the recommended way to simplify your measurement and attribution strategy.

Refer to [Conversions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview) for more information, including eligibility criteria.

### Test and install pixels overview

You’ll the following steps to measure user activities with Pixel conversions or Universal Pixel conversions:

1. Obtain the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code by either creating a new conversion event or copying the code from one that you’ve already created.
2. Install the pixel directly in a website’s header or integrate it via Google Tag Manager (GTM).
3. Test the pixel to confirm that it was installed correctly.

## Obtain a Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code

When you create a new Pixel conversion or Universal Pixel conversion, you’ll automatically be directed to the newly generated Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code. You can also obtain the code of an existing conversion.

Refer to [Create or manage a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion) for step-by-step instructions on obtaining a Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code for a new or existing conversion.

## Install a pixel

### Choose an installation method

You can choose to install a standard pixel tag or a Universal Pixel in one of two ways: directly on a webpage, or via Google Tag Manager (GTM).

To install a pixel directly on a webpage, you’ll need access to the website’s header section. It plays a pivotal role on any webpage and contains essential information about the site. Depending on your setup, you may need to either locate the header within the website’s code or, if you’re using content management systems (CMS) or web platforms like WordPress, you may have a dedicated header template available to you.

GTM is a powerful tool that simplifies the process of managing various tags—including pixels—without altering your website’s code. It allows you to define when the pixel should fire, and helps reduce the need for manual adjustments to your website’s code each time you’d like to install another pixel or apply any changes.

The choice between webpage installation or GTM integration is ultimately based on your preference. Whether you approach pixel deployment through your website or GTM, you’ll maximize the effectiveness of your tracking efforts and gather rich data insights from user interactions.

### Install a pixel on a webpage

> **More on a website’s header section:** The header section immediately follows “<head>” in a website’s code. The “<head>” element is a container that stores information that isn’t directly displayed to the end user. For example, it can include a tracking pixel, define webpage styles and scripts, and determine other metadata. You can locate the “<head>” element by reviewing the code placed between the “<html>” tag and the “<body>” tag.

Follow these steps to integrate the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code, and refer to the simplified representation of what your header might look like in the code snippet shown above.

1. Obtain the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code and copy it to your clipboard.
2. Locate the header section of the website’s code. If you’re using a CMS or web platform to manage the site, locate the header template instead.
3. Locate the section’s closing tag, “</head>”.
4. Paste the code directly above “</head>”.
   1. By placing the code here, you’ll ensure that the script loads early in the page’s overall rendering process. This allows the pixel to collect data efficiently.

If installed correctly, the pixel will immediately begin firing and collecting user-visit data. However, note that it may take up to two hours for pixel fires to reflect in the IQM platform.

### Integrate a pixel using Google Tag Manager (GTM)

To integrate a standard pixel tag or a Universal Pixel using GTM, follow the steps outlined in the [Tag Manager Help Center](https://support.google.com/tagmanager/topic/14841964?hl=en&ref_topic=15191151,3441645,2789291,&sjid=13118880140918701675-NC) (external link), and refer to a summary of the process below:

1. **Create an account and container.** Sign in with your Google account and follow the prompts to set up an account for your organization. You’ll also set up a container, which includes adding the website’s top-most URL (e.g., [www.IQM.com](http://www.iqm.com) rather than [www.IQM.com/company/about-us](http://www.iqm.com/company/about-us)).
2. **Install a web container.**
   Install the necessary code snippets for the GTM container you created in step 1. Select the container ID and directly from GTM and paste it in your website’s “<head>” tag.
3. **Create a new tag.**
   Select the GTM container you want to edit and add a new tag. This is where you’ll choose a tag type, paste the pixel code into the HTML field, and choose a name for the tag. In most cases, you’ll choose the “Custom HTML” tag type.
4. **Choose the tracking URL’s triggering settings.**
   Define the conditions under which your pixel will be activated and capture user conversion. For example, you might choose to capture data when a user views the page or reaches a certain scroll depth.
5. **Verify and publish the tag.**
   Once you’ve configured your pixel tag and associated triggers, save your changes and publish the new configuration in GTM. This action ensures that the pixel tag becomes active on your website, and allows you to enter a name and description for this new version of your website’s code.

## Test a Pixel or Universal Pixel conversion

Test the pixel after you add it to your website to confirm that it’s capturing events as expected.

Follow these steps to test a Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code that you’ve installed:

1. Open the Conversions app.
2. Locate the Pixel conversion or Universal Pixel conversion that you’d like to test.
3. Select **Test** from the **Status** column. This will open a **Test Pixel Conversion** or **Test Universal Pixel Conversion** pop-up window.
4. Use the **Integration page URL** field to add the URL of the webpage where you installed the Pixel Script Code or Universal Pixel Code.
5. Select **Test Pixel**. A new tab will open and redirect you to the webpage that you entered in step 4.
6. Complete the conversion action on the webpage to determine whether or not the pixel is capturing events.

Note that you’ll need to complete steps 5 and 6 in the new browser tab to register the conversion and confirm that you installed the pixel correctly.

## Locate additional pixel tag resources

- [Conversions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview)
- [Create or manage a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion)
- [Troubleshoot a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11996280-troubleshoot-a-conversion)

title: Frequency capping overview

blocks.text: Frequency capping is a campaign-level setting that limits the number of times you’ll serve your ad to the same user within a specific timeframe. With the rise of devices and content channels, this tool is essential for preventing ad fatigue while maintaining audience engagement.

Frequency capping is one of four elements that compromise a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings, alongside Optimization (Rule Based, AI Based), Budget Capping, and Bid Pacing. These features determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively the campaign should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad.

Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the differences between Optimization, Frequency Capping, Budget Capping, and Bid Pacing; and review [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to define or adjust your campaign’s frequency-cap settings.

The IQM platform implements a sophisticated “waterfall” method to execute a campaign’s frequency capping settings. This process ultimately helps ensure the number of impressions served to that individual can be governed and limited.

It first prioritizes assigning a device identifier to an [IQM ID](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview#h_f6e9ec243c), then redirects to the Ramp ID if an IQM ID isn’t feasible. If neither is associated, the platform counts unique impressions at the Device or Cookie level, and in certain cases, progresses to IPV 6 or IPV4 to collectively cap impressions for the user.
**Description**
**IQM ID**

A unique [pseudonymized identifier](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview#h_e7b753d35b) that’s exclusive to IQM and tied to device and IP identifiers in the [IQM Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview). Each ID can be thought of as related to an individual person with a comprehensive profile for precise targeting.
**Ramp ID**
A unique people-based [pseudonymized identifier](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview) that’s offered by LiveRamp and aids in the identification of individuals.
**Device**
A unique identifier associated with a range of devices such as mobile devices, tablets, and connected TV (CTV) or over-the-top (OTT) platforms.
**Cookie**
A unique identifier tied to web browsers.
**IPV6 and IPV4**
An internet protocol (IP) system that gives devices a unique IP address on the internet and allows precise identification in the digital landscape.

blocks.text: Note that the waterfall approach may allow for additional impressions to be served to a device identifier if higher-level identifiers (IQM ID, Ramp ID) aren’t associated during bidding.

An advertiser creates a campaign and enables [Frequency Capping](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-bid-strategy-overview#h_a8647394e9) in the campaign’s [Optimization & Delivery](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) section. The advertiser chooses a frequency cap of **5** impressions per **Day**.

Assuming limited associations of the IQM ID and Ramp ID with the devices, cookies, and IPs in the campaign’s available bid requests, the impression-distribution scenario pictured above unfolds. The campaign earns a maximum of five impressions per user, but the distribution of these impressions varies depending on the presence or absence of an associated IQM ID or Ramp ID for a given user.
In this example, the campaign reached six unique users and served a total of 30 impressions. These impressions were distributed in the following way:
**Identifier**
**Impression distribution**
**Total impressions**
**IQM ID 1**
MAID 1 (1 impression)
MAID 2 (1 impression)
Cookie 1 (3 impressions)
**Ramp ID 1**
MAID 3 (2 impressions)
Cookie 2 (3 impressions)
**MAID 4**
MAID 4 (5 impressions)
**Cookie 3**
Cookie 3 (5 impressions)
IPV6 (5 impressions)
IPV4 (5 impressions)

blocks.table_reason: header row with 2+ filled cells and rectangular rows

blocks.text: In summary, **IQM ID 1**–associated with MAID 1, MAID 2, and Cookie 1–underwent frequency capping at the IQM ID level. **Ramp ID 1**–associated with MAID 3 and Cookie 2–underwent frequency capping at the Ramp ID level. For **MAID 4**, **IPV 6**, and **IPV4**, a maximum of 5 impressions were served with the absence of an associated IQM ID or Ramp ID.

A maximum of four frequency capping rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign). Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview: Frequency values](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_164a694b1a) for more details on these individual options.
A campaign will apply an “AND” relationship to the rules you add. This means that a campaign can only target a user when every frequency rule is met.
For example, a user adds the following two rules to a campaign:
**2** impressions every **1 Day**
**10** impressions every **1 Week**

By the last day of the week, a user was only served your ad a total of eight times. However, they saw your ad twice today. Since the first rule was already satisfied, the user will not be served more ads today to reach the total allowed **10** weekly impressions.
**Q:** What is the purpose of a campaign’s frequency cap?

**A:** Frequency caps limit the number of impressions a user can see during a given time frame. This setting helps advertisers walk the fine line of driving brand awareness and earning conversions without over-serving ads.
**Q:** What frequency cap do you recommend for my campaign?

**A:** Each campaign is unique based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended frequency cap for optimal campaign performance. We recommend starting with a lower frequency cap (e.g., 3 impressions per day) and gradually increasing it, as needed, based on the campaign’s reach and overall performance.
**Q:** Can I set a different frequency cap for a campaign’s creatives, audiences, or inventory?
**A:** No, frequency capping is set at the campaign level rather than for individual campaign elements.
**Q:** Can I set a different frequency cap for multiple durations?
**A:** Yes, a maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign).
**Q:** What happens if I choose a frequency cap rule based on Campaign Duration, but I haven’t chosen an end date for the campaign?

**A:** You’ll need to define a campaign end date before you can save a frequency cap rule that’s based on Campaign Duration. You can complete this step directly from the Frequency Capping section of your campaign.
**Q:** What is the relationship between my campaign’s multiple frequency cap rules?

**A:** Your campaign applies an "AND" relationship to frequency cap rules. If any single rule is met within a timeframe, it takes precedence, preventing further impressions to the user during that period.
**Q:** What are the devices for which IQM receives Device IDs?
**A:** We receive Device IDs for mobile, connected TV (CTV), over-the-top (OTT), and tablet devices.
**Q:** What scenarios might cause a campaign to exceed its frequency cap?
**A:** A given user may get served your ad additional times depending on whether a unique identifier (IQM ID or Ramp ID) is available.

For example, consider an advertiser who sets a frequency cap of 1 impression for a campaign. The first impression is counted at the Ramp ID level. Later, the campaign bids on a request for the same user because no unique identifier–such as a Ramp ID–is available. In this scenario, the cookie ID becomes the primary identifier and the bid is sent again. The cookie ID is counted as a unique user.
**Q:** What percentage of traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level?
**A:** Approximately 45-50% of bid request traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level. The remaining traffic is capped at the Device ID, Cookie ID, or IP Address level.
**Q:** When does frequency capping management take place?

**A:** You can add optional frequency capping settings to your campaign when you complete the campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section. A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the three elements that comprise a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings.
**Q:** How do I set up new frequency capping settings for a campaign?

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.
**Q:** How do I change existing frequency capping settings for a campaign?

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.
**Q:** What happens if I choose AI Based Optimization for my campaign and I don’t enable Frequency Capping?

**A:** Depending on campaign performance, the AI engine may apply Frequency optimizations. A limit of 100 impressions will be set to help your target audience avoid ad fatigue. You can enable Frequency Capping at any time to choose custom settings that will take precedence over [AI Based Optimizations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_4753688f6d).
[Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview)
[Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings)

### Multiple frequency capping rules

A maximum of four frequency capping rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign). Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview: Frequency values](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_164a694b1a) for more details on these individual options.

A campaign will apply an “AND” relationship to the rules you add. This means that a campaign can only target a user when every frequency rule is met.

For example, a user adds the following two rules to a campaign:

- **2** impressions every **1 Day**
- **10** impressions every **1 Week**

By the last day of the week, a user was only served your ad a total of eight times. However, they saw your ad twice today. Since the first rule was already satisfied, the user will not be served more ads today to reach the total allowed **10** weekly impressions.

## Frequency capping frequently asked questions (FAQ)

**Q:** What is the purpose of a campaign’s frequency cap?

**A:** Frequency caps limit the number of impressions a user can see during a given time frame. This setting helps advertisers walk the fine line of driving brand awareness and earning conversions without over-serving ads.

**Q:** What frequency cap do you recommend for my campaign?

**A:** Each campaign is unique based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended frequency cap for optimal campaign performance. We recommend starting with a lower frequency cap (e.g., 3 impressions per day) and gradually increasing it, as needed, based on the campaign’s reach and overall performance.

**Q:** Can I set a different frequency cap for a campaign’s creatives, audiences, or inventory?

**A:** No, frequency capping is set at the campaign level rather than for individual campaign elements.

**Q:** Can I set a different frequency cap for multiple durations?

**A:** Yes, a maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign).

**Q:** What happens if I choose a frequency cap rule based on Campaign Duration, but I haven’t chosen an end date for the campaign?

**A:** You’ll need to define a campaign end date before you can save a frequency cap rule that’s based on Campaign Duration. You can complete this step directly from the Frequency Capping section of your campaign.

**Q:** What is the relationship between my campaign’s multiple frequency cap rules?

**A:** Your campaign applies an "AND" relationship to frequency cap rules. If any single rule is met within a timeframe, it takes precedence, preventing further impressions to the user during that period.

**Q:** What are the devices for which IQM receives Device IDs?

**A:** We receive Device IDs for mobile, connected TV (CTV), over-the-top (OTT), and tablet devices.

**Q:** What scenarios might cause a campaign to exceed its frequency cap?

**A:** A given user may get served your ad additional times depending on whether a unique identifier (IQM ID or Ramp ID) is available.

For example, consider an advertiser who sets a frequency cap of 1 impression for a campaign. The first impression is counted at the Ramp ID level. Later, the campaign bids on a request for the same user because no unique identifier–such as a Ramp ID–is available. In this scenario, the cookie ID becomes the primary identifier and the bid is sent again. The cookie ID is counted as a unique user.

**Q:** What percentage of traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level?

**A:** Approximately 45-50% of bid request traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level. The remaining traffic is capped at the Device ID, Cookie ID, or IP Address level.

**Q:** When does frequency capping management take place?

**A:** You can add optional frequency capping settings to your campaign when you complete the campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section. A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the three elements that comprise a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings.

**Q:** How do I set up new frequency capping settings for a campaign?

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

**Q:** How do I change existing frequency capping settings for a campaign?

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

**Q:** What happens if I choose AI Based Optimization for my campaign and I don’t enable Frequency Capping?

**A:** Depending on campaign performance, the AI engine may apply Frequency optimizations. A limit of 100 impressions will be set to help your target audience avoid ad fatigue. You can enable Frequency Capping at any time to choose custom settings that will take precedence over [AI Based Optimizations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_4753688f6d).

## Locate additional frequency capping resources

- [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview)
- [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings)

# Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview

## IO budget overview

An Insertion Order (IO) is a contractual agreement that outlines the terms and conditions for one or more advertising campaigns. The primary function of an IO is to provide an effective means of organizing and managing campaigns that share similar traits. It’s also a means of managing the budgets of those campaigns.

You can assign budgets to individual campaigns after you create the IO. These campaigns will stop serving impressions once their cumulative totals reach the spend budget or impression budget that you defined at the IO level.

Refer to [What is an Insertion Order?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8365220-what-is-an-insertion-order) for more information on IOs and their relationship to campaigns, or keep reading to understand the differences between budget-based and impression-based IOs.

## Budget-based IOs

When monetary budgets are fixed, consider creating a budget-based IO. With budget-based IOs, you set the overall monetary cap for the total spend of the campaigns that are assigned to the IO. In other words, each of the campaigns will stop serving impressions once their cumulative spend reaches that monetary budget. This is to ensure you don’t overspend based on the overall IO budget.

You have the option to regulate spending on a daily, weekly or overall basis.

## Impression-based IOs

When monetary budgets are somewhat flexible and your main intent is to generate a certain number of impressions, consider creating an impression-based IO. With impression-based IOs, you set the overall cap for the total number of impressions of the campaigns that are assigned to the IO. In other words, each of the campaigns will stop serving once their cumulative impressions reach that limit. This is to ensure you don’t overspend based on the overall IO impression budget.

## Budget-based and impression-based IO comparison

When should you choose a budget-based IO or an impression-based IO? The choice depends on your goals, budget preferences and flexibility, and desired outcomes. Refer to the table below for a summary of the key differences between budget-based and impression-based IOs.

| **Consideration** | **Budget-based IO** | **Impression-based IO** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Primary goals** | Regulate overall campaign spending and reach a defined amount of spend. | Emphasize brand exposure and ad visibility. |
| **Monetary budget** | The IO’s spend is fixed. | The IO’s spend is flexible. |
| **Spend preferences** | Gain financial control and ensure each campaign stops spending once their cumulative total reaches the spend cap. | Ensure each campaign stops spending once their cumulative total of impressions reaches the impression cap. |
| **Example** | An e-commerce brand launches a 30-day campaign to promote a new product. They allocate a $10,000 IO budget. Each campaign within the IO will stop spending once their cumulate spend reaches $10,000. | A brand launches a campaign without a defined end date to drive brand awareness during the launch of a new product. They set a 1MM-impression budget. Each campaign within the IO will stop serving impressions once their cumulative impressions reach 1MM. |

## Locate additional IO budget resources

- [Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io)
- [Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)

- Enter a new end in the future
- Select Set
- Status will change back to Active

The campaigns column shows how many campaigns are associated with each IO. Clicking on a campaign count takes you to the Campaign table, which includes details of each campaign, like budgets, pacing and max bid. There is also a creatives count column within this chart. You can manage various actions by selecting an IO and choosing from the action items that appear above the table.

title: IQM Identity Graph overview

blocks.text: Reaching a target audience has become increasingly challenging for advertisers. With the average American owning 22 internet-connected devices, the journey from ad exposure to conversion is more fragmented than ever.

An identity graph is the key to effectively reaching your audience throughout this journey. It recognizes consumers across channels and devices, and unifies these identifiers into a single profile. These profiles help advertisers understand and engage with their target audience. When you target an audience based on this profile rather than individual signals, you create a more holistic marketing strategy that resonates with your audience and drives them to convert. You also have greater control over how often a single user is exposed to your ad. This control leads to smarter budget allocation and helps avoid negative associations with your brand due to overexposure.

The IQM Identity Graph covers the US, with a scale of 250M+ US individuals (~75% of US population) and 102M+ US households (~78% of US households). We refresh the graph daily to account for minor changes based on signals we observed in the previous 24 hours, and monthly to ensure its IP addresses, devices, and cookies are still active and reachable.

Here’s how the IQM Identity Graph works: IQM collects billions of data signals from various sources. We make connections between these sources based on pseudonymized identifiers and probabilistic and deterministic data. This process allows us to figure out which signals likely came from the same user and assign a person-level identifier to them. We call this identifier an IQM ID, which allows you to target the individual across their devices via your programmatic ad campaigns.

The IQM Identity Graph goes beyond the individual user by also spotting when multiple IQM IDs are usually linked to the same signals such as IP addresses. This pattern helps us decide when multiple individuals likely come from the same household. Their IQM IDs are grouped together and given one IQM household-level identifier (HH ID).

The report provides key demographic insights–like ethnicity, household income, gender, and age–and compares your audience to the US national average for each dimension.

The ID graph allows you to report on how many unique individuals you reached via your campaign and how often they were exposed to your message.
