blocks.text: Pseudonymization is a de-identification process. It replaces personally identifiable information (PII) with a pseudonym. This means that the result of the pseudonymization process is an identifier that is unique and acts as a placeholder for sensitive information.
While pseudonymized data has been de-identified, it can be reversed and re-identified. This is different from anonymized data, which has been changed in a way that makes re-identification impossible.

An IQM ID is a pseudonymized identifier that’s universal and tied to devices and cookies in the IQM Identity Graph. Each ID can be thought of as related to an individual person and associated with demographic, psychographic segments. Note that an IQM ID’s segment attribution and links to devices and/or cookies may change over time as we receive more signals and learn more about a given user.

An IQM household identifier (HH ID) is a collection of IQM IDs. These IQM IDs are grouped together under a single IQM HH ID when those individuals likely come from the same household. This is determined by reviewing when multiple IQM IDs are usually linked to the same signals such as IP addresses. An IQM HH ID also has segment attribution as the household level (e.g., household income, family size and mix, etc.)

The IQM HH ID is especially important as we keep the cookieless future in mind. By linking IP addresses to verified households, precise targeting is possible even when cookies or device IDs are unavailable.

A number of the IQM Identity Graph’s source signals are hashed identifiers such as hashed phone numbers, household addresses, and emails. This means that any formerly personally identifiable information (PII) was replaced with a unique string of characters. This process makes it difficult to determine the original phone number, household address, or email, which helps protect users’ privacy and security.
Deterministic data is a user’s known information based on information they’ve provided, such as a record of their email address. It’s ideal for accuracy, but scale is often limited.
Probabilistic data is information that we can infer about users based on similarities and patterns in observed signals. It has the potential to be less accurate, but it provides much greater scale.
The IQM ID Graph employs both probabilistic and deterministic data-linking methodologies to deliver better audience accuracy and higher match rates.

| --- | --- |
| Campaign planning | The ID graph enables audience size and reach forecasting to help you right-size your audience-targeting strategy (demographic, geographic, etc.) before spending campaign budgets. |
| Audience targeting | The ID graph matches your offline customers with their digital identities when you create a Matched audience from your first-party data. This matching process allows you to extend your marketing efforts to digital ad campaigns while keeping user privacy intact. |
| Audience targeting (cont.) | The ID graph recognizes consumers across channels and devices and unifies these identifiers to a single profile. This means you can effectively use cross-device targeting to extend your messaging to your target audience across all of the devices they use. |
| Campaign insights and reporting | The ID graph fuels an [Audience Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview) related to your [Matched audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). The report provides key demographic insights–like ethnicity, household income, gender, and age–and compares your audience to the US national average for each dimension. |
| Campaign insights and reporting (cont.) | The ID graph allows you to report on how many unique individuals you reached via your campaign and how often they were exposed to your message. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Pseudonymized identifiers

Pseudonymization is a de-identification process. It replaces personally identifiable information (PII) with a pseudonym. This means that the result of the pseudonymization process is an identifier that is unique and acts as a placeholder for sensitive information.

While pseudonymized data has been de-identified, it can be reversed and re-identified. This is different from anonymized data, which has been changed in a way that makes re-identification impossible.

### IQM ID

An IQM ID is a pseudonymized identifier that’s universal and tied to devices and cookies in the IQM Identity Graph. Each ID can be thought of as related to an individual person and associated with demographic, psychographic segments. Note that an IQM ID’s segment attribution and links to devices and/or cookies may change over time as we receive more signals and learn more about a given user.

An IQM household identifier (HH ID) is a collection of IQM IDs. These IQM IDs are grouped together under a single IQM HH ID when those individuals likely come from the same household. This is determined by reviewing when multiple IQM IDs are usually linked to the same signals such as IP addresses. An IQM HH ID also has segment attribution as the household level (e.g., household income, family size and mix, etc.)

The IQM HH ID is especially important as we keep the cookieless future in mind. By linking IP addresses to verified households, precise targeting is possible even when cookies or device IDs are unavailable.

### Hashed

A number of the IQM Identity Graph’s source signals are hashed identifiers such as hashed phone numbers, household addresses, and emails. This means that any formerly personally identifiable information (PII) was replaced with a unique string of characters. This process makes it difficult to determine the original phone number, household address, or email, which helps protect users’ privacy and security.

### Probabilistic and deterministic data

Deterministic data is a user’s known information based on information they’ve provided, such as a record of their email address. It’s ideal for accuracy, but scale is often limited.

Probabilistic data is information that we can infer about users based on similarities and patterns in observed signals. It has the potential to be less accurate, but it provides much greater scale.

The IQM ID Graph employs both probabilistic and deterministic data-linking methodologies to deliver better audience accuracy and higher match rates.

## Location additional identity resources

- [“Audience targeting and data management” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11825169-audience-targeting-and-data-management-collection-overview)

# Pacing overview

## Pacing overview

Pacing determines if your strategies are on track to spend in full based on how much they’ve spent so far and how much time is remaining in the campaign or insertion order (IO). Taking an active approach to pacing helps ensure you gather enough trend details to inform your optimization decisions. You’ll decide whether to shift budgets to different strategies in real time based on market changes, or adjust other elements such as frequency caps to drive spend performance.

## Pacing metrics

Monitoring a campaign’s pacing helps ensure that your campaigns spend in full. You can review and manage pacing at both the campaign and insertion order (IO) levels using one of three pacing options:

- Insertion Order (IO) Pacing
- Campaign Pacing
- Daily Pacing

Refer to [Manage pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471928-manage-pacing) for instructions on locating an IO’s or individual campaign’s pacing details in the Campaigns and Dashboards apps.

### Impression-based and budget-based metrics

Budget-based and impression-based IOs both run until a targeted number is reached. Budget-based strategies stop serving once a monetary budget is reached, while impression-based IOs stop serving once a certain impression count is reached.

Pacing performance metrics analyze the percentage of the total monetary budget **Spent** for budget-based IOs, or the percentage of the total impression budget **Served** for impression-based IOs.

The choice between budget-based and impression-based strategies depends on your goals and preferences. Refer to Pacing bar charts for more details on **Spent** and **Served** metrics, and review [What is a Budget vs. Impression-Based IO?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-what-is-a-budget-vs-impression-based-io)for more information and use cases on budget-based and impression-based IOs.

### Insertion Order (IO) Pacing

The IO Pacing metric compares the amount that each of its campaigns have spent so far against how much time is left before the IO’s end date. IO Pacing values are updated once every 24 hours, meaning pacing performance is calculated beginning from the IO’s start date through yesterday.

When an IO is pacing behind, you have the opportunity to allocate resources to the right strategies that’ll get spending back on track.

### Campaign Pacing

The Campaign Pacing metric compares the amount that the campaign has spent so far against how much time is left before its end date. Like IO Pacing, Campaign Pacing values are updated once every 24 hours, meaning pacing performance is calculated beginning from the campaign’s start date through yesterday.

When a campaign is pacing behind, you have the opportunity to adjust your campaign settings to get spending back on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for support.

### Daily Pacing

Monitoring the Daily Pacing metric is recommended for campaigns with shorter durations. It checks how much of your budget was spent in the current day, and calculates what percentage of the total budget that the spend represents. Daily Pacing values are updated once every hour.

## Pacing bar charts

IO and Campaign Pacing are represented by two bar charts in the IQM platform: **Spent/Served** and **Days Left**. Since Daily Pacing is assessed on a day-by-day basis, Daily Pacing is represented by one bar chart: **Spent/Served**.

You’ll review either a **Spent** or **Served** chart depending on whether you defined a monetary (**Spent**) or impression (**Served**) budget for the campaign or IO. These charts feature a color that signals whether pacing is behind, on track, or ahead of schedule. This performance is based on the pacing option you’re reviewing—IO, Campaign, or Daily—and the **Days Left** in the campaign.

### Spent/Served chart

| **Bar color** | **Pacing summary*** | **Pacing description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Purple** | Pacing ahead (>120%) | The campaign is pacing ahead, and will likely spend the campaign budget in full before the end date. |
| **Green** | Pacing on track (90%-120%) | The campaign is pacing as expected, and will likely spend the campaign budget in full by or before the end date. |
| **Orange** | Pacing behind (60-89%) | The campaign is pacing behind, and you should consider applying changes to hit your spending targets. |
| **Gray** | Pacing unknown | The platform hasn’t calculated pacing performance since the campaign doesn’t have an end date. |

*The programmatic bid landscape is dynamic. Regularly monitor pacing performance, regardless of the prior day or week’s performance, to ensure your campaign spends the budget in full by its end date.

### Days Left chart

The **Days Left** chart illustrates the percentage of the campaign’s duration that’s complete. For example, if the campaign’s duration is 10 days, and 5 days have passed, the colored bar will fill half of the **Days Left** chart’s total length. The total days remaining in the campaign are displayed next to the chart.

Note that the **Days Left** chart will always display in the color gray regardless of the campaign or IO’s pacing performance. The gray bar will also fill up 100% of the chart’s total length in any of these scenarios:

- No end date is defined for the campaign.
- The campaign has expired.

## Locate additional pacing resources

- [Manage pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471928-manage-pacing)
- [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind)

title: Pre-bid targeting overview

blocks.text: Advertisers use pre-bid targeting to ensure higher media quality and ad targeting that aligns with the brand’s standards. When you bid on an ad placement, verification partners like DoubleVerify (DV) determine whether or not it’s appropriate for the brand based on a predetermined set of criteria that you define. This verification is performed on an impression-by-impression basis to help ensure you’re not eliminating entire sites or publications unnecessarily.
The predetermined rules can apply to several factors:
**Fraud and invalid traffic (IVT):** Eliminating false online traffic that’s generated from machines or other bot activity that can interact with your ads.
**Brand suitability:** Ensuring an ad appears in environments that are free of any content that conflicts with the brand’s messaging.
**Viewability:** Defining a percentage estimate of how many of the ad’s pixels will be visible on the webpage for at least one second.
**Supply refinement:** Identifying and excluding low-value, cluttered, and Made For Advertising (MFA) inventory.

You can create your own Pre-bid audiences on the IQM platform. Pre-bid audiences allow you to select multiple pre-bid segments and group them together. We recommend creating a Pre-bid audience when you want to use the same set of pre-bid segments across multiple campaigns. You can add the audience to each of those campaigns instead of manually selecting and adding segments for each campaign.

Review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for instructions, or continue reading for more information on Fraud and IVT, Brand Suitability, Viewability, and Supply Refinement pre-bid segments.

sections.heading: Fraud and invalid traffic (IVT) pre-bid targeting
heading_path: Fraud and invalid traffic (IVT) pre-bid targeting

blocks.text: When you target fraud and IVT pre-bid segments, you take a proactive approach to identifying and preventing false online traffic before an ad impression is served. Verification partners analyze real-time data points to detect fraudulent activity and block it during the bidding process. This pre-bid detection means you can save resources that would have otherwise been wasted on non-human activity.
We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for fraud and IVT pre-bid targeting.

sections.heading: DV fraud and IVT segments
heading_path: Fraud and invalid traffic (IVT) pre-bid targeting

blocks.text: DV identifies a range of IVT behaviors including fraud bots, non-human data center traffic, hijacked devices, and emulators. Fraud and IVT segments are used to exclude sites or apps based on the percentage of fraud or IVT detected, ranging from insufficient data to 100% IVT. They also help you avoid invalid traffic, including sites with high fraud percentages or impressions with missing IP addresses.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments#h_7c2ad1d319) for a list of the fraud and IVT segments that you can target, and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

When you target brand suitability and suitability segments, you ensure that your ads will display within environments that align with the brand’s values. Verification partners evaluate content context, keywords, and other factors to determine the appropriateness of each ad placement.
We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for brand suitability pre-bid targeting.

DV segments identify impressions for exclusion targeting based on a variety of brand suitability categories. Target DV brand suitability segments to exclude sites or apps based on their risk level, ranging from moderate to severe, age rating, or consumer-review rating. You can also exclude them based on whether the content is unknown or unrated, or related to copyright infringement or malware.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available brand suitability segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

Verification partners ensure that ad impressions are viewable by real humans. Viewability pre-bid segments define the percentage of time that ads were historically visible on a particular site or app. For example, targeting an “All Sizes - 70% or Higher Viewability Rate” pre-bid segment increases the likelihood that the campaign’s ads will achieve 70% viewability. In this example, this likelihood is based on the fact that 70% of the ads on the sites were visible in the past.
We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for display viewability and video viewability pre-bid targeting.

DV viewability segments identify impressions based on historical display-ad and video-ad viewability performance relative to all measured impressions. Add DV display viewability segments to target rate-based tiers for specific ad sizes (leaderboards, medium rectangles, and skyscrapers) or all ad sizes. A rate-based tier uses historical data to predict whether the site or app will have a viewability rate of a certain percentage or higher.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available display viewability pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

sections.heading: DV video viewability and player size segments
heading_path: DV video viewability and player size segments

blocks.text: Add DV video viewability segments to target sites or apps based on their historical viewability performance, player sizes, and CTV on-screen-environment certification.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available video viewability pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

When you target Supply Refinement pre-bid segments, you take a proactive approach to identifying and preventing low-value inventory before an ad impression is served. Verification partners analyze real-time data points to detect Made For Advertising (MFA) supply and other low-value or cluttered inventory, and block it during the bidding process. This pre-bid detection means you can improve media quality and save resources that would have otherwise been wasted on subpar placements.
We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for Supply Refinement pre-bid targeting.

Add DV Supply Refinement segments to identify and exclude low-value web inventory such as Low Quality Generative AI (GenAI) websites, placements featuring Ad Clutter, and Made For Advertising (MFA) supply across a number of risk tiers.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available Supply Refinement pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

sections.heading: Unknown, Aggregated, and Individual segment types
heading_path: Unknown, Aggregated, and Individual segment types

blocks.text: You may encounter “Unknown,” “Aggregated,” or “Individual” segment types while targeting pre-bid segments. Refer to their definitions below for more information.

**Unknown:** The URL or app hasn’t been evaluated for a particular pre-bid targeting element such as fraud or viewability, or there’s insufficient data available regarding the URL or app’s fraudulence, brand suitability, or viewability.

**Aggregated:** The segment is an aggregation of individual segments. For example, an aggregated “All Moderate Content” segment would include each of the segments within the Moderate Content category.
**Individual:** The segment is a singular, individual segment.

MFA sites are designed to maximize scale and profitability. The tradeoff is that these sites offer a poor consumer experience and little opportunity for impacting user behavior. In other words, they’re just suitable enough to appear on brand inclusion lists, but offer little value to advertisers.
While a standard, industry-approved definition for MFA has yet to be defined, ad verification partners look to the following signals to help identify and exclude MFA inventory:
**Ad clutter:** An excessive number of ads are shown relative to the site’s content.
**Load times:** Ads are taking longer to load compared to ads hosted on non-MFA sites.
**Refresh rates:** The site’s ad auction may auto-refresh more frequently, which causes the ad to be in view for less time.
Targeting MFA pre-bid segments helps ensure that you invest in legitimate ad placements that can impact consumer behavior–not low-quality websites designed solely for generating ad revenue.
GenAI refers to AI engines that can create new ideas. These ideas are presented in the form of conversations; stories; images, video, and audio assets; programming language; and more.
GenAI websites can present risks concerning brand suitability, low-quality content, and wasted ad spend:
**Brand suitability:** The site may include inaccurate, nonsensical, or “junk” content. Uncertainty and lack of control may cause the ad to appear next to harmful content or misinformation.
**Return on investment (ROI):** The site is designed to lure in traffic and capture ad revenue, but its visitors are often bots or irrelevant users, leading to wasted spend.

**User experience and trust:** Users are becoming more adept at spotting AI-generated content, which can negatively impact the perception of brands that appear on these sites. Often generic and impersonal, the site’s content may also result in lower engagement rates compared to ads hosted alongside human-produced content.
Targeting Low Quality GenAI pre-bid segments helps ensure that you avoid dedicating media spend to ad environments that damage the brand’s reputation and offer little to no real value to consumers.

You’ll notice that the IQM platform doesn’t list prices for individual pre-bid segments. Instead, those prices are listed at the category and subcategory levels. For example, you will see a price next to **Brand Suitability - Display**, but not next to options like **Avoid high-risk adult content pages on Desktop or Mobile Web** or **Avoid high risk hate speech content pages on Desktop or Mobile Web**. That’s because each listed price represents the total cost of the segments within that category. In other words, you’ll pay that particular category’s listed CPM price whether you target one or several pre-bid segments within that same category.

There's no cost associated with adding pre-bid segments to a Pre-bid audience. The listed CPM prices will apply once you add the Pre-bid audience and/or individual pre-bid segments to a campaign and it begins spending.
Refer to the table below to review a list of scenarios and how those Pre-bid audience selections would be charged.
**Pre-bid segment price notice:** The prices listed in this example are for illustrative purposes only. Refer to the IQM platform for the current price of each pre-bid segment.
**Example scenario of pre-bid segment selections**
**Example cost (CPM)**
1 segment selected within the **Brand Suitability - Display** category ($0.06 [CPM])
1 segment selected within the **Viewability - Display** category ($0.13 [CPM])
4 segments selected within the **Brand Suitability - Display** category ($0.06 [CPM])

4 segments selected within the **Viewability - Display** category ($0.13 [CPM])

heading_path: Image, HTML, Video, or Audio campaigns

blocks.text: **Compatibility notice:** Supply Refinement, Brand Suitability, and Fraud and IVT segments are compatible with Image, Video, HTML, and Native (Image, Video) creative formats. Audio isn’t supported.

blocks.text: Each pre-bid segment category (**Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, **Supply Refinement**) is creative agnostic. Note, however, that the IQM platform supports one [creative format](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview) per campaign. This means that if you select multiple pre-bid segment formats (Display, Video), they won’t be targeted in this manner. Choose only one format for each Pre-bid audience to avoid incurring extra charges. Review [Target Pre-bid audiences or pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments) for step-by-step instructions.
Pre-bid audiences are executed differently for Native campaigns. Refer to Creative format compatibility - Native campaigns for more details.

Each pre-bid segment category (**Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, **Supply Refinement**) includes both Display and Video segments that you can select based on your campaign criteria. Since a single Native campaign can target both Native Display and Native Video creatives, they can include both Display and Video pre-bid segments.

Native campaigns targeting only one Native format (Native Display, Native Video) should only target Pre-bid audience segments of the same format. Campaigns targeting both Native Display and Native Video pre-bid segments will only be charged based on the segment type that matches the served creative’s format.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments#h_7c2ad1d319) for a list of the fraud and IVT segments that you can target, and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

## Brand suitability pre-bid targeting

When you target brand suitability and suitability segments, you ensure that your ads will display within environments that align with the brand’s values. Verification partners evaluate content context, keywords, and other factors to determine the appropriateness of each ad placement.

We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for brand suitability pre-bid targeting.

### DV brand suitability segments

DV segments identify impressions for exclusion targeting based on a variety of brand suitability categories. Target DV brand suitability segments to exclude sites or apps based on their risk level, ranging from moderate to severe, age rating, or consumer-review rating. You can also exclude them based on whether the content is unknown or unrated, or related to copyright infringement or malware.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available brand suitability segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

## Viewability pre-bid targeting

Verification partners ensure that ad impressions are viewable by real humans. Viewability pre-bid segments define the percentage of time that ads were historically visible on a particular site or app. For example, targeting an “All Sizes - 70% or Higher Viewability Rate” pre-bid segment increases the likelihood that the campaign’s ads will achieve 70% viewability. In this example, this likelihood is based on the fact that 70% of the ads on the sites were visible in the past.

We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for display viewability and video viewability pre-bid targeting.

### DV display viewability segments

DV viewability segments identify impressions based on historical display-ad and video-ad viewability performance relative to all measured impressions. Add DV display viewability segments to target rate-based tiers for specific ad sizes (leaderboards, medium rectangles, and skyscrapers) or all ad sizes. A rate-based tier uses historical data to predict whether the site or app will have a viewability rate of a certain percentage or higher.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available display viewability pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

### DV video viewability and player size segments

Add DV video viewability segments to target sites or apps based on their historical viewability performance, player sizes, and CTV on-screen-environment certification.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available video viewability pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

## Supply Refinement pre-bid targeting

When you target Supply Refinement pre-bid segments, you take a proactive approach to identifying and preventing low-value inventory before an ad impression is served. Verification partners analyze real-time data points to detect Made For Advertising (MFA) supply and other low-value or cluttered inventory, and block it during the bidding process. This pre-bid detection means you can improve media quality and save resources that would have otherwise been wasted on subpar placements.

We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for Supply Refinement pre-bid targeting.

### DV Supply Refinement segments

Add DV Supply Refinement segments to identify and exclude low-value web inventory such as Low Quality Generative AI (GenAI) websites, placements featuring Ad Clutter, and Made For Advertising (MFA) supply across a number of risk tiers.

Refer to [DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments) for a list of available Supply Refinement pre-bid segments and their descriptions, and review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for more details on how to target them in the IQM platform.

## Key terms and concepts

### Unknown, Aggregated, and Individual segment types

You may encounter “Unknown,” “Aggregated,” or “Individual” segment types while targeting pre-bid segments. Refer to their definitions below for more information.

- **Unknown:** The URL or app hasn’t been evaluated for a particular pre-bid targeting element such as fraud or viewability, or there’s insufficient data available regarding the URL or app’s fraudulence, brand suitability, or viewability.
- **Aggregated:** The segment is an aggregation of individual segments. For example, an aggregated “All Moderate Content” segment would include each of the segments within the Moderate Content category.
- **Individual:** The segment is a singular, individual segment.

### Made For Advertising (MFA)

MFA sites are designed to maximize scale and profitability. The tradeoff is that these sites offer a poor consumer experience and little opportunity for impacting user behavior. In other words, they’re just suitable enough to appear on brand inclusion lists, but offer little value to advertisers.

While a standard, industry-approved definition for MFA has yet to be defined, ad verification partners look to the following signals to help identify and exclude MFA inventory:

- **Ad clutter:** An excessive number of ads are shown relative to the site’s content.
- **Load times:** Ads are taking longer to load compared to ads hosted on non-MFA sites.
- **Refresh rates:** The site’s ad auction may auto-refresh more frequently, which causes the ad to be in view for less time.

Targeting MFA pre-bid segments helps ensure that you invest in legitimate ad placements that can impact consumer behavior–not low-quality websites designed solely for generating ad revenue.

### Generative AI (GenAI)

GenAI refers to AI engines that can create new ideas. These ideas are presented in the form of conversations; stories; images, video, and audio assets; programming language; and more.

GenAI websites can present risks concerning brand suitability, low-quality content, and wasted ad spend:

- **Brand suitability:** The site may include inaccurate, nonsensical, or “junk” content. Uncertainty and lack of control may cause the ad to appear next to harmful content or misinformation.
- **Return on investment (ROI):** The site is designed to lure in traffic and capture ad revenue, but its visitors are often bots or irrelevant users, leading to wasted spend.
- **User experience and trust:** Users are becoming more adept at spotting AI-generated content, which can negatively impact the perception of brands that appear on these sites. Often generic and impersonal, the site’s content may also result in lower engagement rates compared to ads hosted alongside human-produced content.

Targeting Low Quality GenAI pre-bid segments helps ensure that you avoid dedicating media spend to ad environments that damage the brand’s reputation and offer little to no real value to consumers.

### Pre-bid audience pricing

You’ll notice that the IQM platform doesn’t list prices for individual pre-bid segments. Instead, those prices are listed at the category and subcategory levels. For example, you will see a price next to **Brand Suitability - Display**, but not next to options like **Avoid high-risk adult content pages on Desktop or Mobile Web** or **Avoid high risk hate speech content pages on Desktop or Mobile Web**. That’s because each listed price represents the total cost of the segments within that category. In other words, you’ll pay that particular category’s listed CPM price whether you target one or several pre-bid segments within that same category.

There's no cost associated with adding pre-bid segments to a Pre-bid audience. The listed CPM prices will apply once you add the Pre-bid audience and/or individual pre-bid segments to a campaign and it begins spending.

#### Example: Pre-bid audience pricing

Refer to the table below to review a list of scenarios and how those Pre-bid audience selections would be charged.

> **Pre-bid segment price notice:** The prices listed in this example are for illustrative purposes only. Refer to the IQM platform for the current price of each pre-bid segment.

| **Example scenario of pre-bid segment selections** | **Example cost (CPM)** |
| --- | --- |
| 1 segment selected within the **Brand Suitability - Display** category ($0.06 [CPM]) 1 segment selected within the **Viewability - Display** category ($0.13 [CPM]) | $0.06 + $0.13 = $0.19 |
| 4 segments selected within the **Brand Suitability - Display** category ($0.06 [CPM]) 1 segment selected within the **Viewability - Display** category ($0.13 [CPM]) | $0.06 + $0.13 = $0.19 |
| 4 segments selected within the **Brand Suitability - Display** category ($0.06 [CPM]) 4 segments selected within the **Viewability - Display** category ($0.13 [CPM]) | $0.06 + $0.13 = $0.19 |

### Creative format compatibility

#### Image, HTML, Video, or Audio campaigns

> **Compatibility notice:** Supply Refinement, Brand Suitability, and Fraud and IVT segments are compatible with Image, Video, HTML, and Native (Image, Video) creative formats. Audio isn’t supported.

Each pre-bid segment category (**Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, **Supply Refinement**) is creative agnostic. Note, however, that the IQM platform supports one [creative format](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview) per campaign. This means that if you select multiple pre-bid segment formats (Display, Video), they won’t be targeted in this manner. Choose only one format for each Pre-bid audience to avoid incurring extra charges. Review [Target Pre-bid audiences or pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments) for step-by-step instructions.

Pre-bid audiences are executed differently for Native campaigns. Refer to Creative format compatibility - Native campaigns for more details.

#### Native campaigns

Each pre-bid segment category (**Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, **Supply Refinement**) includes both Display and Video segments that you can select based on your campaign criteria. Since a single Native campaign can target both Native Display and Native Video creatives, they can include both Display and Video pre-bid segments.

Native campaigns targeting only one Native format (Native Display, Native Video) should only target Pre-bid audience segments of the same format. Campaigns targeting both Native Display and Native Video pre-bid segments will only be charged based on the segment type that matches the served creative’s format.

cleaned_markdown:
# Create or manage a Pre-bid audience

## Pre-bid audience overview

Pre-bid audiences are groups of fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement pre-bid segments that you select. You can create these audiences and seamlessly integrate them into new or existing campaigns.

We recommend creating a Pre-bid audience when you plan to target the same set of pre-bid segments across multiple campaigns. You can add the audience to a campaign instead of manually selecting the individual segments each time. We currently support creating pre-bid audiences with DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments.

Refer to [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information on fraud and IVT, brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement pre-bid targeting.

## Create a Pre-bid audience

> **Pre-bid segment format notice:** Each pre-bid segment category (**Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, **Supply Refinement**) includes both **Display** and **Video** segments that you can select based on your campaign criteria. Note that the IQM platform supports one creative type for non-[Native](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements#h_0cb86eaf0b) campaigns. Refer to [Creative format compatibility](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-fraud-brand-safety-and-viewability-pre-bid-targeting-overview#h_0136cb1e33) to learn more about how pre-bid audience targeting rules are executed and charged for Native and non-Native campaigns.

You can create one Pre-bid audience at a time in the Audiences app. Follow these steps to create a new Pre-bid audience:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Pre-bid Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Pre-bid Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Select **+ Add Segment**.
6. If desired, search for specific criteria.
7. Expand the **Brand Suitability**, **Fraud & IVT**, **Viewability**, and/or **Supply Refinement** sections to browse the available segments.
8. Select one or more segments.
9. Review the total CPM cost associated with your selections.
   1. Review [Pre-bid audience pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-fraud-brand-safety-and-viewability-pre-bid-targeting-overview#h_7d9b739cb7) for more information on how the total cost for each Pre-bid audience is calculated.
10. Review your segment selections.
    1. If the campaigns that will target this audience are not [Native](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements#h_0cb86eaf0b) campaigns, verify that each segment is in the same creative format.
11. If desired, click the trashcan icon next to a segment to remove it from the audience.
12. Select **Create**.

You won't incur any costs until you add this Pre-bid audience to a campaign and that campaign begins serving.

## Manage an existing pre-bid audience

Use the **Pre-bid Audience** page of the Audiences app to review your existing Pre-bid audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them; and assign them to campaigns.

### Review a Pre-bid audience

Follow these steps to review an existing Pre-bid audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Review the Pre-bid audience’s total **Cost (CPM)** in the summary panel.
4. Review the details of the segments you added to the audience in the table:
   1. Provider
   2. Segment category
   3. Segment category cost
   4. Segment
5. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Pre-bid Audience** page.

### Edit a Pre-bid audience

Follow these steps to edit an existing Pre-bid audience:

1. Select the pencil icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column. This will open the **Edit Pre-bid Audience** pop-up window.
2. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Create a Pre-bid audience workflow to add or remove segments.
3. Click **Save** to apply your changes to the existing audience. .

### Duplicate a Pre-bid audience

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Pre-bid audience:

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column
2. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Create a Pre-bid audience workflow to name the audience and add or remove segments.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same segments as the existing audience, and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.
3. Select **Duplicate** to create the duplicated audience.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Campaign Audience** table of the Audiences app. The original audience will remain unchanged.

### Delete a Pre-bid audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating the existing audience and updating it to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Pre-bid audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Pre-bid audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

## Assign a Pre-bid audience to a campaign

You can assign Pre-bid audiences and/or individual segments to new and existing campaigns, and from the Audiences and Campaigns apps. Refer to [Target Pre-bid audiences or Pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments) for step-by-step instructions.

## Locate additional Pre-bid audience targeting resources

- [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview)
- [Target Pre-bid audiences or Pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments)
- [Pre-bid targeting frequently asked questions (FAQ)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698741-pre-bid-targeting-frequently-asked-questions-faq)
- [DoubleVerify Pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874803-doubleverify-dv-pre-bid-segments)
- [Post-bid measurement overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10874423-post-bid-measurement-overview)

blocks.text: **A:** Pre-bid audiences are groups of pre-bid segments that you select. sections.heading: Q: What is the value of targeting pre-bid segments versus applying site blocklists?
heading_path: General pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ
Q: What is the value of targeting pre-bid segments versus applying site blocklists?

blocks.text: **A:** Advertisers typically use a combination of site blocklists and pre-bid segments. With pre-bid targeting, verification is performed on an impression-by-impression basis. This granularity helps ensure you’re not eliminating entire sites or publications unnecessarily, which could impact your campaign's ability to scale.

heading_path: General pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ

blocks.text: **A:** You can currently target display (image, HTML) and video pre-bid segments.

sections.heading: Q: Will my Pre-bid audience get modified if I add or remove segments to/from it within a campaign?
heading_path: Targeting Pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ
Q: Will my Pre-bid audience get modified if I add or remove segments to/from it within a campaign?

blocks.text: **A:** No. Adding or deleting pre-bid segments within a campaign won't modify the original Pre-bid audience that you created in the Audiences app. The changes will only apply to the campaign you're updating.

Refer to [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for step-by-step instructions on how to edit or duplicate an existing Pre-bid audience if you'd like to apply and save changes.

sections.heading: Q: How much does it cost to target pre-bid segments?
heading_path: Targeting Pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ
Q: How much does it cost to target pre-bid segments?

blocks.text: **A:** Pre-bid targeting segments are priced on a CPM basis. These prices can vary depending on the segment category (fraud and IVT, brand suitability, viewability, or supply refinement) and format (display or video). We list the price of each segment on the IQM platform, and update the total cost preview as you add each pre-bid segment to a Pre-bid audience.

Refer to [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information on how pricing works, and [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for instructions on how to locate specific pricing details.

sections.heading: Q: Can I target both Display and Video pre-bid segments for a non-Native campaign?
heading_path: Targeting Pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ
Q: Can I target both Display and Video pre-bid segments for a non-Native campaign?

blocks.text: **A:** Note that the IQM platform supports one creative type per non-Native campaign. This means that if you select multiple pre-bid segment formats (**Display**, **Video**), they won’t be targeted in that manner. Choose only one format for each pre-bid audience to avoid incurring extra charges.

sections.heading: Q: How does pricing work for Native campaigns targeting both Display and Video pre-bid segments?
heading_path: Targeting Pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ

cleaned_markdown:
# Pre-bid targeting frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Expand the drop-down arrow next to a question to reveal its answer.

## General pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ

##### Q: What is a Pre-bid audience?

**A:** Pre-bid audiences are groups of pre-bid segments that you select. We recommend creating a Pre-bid audience when you plan to use the same set of pre-bid segments across multiple campaigns. You can add the audience to a campaign instead of manually selecting the segments each time. We currently support creating Pre-bid audiences with DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments.

##### Q: Where can I learn more about fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement pre-bid targeting?

**A:** Refer to [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for details on these pre-bid targeting options, and an overview of Pre-bid audience targeting on the IQM platform.

##### Q: Where can I learn how to create or edit a Pre-bid audience?

**A:** Refer to [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for step-by-step instructions.

##### Q: What is the value of targeting pre-bid segments versus applying site blocklists?

**A:** Advertisers typically use a combination of site blocklists and pre-bid segments. With pre-bid targeting, verification is performed on an impression-by-impression basis. This granularity helps ensure you’re not eliminating entire sites or publications unnecessarily, which could impact your campaign's ability to scale.

##### Q: Which formats are supported?

**A:** You can currently target display (image, HTML) and video pre-bid segments.

## Targeting Pre-bid audiences and segments FAQ

##### Q: Will my Pre-bid audience get modified if I add or remove segments to/from it within a campaign?

**A:** No. Adding or deleting pre-bid segments within a campaign won't modify the original Pre-bid audience that you created in the Audiences app. The changes will only apply to the campaign you're updating.

Refer to [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for step-by-step instructions on how to edit or duplicate an existing Pre-bid audience if you'd like to apply and save changes.

##### Q: How much does it cost to target pre-bid segments?

**A:** Pre-bid targeting segments are priced on a CPM basis. These prices can vary depending on the segment category (fraud and IVT, brand suitability, viewability, or supply refinement) and format (display or video). We list the price of each segment on the IQM platform, and update the total cost preview as you add each pre-bid segment to a Pre-bid audience.

Refer to [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information on how pricing works, and [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for instructions on how to locate specific pricing details.

##### Q: Can I target both Display and Video pre-bid segments for a non-Native campaign?

**A:** Note that the IQM platform supports one creative type per non-Native campaign. This means that if you select multiple pre-bid segment formats (**Display**, **Video**), they won’t be targeted in that manner. Choose only one format for each pre-bid audience to avoid incurring extra charges.

##### Q: How does pricing work for Native campaigns targeting both Display and Video pre-bid segments?

**A:** Campaigns targeting both Native Display and Native Video pre-bid audience segments will only be charged based on the segment type that matches the served creative’s format. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Creative format compatibility](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-fraud-brand-safety-and-viewability-pre-bid-targeting-overview#h_0136cb1e33) for more information.

##### Q: Where can I learn how to target pre-bid segments or Pre-bid audiences?

**A:** Refer to [Target Pre-bid audiences or pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments) for instructions on how to add pre-bid audiences or pre-bid segments to new or existing campaigns.

##### Q: Why are the Add To Campaign and Create Campaign options disabled for my Pre-bid audience?

**A:** Follow these steps to enable these options:

1. Refer to the **Vendor** column to confirm that each segment you selected includes segments from the same data provider.
2. Refer to the **Status** column to confirm that each segment you selected featured a **Processing** or **Ready** status.

If only the **Add To Campaign** option is disabled, none of your existing audiences are eligible to target the audience(s) you selected.

##### Q: In the Campaigns app, where is the option to add a Pre-bid audience to a new or existing campaign?

**A:** Unlike other audience types, Pre-bid audiences are segmented into their own section of the campaign. This means you won’t find it in the **Audience** panel.

Locate the dedicated **Pre-bid Audience** section to add a Pre-bid audience or individual pre-bid segments to the campaign, and refer to [Target Pre-bid audiences or pre-bid segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9949037-target-pre-bid-audiences-or-pre-bid-segments) for step-by-step instructions.

##### Q: Why is my existing audience missing from the Add To Campaign workflow?

**A:** Only eligible campaigns are included in the **Campaigns** menu of the **Add To Campaign** pop-up window. Eligible campaigns are ones with either no Pre-bid audiences or segments assigned to them, or ones with Pre-bid audiences and segments assigned to them from the same data provider.

## Post-bid blocking and measurement FAQ

##### Q: What is the difference between pre-bid filtering and post-bid blocking?

**A:** Pre-bid filtering blocks unwanted impressions before a bid is placed. It filters out fraudulent, irrelevant, or unsuitable ad inventory based on the pre-bid segments that your campaign is targeting.

As its name suggests, post-bid blocking occurs after a winning bid is placed. Impressions that are identified as fraudulent or unsuitable are blocked before they’re shown to users.

There are benefits and use cases for both pre-bid and post-bid approaches. Refer to their comparisons below for more details.

| **Consideration** | **Pre-bid filtering** | **Post-bid blocking** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Primary benefit** | Provides upfront defense against known fraudulent or unsuitable inventory. | Provides a final line of defense against previously missed fraudulent or unsuitable inventory. |
| **Primary drawback** | Increased chance of missing newly detected fraud. | Increased chance of paying for impressions that will ultimately be blocked. |
| **Budget impact** | Blocks impressions before bidding. | Blocks impressions after a bid is placed and won. |
| **Scale impact** | Limits scale when an excess number of filters are applied. | Opens scale by not excluding inventory opportunities prior to the auction. |
| **User experience** | Detects and eliminates fraudulent or unsuitable impressions before they’re shown to users. | Detects and eliminates fraudulent or unsuitable impressions before they’re shown to users. |

##### Q: What is post-bid measurement?

**A:** Post-bid measurement allows you to review data about ad impressions that DV has measured for viewability. When you target pre-bid segments from verification partners like DoubleVerify (DV), that verification partner assesses the ad environments where your creative(s) ran to:

- Confirm the apps/sites and exchanges.
- Derive the actual viewability performance.
- Determine whether there were any indications of brand suitability issues or fraud/IVT.

DV uses the following campaign details to measure ad impressions for viewability performance:

- Auction ID
- Advertiser ID
- Placement ID
- Creative ID
- Deal ID
- Seller ID
- Publisher ID
- Deal ID
- Order ID

##### Q: How can I report on post-bid measurement details after targeting pre-bid segments?

**A:** We currently partner with DoubleVerify (DV) for pre-bid targeting. DV provides a post-bid measurement solution that you can use to review performance data and confirm inventory quality.

Post-bid measurement data is recorded by DV, meaning it isn’t currently available via the IQM platform’s self-serve apps. This data will be made available in the IQM platform in the near future. In the meantime, contact us at [support@IQM.com](mailto:support@IQM.com) to request DV post-bid measurement data for a given campaign. DV measurement tags are automatically applied to creatives to collect the metrics required for both display and video environments.

blocks.text: If desired, you can specify external tags or tracking URLs and add them to your native creatives in the IQM platform to measure performance independently:

**3rd Party ID (Image, Video):** Reconcile performance data with IQM using the ID that you assigned to a creative on an external, third-party platform. This field is optional with the following use cases:
Keep track of your uploaded ads.
Reconcile data and compare delivery information.
Apply the identifier for your own reporting purposes such as for use in an external data visualization tool.
**Custom Tracking - Impression Tracking URL (Video):** Calculate the number of times the ad displays, and measure post-view attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define.
**Custom Tracking - Duration Tracking URL (Video):** Measure how much of the video ad was played and determine whether it was started or reached 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% of its total duration.

**Pixel URL:** Calculate the number of times a one-pixel-by-one-pixel image loads. Advertisers typically embed the code into their website’s header to measure page visits, or in an email marketing message to measure its open rate. Up to five Pixel URLs are supported per creative.

# Upload a native creative

## Native creative overview

Advertisers rely on native creatives to seamlessly blend their image and video ads with the content that surrounds them. Add native creatives to your creative library in the IQM platform one by one or in bulk, and in the following ways:

- From the Creatives app - Using a new image
- From the Creatives app - Using an existing image
- From the Creatives app - Using a new video
- From the Creatives app - Using an existing video
- From the Campaigns app - Using a new or existing image
- From the Campaigns app - Using a new or existing video

Like with standard video creatives, you can choose between video files and VAST extensible markup language (XML)/URLs, or use a combination of the two, in your native video campaigns.

Refer to [Creative ad specs and requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements) to confirm that your native video and native image creatives follow IQM and industry requirements before you add them.

### Variations overview

Introduce variety to your campaigns by adding multiple images, titles, and descriptions to the same native creative. This generates different combinations, or variations, of the same ad.

### Variations example

An advertiser uploads one native image creative to the Creatives app and adds a second title and a second description.

| **Creative** | **Title** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 1 | Description 1 |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 2 | Description 2 |

The following variations of the native image creative are automatically generated for the advertiser.

| **Creative** | **Title** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 1 | Description 1 |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 1 | Description 2 |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 2 | Description 1 |
| **Native Image 1** | Title 2 | Description 2 |

## Video tutorials

### Upload a native image creative

### Upload a native video creative

## Upload a native image creative

> **Native creative template:** Select **Sample File** in the **Native Creative** pop-up window to download a spreadsheet template if you plan to add one or more native image or native video creatives via a spreadsheet upload. Follow its formatting guidelines. You can save and reupload the spreadsheet to easily add your native creatives individually or in bulk. Note that uploading a spreadsheet will automatically populate certain fields with the items you included in the file. We recommend reviewing these fields prior to selecting **Create** to identify and address any mistakes that may have been included in the spreadsheet.

### Creatives app - New image

Follow these steps to add a native image creative from the Creatives app by uploading a new image:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Native**.
3. Choose **Upload New Images or Videos** from the **Add New** menu. This will open the **Native - by uploading Images or Videos** pop-up window.
4. Choose which method you’d like to follow to upload the native image.
   1. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   2. Drag-and-drop a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   3. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   4. Upload an image file.
5. To upload a spreadsheet from your computer’s local files, select **Upload CSV**, choose the file, and click **Open**.
6. To drag-and-drop a spreadsheet, open your computer’s local files, select the file, and drag your cursor from that file to the **Drag or Paste files here** section.
7. To upload a spreadsheet from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired files from your online drive.
8. To upload an image file, select **+ Add**.
9. Locate the **Creative** section and choose **Image**.
10. Select **Upload File**, choose up to five image files from your computer, and click **Open**.
    1. Select **Add Image URL** to enter a cloud source link for the image instead.
11. Enter a name for the creative.
12. Use the **Ad Details** section to add a title and description for the native image creative.
    1. Select **Add Variation** to include up to five titles and/or descriptions and click **Generate Variations**. This generates different combinations, or variants, of the same native creative for your end users.
13. Use the **Targeting** section to add targeting details to the native image creative.
    1. In the **Click URL** field, enter the full URL address where users will be directed to when they click on the creative’s call to action (CTA).
    2. In the **CTA** field, choose from a list of CTAs, or enter your own and select **+ Add**.
    3. Complete the **3rd Party ID** and/or **Pixel URLs** fields, if desired. Refer to Add custom tracking to a native creative for more details and instructions.
    4. To apply the same click URL, CTA, and/or pixel URL to each of the creatives you’re adding, select **Update in all creatives** under the applicable field(s).
14. Use the **Brand Info** section to add the brand’s name and logo.
15. Locate the **Preview** panel to confirm that each creative renders as expected; and that all titles, descriptions, logos, brand names, and CTAs are correct.
    1. If you added variations, select each creative listed in the **Creatives** column to preview each one.
16. Repeat steps 4 through 15, as needed, to add up to 200 native image creatives or variations.
17. Select **Create** to save the creative(s) to the Creatives app.

### Creatives app - Existing image

Follow these steps to add a native image creative from the Creatives app by selecting an existing image:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Native**
3. Choose **Select Existing Images or Videos** from the **Add New** menu. You must have previously uploaded an image creative or video creative to select this option.
4. Select the checkbox next to the existing image creative(s) that you’d like to use to generate the new native image creative.
5. Click **Next**. This will redirect you to the **Native - by uploading Images or Videos** pop-up window.
6. Follow steps 11 through 17 of the Upload a native image from the Creatives app - New image workflow to add key details to the creative(s) and generate them.

### Campaigns app - New or existing image

Follow these steps to add a native image creative from the Creatives app by uploading a new image or selecting an existing image:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a new creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.
4. Locate the **Native Creatives** section.
5. Select **Add New Creatives**.
6. Choose **By uploading Images or Videos** or **Using existing Images or Videos**, depending on your preference.
7. If you selected **By uploading Images or Videos**, follow steps 4 through 17 of the Upload a native image from the Creatives app - New image workflow.
   1. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Create** button.
8. If you selected **Using existing Images or Videos**, follow steps 4 through 6 of the Upload a native image from the Creatives app - Existing image workflow.
   1. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Create** button.
9. Save the creative(s) to the campaign.
   1. If this is an existing campaign, click **Save** on the campaign’s landing page.
   2. If this is a new campaign, click **Save as Draft** on the campaign’s landing page, or click **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections for this campaign.

## Upload a native video creative

### Creatives app - New video

> **VAST XML/URL template:** Select **Sample File** in the **Native Video** pop-up window to download a spreadsheet template if you plan to add one or more VAST XML/URLs via a spreadsheet upload. Follow its formatting guidelines: Add the Creative Name to Column A.; Add the XML or URL code to Column B.; Add each additional creative via a separate row. You can save and reupload the spreadsheet to easily add your native video creatives individually or in bulk.

Follow these steps to add a native video creative from the Creatives app by uploading a new video:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Native**.
3. Choose **Upload New Images or Videos** from the **Add New** menu. This will open the **Native - by uploading Images or Videos** pop-up window.
4. Choose which method you’d like to follow to upload the native video.
   1. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   2. Drag-and-drop a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   3. Upload a spreadsheet that contains the creative details from your computer’s local files.
   4. Upload a video file.
5. To upload a spreadsheet from your computer’s local files, select **Upload CSV**, choose the file, and click **Open**.
6. To drag-and-drop a spreadsheet, open your computer’s local files, select the file, and drag your cursor from that file to the **Drag or Paste files here** section.
7. To upload a spreadsheet from an external Google Drive or Dropbox account, select the corresponding company’s icon.
   1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired files from your online drive.
8. To upload a video file, select **+ Add**.
9. Locate the **Creative** section and choose **Video**.
10. Select **Upload File**, choose up to five video files from your computer, and click **Open**.
    1. Select **+ Add VAST XML/URL** to paste a VAST code instead, and select **Add** to apply it.
11. Enter a name for the creative.
12. In the **Thumbnail** section, select **Upload File** to add a thumbnail image from your computer’s local files.
    1. Select **+** **Add Image URL** to enter a cloud source link for the thumbnail image instead.
13. Use the **Ad Details** section to add a title and description for the native video creative.
    1. Select **Add Variation** to include up to five titles and/or descriptions and click **Generate Variations**. This generates different combinations, or variants, of the same native creative for your end users.
14. Use the **Targeting** section to add targeting details to the native video creative.
    1. In the **Click URL** field, enter the full URL address where users will be directed to when they click on the creative’s call to action (CTA).
    2. In the **CTA** field, choose from a list of CTAs, or enter your own and select **+ Add**.
    3. Complete the **3rd Party ID**, **Custom Tracking**, and/or **Pixel URLs** fields, if desired. Refer to Add custom tracking to a native creative for more details and instructions.
15. Use the **Brand Info** section to add the brand’s name and logo.
16. Locate the **Preview** panel to confirm that each creative renders as expected; and that all titles, descriptions, logos, brand names, and CTAs are correct.
    1. If you added variations, select each creative listed in the **Creatives** column to preview each one.
17. Repeat steps 4 through 16, as needed, to add up to 200 native video creatives or variations.
18. Select **Create** to save the creative(s) to the Creatives app.

### Creatives app - Existing video

Follow these steps to add a native video creative from the Creatives app by selecting an existing video:

1. Open the Creatives app.
2. Select **Native**.
3. Choose **Select Existing Images or Videos** from the **Add New** menu. You must have previously uploaded an image creative or video creative to select this option.
4. Select the checkbox next to the existing video creative(s) that you’d like to use to generate the new native video creative.
5. Click **Next**. This will redirect you to the **Native - by uploading Images or Videos** pop-up window.
6. Follow steps 11 through 17 of the Upload a native video from the Creatives app - New image workflow to add key details to the creative(s) and generate them.

### Campaigns app - New or existing video

Follow these steps to add a native video creative from the Creatives app by uploading a new video or selecting an existing one:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a new creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
   1. Select **+ Create Campaign** instead if you’d like to add the new creative to a new campaign.
4. Locate the **Native Creatives** section.
5. Select **Add New Creatives**.
6. Choose **By uploading Images or Videos** or **Using existing Images or Videos**, depending on your preference.
7. If you selected **By uploading Images or Videos**, follow steps 4 through 19 of the Upload a native video from the Creatives app - New video workflow.
   1. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Create** button.
8. If you selected **Using existing Images or Videos**, follow steps 4 through 6 of the Upload a native video from the Creatives app - Existing video workflow.
   1. This process will end with an **Add to Campaign** button in place of the **Create** button.
9. Save the creative(s) to the campaign.
   1. If this is an existing campaign, click **Save** on the campaign’s landing page.
   2. If this is a new campaign, click **Save as Draft** on the campaign’s landing page, or click **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections for this campaign.

## Add custom tracking to a native creative

### Custom tracking overview

If desired, you can specify external tags or tracking URLs and add them to your native creatives in the IQM platform to measure performance independently:

- **3rd Party ID (Image, Video):** Reconcile performance data with IQM using the ID that you assigned to a creative on an external, third-party platform. This field is optional with the following use cases:
  - Keep track of your uploaded ads.
  - Reconcile data and compare delivery information.
  - Apply the identifier for your own reporting purposes such as for use in an external data visualization tool.
- **Custom Tracking - Impression Tracking URL (Video):** Calculate the number of times the ad displays, and measure post-view attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define.
- **Custom Tracking - Duration Tracking URL (Video):** Measure how much of the video ad was played and determine whether it was started or reached 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% of its total duration.
- **Pixel URL:** Calculate the number of times a one-pixel-by-one-pixel image loads. Advertisers typically embed the code into their website’s header to measure page visits, or in an email marketing message to measure its open rate. Up to five Pixel URLs are supported per creative.

### Add a 3rd Party ID, tracking URL, or Pixel URL to a Native creative

1. Go to the desired third-party system to create the tracking event and obtain a URL or ID.
2. After opening the creative in the Creatives app, use the scroll bar to reveal the **Targeting** section.
3. If desired, expand the **Custom Tracking** section and enter the applicable tracking solutions.
4. If desired, add unique Pixel URLs to each creative.
   1. Expand the **Pixel URLs** section.
   2. Add the first Pixel URL.
   3. Select **+ Add More** to add up to four additional Pixel URLs.
   4. Click **Update in all creatives** to add the same Pixel URLs to each creative.
5. Once you’ve completed all other required and applicable fields, click **Add Creative** to finish.

# Curated inventory groups overview

## Curated inventory groups overview

Curated inventory groups include collections of Private Marketplace (PMP) or Open Exchange inventory that is grouped based on device type and content-subject-matter categories.

The Inventory app also supports the creation of custom Open Exchange, PMP, or Contextual inventory groups. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information.

### Benefits

With curated inventory groups, you can quickly target specific inventory and increase the relevance of your campaigns without the need for extensive manual setup. This can introduce better time efficiency and relevance compared to manual inventory group setup.

Through curated PMP inventory groups, you can also cut out intermediaries by leveraging a more direct SSP-to-DSP supply path.

## Requirements and considerations

Curated inventory groups are readily available to all advertisers. Note, however, that a single curated inventory group must include exclusively Open Exchange or PMP inventory, and not a combination of these two group types.

Refer to Curated inventory group sources for more information on the differences between curated Open Exchange and PMP inventory groups.

## Curated inventory group types

Curated inventory groups are classified by either **Device Targeting** or **Content Targeting** characteristics.

**Device Targeting** involves targeting inventory based on the type of device through which the inventory is delivered. These devices can include, for example, connected TV (CTV), over the top (OTT), or online video (OLV).

**Content Targeting** involves targeting inventory based on the content’s subject matter. These content categories can include general or specific topics including, for example, news, politics, sports, healthcare, cannabis, and more.

## Curated inventory group sources

Curated inventory group sources include **Private Marketplace (PMP)** deals and **Open Exchange** inventory.

**PMP** deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction. Unlike Open Exchange inventory, PMP deals provide more control and premium inventory. These deals not only facilitate a more direct link between the buyer and the seller, but also include a set price floor and predetermined inventory quality. PMP deals can be made with publishers (e.g., The Washington Post, Yahoo.com), device manufacturers (e.g., Roku, Sling, LG, Samsung), streaming services (e.g., Hulu, Fubo, Tubi, Pluto, Vudu, Freevee), and SSPs (e.g., Magnite, Pubmatic, SpotX).

**Open Exchange** inventory groups include inventory that’s available to all bidders in a programmatic auction. This “raw” inventory is grouped based on shared characteristics. For example, they may be grouped based on where the ads will be published, which SSP’s inventory will be targeted, or what device types the ads will serve on. The inventory included in these groups is transacted across Open Exchanges such as Google AdX, OpenX, and Index Exchange, for example.

### Available curated inventory groups by source type

The following curated **PMP** and **Open Exchange** inventory groups are currently available for campaign targeting:

| **Group Name** | **Description** | **PMP** | **Open Exchange** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CTV PMP Deals | Streaming inventory on CTV devices | ✓ | ✗ |
| CTV + OTT Open Exchange | Open Exchange CTV and OTT inventory | ✗ | ✓ |
| OLV Open Exchange | In-stream video on sites and apps | ✗ | ✓ |
| High Video Completion Rate | Sites and apps that are more likely to result in higher video completion rates (VCRs) | ✗ | ✓ |
| News & Politics Content* | Sites included in the News & Politics category | ✓ | ✓ |
| Sports Content* | Sites included in the Sports Content category | ✓ | ✓ |
| Cannabis Content | Inventory with publishers who accept cannabis-related content | ✗ | ✓ |
| Healthcare Content | Healthcare category sites | ✗ | ✓ |

*While both **Open Exchange** and **PMP** are supported, curated inventory groups can include only one inventory source type (**Open Exchange**, **PMP**) per group.

### Curated inventory group use case examples

| **Curated Inventory Group Source** | **Use Case Example** |
| --- | --- |
| Open Exchange | A specialty advertiser reaches audiences who are most likely to watch all–or almost all–of their video ad through the High Completion Rate inventory group. |
| Open Exchange | An advertiser operating within a sensitive vertical (e.g., cannabis) reduces creative approval times and ensures that publishers sending bid requests will accept their ads. |
| PMP | A healthcare advertiser runs high-quality, full-length video ads at scale on CTV devices through the CTV PMP Deals inventory group. |

## Browse and target curated inventory groups

Access curated inventory groups in the **Groups** tab of the Inventory app. Refer to [Assign PMP deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign#h_078f0c870c) when you’re ready to target them.

## Locate additional inventory group resources
