# Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category

## Bid Model overview

A Bid Model is an optimization tool that you can control to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities to optimize campaign performance.

Certain factors, such as eligibility requirements, differ based on the individual [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f) that you define for a campaign. Refer to these resources before beginning the process of applying a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension:

- [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview)
- [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview)
- [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview)
- [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview)

In this article, you’ll learn how to apply a Bid Model setting (Spend Ratio, Priority, Bid Modifier) to a Location dimension. You can also add Bid Model settings to Creative, Inventory, and Device dimensions. Refer to these resources for more details:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

## Video tutorial: Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension

## Apply Bid Model settings

> **Dimension category notice:** Bid Modeling can be applied to one Location dimension at a time. This means that you can apply Bid Model settings to either States, Cities, or ZIP Codes for Location dimensions—not a combination of them. Since cities are subsets of states—and ZIP codes are subsets of cities—ad serving might only be possible for certain dimensions that your campaign is targeting when you apply Spend Ratios to Location dimensions. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Spend Ratios applied to Location dimensions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_0bb2867bd8) for more information and examples.

You can add Bid Model settings to one campaign at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

1. Select the Bid Model app from the homepage.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
   1. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
4. Expand the **Location** menu.
5. Choose **State**, **City**, or **ZIP Codes** depending on the dimensions for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
6. In the **All States**, **All Cities**, or **All ZIP Codes** tab, click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
7. Select **+ Add to Modeling**.
8. Select the **Modeled States**, **Modeled Cities**, or **Modeled ZIP Codes** tab, depending on the dimension values you selected.
9. To apply a Spend Ratio to these locations:
   1. Locate the **Spend Ratio Method** column and choose **Flexible** or **Strict**.
      1. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options.
      2. Note that [Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) are required for any locations featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
   2. Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each location.
      1. The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
   3. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
10. To apply a Priority to these locations:
    1. Locate the **Priority** column.
    2. Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each location, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
    3. Refer to steps 9a-9b to apply Spend Ratios to these locations. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimension values that are assigned a Priority.
    4. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
11. To apply a Bid Modifier to these locations:
    1. Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
    2. Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
    3. Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired location.
       1. 1X indicates that you want the location to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than the campaign’s Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
    4. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.

The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Bulk operations:** Steps 9, 10, and 11 share how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Campaigns app

1. Choose the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Campaign Locations** section.
4. Select **Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Advanced Modeling** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling and one or more locations are added to the **List of Targeted Locations**. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Dashboard app

You can choose to optimize a campaign via Bid Model settings from the Dashboard app. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app and preload key details such as the campaign’s name and status.

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter the dashboard to determine which campaigns populate in the table.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign you’d like to optimize.
4. Select **Optimize Campaign** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Optimize Campaign** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling, and when only one campaign is selected. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

## Block or unblock serving for a location

Follow these steps to block or enable ad serving for individual dimensions:

1. Select the checkbox next to the Location dimension value(s) that you’d like to manage.
2. Select **Block** or to stop ad serving or **Unblock** to enable ad serving.

## Manage Dimension Bundles

> **More on Bundles:** A **Bundle** is a feature that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Note that all dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

### Save dimension values to a Bundle

Follow these steps to save one or more dimension values to a new or existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All States**, **All Cities**, or **All ZIP Codes** tab; or the **Modeled States, Modeled Cities,** or **Modeled ZIP Codes** tab.
2. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
3. Select **Save To Bundle**. This will open the **Bundle States**, **Bundle Cities**, or **Bundle ZIP Codes** pop-up window, depending on the type of dimension value(s) you chose.
4. To add the dimension values to a new bundle:
   1. Click **New Bundle**.
   2. Enter a unique name for the **Bundle** to differentiate it from others that you may create.
5. To add the dimension values to an existing **Bundle**:
   1. Click **Existing Bundle**.
   2. Open the **Bundle Name** menu and select the desired **Bundle**.
6. Select **Save**.

The **Bundle** “shell” will feature a dedicated row in the Bid Model table, with each bundled dimension value nested below it.

### Remove dimension values from a Bundle

Follow these steps to remove one or more dimension values from an existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All States**, **All Cities**, or **All ZIP Codes** tab; or the **Modeled States, Modeled Cities,** or **Modeled ZIP Codes** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the dimension value(s) you’d like to remove.
4. Select **Remove From Bundle**. This will separate the dimension value out from the **Bundle** and list it as its own standalone item in the Bid Model table.

### Delete a Bundle

A **Bundle** is automatically deleted when all dimension values associated with it are removed from the **Bundle**. Refer to the steps outlined in Remove From Bundle for more details.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier to a Bundle

You can follow the steps outlined in Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app to configure these settings for a **Bundle**. Instead of in individual dimension values’ rows, however, you’ll apply each of your settings in the **Bundle’s** top-most row. All dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level.

### Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle

> **Modeling removal notice: Remove From Bundle** and **Remove Modeling** are two different actions. When you **Remove From Bundle**, the dimension value is separated from the Bundle and is modeled as an independent dimension. However, when you **Remove Modeling**, the dimension value moves to the **Others** category. If you have applied Bid Model settings to the **Others** category, then the dimension value(s) will inherit those settings.

Follow these steps to remove Bid Model settings from a **Bundle** or a **Bundled** dimension:

1. Select the **Modeled States, Modeled Cities,** or **Modeled ZIP Codes** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox next to the **Bundle’s** name to select every dimension value within it, or click the checkbox(es) next to individual **Bundled** dimension values.
4. Select **Remove Modeling**.

## Manage an existing Bid Model

There’s no limit to the number of times you can add, change, or remove a running campaign’s Bid Model components.

### Review Bid Model settings

You can review a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Activity Log

### Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Open the Bid Model app.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to review Bid Model settings.
4. Expand the **Location** menu.
5. Choose **State**, **City**, or **ZIP Codes** depending on the dimensions you want to review.
6. Select the **Modeled States**, **Modeled Cities**, or **Modeled ZIP Codes** tab, depending on the dimension you selected.
7. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.
8. Select the magnifying glass icon to search for individual dimension values, and click **Advanced Search** to search up to 50 of them.
   1. Type the desired dimensions individually into the available field.
   2. Select **Upload** to add a CSV file containing the desired dimension values. We recommend starting with the provided sample file to ensure your keywords follow formatting and other guidelines.
   3. Click **Search** to apply the search criteria to the listed dimension values.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Select the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Campaign Locations** section.
4. Select **View Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
5. Follow steps 4 through 8 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Activity Log

The Activity Log records when a user adds or edits a dimension rule across any [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f).

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more details on the types of activities recorded in an Activity Log, and [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log) for instructions on how to monitor or filter one.

### Edit Bid Model settings

You can edit a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

> **Spend Ratio notice:** When you change an existing Spend Ratio, you must define a Spend Ratio exceeding the amount the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to a value of 21% or higher. For **Bundled** dimension values, the **Bundle’s** Spend Ratio must equal or exceed the total amount the campaign has already spent on its dimension values. Refer to in-platform descriptions for further assistance.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one location’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one location’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those locations. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of **Bundled** dimension values–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one location’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one location’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those locations. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimensions’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings

> **Targeting notice:** There may be certain instances when you’d like for a campaign to stop targeting dimension values that you’ve modeled. You’ll need to delete all Bid Model settings from a dimension value before you can remove it from your campaign.

You can remove a Location dimension value’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Location dimension value(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Refer to Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle to complete this process for **Bundled** dimension values, if applicable.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Location dimension(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Location dimension values by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All (States, City, Zip Codes)** tab, or select the **Modeled (State, City, ZIP Codes)** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

# Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category

## Bid Model overview

A Bid Model is an optimization tool that you can control to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities to optimize campaign performance.

Certain factors, such as eligibility requirements, differ based on the individual [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f) that you define for a campaign. Refer to these resources before beginning the process of applying a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension:

- [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview)
- [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview)
- [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview)
- [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview)

In this article, you’ll learn how to apply a Bid Model setting (Spend Ratio, Priority, Bid Modifier) to a Creative dimension. You can also add Bid Model settings to Location, Inventory, and Device dimensions. Refer to these resources for more details:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

## Video tutorial: Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension

## Apply Bid Model settings

You can add Bid Model settings to one campaign at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

1. Select the Bid Model app.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
   1. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
4. Select the **Creative** tab.
5. Click the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) for which you’d like to apply a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier.
6. Select **+ Add to Modeling**.
7. Select the **Modeled Creatives** tab.
8. To apply a Spend Ratio to these creative IDs:
   1. Locate the **Spend Ratio Method** column and choose **Flexible** or **Strict**.
      1. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options.
      2. Note that [Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) are required for any creative IDs featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
   2. Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each ID.
      1. The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
   3. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
9. To apply a Priority to these creative IDs:
   1. Locate the **Priority** column.
   2. Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each creative ID, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
   3. Refer to steps 8a-8b to apply Spend Ratios to these creative IDs. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimensions that are assigned a Priority.
   4. Select **Update Changes**.
10. To apply a Bid Modifier to these creative IDs:
    1. Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
    2. Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
    3. Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired creative ID.
       1. 1X indicates that you want the creative to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than the campaign’s Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.

The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Bulk operations:** Steps 8, 9, and 10 show how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Campaigns app

1. Choose the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Creatives** section.
4. Select **Advanced Modelling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Advanced Modelling** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 10 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Dashboard app

You can choose to optimize a campaign via Bid Model settings from the Dashboard app. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app and preload key details such as the campaign’s name and status.

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter the dashboard to determine which campaigns populate in the table.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign you’d like to optimize.
4. Select **Optimize Campaign** from the **More** dropdown menu. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Optimize Campaign** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling, and when only one campaign is selected. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 10 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

## Block or unblock serving for a creative

Follow these steps to block or enable ad serving for individual dimensions:

1. Select the checkbox next to the creative(s) that you’d like to manage.
2. Select **Block** to stop ad serving or **Unblock** to enable ad serving.

## Manage Dimension Bundles

> **More on Bundles:** A **Bundle** is a feature that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Note that all dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

### Save dimension values to a Bundle

Follow these steps to save one or more dimension values to a new or existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Creatives** tab or the **Modeled Creatives** tab.
2. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
3. Select **Save To Bundle**. This will open the **Bundle Creatives** pop-up window.
4. To add the dimension values to a new bundle:
   1. Click **New Bundle**.
   2. Enter a unique name for the **Bundle** to differentiate it from others that you may create.
5. To add the dimension values to an existing **Bundle**:
   1. Click **Existing Bundle**.
   2. Open the **Bundle Name** menu and select the desired **Bundle**.
6. Select **Save**.

The **Bundle** “shell” will feature a dedicated row in the Bid Model table, with each bundled dimension value nested below it.

### Remove dimension values from a Bundle

Follow these steps to remove one or more dimension values from an existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Creatives** tab or the **Modeled Creatives** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the dimension value(s) you’d like to remove.
4. Select **Remove From Bundle**. This will separate the dimension value out from the **Bundle** and list it as its own standalone item in the Bid Model table.

### Delete a Bundle

A **Bundle** is automatically deleted when all dimension values associated with it are removed from the **Bundle**. Refer to the steps outlined in Remove dimension values from a Bundle for more details.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier to a Bundle

You can follow the steps outlined in Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app to configure these settings for a **Bundle**. Instead of in individual dimension values’ rows, however, you’ll apply each of your settings in the **Bundle’s** top-most row. All dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level.

### Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle

> **Modeling removal notice: Remove From Bundle** and **Remove Modeling** are two different actions. When you **Remove From Bundle**, the dimension value is separated from the Bundle and is modeled as an independent dimension. However, when you **Remove Modeling**, the dimension value moves to the **Others** category. If you have applied Bid Model settings to the **Others** category, then the dimension value(s) will inherit those settings.

Follow these steps to remove Bid Model settings from a **Bundle** or a **Bundled** dimension:

1. Select the **Modeled Creatives** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox next to the **Bundle’s** name to select every dimension within it, or click the checkbox(es) next to individual **Bundled** dimension values.
4. Select **Remove Modeling**.

## Manage an existing Bid Model

There’s no limit to the number of times you can add, change, or remove a running campaign’s Bid Model components.

### Review Bid Model settings

You can review a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Activity Log

### Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Select the Bid Model app from the homepage.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to review Bid Model settings.
4. Select the **Creative** tab.
5. Click **Modeled Creatives**.
6. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.
7. Select the magnifying glass icon to search for individual dimensions, and click **Advanced Search** to search up to 50 of them.
   1. Type the desired dimensions individually into the available field.
   2. Select **Upload** to add a CSV file containing the desired dimensions. We recommend starting with the provided sample file to ensure your keywords follow formatting and other guidelines.
   3. Click **Search** to apply the search criteria to the listed dimensions.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Select the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Creatives** section.
4. Click **View Advanced Modelling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
5. Select the **Creative** tab.
6. Click **Modeled Creatives**.
7. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Activity Log

The Activity Log records when a user adds or edits a dimension rule across any [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f).

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more details on the types of activities recorded in an Activity Log, and [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log) for instructions on how to monitor or filter one.

### Edit Bid Model settings

You can edit a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

> **Spend Ratio notice:** When you change an existing Spend Ratio, you must define a Spend Ratio exceeding the amount the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to a value of 21% or higher. For **Bundled** dimensions, the **Bundle’s** Spend Ratio must equal or exceed the total amount the campaign has already spent on its dimensions. Refer to in-platform descriptions for further assistance.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-6 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one creative’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one creative’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those creatives. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s), and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimensions values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one creative’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one creative’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those creatives. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s), and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings

> **Targeting notice:** There may be certain instances when you’d like for a campaign to stop targeting a dimension that you’ve modeled. You’ll need to delete all Bid Model settings from that dimension before you can remove it from your campaign.

You can remove a creative ID’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled creative(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-6 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled creative(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Refer to Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle to complete this process for **Bundled** dimension values, if applicable.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Creative dimensions by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All Creatives** tab, or select the **Modeled Creatives** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

blocks.text: Select the Bid Model app.

Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each dimension value.

To apply a Priority to these Inventory dimensions:
Locate the **Priority** column.
Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each dimension value, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.

To apply a Bid Modifier to these Inventory dimension values:
Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired dimension value.

1X indicates that you want the Inventory dimension to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than the campaign’s Base Bid Price for that dimension value.

      1. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options. Note that Priorities are required for any items featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
   2. Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each dimension value.
      1. The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
   3. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
10. To apply a Priority to these Inventory dimensions:
    1. Locate the **Priority** column.
    2. Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each dimension value, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
    3. Refer to steps 9a-9b to apply Spend Ratios to these dimension values. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimension values that are assigned a Priority.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.
11. To apply a Bid Modifier to these Inventory dimension values:
    1. Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
    2. Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
    3. Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired dimension value.
       1. 1X indicates that you want the Inventory dimension to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than the campaign’s Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.

The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Bulk operations:** Steps 9, 10, and 11 share how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Campaigns app

1. Choose the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Inventory** section.
4. Select **Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Advanced Modeling** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Dashboard app

You can choose to optimize a campaign via Bid Model settings from the Dashboard app. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app and preload key details such as the campaign’s name and status.

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter the dashboard to determine which campaigns populate in the table.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign you’d like to optimize.
4. Select **Optimize Campaign** from the **More** dropdown menu. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Optimize Campaign** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling, and when only one campaign is selected. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

## Block or unblock serving for an inventory dimension

Follow these steps to block or unblock ad serving for an Inventory dimension:

1. Select the checkbox next to the inventory dimension value(s) that you’d like to manage.
2. Select **Block** or to stop ad serving or **Unblock** to enable ad serving.

## Manage Dimension Bundles

> **More on Bundles:** A **Bundle** is a feature that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Note that all dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

### Save dimension values to a Bundle

Follow these steps to save one or more dimension values to a new or existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Deal IDs**, **All Open Exchanges**, or **All Publisher Categories** tab; or the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab.
2. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
3. Select **Save To Bundle**. This will open the **Bundle Deal IDs**, **Bundle Open Exchanges**, or **Bundle Publisher Categories** pop-up window, depending on the type of dimension value(s) you chose.
4. To add the dimension values to a new bundle:
   1. Click **New Bundle**.
   2. Enter a unique name for the **Bundle** to differentiate it from others that you may create.
5. To add the dimension values to an existing **Bundle**:
   1. Click **Existing Bundle**.
   2. Open the **Bundle Name** menu and select the desired **Bundle**.
6. Select **Save**.

The **Bundle** “shell” will feature a dedicated row in the Bid Model table, with each bundled dimension value nested below it.

### Remove dimension values from a Bundle

Follow these steps to remove one or more dimension values from an existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Deal IDs**, **All Open Exchanges**, or **All Publisher Categories** tab; or the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the dimension value(s) you’d like to remove.
4. Select **Remove From Bundle**. This will separate the dimension values out from the **Bundle** and list it as its own standalone item in the Bid Model table.

### Delete a Bundle

A **Bundle** is automatically deleted when all dimension values associated with it are removed from the **Bundle**. Refer to the steps outlined in Remove dimension values from a Bundle for more details.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier to a Bundle

You can follow the steps outlined in Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app to configure these settings for a **Bundle**. Instead of in individual dimension values’ rows, however, you’ll apply each of your settings in the **Bundle’s** top-most row. All dimensions in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level.

### Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle

> **Modeling removal notice: Remove From Bundle** and **Remove Modeling** are two different actions. When you **Remove From Bundle**, the dimension value is separated from the Bundle and is modeled as an independent dimension. However, when you **Remove Modeling**, the dimension value moves to the **Others** category. If you have applied Bid Model settings to the **Others** category, then the dimension value(s) will inherit those settings.

Follow these steps to remove Bid Model settings from a **Bundle** or a **Bundled** dimension:

1. Select the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox next to the **Bundle’s** name to select every dimension value within it, or click the checkbox(es) next to individual **Bundled** dimension values.
4. Select **Remove Modeling**.

## Manage an existing Bid Model

There’s no limit to the number of times you can add, change, or remove a running campaign’s Bid Model components.

### Review Bid Model settings

You can review a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Activity Log

#### Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Open the Bid Model app.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to review Bid Model settings.
4. Expand the **Inventory** menu.
5. Choose **Deal ID**, **Open Exchange**, or **Publisher Category**.
6. Select the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab, depending on the inventory category you selected.
7. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.
8. Select the magnifying glass icon to search for individual dimension values, and click **Advanced Search** to search up to 50 of them.
   1. Type the desired dimension values individually into the available field.
   2. Select **Upload** to add a CSV file containing the desired dimension values. We recommend starting with the provided sample file to ensure your keywords follow formatting and other guidelines.
   3. Click **Search** to apply the search criteria to the listed dimension values.

#### Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Select the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Inventory** section.
4. Select **View Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
5. Follow steps 4 through 7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.

#### Review Bid Model settings from the Activity Log

The Activity Log records when a user adds or edits a dimension rule across any [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f).

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more details on the types of activities recorded in an Activity Log, and [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log) for instructions on how to monitor or filter one.

### Edit Bid Model settings

You can edit a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

> **Spend Ratio notice:** When you change an existing Spend Ratio, you must define a Spend Ratio exceeding the amount the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to a value of 21% or higher. For **Bundled** dimension values, the **Bundle’s** Spend Ratio must equal or exceed the total amount the campaign has already spent on its dimension values. Refer to in-platform descriptions for further assistance.

#### Edit Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one dimension value’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one dimension values’ Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those items. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

#### Edit Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one dimension value’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one dimension values’ Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those inventory dimension values. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of **Bundled** dimension values–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings from Inventory dimensions

> **Targeting notice:** There may be certain instances when you’d like for a campaign to stop targeting dimension values that you’ve modeled. You’ll need to delete all Bid Model settings from a dimension value before you can remove it from your campaign.

You can remove an Inventory dimension value's existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

#### Delete Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Inventory dimension(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Refer to Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle to complete this process for **Bundled** dimension values, if applicable.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

#### Delete Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Inventory dimension value(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Inventory dimension values by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All Deal ID, Open Exchange, Publisher Category)** tab, or select the **Modeled (Deal ID, Open Exchange, Publisher Category)** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

## Locate additional Bid Model resources

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

# Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal

## PMP inventory deal overview

> **More on PMP inventory targeting:** Consider creating a PMP inventory group if you plan to target or block the same group of PMP deals across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more details, and review [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for step-by-step instructions.

Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction. Unlike Open Exchange inventory, PMP deals provide more control and access to more premium inventory.

In this article, you’ll learn how to add your PMP deals to the IQM platform. Refer to [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign) when you’re ready to choose which campaigns will target or block those deals.

## Video tutorial: Create or manage a PMP inventory deal

## Create a PMP inventory deal

You can add a PMP inventory deal to the IQM platform in the following ways:

- From the Inventory app
- From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - New campaign

### Inventory app

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal to the Inventory app:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **PMP** tab.
3. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
4. Enter the unique **Deal ID** provided by the supply-side platform (SSP) or publisher partner.
5. Enter a **Deal Name** to help you identify this deal in the IQM platform.
6. Select the one **Exchange** in which the auction for the PMP inventory deal will take place.
7. Choose whether the current **Deal Status** is **Active** or **Inactive**.
   1. Campaigns can target or block only **Active** PMP inventory deals.
8. If desired, complete the optional **Creative Types**, **CPM**, and/or **Description** fields.
   1. **CPM** refers to the CPM information provided by the SSP or publisher, which you can store within this deal for reference. The CPM value you enter won’t be used in auctions.
9. Select **Add** to finish adding the new PMP inventory deal to the Inventory app.

### Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal from a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add the deal.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals**.
6. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
7. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Inventory app workflow.
   1. The deal(s) will appear in a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal to a new campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals**.
6. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
7. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Inventory app workflow.
   1. The deal(s) will appear in a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign
8. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format or click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

## Manage a PMP inventory deal

> **Shared PMP deals notice:** Shared PMP deals feature a folder icon next to their name. They’ve been added by your Workspace admin and are available for inventory targeting in your campaigns. While you can use these PMP inventory deals, note that only the Workspace admin can apply changes to them or delete them.

You can complete the following actions for PMP inventory deals that you’ve added to the Inventory app:

- Edit
- Delete

### Edit a PMP inventory deal

You can edit one PMP inventory deal at a time. Follow these steps to apply changes to a PMP inventory deal from the Inventory app:

1. Select the **PMP** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search, filter, or browse the deals to locate the one you want to edit.
3. Select the checkbox next to the deal.
4. Click **Edit**. This will open the **Edit Deal** pop-up window.
5. Apply your desired changes.
   1. In certain cases, the **Deal Status** field may be uneditable. You can change the status of a deal from **Active** to **Inactive** only when the deal isn’t currently assigned to any campaigns. Those campaigns are listed in the table toward the bottom of the **Edit Deal** pop-up window.
6. Select **Save** to apply your changes.

Any campaigns that are currently targeting the deal will be updated accordingly.

### Delete a PMP inventory deal

> **PMP inventory deal deletion notice:** Both **Active** and **Inactive** deals are eligible for deletion, but only if they aren’t currently assigned to any **Pending**, **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** campaigns.

You can delete PMP inventory deals individually or in bulk. Follow these steps to delete PMP inventory deals from the Inventory app:

1. Select the **PMP** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search or browse the deals to locate the one(s) you want to delete.
3. Select the checkbox next to the deal(s).
4. Click **Delete**.
5. Review any disclaimers and confirm your selection.

## Assign a PMP inventory deal to a campaign

You can assign PMP deals that you created in the Inventory app to new and existing campaigns. Refer to [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

## Determine which campaigns are assigned to a PMP inventory deal

Locate the **Status** column to review a PMP inventory deal’s list of assigned campaigns. The number listed next to deals with an **Active** status indicates how many campaigns are currently associated with that deal. Select the number to view a list of those campaigns and their individual statuses.

- [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign)

# Inventory groups overview

## Inventory groups overview

An inventory group is a collection of inventory sources. The collection is categorized based on specific criteria such as ad format, placement type, or other relevant attributes that each inventory source has in common. You’ll group inventory when you want to target or block the same set of inventory across multiple campaigns to streamline your operations and manage your campaigns effectively.

Create and target custom Open Exchange, CTV, PMP, or Contextual inventory groups; or take advantage of Curated inventory groups.

### Open Exchange inventory groups

Open Exchange inventory is available to all bidders in a programmatic auction. This “raw” inventory is listed in the Inventory app for targeting individually, or for targeting via groups that you form based on shared characteristics.

When you create an Open Exchange inventory group, you specify criteria such as where you want the ads to be published (countries, device types), which SSPs you’d like to target inventory from, what device types you’d like to serve on, and more. Consolidate the inventory of your choice into a single collection, then target or block the group across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

### Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups

CTV inventory is purchased via the Open Exchange. CTV inventory includes ads served on internet-connected TVs via built-in functions (smart TV) or external hardware (streaming player, step-top box, game console). It may include both OEM surfaces and streaming app environments.

CTV groups consolidate the CTV inventory of your choice into a single collection, which you can easily target or block across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

### Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory groups

Private Marketplace (PMP) deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction. Unlike Open Exchange inventory, PMP deals provide more control and premium inventory.

PMP groups consolidate the PMP deals of your choice into a single collection. Target or block this same group of PMP deals across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

### Contextual inventory groups

> **More on contextual targeting:** Targeting contextual inventory is one way to reach users based on a site’s keywords or URL. Targeting contextual audiences is another way. These audiences are formed by grouping users together based on their online activity. You determine these groups by indicating a list of relevant keywords and/or URLs and a timeframe. We add a user to the contextual audience when they visit sites that feature those keywords or URLs, browse them during the time period you select, and meet any other parameters that you specify during audience setup. Refer to [Contextual audience overview](https://intercom.help/IQM-Corp/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) for more information.

Contextual inventory groups rely on contextual signals to target ads based on the content of a webpage or a given URL. Delivering ads alongside relevant content helps ensure alignment with users’ interest and intent, and can lead to higher engagement.

When you create a contextual inventory group, you specify the specific keywords and/or URLs that you’d like to target, then add the group to a campaign. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

### Curated inventory groups

Unlike custom Open Exchange, PMP, and Contextual inventory groups, Curated inventory groups are readily available. They include collections of inventory that are grouped based on device type and content-subject-matter categories.

Refer to [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview#h_9c1dfdaf7d) for more information, including how to access and target these groups.

## Assign an inventory group to a campaign

9. Click **Save** to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign inventory groups to a new campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **Inventory Groups**.
6. Open the **+ Select Inventory Group** menu.
7. Search or browse and select the desired group(s).
   1. Filter the available groups by group type (Open Exchange, CTV, PMP, Contextual), if desired.
8. Click **Select**. This will add the group(s) to an **Inventory Groups** subsection of the campaign.
9. Save your changes.
   1. Click **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format.
   2. Click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

## Assign a PMP deal to a campaign

You can assign **Active** PMP deals to existing campaigns from the Inventory or Campaigns apps, or to new campaigns from the Campaigns app.

- From the Inventory app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - New campaign

Note that you can also save multiple PMP deals to an inventory group. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details.

### Inventory app - Existing campaign

1. Select the **PMP** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search or browse and select the PMP deal(s) that you’d like to assign to an existing campaign.
   1. Each of the deals must feature an **Active** status before you can assign them to a campaign.
3. Click **Assign To Campaign**. This will open the **Assign To Campaigns** pop-up window.
4. Open the **Campaigns** menu to search and select the desired campaign(s).
   1. Campaigns featuring a Draft, Pending, Running, or Paused status are eligible.
5. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

### Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to assign PMP deals to campaigns that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to target a PMP deal.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals** and open the **+ Select Deals** menu.
6. Search or browse and select the desired deal(s).
   1. Filter the available deals by exchange, if desired.
7. Click **Select**. This will add the deals(s) to a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign PMP deals to a new campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals** and open the **+ Select Deals** menu.
6. Search or browse and select the desired deal(s).
   1. Filter the available deals by exchange, if desired.
7. Click **Select**. This will add the deals(s) to a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format or click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

## Target exchanges or publisher categories

In a campaign’s **Inventory** section, open the **Exchanges** and/or **Publisher Category** menus to search and select the desired items. Save your changes to apply these settings to the campaign.

Note that your selection will limit the campaign’s available ad inventory to only the bid requests that match these specific exchanges and publisher categories. We recommend using the **Run Campaign Estimations** option to help ensure that your inventory targeting settings are scalable. Refer to[Estimate reach, impression, and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more details.

## Set up an inventory Allowlist or Blocklist

You can add Android package names, iOS Apple IDs, and/or site domains to an inventory Allowlist or Blocklist. Refer to [Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists - Inventory Allowlist/Blocklist](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472023-manage-campaign-allowlists-and-blocklists#h_e6effd1727) to learn more about these options and set them up for your campaign.

## Remove inventory targeting from a campaign

### Remove inventory targeting from the Inventory app

Follow these steps to unassign inventory groups from a campaign:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Inventory app - Existing campaign workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaigns.
   1. Select the checkbox in the header row of the table to select all assigned campaigns instead.
3. Click **Unassign**.
4. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

### Remove inventory targeting from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to remove inventory targeting rules that you’ve already applied to a campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to remove inventory.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select the trashcan icon next to any PMP deals or inventory groups that you’d like to remove.
6. Open the **Exchanges** and/or **Publisher Category** menus to deselect the exchanges or publisher categories that you’d like to remove.
7. Click **Save** to apply your changes to the campaign.
