# Create or manage an inventory group

## Inventory group overview

Inventory groups are collections of inventory that you categorize based on a set of criteria such as ad format, placement type, targeting options, or other attributes. In this article, you’ll learn how to create Open Exchange, Connected TV (CTV), Private Marketplace (PMP), or Contextual [inventory groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-what-is-an-inventory-group) in the IQM platform. Refer to Assign an inventory group to a campaign when you’re ready to target an existing group.

In addition to the inventory groups you create yourself, you can take advantage of curated inventory groups and assign them to your campaigns. These groups are segmented by inventory that’s available on specific devices and belonging to particular content categories. Review [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview) for more information on available inventory group types and inventory sources.

## Video tutorials: Create an inventory group

### Create an Open Exchange inventory group

### Create a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory group

### Create a Contextual inventory group

## Create an inventory group

> **Data refreshes in the Inventory app:** Data available across the Open Exchange, CTV, and PMP tabs of the Inventory app is refreshed daily and reflects the most recent seven days of request-log data.

You can create the following types of inventory groups in the Inventory app:

- [Open Exchange inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_64b8b6de94)
- Connected TV (CTV) inventory group
- [Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_bc8dfb92a9)
- [Contextual inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_a434266d9d)

Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for descriptions of, and the differences between, each type of inventory group.

### Create an inventory group from the Campaigns app

This article outlines ways to create and manage inventory groups in the Inventory app. You can also take a shortcut to these workflows directly from the Campaigns app when you create a new campaign or manage an existing one.

Follow these steps to access the inventory-group-creation workflow from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to target an inventory group.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **Add New Inventory Group** to open the Inventory app, where you’ll complete the workflows outlined in this article.

### Create an Open Exchange inventory group

Follow these steps to create a new Open Exchange inventory group in the Inventory app:

1. Select the **Open Exchange** tab in the Inventory app.
2. From the side panel, search or filter the available Open Exchange inventory based on your criteria.
   1. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) to review the available filters.
   2. If desired, upload a file containing the desired inventory instead of typing keywords.
3. Select **Search** to apply your search and filter criteria to the items listed in the inventory table.
4. Confirm whether the resulting inventory is scalable for the campaigns that will target this inventory group.
   1. The summary panel’s insights related to all of the inventory listed in the table based on the search criteria you applied—it’s not limited to the individual inventory you select to add to the new group.
5. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory.
6. Select **Save To New Group**. This will open the **Create New Group** pop-up window.
7. Enter a name for the group.
8. Click **Create** to save the inventory you selected to the new group.

### Create a Connected TV (CTV) inventory group

Follow these steps to create a new CTV inventory group in the Inventory app:

1. Select the **CTV** tab in the Inventory app.
2. From the side panel, filter the available CTV inventory based on your criteria.
   1. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) to review the available filters.
3. Select **Search** to apply your search and filter criteria to the items listed in the inventory table.
4. If desired, search by app name or publisher.
5. If desired, download the filtered table as a CSV or XLSX file.
6. Confirm whether the resulting inventory is scalable for the campaigns that will target this inventory group.
   1. The summary panel’s insights relate to all of the inventory listed in the table based on the filter and search criteria you applied—it’s not limited to the individual inventory you select to add to the new group.
   2. Refer to the table to review **Avails**, **Reach**, and **Streaming Devices** data by individual CTV inventories.
7. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory.
8. Select **Save To New Group**. This will open the **Create New Group** pop-up window.
9. Enter a name for the group.
10. Click **Create** to save the inventory you selected to the new group.

### Create a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory group

Follow these steps to create a new PMP inventory group in the Inventory app:

1. Select the **PMP** tab in the Inventory app.
2. From the side panel, search or filter the available PMP inventory based on your criteria.
   1. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) to review the available filters.
3. Select **Search** to apply your search and filter criteria to the items listed in the inventory table.
4. Review potential delivery details.
   1. Select a value in the **Inventories** column to review the inventories recently associated with the deal.
   2. Review the values in the **Avails** column to review total impressions based on the last seven days of request-log data.
5. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory.
6. Select **Save To New Group**. This will open the **Create New Group** pop-up window.
7. Enter a name for the group.
8. Click **Create** to save the inventory you selected to the new group.

### Create a Contextual inventory group

Follow these steps to create a new Contextual inventory group in the Inventory app:

1. Select the **Contextual** tab in the Inventory app.
2. To add keywords:
   1. Select the **By Keywords** tab.
   2. Type a keyword into the available field and select **Enter** on your keyboard.
   3. Additional, optional keyword recommendations will appear. Browse the list and select one or more keywords by clicking **+** **Add** next to them.
   4. You can add keywords in bulk by uploading a spreadsheet instead.
3. To add URLs:
   1. Select the **By URLs** tab.
   2. Type a URL into the available field and select **Enter** on your keyboard.
   3. You can add URLs in bulk by uploading a spreadsheet instead.
4. Each keyword and URL that you added is listed in the inventory table. Click the checkbox(es) next to the keywords and/or URLs that you’d like to add to the same group.
5. Select **Save To New Group**. This will open the **Create New Group** pop-up window.
6. Enter a name for the group.
7. Click **Create** to save the items you selected to the new group.

### Create any inventory group type

You can also create any type of inventory group directly from the **Groups** tab of the Inventory app:

1. Select the **Groups** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Click **+ Create Group**. This will open the **Create Group** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name for the group.
4. Select the type of inventory that the group will include: **Open Exchange**, **CTV**, **PMP**, or **Contextual**.
5. Click **Create**. This will redirect you to the details page for the new inventory group.
6. Select **+ Add Inventory**.
7. Depending on the **Group Type** you selected, follow the steps outlined in Create an Open Exchange inventory group, Create a CTV inventory group, Create a PMP inventory group, or Create a Contextual inventory group to add inventory to the new group.

## Add inventory to an existing group

1. Depending on the inventory group type, complete steps:
   1. 1 through 5 of Create an Open Exchange inventory group
   2. 1 through 7 of Create a CTV inventory group
   3. 1 through 4 of Create a PMP inventory group
   4. 1 through 4 of Create a Contextual inventory group.
2. Select **Save To Existing Group**. This will open the **Save To Existing Inventory Group** pop-up window.
3. Search or browse and select the desired inventory group that you’d like to update.
4. Click **Save** to apply your changes to the existing inventory group.

If desired, you can also add inventory to an existing group directly from the **Groups** tab.

## Manage an inventory group

> **Shared groups notice:** Shared inventory groups feature a folder icon next to their name. They’re prepared by your Workspace admin and available for inventory targeting in your campaigns. While you can use these groups, note that only the Workspace admin can apply changes to them.

The way you’ll manage groups that you’ve already created is the same for Open Exchange, PMP, and Contextual inventory groups. You can complete the following actions for inventory groups in the Inventory app:

- Review the group
- Review the group's recent Impressions and Avails
- Rename the group
- Remove inventory from the group
- Download a table featuring key details about the group’s inventory
- Delete the group

### Review an inventory group

Follow these steps to locate a previously created group and review its details:

1. Select the **Groups** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search or filter the **Inventory Group** table to locate the desired group.
3. Select the group’s ID from the **ID** column. This will redirect you to the details page for the existing inventory group.
4. Review an inventory group summary, such as details about the group’s cumulative impressions and reach for Open Exchange groups; or the group’s total number of keywords for Contextual groups.
5. For Open Exchange or CTV inventory groups, select the **Inventory Overview** toggle to review more group-level inventory insights.
6. Search the group to locate inventory featuring a particular ID, name, or publisher.
7. Review the table for a full list of the inventory that’s included in the group, and related metrics.

### Review a PMP inventory group’s Avails and Inventories

Follow steps 1 through 2 of the Review an inventory group workflow. You can select a value in the **Inventories** column to review the inventories recently associated with the deal, or select a value in the **Avails** column to review total impressions based on the last 7 days of request-log data.

### Rename an inventory group

#### Rename from the group details page

Follow these steps to change the name of an existing inventory group:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review an inventory group workflow.
2. Open the ellipses menu.
3. Click **Change Name**. This will open the **Change name of the group** pop-up window.
4. Enter the new name.
5. Select **Change** to apply your edits.

#### Rename from the Inventory Groups table

1. Select the **Groups** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Double-click the cell in the desired group’s **Name** column.
3. Enter the new name.
4. Select the checkmark icon to apply your changes.

### Remove inventory from an inventory group

> **Inventory removal notice:** Any campaigns targeting an inventory group will be impacted by the changes you apply to that group in the Inventory app. Determine which campaigns are targeting or blocking an inventory group and review those campaigns before removing inventory from the group.

Follow these steps to remove inventory from an inventory group:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review an inventory group workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to each item that you’d like to remove from the inventory group.
3. Click **Remove From Group**.

### Download an inventory group table

Follow these steps to download details about each of the individual inventory items included in an inventory group:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review an inventory group workflow.
2. Click the download icon.

### Delete an inventory group

> **Inventory deletion notice:** Inventory-group deletion is permanent. Determine which campaigns are targeting or blocking an inventory group prior to attempting to delete that inventory group.

#### Delete one by one

Follow these steps delete one inventory group at a time:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Review an inventory group workflow.
2. Open the ellipses menu.
3. Click **Delete**.

### Delete in bulk

Follow these steps delete inventory groups in bulk:

1. Select the **Groups** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory group(s).
3. Click **Delete**.

## Assign an inventory group to a campaign

You can assign up to 250 custom or curated inventory groups to new and existing campaigns. Refer to [Assign PMP deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign#h_078f0c870c) for step-by-step instructions.

## Determine which campaigns are targeting or blocking an inventory group

1. Select the **Groups** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Locate desired inventory group’s **Allowlist/Blocklist** column.
3. Select **Allowlist** digits (to the right of the green circle) or **Blocklist** digits (to the right of the red circle) to review which campaigns are targeting or blocking the selected inventory group.

After selecting the digits, you can also manage whether each campaign should allow or block the selected inventory group. Refer to [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign#h_078f0c870c) for step-by-step instructions.

## Locate additional inventory resources

- [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview)
- [Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9613510-create-or-manage-a-private-marketplace-pmp-inventory-deal)
- [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign#h_078f0c870c)
- [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview)

# Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview

## VLD report overview

The Voter Level Data (VLD) report surfaces insights about users you targeted in current or prior political campaigns. It includes ad exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and voting-history details, by voter. Generate and apply these insights to improve current and future campaigns, strengthen your brand’s messaging across channels, and create segmented audience strategies, for example.

You can generate a VLD report if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to the VLD report eligibility requirements and considerations section for more information.

> **More on voting data and VLD report insights**
> Like your favorite brands tailor their marketing strategies based on their end users’ demographics and interests, political advertisers use voting data to tailor their political campaigns. Voting data is public, and nonprofit companies are exempt, meaning they can use this data without consent from consumers. The insights we generate for and include in VLD reports are non-sensitive.

## VLD report eligibility requirements

If you are a political advertiser and have signed IQM’s master service agreement (MSA), you may be eligible to generate a VLD report.

Other VLD report requirements include:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign vertical** | Political* |
| **Campaign status** | Running Expired (within the past two years) Paused |
| **Campaign duration** | 3 or more days |
| **Campaign creation date** | September 16, 2024 or later (or earlier upon request to IQM's support team) |
| **Voter location** | All US states except Oregon** |
| **Audience type***** | [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651480-selecting-a-matched-audience) created from L2 IDs [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651480-selecting-a-matched-audience) created from raw data**** |

***Political:** Any campaign created under a political advertiser account is a “Political” campaign.

****Voter location:** Due to privacy laws in the state of Oregon, we are unable to generate the VLD Insights Report on any voters located there. Contact your account representative for more detailed information on the legality of reidentifying voters at the user level.

*****Audience type:** Your campaign must only include the audience types listed in this requirements table. For example, you cannot generate a VLD report for a campaign if it includes a Matched Audience created from L2 IDs and a Retargeted Audience consisting of your website’s past visitors.

******Raw data:** The VLD report supports audiences you create using First Name, Last Name, Address, and Phone Number. IQM anonymizes the data in the matching process, encrypts the files, and stores them behind a firewall to protect them against information leaks.

## VLD Insights reporting method

We take seven steps to transform your customer data into VLD insights:

1. Your customer data is uploaded to Amazon S3 Storage, IQM’s secure, cloud-based storage solution.
2. IQM’s processing environment ingests and pseudonymizes consumer data before matching it with L2 partner data, which is also also pseudonymized.
   1. When data is pseudonymised, it’s been de-identified, but the process can be reversed. This means the data can be re-identified. When data is anonymized, it’s been charged in such a way that re-identification is impossible.
   2. Because of our direct relationship with L2 Data, the linkage between L2 ID and the customer’s pseudonymized data is maintained. That linked data, along with Target IDs (MAIDs, Cookies, and RampID) forms our proprietary Voter ID Graph.
3. Matched and pseudonymized data is anonymized for targeting.
4. Anonymized data is segmented and ready for activation within your digital campaigns.
5. As the campaign serves impressions, Target IDs are collected and added into IQM’s Voter ID graph.
6. The graph is used to reverse-map matched and pseudonimized data to L2’s Voter ID.
7. IQM generates your VLD Insights report, tying ad exposure and engagement to L2’s Voter ID.

The VLD Insights report may only be utilized with L2 data. You can either bring a list of L2 IDs to target, or submit your CRM data containing First Name, Last Name, Home Address, and Phone Number. We’ll match that data to L2 IDs for targeting.

## VLD report pricing

There is a cost associated with generating a VLD report. You can reference the VLD report price after you enter key details–like the campaign’s total number of impressions and date range–and before you generate the report. We calculate these impressions on a CPM basis.

Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-report) report page for more information on where to reference the report-price preview.

### Report price surcharges

Agencies with workspace permissions can apply a markup to IQM’s VLD rate for individual advertisers. These surcharges can use either a percentage- or rate-based markup.

When you apply a markup, we’ll show advertisers a consolidated “VLD Insights Cost.” Here’s how it’s calculated:

Follow these steps to apply a **VLD Rate Markup** to an advertiser in the **Customers** app:

1. Go to the **Customers** app and select the **Finance** tab.
2. Locate and select the advertiser for which you'd like to apply the surcharge.
3. In the **Voter Level Data Rate** section, choose whether you'd like to add an **Absolute** markup or **Percentage** markup.
   1. An **Absolute** markup is a dollar amount, while the **Percentage** markup is a percentage of the listed IQM VLD rate.
4. Enter your markup value or percentage, and select the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

### Price deduction - Sufficient funds

The workflow to generate a VLD report ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create your report. We will deduct the **VLD Insights Cost** from your account’s available balance immediately after you select this button in the **Generate VLD** widget.

### Price deduction - Insufficient funds

> Organization administrators can add funds to an account. Contact yours to complete this process.

The workflow to generate a VLD report ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create your report. If your account’s available balance is less than the **VLD Insights Cost**, then this button will prompt you to add funds to your account instead. We will redirect you to enter a fund amount and select a payment method when you click **Add Funds**.

### Pricing for VLD reports with overlapping datasets

There may be instances when you generate multiple VLD reports with partially overlapping date ranges for the same campaign. This means that the insight data also overlaps. You will pay only once for VLD insights for each date.

**Example:** You generate two reports for the same campaign–one with a date range of August 1st-10th, and another with a date range of August 5th-20th. Since you already paid for the insights from August 1st-10th, we will only change you for a portion of the second report: the new data generated for the August 11th-20th date range. We will still aggregate data from the full August 5th-20th date range in the second report.

## VLD report metrics

VLD reports return ad exposure metrics (Impressions, Clicks, Conversions) at a user level. If you used L2 data for audience creation, you can also reference each user’s L2 ID and multiple demographic data points.

| **Metric title** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Impressions** | The number of times the user viewed your ad. |
| **Clicks** | The number of times the user clicked on your ad. |
| **Conversions** | The number of a user’s conversions that can be attributed to your ad. |
| **L2 ID** | The user’s L2 ID, which is available when your campaign includes a matched audience that uses L2 IDs. |
| **First Name** | The user's legal first name. |
| **Middle Name** | The user's legal middle name. |
| **Last Name** | The user's legal last name. |
| **Address** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **ZIP Code** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **State** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **Phone 1, Phone 2** | The user’s primary and/or secondary phone number(s). |
| **Registration status** | “Active” or “Not Active” depending on the user’s current voter registration status. |
| **Age** | The user's age. |
| **Gender** | “M” for “Male” or “F” for “Female” based on a user’s legal sex. |
| **Marital Status** | “Single,” “Married,” “Divorced,” or “Widowed” depending on the user’s current legal marital status. |
| **Net Worth** | The total value of the user’s assets once their liabilities and debts are subtracted. |
| **Home Owner** | “Yes” or “No” depending on the user’s home ownership status. |
| **Income** | The money the user earns on an annual basis. |
| **Education** | The extent of formal, certified instruction that the user has completed. |
| **Presidential_primary_2000 (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, etc.)** | “Y” or “N” depending on the user’s voting status during this election type and cycle. |
| **General_2023_11_07 (2022_11_08, etc.)** | Y” or “N” depending on the user’s voting status during this election type and cycle. |

## VLD report statuses

You can review a VLD report’s current status on the **Voter Level Data** page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your insights are generated. You can view, download, or email the VLD report. |
| **Processing** | We are working on generating your insights. Check back in about 15 minutes. |
| **Failed*** | You either encountered a technical error during report generation, or the campaign you selected is no longer eligible for VLD insights. Try again in a few minutes to rule out a technical error. |

* If a VLD report features a **Failed** status, we will credit the cost to your account immediately.

## Locate additional VLD report resources

- [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-report#h_68c96f97e1)
- [Troubleshoot a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827650-troubleshoot-a-voter-level-data-vld-report#h_1faef58b68)

# Generate or manage a Voter Level Data
(VLD) Insights report

## VLD Insights report overview

The Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report surfaces insights about users you targeted in current or prior political campaigns. It includes data such as demographic, ad-exposure, and voting-history details. Generate and apply these insights to improve current and future campaigns, strengthen your brand’s messaging across channels, and create segmented audience strategies, for example.

You can generate a VLD report if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to the [Voter Level Data (VLD) report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-report-overview#h_1f80984123) page for more information on eligibility requirements, metrics, and costs.

## Video tutorial: Generate a VLD Insights report

## Generate a VLD Insights report

> **Voter location notice:** Due to privacy laws in the state of Oregon, we are unable to generate the VLD Insights report on any voters located there. Contact your account representative for more detailed information on the legality of reidentifying voters at the user level.

You can generate a VLD report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboards app

### Generate a VLD Insights report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to access the **+ Generate New** workflow:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Select **Voter Level Data**.
3. Click **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Voter Level Data** pop-up window.
4. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu.
5. Search and select the campaign for which you want to generate insights.
   1. Search for the campaign’s name or ID, or the Insertion Order’s (IO) name or ID.
   2. If a desired campaign or IO is missing from the list, its status doesn’t match the **Campaign Status** you selected and/or it isn’t eligible for VLD Insights generation.
6. Select a date range from the **Date Range** field.
   1. Date ranges use the same time zone as the location where the campaign was initially created.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Review your campaign selection, and a summary of the report’s chargeable impressions and the associated cost.
   1. We calculate the **VLD Insights Price** based on the number of impressions that your campaign or IO delivered during the specified date range at a CPM rate.
9. Select **Previous** to change the report’s settings, if desired.
10. Click **Generate** to create the VLD Insights report.
    1. The **VLD Insight Price** is deducted from your account’s available balance immediately after you select this button.

VLD reports are typically ready within 15 minutes. Once generated, you can find the VLD insights on the Insights app’s **Voter Level Data** page. Review Manage a VLD report for details on how to review, download, or delete a report.

### Generate a VLD Insights report from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to VLD report creation from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose the insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to generate insights.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Click **Generate VLD Insights** from the **More** menu.
   1. You can only select **Generate VLD Insights** if the selected campaign is eligible for VLD reporting.
5. You’ll be redirected to the **Voter Level Data** page of the Insights app, where the campaign’s name and date range will be auto-populated.
6. Follow steps 7 through 9 of the Generate a VLD Insights report from the Insights app workflow to generate the report.

### Generate a VLD Insights report from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to VLD report creation from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter or search the dashboard to locate the desired IO or campaign.
3. Click the checkbox next to the IO or campaign.
4. Select **Generate VLD Insights** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Voter Level Data** page of the Insights app, and auto-populate the campaign or IO’s name and date range.
   1. This option is available only when your account and the selected IO or campaign are eligible for VLD Insights reporting.
5. Follow steps 7 through 9 of the Generate a VLD Insights report from the Insights app workflow to generate the report.

## Manage a VLD Insights report

> **Data retention notice:** You can access generated reports for three years after their creation date, in alignment with the IQM platform data-retention policy.

The **Voter Level Data** page displays each of your VLD reports and their statuses. You can use the **Actions** column to download a VLD report to your device or send it as an email attachment once it’s **Ready**.

- Download
- Email
- Delete

### Download a VLD Insights report

Follow these steps to download a VLD Insights report:

1. Filter or search the table to locate the desired report.
2. Open the **Download** menu in the **Actions** column.
3. Click **Download as CSV** or **Download as XLSX**, depending on your preference.

You’ll receive your insights as a single CSV or XLSX file if the spreadsheet contains 100K or less rows. Otherwise, you’ll receive them as a ZIP file containing multiple CSV or XLSX files. For example, if the report contains a total of 150K rows and you choose to download the insights as an XLSX file, then your download will include one ZIP file containing two XLSX files: one with 100K rows, and one with 50K rows.

### Email a VLD Insights report

Follow these steps to email a VLD Insights report:

1. Filter or search the table to locate the report you want to send.
2. Select the envelope icon from the report’s **Actions** column.
3. Click **Email as CSV** or **Email as XLSX**, depending on your preference. This will open an **Email Voter Level Data** pop-up window.
4. Add up to 15 email aliases to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
5. Select **Send Email**.

The email will include a link that the recipients can use to download the report. This link expires 24 hours after you select **Send Email**.

### Delete a VLD Insights report

We limit the ability to delete most VLD reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights. You can, however, delete **Failed** VLD reports.

Follow these steps to delete a **Failed** VLD report from the **Voter Level Data** page:

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the **Failed** report(s) you want to delete.
2. Click **Delete**.

## Review past VLD Insights report spend

Follow these steps to review the total amount spent on VLD report generation from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open the **View By** menu and click **Campaigns**, **Insertion Orders**, or **Advertiser**, depending on your preference.
   1. Workspace admins also have the option to select **Workspace**.
3. Select **VLD Report Cost** from the **Columns** menu.
   1. The **VLD Report Cost** column will populate in the table.
4. Adjust the dashboard’s **Time Zone** and **Date Range** details to view the amount spent on VLD report generation within a specific timeframe, if desired.

# Troubleshoot a Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report

## VLD troubleshooting overview

Certain advertisers can create Voter Level Data (VLD) reports if their account and campaigns meet certain eligibility requirements. They must also follow specific steps to successfully generate a report.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating or managing a VLD report, refer to these resources first:

- [Voter Level Data (VLD) report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report-overview)
- [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report)

Return to this article to address and resolve other factors that may block your ability to create or manage a VLD report.

## VLD report creation - Insufficient funds

> Organization administrators can add funds to an account. Contact yours to complete this process.

The workflow to generate a VLD report ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create your report. If your account’s available balance is less than the price of the VLD report, this button will prompt you to add funds to your account instead.

### Add funds from the Insights app

Follow these steps to add funds directly from the **Generate VLD** widget:

1. Select **Add Funds** directly from the **Generate VLD** widget.
2. We will redirect you to enter a fund amount and select a payment method.

### Add funds from the Dashboard app

Follow the steps listed in the [Adding Funds](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5734663-adding-funds) article to add funds from the **Dashboard** app.

## VLD report creation - Campaign missing from list

### Review campaign eligibility criteria

If you are in the **Insights** app, the **Campaign** field in the **Generate Voter Level Data** pop-up window only includes campaigns that are eligible for VLD report creation.

If you are in the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** app, the option to generate a VLD report is only available for eligible campaigns.

Refer to the [Voter Level Data (VLD) report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report-overview) page for more information on the factors that make you or your campaign eligible for VLD insights.

### Check the campaign’s current status

If you are generating a VLD report in the **Insights** app, you are first prompted to select the campaign’s current status from the **Campaign Status** drop-down menu. This selection narrows the available **Campaign** field options to those with that status. For example, if you choose **Expired**, we will only make eligible campaigns with an **Expired** status searchable in the **Campaign** field.

Check the campaign’s current status and update the **Campaign Status** field accordingly, if applicable.

To help reduce user errors next time, consider generating a VLD report from the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** apps. Unlike VLD report creation via the **Insights** app, these two workflows will pre-populate the **Campaign Status**, **Campaign**, and **Date Range** fields during setup. Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report) article for more information on how to generate a VLD report from the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** apps.

## VLD report creation - Cannot generate a report

You may encounter a warning message or another issue that blocks you from generating VLD data from a particular campaign and across a particular date range. We build in certain blocks to help avoid charging you for highly similar datasets more than once, or generating reports inaccurately.

These blocks typically occur for one of the following reasons:

1. You can generate one VLD report at a time for each campaign.
   1. You can generate another VLD report once your in-progress report displays a **Ready** status on the **Voter Level Data** page. Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report) page to learn how to access this page.
2. You can generate one VLD report total when you choose the same report dates for the same campaign.
   1. The **Generate** option will not be available in the **Generate Voter Level Data** widget. Instead, you can review the VLD report you already generated for this campaign and date range.

There may be certain cases where you’ve previously generated VLD reports, but your access is now revoked. For example, your signed MSA for VLD Insights reporting may have expired. You won’t be able to generate new insights, but you can continue to access reports you’ve already generated for three years after their creation date, in alignment with the IQM platform data-retention policy.

## VLD report insights - Cannot delete a report

We limit the ability to delete VLD reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights.

The **Voter Level Data** page displays each of your VLD reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can delete **Failed** VLD reports.

## VLD report insights - Insufficient impressions

Your campaign must have reached at least 10K chargeable impressions across the date range you selected before you can generate VLD insights for it.

## VLD report insights - Cannot locate a generated report

Unlike with campaigns and other IQM platform workflows, you were not prompted to name your report during the VLD report setup process. Instead, your VLD report’s name will begin with the campaign ID or insertion order (IO) ID, followed by “_VLD_Insights”. We will add a number to the end of the VLD report’s name each time you generate one for the same campaign or IO.

Use the search field on the **Voter Level Insights** page in the **Insights** app to enter your campaign ID or IO ID, and locate your generated VLD report.

- [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report)

# Import an audience from the L2 DataMapping platform

## L2 audience import overview

IQM partners with data provider “L2” to offer comprehensive voter and constituent targeting solutions. Our direct integrations allow you to export audiences directly from the L2 platform and import them into the IQM platform. You can manage these audiences in the **Audiences** app, or add them directly to your campaigns.

## Import an L2 audience

### Prepare to import an L2 audience

You’ll need these three items before you can import an L2 audience:

1. An L2 platform account login.
2. Your IQM account ID.
3. The segment name.

Follow these steps to locate your IQM account ID:

1. Select **My Profile** from the IQM homepage.
2. Click **Organizations**.
3. Locate the code listed in the **ID** field.

### Send universe

Follow these steps to send an audience from the L2 platform to your account on the IQM platform:

1. Navigate to the [L2 DataMapping](https://www.l2datamapping.com/account/login?&r0=/) platform (external link) and log into your account.
2. Search for and select the audience you’d like to send to the IQM platform.
3. Locate the **SOURCE** category.
4. Select the **+** icon next to the **Universes** dropdown menu to create a new universe.
5. Enter a name for the universe using the following naming convention: IQM_[IQM account ID]_[Segment name].
   1. Replace the items in brackets with the correct values, and remove the brackets. For example, “IQM_123456_CustomSegment”.
6. Select the universe name you entered to open the **Universe Details** page.
7. Click the house icon.
8. Select **Transmit this Universe to a third-party application**.
9. Choose **IQM** from the list of third-party applications that populate.
10. Click **SEND UNIVERSE** to export the universe to the IQM platform.

## Manage an imported L2 audience

You can manage an imported L2 audience in the same way that you’d manage a standard Segmented audience.

Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) for step-by-step instructions on locating and managing your audience.

## Assign an imported L2 audience to a campaign

You can add an L2 audience to new or existing campaigns, and from the Audiences or Campaigns apps. The steps you’ll take to complete these processes are the same as a standard Segmented audience.

Refer to [Assign an audience to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions on assigning an L2 audience—or any audience type—to a campaign.

When bid requests pass through the IQM platform, it assesses which campaigns should proceed to auction. This decision is based on whether the campaign’s targeting criteria and other details match the bid request.

A bid request passes through 11 categories, or **Campaign drop-off reasons**, before we can match it to your campaign and allow it to place a bid in the programmatic auction. # Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report

## Campaign Bidding Insights report overview

The Campaign Bidding Insights report captures each time that a campaign was rejected, then segments those occurrences into specific rejection reasons. You can use this data to assess which targeting parameters are limiting a campaign’s number of bid requests, then apply strategic optimizations to increase scale.

You can generate Campaign Bidding Insights for campaigns that meet certain eligibility criteria. Refer to [Campaign Bidding Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview) for more information.

## Video tutorial: Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report

## Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report

You can generate Campaign Bidding Insights for one campaign at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

### Generate a report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to review Campaign Bidding Insights from the Insights app:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Select **Campaign Bidding Insights.**
3. Choose whether the desired campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu.
4. Search and select the campaign for which you want to generate insights.
   1. Search for the campaign’s name or ID, or the insertion order’s (IO) name or ID.
   2. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Campaign** field when it’s [eligible for Campaign Bidding Insights report generation](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview#h_3952d00349), and its status matches the **Campaign Status** you chose in step 3.
5. Select a time frame from the **Calendar** field.
   1. Choose a time frame ranging from the past one hour up to the past two weeks.
   2. The **Calendar** field uses the same time zone as the location where the campaign was created.

Campaign Bidding Insights will generate automatically once you complete the **Campaign Status**, **Campaign**, and **Calendar** fields.

### Generate a report from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to Campaign Bidding Insights report creation from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to generate insights.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Click **View Bidding Insights** from the **More** dropdown menu.
   1. If the **View Bidding Insights** option is disabled, make sure you’ve selected only one campaign and that it’s [eligible for Campaign Bidding Insights reporting](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview#h_3952d00349).
5. You’ll be redirected to the **Campaign Bidding Insights** page of the Insights app, where the campaign’s name and status will be auto-populated.
6. Follow step 5 of the Generate a report from the Insights app workflow to generate the report.

### Generate a report from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to Campaign Bidding Insights report creation from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter or search the dashboard to locate the desired campaign.
3. Click the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Select **View Bidding Insights** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Campaign Bidding Insights** page of the Insights app, and auto-populate the **Campaign Status** and **Campaign** fields.
   1. If the **View Bidding Insights** option is disabled, make sure you’ve selected only one campaign and that it’s [eligible for Campaign Bidding Insights reporting](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview#h_3952d00349).
5. Follow step 5 of the Generate a report from the Insights app workflow to generate the report.

## Interpret Campaign Bidding Insights

### Campaign drop-off reason considerations

When bid requests pass through the IQM platform, it assesses which campaigns should proceed to auction. This decision is based on whether the campaign’s targeting criteria and other details match the bid request.

A bid request passes through 11 categories, or **Campaign drop-off reasons**, before we can match it to your campaign and allow it to place a bid in the programmatic auction. Refer to [Bid rejection reasons](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview#h_aec4b363ee) for a list of these 11 categories and the subcategories that are associated with them.

The **Campaign Bidding Insights** page lists all 11 categories, regardless of whether they contributed to bid drop-offs. The values listed for each category will differ based on actual performance. For example, if the campaign doesn’t have any device targeting rules applied to it, the **Device Targeting** campaign drop-off reason will continue to appear in the Campaign Bidding Insights. We’ll display **0** to let you know that it didn’t impact the campaign’s number of bid requests.

Refer to the listed percentage and **Rejected** figures to determine a particular category’s impact on rejections.

The drop-off funnel also lists the 11 rejection categories in the same order each time, regardless of how many rejections occurred in each category. Refer to the **Top Rejection Reasons** and **Top Rejection Sub Reasons** sections for an ordered list that’s sorted by bid request drop-off counts. Click any reason or sub reason to view the Campaign Bidding Insights associated with it.

### Numbers and percentages

The charts and figures included in the Campaign Bidding Insights report represent:

- how a particular targeting parameter caused bid requests to drop off for a campaign
- how many bid requests remained and passed through each subsequent stage

Refer to the example below for a walkthrough of a generated Campaign Bidding Insights report.

> **Campaign drop-off notice:** The drop-off counts listed in this example are for illustrative purposes only. Drop-offs vary based on an individual campaign’s targeting rules, the current bid stream environment, and the selected timeframe for the insights. Refer to your specific campaign’s Campaign Bidding Insights for details on each targeting parameter’s impact on it.

**Example:**

1. The campaign saw **1B** available bid requests before any targeting parameters caused bid rejections.
2. **Campaign Settings** caused the bidder to reject about 980M requests, meaning the campaign didn’t bid on them in the programmatic auction.
3. In particular, the **Schedule** you defined to determine which time and day your ads will display caused bids to drop off.
4. The 980M rejected requests represent about **98%** of the total available bid requests at this stage of the funnel (**98% of 1B = 980M**).
5. **2%** of the **1B** available bid requests remained, and passed to the next stage.
6. The campaign was left with **20M** available bid requests.
7. **IO Budget** caused the bidder to reject about 2M requests.
8. The 2M requests represent about **10%** of the total available bid requests at this stage of the funnel (**10% of 20M = 2M)**.
9. **90%** of the remaining **20M** bid requests remained, and passed to the next stage.
10. The campaign was left with **18M** available bid requests.
11. **Inventory Targeting** caused the bidder to reject about **14.4M** of these requests.
12. The 14.4M requests represent about **80.50%** of this funnel stage’s ~18M available bid requests (**80.50% of 18M = 14.4M**).
13. **19.50%** of the remaining **18M** bid requests remained, and passed to the next stage.
14. The campaign was left with **3.6M** available bid requests.

This Campaign Bidding Insights report continued on to list each of the remaining **Campaign drop-off reasons** categories in order, along with any applicable **Sub Reasons**, drop-off counts, numbers, and percentages.

1. Following the complete list of rejection categories and their corresponding figures, you’re left with **Successful Bids** toward the bottom of the funnel.
2. In this campaign and during the selected timeframe, **1.58K** bids were placed in programmatic auctions.
3. **1.26K** bids lost in the auctions.
4. The 1.26K lost bids represent about **80%** of the total 1.58K bids that were placed.
5. 350 placed bids won at auction.
6. The 350 placed bids represent about **20%** of the total 1.58K bids that were placed.

## Apply Campaign Bidding Insights to a campaign

> **Editable campaign notice:** Campaigns featuring a **Running** or **Paused** status can be edited from the **Campaign Bidding Insights** page.

Select **Edit** at the top of the report. We’ll redirect you to the campaign’s details in the **Campaigns** app, where you can apply and save changes.

We recommend adjusting the campaign’s targeting rules based on the order they appear in the **Top Rejection Reasons** and **Top Rejection Sub Reasons** sections. Approach these lists with a waterfall method: if the factor causing the highest drop-off counts must remain unchanged, then move onto the next and determine what changes, if any, you should apply to the campaign.

Return to the **Campaign Bidding Insights** page and generate another report to assess the impact of your changes on bid requests. Campaign Bidding Insights data refreshes on an hourly basis.

title: Planner proposal overview

blocks.text: When defining your ad strategy, it’s critical to craft a plan that meets your client’s requirements while achieving campaign goals and objectives. Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions once those parameters are layered onto your campaigns. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full–all without allocating resources to test-and-learn campaigns.

Your proposals will automatically sync with campaign management tools. This means you can easily transition from planning to execution once you gain client buy-in. Simply convert a proposal to campaigns in one click, add your creatives, and launch the campaigns.
You’ll define the name, dates, and creative type(s) for each proposal. You can also apply targeting parameters, if applicable, across five optional categories:
**Location:** Choose one or more states, DMAs, counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses.

**Audience:** Add segmented audiences from IQM or any of our data providers. These audiences are made up of groups of users who share common characteristics like age, gender, or home ownership status, for example.
**Device:** Select one or more device types (TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile) or channels (app, web, connected TV [CTV], or over the top [OTT]).

**Inventory:** Choose Open Exchange inventory, or choose an existing [Open Exchange inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_64b8b6de94) or [Connected TV (CTV) inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_c7fa0236ff) that you previously created in the **Inventory** app. If you select Open Exchange inventory, you can add IAB categories and/or specific exchanges.

**Advanced:** Segment the proposal’s campaigns by one or more of the targeting rules that you add to the proposal. For example, if you choose location and audience targeting, you can segment the campaigns by **Locations**, **Audiences**, or both.
A single proposal may contain up to 250 campaigns. Refer to the table below for a list of the elements that are generated for each campaign, and which ones you can update.

**Impact of editing element***

cleaned_markdown:
# Planner proposal overview

## Proposal overview

When defining your ad strategy, it’s critical to craft a plan that meets your client’s requirements while achieving campaign goals and objectives. Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions once those parameters are layered onto your campaigns. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full–all without allocating resources to test-and-learn campaigns.

Your proposals will automatically sync with campaign management tools. This means you can easily transition from planning to execution once you gain client buy-in. Simply convert a proposal to campaigns in one click, add your creatives, and launch the campaigns.

## Proposal inputs

You’ll define the name, dates, and creative type(s) for each proposal. You can also apply targeting parameters, if applicable, across five optional categories:

1. **Location:** Choose one or more states, DMAs, counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses.
2. **Audience:** Add segmented audiences from IQM or any of our data providers. These audiences are made up of groups of users who share common characteristics like age, gender, or home ownership status, for example.
3. **Device:** Select one or more device types (TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile) or channels (app, web, connected TV [CTV], or over the top [OTT]).
4. **Inventory:** Choose Open Exchange inventory, or choose an existing [Open Exchange inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_64b8b6de94) or [Connected TV (CTV) inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_c7fa0236ff) that you previously created in the **Inventory** app. If you select Open Exchange inventory, you can add IAB categories and/or specific exchanges.
5. **Advanced:** Segment the proposal’s campaigns by one or more of the targeting rules that you add to the proposal. For example, if you choose location and audience targeting, you can segment the campaigns by **Locations**, **Audiences**, or both.

## Proposal outputs

### Campaigns

A single proposal may contain up to 250 campaigns. Refer to the table below for a list of the elements that are generated for each campaign, and which ones you can update.

| **Campaign element** | **Is the element editable?** | **Impact of editing element*** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Campaign name** | Yes | - |
| **Start date*** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Daily Frequency Cap**, **Impressions**, and **Budget** fields regenerate |
| **End date*** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Daily Frequency Cap**, **Impressions**, and **Budget** fields regenerate |
| **Strategy** | No | - |
| **Creative** | No | - |
| **Duration** | No | - |
| **Model** | No | - |
| **Reach** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Impressions** and **Budget** fields regenerate; full media plan's **Total Budget** field regenerates |
| **Daily Frequency Cap** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Impressions** and **Budget** fields regenerate; full media plan's **Total Budget** field regenerates |
| **Impressions** | Yes | Full media plan's **Total Budget** field regenerates |
| **CPM** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Budget** field regenerates |
| **Budget** | Yes | Individual campaign’s **Impressions** field regenerates; full media plan's **Total Budget** field regenerates |

*Changing an editable campaign value impacts other fields or, in certain cases, the entire proposal. This column describes which values will change when you update an editable field in a generated proposal.

### Forecasts

In addition to customized campaigns, Planner proposals return forecasting metrics that help you evaluate the potential reach of your campaigns before launching them. You can review these estimates while you build the proposal and after you create it.

> **Forecasting notice:** Provided forecasts represent estimates and are based on the last seven days of data across the IQM bid landscape. The bid landscape is variable based on changes in available impressions, market seasonality, and other dynamic factors.

| **Forecasting metric** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Reach** | Listed metric | The estimated number of individual users who can be exposed to an ad while the campaign is active and has available budget. |
| **Impressions** | Listed metric | The estimated number of times the ad will be served to the audience. |
| **Total budget** | Listed metric | The estimated total dollar amount that the proposal’s campaign can spend, which is calculated by using a formula of (impressions/1,000)*CPM. |
| **Bid landscape** | Interactive graph | A visualization of how different bid prices (CPM) might impact the potential number of impressions that you can win. This data is segmented based on the creative formats that you choose for the proposal. |
| **Device** | Interactive graph | The estimated percentage of impressions that will come from each device that the proposal’s campaigns are targeting. |
| **Channel** | Interactive graph | The estimated percentage of impressions that will come from each channel that the proposal’s campaigns are targeting. |

Refer to Key terms and concepts for more information on how your targeting parameters can impact a campaign’s ability to scale and spend.

## Proposal statuses

You can review a proposal’s current status on the **Proposals** page of the **Planner** app.

| **Status*** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Draft** | You started building a proposal, but haven’t selected **Generate Campaigns** to begin processing it. |
| **Ready** | The proposal is generated, and its forecasting metrics and campaigns are ready for your review. |
| **Processing** | You selected **Generate Campaigns**, and we’re creating your proposal’s campaigns. |
| **Converted** | You selected **Generate Campaigns**, and the campaigns were created. Now you can manage and launch them. |
| **Expired** | A proposal that featured a **Ready** or **Failed** status reached the end date that you specified in the proposal. Refer to [Restore an expired proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal#h_6c067353c0) for support. |
| **Failed** | You selected **Generate Campaigns**, and we were unable to create your proposal’s campaigns. Refer to [Troubleshoot a Planner proposal or campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111124-troubleshoot-a-planner-proposal-or-campaign) for support. |

* If a proposal fails to generate after you select **Generate Proposal**, we’ll notify you and revert its status to **Draft**.

## Key terms and concepts

### IQM universe

The IQM universe refers to the total targetable audience that you can reach when you use the IQM platform to buy digital ad inventory. This universe changes based on your campaign’s targeting criteria, and narrows each time you layer on additional targets and blocks. The addressable audience you’re left with after you apply this criteria is represented by your proposal’s targeted reach and impressions.

Forecasting metrics provide a sense of scale to help you determine whether you have the right strategies in place to spend your campaign budget in full and achieve campaign objectives. If a proposal’s scale isn't what you were anticipating, or if potential spend is less than your actual budget, then you have the opportunity to make adjustments to your strategies before you launch a live campaign.

Adjust your targeting criteria to reach more of the IQM universe and achieve scale. If the targets you applied are nonnegotiable from your client, consider thinking about the strategies you may need to add to the campaigns to fulfill your budget.

## Locate additional Planner proposal resources

- [Create or manage a proposal with Planner](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal)
- [Generate campaigns from a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104871-generate-a-campaign-from-a-planner-proposal)
- [Troubleshoot a Planner proposal or campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111124-troubleshoot-a-planner-proposal-or-campaign)

title: Create or manage a Planner proposal

blocks.text: Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions once you layer targeting parameters onto your campaigns. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full–all without spending resources on test-and-learn campaigns.
Visit [Planner proposal overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104696-planner-proposal-overview) to learn more about Planner proposals, or refer to the instructions below to create one.
You can create a new proposal from the **Planner** app.
Select the **Planner** app from the homepage.
Click **+ Create Proposal**. This will open the **New Proposal** page.
Complete the following sections to create the proposal:
Proposal Information - Required
Location- Optional
Audience - Optional
Creatives - Required
Device - Optional
Inventory - Optional
Advanced - Optional

In addition to customized campaigns, Planner proposals return forecasting metrics that help you evaluate the potential reach of your campaigns before launching them. You can review these estimates while you build the proposal and after you create it.

We recommend selecting **Refresh** in the **Proposal Summary** panel after you complete each applicable section of your proposal. The result will give you a better understanding of how each targeting parameter will impact your proposal’s ability to scale.
Refer to [Forecasts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104696-planner-proposal-overview#h_f56d612c1b) for more information on each of the **Proposal Summary** panel’s forecasting metrics.
Type a name into the **Proposal Name** field.
Choose a unique name to differentiate this proposal from others that you may create. For example, “Sports Enthusiasts Q4 2024.”
Use the **Start Date** and **End Date** fields to select a date range for the proposal.
Click the **This proposal is for a political campaign**, if applicable.
Open the **Political Advertiser** dropdown menu to search and select the correct advertising organization. This field will only appear when **This proposal is for a political campaign** is selected.
You’ll need to create a profile for the political advertiser if its name isn’t shown in the list. Follow these steps to complete the process:
Open the **Organization** app from the IQM homepage.
Selecting the **Profile** tab.
Click **Advertiser Profile Settings**.
Select **+** **Add New**.
Planner proposals support location targeting within the United States. Follow these steps to add location-targeting parameters to a proposal:
Select the **Search Locations** field.
Type or browse and select the location by **State**, **DMA**, **Country**, **City**, **Congressional District**, **State Senate**, or **State House**.
Filter the location results by any of these categories, if desired.
Select the **Zip Codes** tab to search and select locations by ZIP code.
Review your selections in the **List of Targeted Locations** panel.

**More on location targeting:** Planner proposals apply an “OR” relationship to your location targeting selections. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re located in any of the locations you chose, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

blocks.text: Planner proposals use segmented audiences. Segmented audiences are made up of groups of users who share common characteristics like age, gender, or home ownership status, for example.
Follow these steps to add a segmented audience to a proposal:
Select the search field.
Type or browse and select a data provider.
Separate terms by a comma to search for multiple ones simultaneously.
Select the funnel icon to filter the results by dimensions such as **Vertical** or **Source**.
You can target audience segments from one data provider per proposal.
Select up to 100 audience segments.
Review segment-level reach and pricing details.
You’ll pay the CPM of the highest priced segment that you selected.
There's no cost associated with adding data segments to a proposal. The listed CPM price will apply, however, once you generate the proposal’s campaigns and they begin spending.
Sort the selected audience segments **By Reach** or **By Price**, or filter by audience elements such as **Vertical** or **Source**, if desired.
Select **Remove all** to remove all audience segments from the proposal, or click the trashcan next to individual audience segments to remove them, if desired.

The new segmented audience will generate automatically when you select **Generate Proposal** at the end of the proposal creation process. You’ll be able to manage it in the **Segmented Audience** section of the **Audiences** app and add it to future campaigns. Easily locate the new audience by referring to the audience’s name, which will feature the proposal ID.

**More on audience targeting:** Planner proposals apply an “OR” relationship to your audience targeting selections. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the data segments you chose, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

blocks.text: Choose one or more creative formats from the **Select Creative Type** list. If you plan to run on connected TV (CTV) or over-the-top (OTT) devices, select both the **Video** tile and **TV-Ad Buying** toggle.

blocks.text: Use the **Inventory** category to target Open Exchange inventory and/or inventory groups:
**Open Exchange inventory:** Public inventory sources made available via real-time bidding auctions.

**Inventory groups:** The eligible Open Exchange or Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups previously created in the Inventory app. Note that Open Exchange and CTV inventory groups created purely for blocking and groups with zero or unknown Reach are not eligible. Private Marketplace (PMP), Programmatic Guaranteed (PG), and Contextual inventory groups also aren’t eligible at any time.
Follow these steps to add Open Exchange inventory targeting to a proposal:
Select **Open Exchange**.
Choose whether to target one or more of the IAB Tech Lab’s page content categories, individual exchanges, or both.
To target IAB Categories, select the **IAB Categories** dropdown menu.
Search or browse and select all desired categories.
To target exchanges, click the **Select Exchange** field.
Search or browse and select exchanges.

You’ll need to create an inventory group in the Inventory app before you can add it to your proposal. Otherwise, use the **Open Exchange** option to make individual selections directly in the proposal. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information, and keep in mind that only the Open Exchange and Connected TV (CTV) inventory group type is supported in Planner proposals.
Follow these steps to add inventory group targeting to a proposal:
Select **Inventory Groups**.
Search or browse the list of Open Exchange and Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups.
If desired, filter the groups by group type.
Review key details about each inventory group:
**Icons:** A circle icon next to the group name represents that the group is an Open Exchange inventory group, while the internet-connected TV icon represents that it’s a CTV inventory group.
**Creative Type:** All supported creative format types are listed next to each inventory group’s name.
**Count:** The total number of ad placements (**Inventories** or **Apps**) that match the search criteria you applied when you created the inventory group.
**Device Breakdown:** The breakout of devices for each inventory group.
Click the checkbox(es) next to the inventory group(s) you wish to target.
You can segment your campaigns by **Location**, **Audience**, **Device Type**, or **Inventory** if you made selections within any of these proposal categories.
Click the checkbox next to a targeting dimension to segment your campaigns by it.
Open any drop-down menus that appear below a segment category to make your campaigns even more targeted, if desired.

For example, if you choose the **TV** and **Tablet** in the **Devices** section, you can use the **Advanced** section to segment your campaigns by **Device Type**, or by the individual **TV** or **Tablet** devices.
Review the number of campaigns that your proposal will include.
The more detailed you make your selections, the more campaigns we’ll include in your generated proposal.
One proposal can include up to 250 campaigns.
Select **Save As Draft** at any time to save your progress. Refer to Manage a proposal (media plan) for steps on how to access and update an existing proposal draft.
Follow these steps after you’ve completed all mandatory and other applicable sections of the proposal:
Locate the **Proposal Summary** panel.
Select **Refresh** to update each forecast metric.
Review the proposal’s projections for each [forecasting metric](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104696-planner-proposal-overview#h_f56d612c1b).
Adjust any targeting parameters you added to the proposal, if desired, to increase your proposal’s ability to scale and spend.
Click **Generate Proposal** to submit your selections and create the proposal.

Review a proposal
Edit a proposal
Download a proposal
Duplicate a proposal
Delete a proposal
Restore an expired proposal
Edit a proposal’s campaigns
Delete a proposal’s campaigns

Applying changes to an existing proposal or its campaigns will impact forecasted figures such as reach and impressions. We recommend selecting **Refresh** in the **Proposal Summary** panel after you complete each change. Open the **Planner** app.
Locate the proposal on the **Proposals** page.

Click the proposal’s **Name** to open and review it.
