The Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report surfaces insights about users that political advertisers targeted in current or prior political campaigns. It includes data such as demographic, ad-exposure, and voting-history details.
VLD Insights cost represents the total amount spent on VLD Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM VLD rate and any percentage- or rate-based agency markups.
Refer to [VLD report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report-overview#h_b1578de93e) for more information on report pricing.

The Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report surfaces insights that validate your individual audiences’ and overall campaign’s patient reach. It includes [AQ Scores](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview#h_8fb9477bc1) that indicate to what extent your campaign and its individual audiences included qualified patient segments, and features detailed data across several dimensions for deeper healthcare campaign insights.
AQ Insights Cost represents the total amount spent on AQ Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM AQ rate and any percentage- or rate-based agency markups.
Refer to [AQ Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview#h_7055cddf96) for more information.

The Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights report surfaces key details about healthcare professionals that you targeted in current and prior campaigns. It uncovers ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your healthcare audiences. With these insights, you can compliantly assess and optimize your campaign’s targeting strategy while upholding stringent healthcare data-privacy regulations.
PLD Insights Cost represents the total amount spent on PLD Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM PLD rate and any agency markups.
Refer to [PLD Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview#h_0d91cd86da) for more information.

The NLD Insights report surfaces key details about nurses that you targeted in current and prior campaigns. It uncovers ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your Non-NPI Nurse healthcare audiences. With these insights, you can compliantly assess and optimize your campaign’s targeting strategy while upholding stringent healthcare data-privacy regulations.
NLD Insights Cost represents the total amount spent on NLD Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM NLD rate and any agency markups.
Refer to [NLD Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/14125106-nurse-level-data-nld-insights-report-overview#h_7282953ab8) for more information.

The ICT Insights report surfaces key details about targeted [ICT audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13943736-integrated-care-team-ict-audience-overview), including ad-exposure, engagement, demographic, and physician-specialty data, to reveal campaign reach and impact. ICT audiences expand reach beyond NPI lists to include relevant care-team cohorts, eliminating the need for manual audience creation. Reporting on these audiences helps validate campaign effectiveness in reaching the right healthcare professionals across channels.
ICT Insights Cost represents the total amount spent on ICT Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM ICT rate and any agency markups.
Refer to [ICT Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/14125991-integrated-care-team-ict-insights-report-overview#h_c9b3cf0a7a) for more information.

The Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report surfaces key details about prescribing behaviors and how they may be influenced by current and previous healthcare campaigns. It uncovers pre-and post-campaign comparison data, prescription trends (Rx, TRx) for exposed and unexposed NPIs, and Rx and TRx volumes for competitor brands over the same time period. With these insights, you can compliantly assess and optimize your campaigns’ targeting strategies.
SLS Insights Cost represents the total amount spent on SLS Insights report generation. This figure includes the sum of the IQM SLS rate and any agency markups.
Refer to [SLS Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_46a38ac648) for more information.

Total Spent represents the cost of a campaign. This metrics how much you paid to place the campaign’s ads after layering on all data targeting, media buying, and other costs associated with the campaign.
Advertisers typically assess this metric against the revenue earned from the campaign to review overall campaign performance and determine whether optimizations are needed.
Total CPM represents the cumulative cost per mille based on the various cost components you include in the campaign.
This value updates dynamically as you add parameters to your campaign that have costs associated with them. The breakdown of Total CPM includes the following metrics:
[Max Bid Price](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343824-budget-reporting-metrics-overview#h_b1d212d790): Applies when a Max Bid Price is defined for the campaign.
Data Cost: Applies when paid audience segments are included.
Pre-bid Cost: Applies when paid pre-bid segments are used.
3rd Party Cost: Applies to the Total CPM when an agency with Workspace-level permissions enables a 3rd Party Cost for your account.
Ad Serving Cost: Applies when a hosted creative is added.
Data Cost represents the campaign’s total spend on targeting and/or blocking data segments.

Data Cost reporting can help inform your audience targeting strategy to ensure spend aligns with your goals. For example, if your data cost is higher than expected, you might consider leveraging more first-party data in the campaign or creating lookalike audiences based on your most engaged and high-value users.
Pre-bid Cost represents the total amount paid for targeting pre-bid brand suitability, fraud, invalid traffic (IVT), viewability, or supply refinement segments.

Pre-bid targeting segments are priced on a CPM basis. These prices can vary depending on the segment category (fraud and IVT, brand suitability, viewability, supply refinement) and format (display, video). We list the price of each segment on the IQM platform, and update the total cost preview as you add each pre-bid segment to a Pre-bid audience.

Refer to [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information on how pricing works, and[Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) for instructions on how to locate specific pricing details.

3rd Party Cost represents costs incurred on behalf of the advertiser outside of the platform such as ad serving or tech fees. This cost allows agencies to pass these expenses back to the advertiser as an additional CPM price for all new and existing campaigns. The 3rd Party Cost applies only to the impressions served after the agency enabled it–no retroactive charges on previously delivered impressions are applied.
The 3rd Party Cost metric is calculated by dividing the impressions served by 1K, and multiplying the result by the 3rd Party Cost set by the agency.

Certain other metrics include 3rd Party Cost in their calculations. For example, the Total Advertiser Spent spending reporting metric, and the Total eCPM and Total eCPC [Cost reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343783-cost-reporting-metrics-overview), include 3rd Party Cost when applicable.
All campaigns subject to a 3rd Party Cost include the 3rd Party Cost line item in their Total CPM breakdown.

Ad Serving Cost represents the cost associated with serving the campaign(s)’ hosted creatives per thousand impressions. Since this cost only applies when a hosted creative is added, advertisers are not charged for [HTML](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview#h_e1e7270928) or [VAST](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview#h_07352a2af6) tags.
Media Spent represents the total amount spent on media delivery in a campaign.
**Workspace Spent notice:** Access to this metric is limited to agencies which run campaigns for multiple advertisers.

All campaigns subject to a 3rd Party Cost include the 3rd Party Cost line item in their Total CPM breakdown.

## Ad Serving Cost

Ad Serving Cost represents the cost associated with serving the campaign(s)’ hosted creatives per thousand impressions. Since this cost only applies when a hosted creative is added, advertisers are not charged for [HTML](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview#h_e1e7270928) or [VAST](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview#h_07352a2af6) tags.

## Media Spent

Media Spent represents the total amount spent on media delivery in a campaign.

## Workspace Spent

> **Workspace Spent notice:** Access to this metric is limited to agencies which run campaigns for multiple advertisers.

Workspace Spent represents the sum of the Total spent metric across all campaigns created under the workspace.

# Performance reporting metrics overview

## Performance reporting overview

Analyzing performance metrics together surfaces insights into both the breadth and effectiveness of a campaign. Review this data to adjust the campaign for improved reach, engagement, and overall return on investment (ROI).

You can review data and analytics related to seven performance metrics in the IQM platform:

- Impressions
- Reach
- Frequency
- Win rate
- Clicks
- Household Reach
- Household Frequency

## Impressions

Impressions represent the number of times the ad was displayed, regardless of whether a user clicked on it. Each Impression is measured when the ad server sends the ad to a webpage. This is known as a “served Impression.”

Whether you review Impressions details in the Campaigns, Dashboard, or Reports apps, the data will reflect the specific date range you select.

Impressions provide critical insight into potential exposure, but they aren’t a measure of user interest or engagement. Consider assessing your campaign’s Impressions compared to its Clicks to ensure the ad resonates with your campaign’s target audience. For example, if a campaign earned 10MM impressions but only 10 clicks, you may wish to optimize your creatives to earn an attributed click-through conversion rate higher than only .0001%.

## Reach

Reach represents the number of unique individuals who were exposed to your ad. Unlike impressions, this metric doesn’t count repeat views.

When you review Reach details in the Campaigns or Dashboard apps, the data will represent an aggregated (lifetime) value; however, when you [generate a custom report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) in the Reports app, the Reach will reflect the specific date range you select for the report.

The total targetable audience that you can reach changes based on your campaign’s targeting criteria. It narrows each time you layer on additional targets and blocks. The addressable audience you’re left with after you apply this criteria is represented by your campaign’s reach.

Certain campaign strategies are expected to have limited reach–particularly for highly regulated industries or premium products and services. But if your targeting parameters are flexible, you can use the reach metric to ensure you have the right strategies in place. Adjust your targeting criteria to reach more users, fulfill budget requirements, and achieve campaign objectives.

## Frequency

Frequency represents the average number of times each user was exposed to your ad. We arrive at this metric by dividing impressions by reach. While a higher frequency can indicate increased ad exposure, it also may suggest ad fatigue.

When you review Frequency details in the Campaigns or Dashboard apps, the data will represent an aggregated (lifetime) value. It’s calculated by dividing the campaign or insertion order’s aggregated (lifetime) Impressions by its aggregated (lifetime) Reach. However, when you [generate a custom report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) in the Reports app, the Frequency will reflect the specific date range you select for the report.

Together, impressions, reach and frequency highlight how broadly your ad is served and whether the campaign is striking the balance between new and repeat ad exposures.

## Win rate

Win rate represents the percent of auctions you participated in that resulted in a winning bid. This means the ad server sent the ad to a web page or app. This metric affects impressions, reach, and ultimately, campaign performance.

Higher win rates show that your bids are consistently competitive, but may also signal that you could be overpaying for ad placements. You can define a bid strategy for the campaign to optimize which impressions to prioritize and define how aggressively to bid.

## Clicks

Clicks represent the number of times a user clicked on the ad, which indicates engagement and interest in the advertised products or services, and overall ad appeal.

Refer to Impressions for details on gauging ad effectiveness by comparing overall impressions to clicks for your campaigns.

## Household Reach

> **Metric availability notice:** Household Reach is supported in the Reports app, and is currently available only for campaigns targeting Matched audiences.

Household Reach represents the number of unique households reached by a campaign. A household is identified by a shared IP address or a device-graph connection. In other words, Household Reach describes the number of distinct household IDs identified across all served impressions.

Political Matched audiences also display an audience-level Household Reach metric, which is calculated differently. Refer to [Matched audience overview - Household Reach (Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf) for more information.

Refer to [Household Reach overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15656937-household-reach-overview) for more information.

## Household Frequency

> **Metric availability notice:** Household Frequency is supported in the Reports app, and is currently available only for campaigns targeting Matched audiences.

Household Frequency represents the average number of times a unique household was shown an ad. This metric is calculated by dividing the campaign’s Impressions by its Household Reach.

## Locate additional reporting resources

- [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report)
- [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report)

blocks.text: Budget metrics are essential for allocating resources effectively based on actual campaign performance. Use these metrics in combination with other report insights to understand whether elements are supporting or hindering performance. For example, you can assess whether a max bid price is impacting your ability to spend the campaign’s budget in full and reach the intended audience.
You can review data and analytics related to seven budget metrics in the IQM platform:
Insertion order (IO) budget
Daily budget
Total budget
Max bid price
Min bid price
Budget completion
Bid shading savings

Note that each metric in the **Budget** category will only appear after certain dimensions are added to the report. Refer to [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report) for more details on these conditional fields.

The IO budget represents the total monetary value or impression amount that can be reached before the campaign must stop spending. The choice between the two depends on the campaign’s goals, budgeting preferences, and desired outcomes, and the budget type was defined during initial IO setup. Refer to [What is a budget vs. impression-based IO?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-what-is-a-budget-vs-impression-based-io) for more information.

Advertisers can define daily spending limits to manage pacing for a campaign. Daily budget represents the maximum amount that the campaign can spend per day including any applicable data, media, and pre-bid expenses.

Daily budget metrics can display as a monetary value or impression value depending on whether a budget-based or impression-based budget was defined for the campaign. Budget-based campaigns run until the designated budget is spent, with options to regulate spending on a daily, weekly, or overall basis. Impression-based budgets include a target number of impressions per day. The campaign can continue to spend until that impression count is reached.

Total budget represents the full amount that the campaign can spend in total including any applicable data, media, and pre-bid expenses. You can set this budget at the campaign level, or distribute a single total budget across multiple campaigns.

Total budget metrics can display as a monetary value or impression value depending on whether a budget-based or impression-based budget was defined for the campaign. Budget-based campaigns run until the designated budget is spent, with options to regulate spending on a daily, weekly, or overall basis. Impression-based budgets include a target number of impressions. The campaign can continue to spend until that impression count is reached.

Max bid price represents the highest bid amount that we can place for your ad at auction. You specify this amount during campaign setup, or adjust it while the campaign is running. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.

Min Bid Price represents the lowest bid amount that we can place for your ad at auction. You specify this amount during campaign setup, or adjust it while the campaign is running. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.
Budget completion represents the percentage of the total budget that the campaign spent. A campaign will stop spending when its end date is reached or its budget is depleted (100% budget completion).

We recommend using budget completion in combination with the **Dashboard** app’s **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** reporting columns to assess whether your campaign is on track to spend its full budget by its end date. Refer to [A guide to IO pacing, campaign pacing, and daily pacing in IQM’s platform](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform)for more information.

Advertisers didn’t need to worry about overpaying for ad placements when second-price auctions were the norm. In first-price auction environments, however, you’ll pay the amount you bid if it wins—regardless of the next-highest bid. For example, if your bid won at $4, and the next-highest bid was $2, you would still pay $4. This can lead to inefficient bidding and increased costs, making paying the right price more important than ever.

With bid shading, we’ll lower your bid when you can win the auction for a lower price than the max bid you specified for the campaign. We enable bid shading by default across all campaigns to help you bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying.

Bid shading savings represents the costs saved through using bid shading on the campaigns that served ads in first-party auctions. For example, if you set a max bid of $10 but bid shading allowed you to win at $9.30, you’ll see a bid shading savings of $0.70 in the **Reports** app for this campaign. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.

# Budget reporting metrics overview

## Budget reporting overview

Budget metrics are essential for allocating resources effectively based on actual campaign performance. Use these metrics in combination with other report insights to understand whether elements are supporting or hindering performance. For example, you can assess whether a max bid price is impacting your ability to spend the campaign’s budget in full and reach the intended audience.

You can review data and analytics related to seven budget metrics in the IQM platform:

- Insertion order (IO) budget
- Daily budget
- Total budget
- Max bid price
- Min bid price
- Budget completion
- Bid shading savings

Note that each metric in the **Budget** category will only appear after certain dimensions are added to the report. Refer to [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report) for more details on these conditional fields.

## Insertion order (IO) budget ($, #)

The IO budget represents the total monetary value or impression amount that can be reached before the campaign must stop spending. The choice between the two depends on the campaign’s goals, budgeting preferences, and desired outcomes, and the budget type was defined during initial IO setup. Refer to [What is a budget vs. impression-based IO?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-what-is-a-budget-vs-impression-based-io) for more information.

## Daily budget ($, #)

Advertisers can define daily spending limits to manage pacing for a campaign. Daily budget represents the maximum amount that the campaign can spend per day including any applicable data, media, and pre-bid expenses.

Daily budget metrics can display as a monetary value or impression value depending on whether a budget-based or impression-based budget was defined for the campaign. Budget-based campaigns run until the designated budget is spent, with options to regulate spending on a daily, weekly, or overall basis. Impression-based budgets include a target number of impressions per day. The campaign can continue to spend until that impression count is reached.

## Total budget ($, #)

Total budget represents the full amount that the campaign can spend in total including any applicable data, media, and pre-bid expenses. You can set this budget at the campaign level, or distribute a single total budget across multiple campaigns.

Total budget metrics can display as a monetary value or impression value depending on whether a budget-based or impression-based budget was defined for the campaign. Budget-based campaigns run until the designated budget is spent, with options to regulate spending on a daily, weekly, or overall basis. Impression-based budgets include a target number of impressions. The campaign can continue to spend until that impression count is reached.

## Max bid price ($)

Max bid price represents the highest bid amount that we can place for your ad at auction. You specify this amount during campaign setup, or adjust it while the campaign is running. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.

## Min bid price ($)

Min Bid Price represents the lowest bid amount that we can place for your ad at auction. You specify this amount during campaign setup, or adjust it while the campaign is running. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.

## Budget completion (%)

Budget completion represents the percentage of the total budget that the campaign spent. A campaign will stop spending when its end date is reached or its budget is depleted (100% budget completion).

We recommend using budget completion in combination with the **Dashboard** app’s **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** reporting columns to assess whether your campaign is on track to spend its full budget by its end date. Refer to [A guide to IO pacing, campaign pacing, and daily pacing in IQM’s platform](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform)for more information.

## Bid shading savings ($)

Advertisers didn’t need to worry about overpaying for ad placements when second-price auctions were the norm. In first-price auction environments, however, you’ll pay the amount you bid if it wins—regardless of the next-highest bid. For example, if your bid won at $4, and the next-highest bid was $2, you would still pay $4. This can lead to inefficient bidding and increased costs, making paying the right price more important than ever.

With bid shading, we’ll lower your bid when you can win the auction for a lower price than the max bid you specified for the campaign. We enable bid shading by default across all campaigns to help you bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying.

Bid shading savings represents the costs saved through using bid shading on the campaigns that served ads in first-party auctions. For example, if you set a max bid of $10 but bid shading allowed you to win at $9.30, you’ll see a bid shading savings of $0.70 in the **Reports** app for this campaign. This metric is calculated on a CPM basis.

## Locate additional reporting resources

- [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview)
- [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report)
- [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report)

# Reporting dimensions overview

## Reporting dimensions overview

Dimensions are the subject that a report’s numeric values (metrics) relate to. These attributes are listed as individual rows in the report and are used to segment the data. For example, you might create a report to assess the number of Impressions (metric) related to a particular Congressional District location (dimension).

You can segment data and analytics by eight dimension categories in the IQM platform:

- Insertion Order Specifics
- Campaign Specifics
- Creative Specifics
- Audience Specifics
- Demographics
- Technologies
- Deliveries
- Locations

Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) for more information on how to filter a report by these dimensions.

## Available reporting dimension categories

### Insertion Order Specifics dimension

Insertion Order Specifics allow you to review campaign metrics by IO elements such as the specific IO or the dates it was running.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Insertion Order | The name of the insertion order. |
| Insertion Order ID | The ID of the insertion order, which was generated automatically. |
| Insertion Order Start Date | The first date that the insertion order served an impression. |
| Insertion Order End Date | The last date that the insertion order was permitted to serve an impression. The actual final date may differ depending on budget availability and other factors. |

### Campaign Specifics dimension

Campaign Specifics allow you to review campaign metrics by campaign elements such as the specific campaign, the dates it was running, or the days and hours it was scheduled to serve impressions.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Campaign | The name of the campaign. |
| Campaign Type | “PG” for Programmatic Guaranteed, or “Advanced” for all other campaign types. |
| Campaign ID | The ID of the campaign, which was generated automatically. |
| Campaign Start Date | The first date that the campaign served an impression. |
| Campaign End Date | The last date that the campaign was permitted to serve an impression. The actual final date may differ depending on budget availability and other factors. |
| Campaign Status | The state of the campaign, whether Draft, Pending, Running, Paused, Expired, Deleted, or Rejected. |
| Campaign Budget Type | The type of budget that is defined for the campaign, whether budget based (monetary) or impression based. |
| Hour | The hour(s) you chose to allow the ads to display when you used the campaign **Scheduling** feature. |
| Day | The day(s) you chose to allow the ads to display when you used the campaign **Scheduling** feature. |

### Creative Specifics dimension

Creative Specifics allow you to review campaign metrics by creative elements such as player size and whether an ad was skippable or non-skippable. Apply these insights to ensure your campaigns serve the creatives and related settings that drive the best performance.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Creative | The name of the creative. |
| Creative ID | The ID of the creative, which was generated automatically. |
| Creative Type | The format of the creatives that your campaign served, including “Image,” “HTML,” “Video,” “Audio,” or “Native.” |
| Creative Group | Two or more creatives of the same **Creative Type** that you grouped together and added to the campaign. |
| Playback Method | The audio settings of the creative, whether “Sound On,” “Mute,” or “Unknown.” |
| Player Size | The dimensions of the video player, which represent the maximum space available for showing the ad. |
| Placement Type | The location of the creative, whether “In-Stream,” “Out-Stream,” or “Unknown.” |
| Roll Position | The position of a video ad that determined when the ad played while the user viewed the content. Roll position can include “Pre-roll,” “Mid-roll,” or “Post-roll” to indicate that the video played before, during, or after the video content, respectively. |
| Skippability | The video player’s ad settings that defined whether the ad could or could not be skipped by the user. |
| Click URL | The string of HTML code that loaded when a user clicked on the ad. This custom tracking solution records the number of times a user clicked on the ad, and allows you to complete post-click attribution based on a conversion time frame that you define. |

### Audience Specifics dimension

> **Beta notice:** Access to certain Audience Specifics dimensions are currently limited to users participating in a closed, invitation-only beta testing program. General availability for these dimensions is coming soon.

Audience Specifics allow you to analyze performance by individual audience elements such as the Audience Type.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Audience | The name of the audience. |
| Audience ID | The ID of the audience, which was generated automatically. |
| Audience Type | The category of the audience (Matched, Segmented, Retargeted, Geofarmed, Contextual, Lookalike, Campaign, or Account Based Marketing). |
| GF-SubType (*Beta*) | The Geofarmed audience details (e.g., Polygon, Circle, Rectangle, State, City, ZIP Code, Address.) |
| Contextual-SubType (*Beta*) | The Contextual audience details (e.g., Keyword, URL.) |
| Segmented-Segment Name (*Beta*) | The name of the data segment included in the Segmented audience. |
| Segmented-Partner (*Beta*) | The category umbrella that contains the data segment (e.g., IQM Healthcare). |
| Segmented-Provider (*Beta*) | The specific provider of the data segment (e.g., Data360, IQVIA, HLD, etc.) |
| Segmented-CPM (*Beta*) | The CPM that’s associated with the Segmented audience. |

### Demographics dimension

Demographics allow you to review campaign metrics by specific audience details. Ensure your ads are reaching the right audience, or discover which audience is most likely to convert to optimize to that group of users.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Age Group | The user’s age range (e.g., “25-34,” “65+”) or “Unknown.” |
| Gender | “Male,” “Female,” or “Unknown” based on a user’s legal sex. |
| Ethnicity | The group that the user identifies with based on factors such as culture or language, which include “European,” “Hispanic,” “African-American,” “Asian,” “Other,” and “Unknown.” |
| Language | The user’s language. |
| Income Range | The range of money that the user earns on an annual basis in US dollars. |

### Technologies dimension

Technologies allow you to review campaign metrics by specific device, company, and connection details. Apply these insights to optimize the campaign’s performance. You may find that a campaign’s target audience is more likely to convert on a specific device or operating system, for example.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Device Type | The devices (TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile) that your ads were served on. |
| Manufacturer | The company that created the devices that your ads were served on. |
| Carrier | The company that provided the cellular data necessary for the ad to serve over SMS, phone calls, or internet access. |
| Connection Type | The type of internet connection that was used to serve the ad, whether “Broadband,” “Cellular,” or “Unknown.” |
| Operating System (OS) | The OS that the user was connected to when they were served the ad. Examples include Microsoft Windows, Apple iOs, Nintendo Wii, and Playstation 4 OS. |

### Deliveries dimension

Deliveries allow you to review campaign metrics by specific inventory elements. Check which deals, channels, and exchanges are driving the best performance for a particular ad, and apply any desired changes to current and future campaigns.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Channel | The channels (app, web, connected TV [CTV], or over the top [OTT]) that your ads were served on. |
| Site | The sites that the campaign targeted. |
| Site ID | The IDs of the sites that the campaign targeted. |
| App | The apps that the campaign targeted. |
| App ID | The IDs of the apps that the campaign targeted. |
| Site & App | The sites and apps that the campaign targeted. |
| Site & App ID | The IDs of the sites and apps that the campaign targeted. |
| Publisher | The entity that owned the ad space on which the ad was displayed. |
| Exchange | The tech platform that made the buying and selling of ad inventory across ad networks possible. Examples include PubMatic, OpenX, and Index Exchange. |
| Deal | The names of the inventory deals that the campaign targeted. |
| Deal ID | The ID of the deal, which was provided by the publisher to help ensure that any pre-arranged terms were met. |
| Deal Type | The type of inventory deal that the campaign targeted such as Private Marketplace (PMP), Open Exchange, Programmatic Guaranteed (PG), or Contextual. |

### Locations dimension

Locations allow you to review campaign metrics by specific geographic regions that you targeted. Certain location details are for informational purposes; for example, if a campaign is meant to reach voters, residents, or businesses in a particular legislative district, you might not adjust your location targeting after reviewing related insights. You might apply location insights for non-political ad campaigns, however, to narrow in on your highest-value users.

| **Dimension name** | **Dimension description** |
| --- | --- |
| Country | The countries that the campaign targeted. |
| State | The states that the campaign targeted. |
| City | The cities that the campaign targeted. |
| County | The counties that the campaign targeted. |
| ZIP Code | The ZIP codes that the campaign targeted. |
| Congressional District | The Congressional District that the campaign targeted, which is the location from which a member of the U.S. House of Representatives is elected. |
| State Senate | The locations that the campaign targeted, which align with the boundaries of State Senate districts. |
| State House | The locations that the campaign targeted, which align with the boundaries of State House districts. |
| Designated Market Area (DMA) | The DMA that the campaign targeted, which is a region of the United States that Nielsen defined to measure local television viewership. |

## Locate additional reporting resources

- [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview)
- [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report)
- [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report)

# Generate, manage, or send a report

## Report overview

> **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing custom reports in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

The **Reports** app surfaces data and analytics that you can use to assess your campaigns’ performance. Apply these insights to make informed decisions about where to adjust budgets, refine targeting dimensions, optimize ad creatives, and more.

Refer to [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) for more information on the campaign metrics and dimensions that you can review in the **Reports** app.

## Video tutorials

### Generate a custom report

### Manage or send a custom report

## Generate a report

You can generate a custom report in the following ways:

- With Manual Mode
- With AI Assist

### Generate a report with Manual Mode

Open the Reports app, then follow these steps to manually create a new custom report:

1. Click **+ Create Report**. This will open the **Create New Report** page.
2. Select the **Manual Mode** tab.
3. Type a name into the **Report Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique name to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
4. Search or browse and select a timezone from the **Timezone** dropdown menu.
5. Choose a **Date Range** of up to one year that took place within the past three years, and click **Apply**.
   1. The past three months are selected by default.
6. Search by a dimension or metric, or expand a dimension or metric category to browse them.
7. Select and drag each desired dimension into the **Rows** field and metric into the **Columns** field.
   1. Dimension categories are outlined in orange, and metric categories are outlined in purple. Refer to [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) for dimension and metric definitions and details.
   2. Up to 10 dimensions are supported per report.
8. Click the **X** icon next to any selected dimensions or metrics to remove them from the report, if desired.
9. Select the funnel icon next to any item in the **Rows** section to filter the report by those dimensions.
10. Select the **Aggregate** toggle switch, if desired.
    1. The **Aggregate** toggle switch appears after you add one or more filters to the first dimension listed in the **Rows** section.
11. Click **Execute Report** to generate the data.
12. Select **Save Report**.

### Generate a report with AI Assist

Open the Reports app, then follow these steps to manually create a new custom report:

1. Click **+ Create Report**. This will open the **Create New Report** page.
2. Select the **AI Assist** tab.
3. Type a name into the **Report Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique name to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
4. Search or browse and select a timezone from the **Timezone** dropdown menu.
5. Choose a **Date Range** of up to one year that took place within the past three years, and click **Apply**.
   1. The past three months are selected by default.
6. If desired, select a chat preset.
7. Describe your preferred report parameters in the available field.
8. Hit **Enter** on your device’s keyboard or select the arrow icon next to your description.
   1. The reports **Rows** and **Columns** sections will automatically update to include the dimensions and metrics related to your query.
9. Browse the **Rows** and **Columns** lists to review which dimensions and metrics are included in the report.
10. Repeat steps 7 through 9, as needed, to submit more report descriptions and allow the AI to add the relevant rows and columns.
11. If you’d like to apply more dimensions and/or metrics to the AI-generated report–or remove any of them from the report–select the **Manual Mode** tab and follow steps 6 through 10 of the Generate a report with Manual Mode workflow.
    1. Up to 10 dimensions are supported per report.
12. Click **Execute Report** to generate the data.
13. Select **Save Report**.

## Manage a report

You can manage a report in the following ways:

- Review dimensions
- Run
- Download
- Edit
- Duplicate
- Delete

### Review dimensions

You can review the dimensions associated with each of your reports.

Follow these steps to review dimensions:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to review.
2. Select **Dimensions** from the **Dimensions** column. This will open a pop-up window that features the title of the report.
3. Review the list of dimension tabs on the left panel, and filtered values, if any, on the right panel.
4. Click **Run Now** to generate the most up-to-date data across each included dimension.

### Run a report

You can run a report to generate the most up-to-date data across each of its dimensions and metrics.

Follow these steps to run a report:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to edit.
2. Select **Run Now** from the **Actions** column. This will open the report, where you can review **Aggregated** or **Daily** data and Download the report, if desired.

### Download a report

You can Download a report in one of two ways:

- From the **Report** page
- From inside a report

### Download a report from the Report page

Follow these steps to download a report from the **Report** page:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to download.
2. Select the downward-arrow icon from the **ID** column.
   1. You must hover your cursor over the report row for the icon to appear in the **ID** column.
3. Choose to download the report as an **XLSX** or **CSV** file, depending on your preference.

### Download a report from inside a report

Follow these steps to download a report after you’ve clicked into it:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to edit.
2. Select **Run Now** from the **Actions** column. This will open the report.
3. Click the CSV page icon to download the report as a **CSV** file, or the XLSX page icon to download it as an **XLSX** file, depending on your preference.

### Edit a report

Follow these steps to edit an existing report:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to edit.
2. Select **Run Now** from the **Actions** column. This will open the report.
3. Make any desired changes to the report’s **Report Name**, **Timezone**, **Date Range**, **Rows,** or **Columns** fields; and any filters.
4. Select **Update Changes** to apply your edits, or **Cancel** to leave the original report unchanged.

### Duplicate a report

You can duplicate a report to create another report with the same parameters, and without carrying over email schedules that you’ve previously defined.

Follow these steps to duplicate a report:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to duplicate.
2. Select **Run Now** from the **Actions** column. This will open the report.
3. Select the duplicate icon. This will open the **Duplicate Report** pop-up window.
4. Type a name into the **Report Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique name to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
   2. If you don’t update the **Report Name** field, we’ll automatically name this report “Copy of,” followed by the name of the report that you duplicated.
5. Click **Duplicate Report**.

Refer to Edit a report for instructions on updating the report’s dimensions, metrics, filters, and other fields.

### Delete a report

> **Report deletion notice:** Consider downloading a report before deleting it as this action is irreversible.

You can delete a report in one of two ways:

- From the **Report** page
- From inside a report

### Delete a report from the Report page

Follow these steps to delete a report from the **Report** page:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to delete.
2. Select the trashcan icon from the **Actions** menu.
3. Use the pop-up window to review any warnings and confirm your selection.

### Delete a report from inside a report

Follow these steps to delete a report after you’ve clicked into it:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to delete.
2. Select **Run Now** from the **Actions** column. This will open the report.
3. Select the trashcan icon.
4. Use the pop-up window to review any warnings and confirm your selection.

## Send a report

You can email a report once or set up recurring delivery to a list of recipients.

### Schedule one-time email delivery

Follow these steps to send a report once:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to send on a recurring basis.
2. Select the envelope icon from the **Email Scheduled** column. This will open the **Schedule Email Delivery** pop-up window.
3. Add each email alias into the **Recipient Email Addresses** field, separated by commas.
4. Choose to email the report as an **XLSX** or **CSV** file, depending on your preference.
5. Open the **Delivery Frequency** dropdown menu and select **One time now**
6. Select **Send**.

We’ll immediately send the report to the inboxes of the email alias(es) you entered.

### Schedule recurring email delivery

Follow these steps to schedule a recurring report:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to send on a recurring basis.
2. Select the envelope icon from the **Email Scheduled** column. This will open the **Schedule Email Delivery** pop-up window.
3. Add each email alias into the **Recipient Email Addresses** field, separated by commas.
4. Choose to email the report as an **XLSX** or **CSV** file, depending on your preference.
5. Open the **Delivery Frequency** dropdown menu and select how often we should send this report to the recipients you entered.
   1. Refer to [Delivery frequency](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview#h_22b898e667) for more information on each delivery frequency.
6. Enter when we should stop sending the recurring report into the **End Date** field.
7. If you chose a **Weekly until** frequency, use the second **Delivery Frequency** field to choose which day of the week to send the recurring report.
8. If you chose a **Monthly until** frequency, use the second **Delivery Frequency** field to choose which day of the month to send the recurring report.
9. Review the preview next to the information icon to confirm that your selections are correct.
10. Click the **Running Total** toggle switch if you’d like each recurring report to use the report’s start date through the most recent report delivery date. Otherwise, each report will include only the most recent day/week/month’s data, depending on the frequency you selected.
11. Click **Schedule** to initiate the recurring email delivery.

We’ll send the report once the first recurring date arrives. For example, if you selected **Monthly until** and **Last Day of Month**, we’ll send the first report at the end of this month. Refer to Schedule one-time email delivery if you’d like to send the report immediately.

### Edit or stop a report schedule

Follow these steps to update the cadence of a report that you previously scheduled for recurring delivery:

1. Filter or search your reports to locate the one you want to edit.
2. Select the pencil icon from the **Email Scheduled** column. This will open the **Schedule Email Delivery** pop-up window that you used when you first created the email schedule.
   1. You must hover your cursor over the report row for the pencil icon to appear in the **Email Scheduled** column.
3. Apply any desired changes to the email delivery recipients, file format, or delivery frequency.
4. Click **Stop Schedule** to cancel all future scheduled email deliveries, if desired.
5. Select **Update Changes** to apply your edits, or **Cancel** to leave the original schedule unchanged.

## Locate additional reporting resources

- [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report)

# Troubleshoot a report

## Report troubleshooting overview

You’ll need to follow specific steps to successfully create and manage a report. If you encounter an error or are blocked from completing certain actions, refer to these resources first:

- [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview)
- [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report)

Return to this article to address and resolve other factors that may block your ability to create or manage reports in the **Reports** app.

## Report creation troubleshooting

### Create Report option is missing

You must run a campaign to enable the **+ Create Report** button in the **Reports** app.

### No reports are listed

You must generate a report for it to appear on the **Report** page of the **Reports** app. Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) for further instructions.

### Unable to add more dimensions (rows)

You can add up to 10 dimensions per report. Certain dimension combinations, however, count as a single dimension.

| **Dimensions** | **Count toward dimension limit** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign** and/or **Campaign ID** and/or **Campaign Start Date** and/or **Campaign End Date** | Any combination counts as only one dimension toward the dimension limit |
| **Insertion Order** and/or **Insertion Order ID** and/or **Insertion Order Start Date** and/or **Insertion Order End Date** | Any combination counts as only one dimension toward the dimension limit |

### Unable to locate a dimension or metric

Refer to [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) to review which dimension and metric you can expect to find in each dimension or metric category.

Follow these steps if the dimension or metric is listed and you are still unable to locate a dimension or metric:

- If you are entering a full metric name, try its abbreviation instead.
- Note that each metric in the **Budget** category and certain items in the **Campaign Specifics** category will only appear after certain dimensions are added to the report. Refer to the table below for more details on these conditional fields.

| **Type** | **Dimension or Metric** | **Requirement** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Budget Metric** | **Daily Budget** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** **Customer** **Customer ID** |
| **Budget Metric** | **Total Budget** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** **Customer** **Customer ID** |
| **Budget Metric** | **Max Bid** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** |
| **Budget Metric** | **Daily Budget Completion** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** |
| **Campaign Specifics** | **Campaign Status** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** |
| **Campaign Specifics** | **Campaign Budget Type** | One or more of the following dimensions must be added to the **Rows** field: **Campaign** **Campaign ID** |

### Unable to aggregate by a certain category

You can aggregate the report’s data by the first dimension listed in the report’s **Rows** field. Drag a different dimension to the top of this section to aggregate the data by that category.

Keep in mind that data can be aggregated by dimensions (rows) and not by metrics (columns).

## Report email scheduling troubleshooting

### Dates missing from monthly schedule

Certain dates (1, 29, 30, 31) are captured by the **First Day of the Month** and **Last Day of the Month** delivery frequency selections. These categories are to account for months of varying lengths and help ensure that the report is still sent on a monthly basis.

### Send button is disabled

You must complete each field in the **Schedule Email Delivery** pop-up window to send the report to the recipients you specified.

If you completed all fields but the button is still disabled, you likely only added one email alias. You’ll need to click anywhere within the **Schedule Email Delivery** window, and outside of the **Recipient Email Addresses** field, for it to register. This will enable the **Send** button automatically.

## Locate additional reporting resources

- [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview)
- [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report)

title: Creative formats overview

blocks.text: Choosing the right ad format helps ensure your message resonates with the intended audience, and affects how users engage with your ad. Some formats work better for grabbing attention quickly, while others can be more effective for storytelling and building deeper connections with a brand over time.

When you approach creatives, we recommend thinking about the type of experience you’d like to create and how your target audience consumes content. A well-matched ad format can enhance the impact of your creative and drive the campaign results you’re aiming for.

The creative you choose depends on a variety of factors such as the target audience, product or service, and the campaign’s goals. Ad-format choices can also depend on bandwidth and skillset, and whether you can meet the requirements necessary for the ad to display correctly.

Review this article for more details about the ad formats that are supported on the IQM platform, and refer to[Creative Ad Specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs) to confirm that your creatives follow IQM and industry requirements.

Capture consumers’ valuable attention with bold visuals that captivate your audience. Image creatives use a static (PNG, JPG) or moving (GIF) image, often paired with a short caption or tagline, to promote a product or service.

Advertisers gravitate toward this format because it’s quick to produce, easy to understand, and grabs consumers’ attention. Image creatives also work well on platforms where users scroll quickly as they deliver a clear and concise message in a small space. For these reasons, it can be critical to apply consistent imagery, color, and design to image creatives to spark brand recognition at a glance.
Refer to [Add an image to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651450-add-an-image-to-your-creative-library) for more information.

Engage your audience with dynamic, interactive content that adapts seamlessly across their devices. HTML creatives rely on an iframe, meaning you can introduce interactive multimedia elements that encourage users to engage with your ad in more ways. These responsive display ads automatically adjust your creative’s design elements, like its size and appearance, based on the size of the ad placement.

Without requiring manual adjustments, HTML creatives can help introduce scale to your operations. However, they require a level of coding knowledge to add source links for videos, graphics, or images; and the elements necessary to make the ad responsive.
Refer to [Add an HTML file to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651452-add-an-html-file-to-your-creative-library) for more information.

Advertisers rely on video creatives to encourage brand recall with rich storytelling content that leaves a lasting impression. The IQM platform supports two video creative types: standard video creatives and Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) video creatives. Both standard video and VAST video creatives can be shown before, during, or after the publisher’s video content plays. The main differences between them relate to how they’re structured and delivered.
Refer to [Upload a video creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651461-upload-a-video-creative) for more information.

Video creatives use standard MP4 or MOV video files. They’re typically hosted on a platform and embedded directly into a web page or app. Video creatives either begin playing immediately or after a user clicks on them—without needing further instructions from an ad server.

You can append tracking solutions onto standard video creatives when you upload them. These tags include click URLs, impression-tracking URLs, and URLs related to how much of the video played for the consumer (e.g., start-tracking URLs and complete-tracking URLs).

Instead of MP4 or MOV video files, VAST video creatives use extensible markup language (XML). This string of code is used to communicate details between the ad server and video player, which lets the video player know how to run each ad.

VAST video creatives allow for more complex ad serving than their standard video counterpart. Their capabilities range from enabling tracking, multiple file versions, companion ads, and dynamic ad insertion; to requesting ads dynamically and including different video sources depending on variables like device type.

The XML code also provides tracking capabilities like impressions, clicks, and other user interactions such as how much of the video played for the consumer (e.g., start-tracking URLs and complete-tracking URLs). Unlike with standard video creatives, these trackers are included directly in the XML code.

Native creatives are designed to blend seamlessly with the content around them. These ads can feel less intrusive than ads in other formats because they don’t interrupt the flow of a platform or website.

Users can be more likely to interact with content that feels organic. Since native ads match the look and feel of their environment, they can create a positive user experience and increase trust. This format is also great for storytelling and providing valuable information in a way that can feel more authentic to your audience.

Advertisers introduce variety to their campaigns on the IQM platform by adding multiple titles, descriptions, and native images and videos to the same creative. This generates different combinations, or variants, of the same native creative.

blocks.table_reason: images in cells (one row, or no text cells)

blocks.text: Refer to [How to set up native ads](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8706031-how-to-set-up-native-ads) for more information.

Reach on-the-go users with brief and memorable audio ads that play on publishers’ digital audio players. While audio creatives bring a brand to life with immersive sound experiences, this ad format is unique because it allows you to reach consumers while they’re engaged in offline activities. Your products or services will stay top-of-mind across their commute or exercise, for example. Advertisers also gravitate toward this format because it allows them to tap into large, highly engaged audiences across categories and genres.

Unlike with other ad formats that allow a clickable call-to-action button, audio creatives benefit from shorter URLs that your audience can remember and easily type into a web browser. You might also choose to mention the brand’s name multiple times since users won’t be able to associate any memorable visual design elements, like colors and logos, with the brand.
Refer to [Add an audio file to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651462-add-an-audio-file-to-your-creative-library) for more information.
Send promotional messages directly to a user’s phone via text. SMS ads are simple, text-only messages, while MMS ads can also include elements such as images, videos, and links.

Advertisers choose these formats because they offer a direct line of communication to customers, and typically feature high open rates compared to other ad formats. These quick-to-consume and highly personalized ads are effective for time-sensitive promotions, special offers, and political campaigns.

Because they reach individuals on their personal devices, SMS and MMS ads can create a sense of urgency and foster a closer connection with the brand. However, this one-to-one connection also makes supporting your audience’s sense of privacy critical, and there are additional regulations for this ad format including mandatory opt-out texts (e.g., “Reply STOP to unsubscribe”). Due to spam rates on mobile devices, you should also confirm any SMS or MMS messages are high quality and error free to help ensure that users trust your ads enough to interact with them.
Refer to [SMS MMS Creative Guidelines and Specifications](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7051626-sms-mms-creative-guidelines-and-specification) for more information.
[Creative ad specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs)
[Add creatives to your campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651477-add-creatives-to-your-campaign)

# Creative formats overview

## Supported ad formats overview

Choosing the right ad format helps ensure your message resonates with the intended audience, and affects how users engage with your ad. Some formats work better for grabbing attention quickly, while others can be more effective for storytelling and building deeper connections with a brand over time.

When you approach creatives, we recommend thinking about the type of experience you’d like to create and how your target audience consumes content. A well-matched ad format can enhance the impact of your creative and drive the campaign results you’re aiming for.

The creative you choose depends on a variety of factors such as the target audience, product or service, and the campaign’s goals. Ad-format choices can also depend on bandwidth and skillset, and whether you can meet the requirements necessary for the ad to display correctly.

Review this article for more details about the ad formats that are supported on the IQM platform, and refer to[Creative Ad Specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs) to confirm that your creatives follow IQM and industry requirements.

## Image creatives

Capture consumers’ valuable attention with bold visuals that captivate your audience. Image creatives use a static (PNG, JPG) or moving (GIF) image, often paired with a short caption or tagline, to promote a product or service.

Advertisers gravitate toward this format because it’s quick to produce, easy to understand, and grabs consumers’ attention. Image creatives also work well on platforms where users scroll quickly as they deliver a clear and concise message in a small space. For these reasons, it can be critical to apply consistent imagery, color, and design to image creatives to spark brand recognition at a glance.

Refer to [Add an image to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651450-add-an-image-to-your-creative-library) for more information.

## HTML creatives

Engage your audience with dynamic, interactive content that adapts seamlessly across their devices. HTML creatives rely on an iframe, meaning you can introduce interactive multimedia elements that encourage users to engage with your ad in more ways. These responsive display ads automatically adjust your creative’s design elements, like its size and appearance, based on the size of the ad placement.

Without requiring manual adjustments, HTML creatives can help introduce scale to your operations. However, they require a level of coding knowledge to add source links for videos, graphics, or images; and the elements necessary to make the ad responsive.

Refer to [Add an HTML file to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651452-add-an-html-file-to-your-creative-library) for more information.

## Video creatives

Advertisers rely on video creatives to encourage brand recall with rich storytelling content that leaves a lasting impression. The IQM platform supports two video creative types: standard video creatives and Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) video creatives. Both standard video and VAST video creatives can be shown before, during, or after the publisher’s video content plays. The main differences between them relate to how they’re structured and delivered.

Refer to [Upload a video creative](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651461-upload-a-video-creative) for more information.

### Standard video

Video creatives use standard MP4 or MOV video files. They’re typically hosted on a platform and embedded directly into a web page or app. Video creatives either begin playing immediately or after a user clicks on them—without needing further instructions from an ad server.

You can append tracking solutions onto standard video creatives when you upload them. These tags include click URLs, impression-tracking URLs, and URLs related to how much of the video played for the consumer (e.g., start-tracking URLs and complete-tracking URLs).

### VAST XML video

Instead of MP4 or MOV video files, VAST video creatives use extensible markup language (XML). This string of code is used to communicate details between the ad server and video player, which lets the video player know how to run each ad.

VAST video creatives allow for more complex ad serving than their standard video counterpart. Their capabilities range from enabling tracking, multiple file versions, companion ads, and dynamic ad insertion; to requesting ads dynamically and including different video sources depending on variables like device type.

The XML code also provides tracking capabilities like impressions, clicks, and other user interactions such as how much of the video played for the consumer (e.g., start-tracking URLs and complete-tracking URLs). Unlike with standard video creatives, these trackers are included directly in the XML code.

## Native creatives

Native creatives are designed to blend seamlessly with the content around them. These ads can feel less intrusive than ads in other formats because they don’t interrupt the flow of a platform or website.
Users can be more likely to interact with content that feels organic. Since native ads match the look and feel of their environment, they can create a positive user experience and increase trust. This format is also great for storytelling and providing valuable information in a way that can feel more authentic to your audience.
Advertisers introduce variety to their campaigns on the IQM platform by adding multiple titles, descriptions, and native images and videos to the same creative. This generates different combinations, or variants, of the same native creative.

Refer to [How to set up native ads](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8706031-how-to-set-up-native-ads) for more information.

## Audio creatives

Reach on-the-go users with brief and memorable audio ads that play on publishers’ digital audio players. While audio creatives bring a brand to life with immersive sound experiences, this ad format is unique because it allows you to reach consumers while they’re engaged in offline activities. Your products or services will stay top-of-mind across their commute or exercise, for example. Advertisers also gravitate toward this format because it allows them to tap into large, highly engaged audiences across categories and genres.

Unlike with other ad formats that allow a clickable call-to-action button, audio creatives benefit from shorter URLs that your audience can remember and easily type into a web browser. You might also choose to mention the brand’s name multiple times since users won’t be able to associate any memorable visual design elements, like colors and logos, with the brand.

Refer to [Add an audio file to your creative library](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651462-add-an-audio-file-to-your-creative-library) for more information.

## SMS/MMS ads

Send promotional messages directly to a user’s phone via text. SMS ads are simple, text-only messages, while MMS ads can also include elements such as images, videos, and links.

Advertisers choose these formats because they offer a direct line of communication to customers, and typically feature high open rates compared to other ad formats. These quick-to-consume and highly personalized ads are effective for time-sensitive promotions, special offers, and political campaigns.

Because they reach individuals on their personal devices, SMS and MMS ads can create a sense of urgency and foster a closer connection with the brand. However, this one-to-one connection also makes supporting your audience’s sense of privacy critical, and there are additional regulations for this ad format including mandatory opt-out texts (e.g., “Reply STOP to unsubscribe”). Due to spam rates on mobile devices, you should also confirm any SMS or MMS messages are high quality and error free to help ensure that users trust your ads enough to interact with them.

Refer to [SMS MMS Creative Guidelines and Specifications](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7051626-sms-mms-creative-guidelines-and-specification) for more information.

## Locate additional creative resources

- [Creative ad specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs)
- [Add creatives to your campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651477-add-creatives-to-your-campaign)

title: Import IQM campaign data into Google Looker Studio

blocks.text: IQM maintains an **IQM Reports** connector to offer comprehensive reporting solutions. You can use this tool to transform your campaign data from the IQM platform into customized, visual reports in Google Looker Studio.

To create these reports and visualizations, you’ll need to use the **IQM Reports** connector to import a campaign into Looker Studio. You can review and customize the reports and share them with your clients.

sections.heading: Set up the IQM Reports connector
heading_path: Set up the IQM Reports connector

blocks.text: **IQM Reports notice:** You must maintain both a Google account and an IQM account to take advantage of the **IQM Reports** connector.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: You’ll need to link your Google account to the **IQM Reports** connector before you can add your campaign data to Looker Studio.
Follow these steps to connect your account to **IQM Reports**:
Log in to your Google account as you normally would.
Select **IQM Reports** from the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio. This will open an account setup pop-up window.
Add your location and company details to the **Country** and **Company** fields.
Review the Google Looker terms and conditions, and select the **Terms of service** checkbox if you accept them.
Click **Continue**.
Return to the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio and select **IQM Reports**.
Review any terms and select **Authorize**.
Click the email alias that’s associated with your IQM account and enter your IQM account password.
Select **Continue**.

Review any terms, policies, and other details, select **Allow** to grant us access to share your IQM campaign data with your Looker Studio account. This selection will automatically close the pop-up window.

sections.heading: Sign in and create a report
heading_path: Sign in and create a report

blocks.text: Return to the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio and select **IQM Reports**.
Use the **Credentials** section to enter your IQM platform username and password.
Click **Submit**.
In the **Parameters** section, choose the time zone that will be used for each date included in the report.
Keep the **Use report template for new reports** checkbox selected to start your visual report from an editable, default template.
Deselect the checkbox to build your visual report from scratch.
Click **Connect**.

Once you connect to the **IQM Reports** data source, you’ll arrive at the **IQM Reports** page in Looker Studio, where you can add fields and parameters to a report. Follow the steps outlined in the official [Looker Studio Help Center](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/topic/6369007?hl=en&ref_topic=6291037) (external link) for steps to manually create a report.

If you selected the **Use report template for new reports** checkbox before you connected to the data source, you’ll arrive at a fully generated report instead of the report-builder screen. You can still add or remove report parameters by following the steps outlined in Edit a data visualization's properties.
The report template provides an editable, default dashboard that displays your IQM ad-serving data and accompanying data visualizations. You can manage these reports in the following ways:
Review a report.
Edit a report’s date range.
Edit a data visualization’s properties, which dictate how the data is grouped and the metrics that the report includes.
Delete a data visualization from the report.
Add a new data visualization to the report or change the chart type of an existing one.
Customize the style of the report.
The default report’s data is spread across several pages. Select the forward and backward arrows located below the report’s title to review the report.
Updating the date range shown on page 2 of the report changes the reporting data that’s loaded into the report.
Follow these steps to update a report’s date range:
Locate and select the **Date Range** drop-down menu.
Choose your preferred dates from the calendar module.
