# Import IQM campaign data into Google Looker Studio

## Data import overview

IQM maintains an **IQM Reports** connector to offer comprehensive reporting solutions. You can use this tool to transform your campaign data from the IQM platform into customized, visual reports in Google Looker Studio.

To create these reports and visualizations, you’ll need to use the **IQM Reports** connector to import a campaign into Looker Studio. You can review and customize the reports and share them with your clients.

## Import data

### Set up the IQM Reports connector

> **IQM Reports notice:** You must maintain both a Google account and an IQM account to take advantage of the **IQM Reports** connector.

You’ll need to link your Google account to the **IQM Reports** connector before you can add your campaign data to Looker Studio.

Follow these steps to connect your account to **IQM Reports**:

1. Log in to your Google account as you normally would.
2. Select **IQM Reports** from the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio. This will open an account setup pop-up window.
3. Add your location and company details to the **Country** and **Company** fields.
4. Review the Google Looker terms and conditions, and select the **Terms of service** checkbox if you accept them.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. Return to the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio and select **IQM Reports**.
7. Review any terms and select **Authorize**.
8. Click the email alias that’s associated with your IQM account and enter your IQM account password.
9. Select **Continue**.
10. Review any terms, policies, and other details, select **Allow** to grant us access to share your IQM campaign data with your Looker Studio account. This selection will automatically close the pop-up window.

### Sign in and create a report

1. Return to the [Connect to Data](https://lookerstudio.google.com/data?search=iqm) page (external link) in Looker Studio and select **IQM Reports**.
2. Use the **Credentials** section to enter your IQM platform username and password.
3. Click **Submit**.
4. In the **Parameters** section, choose the time zone that will be used for each date included in the report.
5. Keep the **Use report template for new reports** checkbox selected to start your visual report from an editable, default template.
   1. Deselect the checkbox to build your visual report from scratch.
6. Click **Connect**.

### Add parameters to a report

Once you connect to the **IQM Reports** data source, you’ll arrive at the **IQM Reports** page in Looker Studio, where you can add fields and parameters to a report. Follow the steps outlined in the official [Looker Studio Help Center](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/topic/6369007?hl=en&ref_topic=6291037) (external link) for steps to manually create a report.

If you selected the **Use report template for new reports** checkbox before you connected to the data source, you’ll arrive at a fully generated report instead of the report-builder screen. You can still add or remove report parameters by following the steps outlined in Edit a data visualization's properties.

## Manage a report

The report template provides an editable, default dashboard that displays your IQM ad-serving data and accompanying data visualizations. You can manage these reports in the following ways:

- Review a report.
- Edit a report’s date range.
- Edit a data visualization’s properties, which dictate how the data is grouped and the metrics that the report includes.
- Delete a data visualization from the report.
- Add a new data visualization to the report or change the chart type of an existing one.
- Customize the style of the report.

### Review a report

The default report’s data is spread across several pages. Select the forward and backward arrows located below the report’s title to review the report.

### Edit a date range

Updating the date range shown on page 2 of the report changes the reporting data that’s loaded into the report.

Follow these steps to update a report’s date range:

1. Locate and select the **Date Range** drop-down menu.
2. Choose your preferred dates from the calendar module.
3. Select **Apply** to update the report.

### Edit a data visualization’s (chart) properties and parameters

#### Edit a chart’s properties and parameters

Follow these steps to edit a specific chart or data visualization:

1. Click on the chart or data visualization. This will open the **Chart** and **Data** properties panels.
2. In the **Setup** tab of the **Chart** panel, select any dimension or metric to open an edit menu dedicated to that particular field.
   1. Dimensions determine how the data is categorized, while metrics contain aggregated data that measures those dimensions.
3. In the **Data** panel, modify any dimensions that the data is grouped by (e.g., campaigns, creatives, and congressional districts) or any metrics that are displayed in the chart (e.g., impressions, clicks, and win rate).

Note that these changes will impact which data is included in a specific data visualization and how that data is grouped. They will not limit which data is included in the entire report. Select **Edit** at the top of the report to apply changes to the report template instead.

### Add or change a data visualization (chart)

#### Add a new chart

Follow these steps to add a new chart to a report:

1. Open the **Page** menu from the report’s header.
2. Select **New page**.
3. Select **Add a chart** from the report’s toolbar.
4. Browse and select your preferred chart type.
   1. Refer to the [Looker Studio Help Center](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/topic/7059081?hl=en&ref_topic=9207420) (external link) for descriptions of each chart type.
5. Follow the steps outlined in Edit a chart’s properties and parameters to choose which dimensions and metrics the chart should visualize.

#### Change chart types

You can switch between different charts without having to add a new chart to the report. Click on an existing chart, select **Chart** in the **Properties** panel, and choose the new chart type.

Looker Studio may adjust the dimensions and metrics based on which ones best suit each individual chart type. Follow the steps outlined in Edit a chart’s properties and parameters to change which dimensions and metrics the chart should visualize.

### Delete a data visualization (chart)

Right-click on a chart and select **Delete** to remove it from your report.

### Style the report

Preset themes let you apply color and style themes to your entire report. You can customize these presets to reflect your brand identity.

#### Choose a preset theme

Follow these steps to apply a preset style theme to the report:

1. Click **Edit** at the top of the report.
2. Select **Theme and layout** from the report’s toolbar.
3. Browse and select the theme you want to apply from the **Theme** tab.

#### Customize a preset theme

Follow these steps to customize a preset style theme:

1. Click **Edit** at the top of the report.
2. Select **Theme and layout** from the report’s toolbar.
3. Click **Customize** in the **Theme and layout** panel.
4. Enter and apply your preferred style customizations.

## Share a report

> **Data source notice:** Consider creating a new data source for each report that you plan to share. This precaution helps ensure that only the intended audience can access the insights.

You can share the IQM reports that you create in Looker Studio. Review each report beforehand to ensure only relevant information is available in them. This includes confirming that you exclude any data from clients other than the one you plan to share the report with.

### IQM platform credentials

By default, the report’s recipients will be asked to input their IQM platform credentials to view the report. You can change this requirement by applying **Owner’s credentials** settings. Follow the steps outlined in the [Looker Studio Help Center](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/answer/6371135?hl=en#types&zippy=%2Cin-this-article) (external link) to complete this process.

### Google credentials

> **Public link sharing notice:** Link sharing may expose your data to a wider audience than you intended. Take caution when managing access to your reports, and check each link-sharing option before sending a shareable link to a client or other personnel.

By default, the report’s recipients will be asked to input their Google credentials to view the report. You can change this requirement by applying **Public link sharing** settings. Follow the steps outlined in the [Looker Studio Help Center](https://support.google.com/looker-studio/answer/7459147?hl=en#get-a-shareable-link) (external link) to complete this process.

## Locate additional reporting resources

# Manage an Activity Log

## Activity Log overview

The Activity Log is a record of events and actions that took place on the IQM platform. This detailed timeline [tracks various activities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview#h_97eb4245b3) performed by individual users. Monitor these activities to refine and optimize your campaigns and operations.

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more information on the types of actions that are captured in the Activity Log.

## Video tutorial: Manage an Activity Log

## Monitor an Activity Log

Follow these steps to locate and monitor an Activity Log:

1. Select the **Activity Log** tab of the Organization app.
2. Select **View Updates** from an activity’s **Actions** column to open a pop-up window related to that action.
   1. Review more details on the specific changes that were applied or activities that took place. These details include the original value or item and the updated value or item.
3. Click **Done** to return to the **Activity Log** page.

## Filter an Activity Log

Select an activity category or apply **Apps** or **Users** filters to narrow in on particular actions. Refer to [Included activities and filters](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview#h_97eb4245b3) for more information on the types of actions that are featured in each of these selections.

### Select an activity category

Select the **All Activities** tab of your Activity Log or choose to filter the record by an activity category. Click **Flagged Activities**, **Administrative Activities**, **Account Level Activities**, **Financial Activities**, or **Campaign Activities** to filter the Activity Log by that category. Otherwise, leave **All Activities** selected.

### Filter by an app or user

1. Open the **Users** menu and click the checkbox next to one or more users to display only the actions that were performed by those individuals.
2. Click the checkbox next to one or more apps in the **Apps** section to display only the actions that were performed within those apps.
   1. Leave **All Apps** selected instead to show actions taken across any app.
3. Deselect a checkbox to remove that filter from your Activity Log, or click **Reset Filter** to clear all filters.

## Flag an activity

Bookmark activities that you’d like to easily retrieve and review in the future.

Select the bookmark icon in an activity’s **Actions** column to flag it for future reference. All flagged activities are stored in the **Flagged Activities** activity category.

## Locate additional Activity Log resources

- [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview)

The **New Total Budget** value that you enter is the exact value that’s used for the campaign’s total budget.
Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **= Set**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.
The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets added to the campaign’s existing total budget.
Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $50,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **+ Add**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.

The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets divided evenly across each of the campaigns you selected. Note that you must select more than one campaign for the **Split** open to appear.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You select four campaigns, enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field, and click **÷ Split**. Each of the four campaigns’ total budgets are $62,5000, which total $250,000 when combined.

Refer to [Compare metrics and group by a metric](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_8d4d685ab9) for more information.

### Filters

Define which insertion orders (IOs) and campaigns will populate in the Dashboard table by searching and/and filtering a dashboard.

| **View By** | Include only campaigns or only IOs in the dashboard table. |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign Type** | Include only campaigns or IOs with a certain campaign type [Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) or Advanced] or budget type [Budget or Impression] in the dashboard table. |
| **Status** | Include only campaigns or IOs featuring a particular status in the dashboard table. |
| **Creative Type** | Include only campaigns or IOs featuring a particular creative format in the dashboard table. |
| **Insertion Orders** | Include only the specific IOs that you select in the dashboard table. |
| **Campaigns** | Include only the specific campaigns that you select in the dashboard table. |

### Dashboard table

A dashboard’s table is your primary command center for monitoring campaign performance details, applying quick edits to campaigns one by one or in bulk, and generating custom reports.

### Data table customizations

Customize the dashboard table to surface your preferred metrics and dimensions at a glance.

Refer to [Create or manage a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard) for details on how to customize the table in the following ways:

- Add, remove, or move a dashboard table’s columns.
- Search or filter to specify the types of campaigns or campaign elements that are included in a dashboard table.
- Save the customizations that you apply to a dashboard for future use.

### Campaign management

You can manage certain campaign elements directly from a dashboard table.

Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for details on how to complete the following actions:

- Set or change campaign budgets
- Set or change campaign Max Bid Prices and Min Bid Prices
- Set or change campaign end dates
- Edit, duplicate, or delete campaigns

### General reports and Insights reports

> **Insights report requirements:** Your campaign must meet certain eligibility requirements before you can generate Insights reports for it. Refer to a report type’s overview article (linked below) for more information on the data included in the report and its individual eligibility criteria.

Craft custom reports or generate tailored Insights reports directly from a dashboard table.

| **Report type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| [Custom reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) | Select one or more campaigns from a dashboard to create a general report in one click. You’ll get redirected to the Report app, where you can layer on the individual dimensions and metrics that you’d like to include in the report. |
| [Audience Insights reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview) | Gain a holistic, in-depth view of users’ characteristics, interests, and behaviors for each audience you create. |
| [Campaign Bidding Insights reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview) | Assess which targeting parameters are limiting a campaign’s number of bid requests. |
| [Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights reports (Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report-overview) | Surface ad exposure, engagement, and demographic data; and voting-history details, about the voters that you target in political campaigns. |
| [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) | Compliantly evaluate the effectiveness of your Healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and competitors’ prescription patterns. |
| [Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) | Compliantly assess and optimize Healthcare campaigns. |
| [Audience Quality Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview) | Evaluate how effectively your Healthcare campaigns reached the intended patient audience. |

Refer to [Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471810-generate-performance-and-insights-data-from-a-dashboard) for more details on how to generate reports and insights from a dashboard table.

### AI Insights

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical or high-risk blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for eligible campaigns. This diagnostic tool lets you know which issues are putting your campaign at the greatest risk, and what actions to take to address them.

Note that CampaignPulse is designed to help you detect and address significant risks to campaign delivery. For other campaign-optimization tools and strategies, refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview).

Review [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) to get started with CampaignPulse.

#### CampaignPulse eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to run CampaignPulse for eligible campaigns. Refer to the table below for campaign-eligibility criteria.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| Vertical | Specialty Political Healthcare |
| Campaign type | Advanced |
| Campaign status | Running, with a Start Date in the past |

#### CampaignPulse delivery insights

CampaignPulse checks critical blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. These blockers typically relate to possible errors and misses such as ensuring your account’s balance is sufficient, checking that targeted elements such as creatives and audiences feature a Ready status, and making sure your insertion order (IO) End Date is compatible with the End Dates of its campaigns, for example.

Review all CampaignPulse delivery insights closely for instructions on how to address the issues that can put your campaigns at risk.

### Available balance

The top of each dashboard displays the account’s available balance. Organization administrators can [add funds](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5734663-adding-funds) to an account. Contact yours to complete this process.

## Dashboard metrics and dimensions

> **Reach and Frequency metrics notice:** The **Reach** and **Frequency** metrics are aggregated (lifetime) values that are updated daily. The values shown reflect the campaign’s **Reach** or **Frequency** through yesterday, and any changes you apply today will reflect on the dashboard tomorrow.

The metrics and dimensions included in the dashboard table range from campaign specifics to performance details. Certain ones are featured by default, and others can be added via the **Columns** menu.

Review [Customize a dashboard table](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_f6a2410804) for instructions on how to add or remove a dashboard-table column, and refer to the resources below to learn more about each metric and dimension that’s featured on your dashboard:

- [Conversion reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343706-conversion-reporting-metrics)
- [VCR reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343754-video-completion-rate-vcr-reporting-metrics-overview)
- [Cost reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343783-cost-reporting-metrics-overview)
- [Spending reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview)
- [Performance reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview)
- [Budget reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343824-budget-reporting-metrics-overview)
- [Reporting dimensions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343842-reporting-dimensions-overview)

## Key terms and concepts

### Set, Add, Split

**Set**, **Add**, and **Split** are three options that you’ll encounter when you edit a campaign’s total budget from a dashboard. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for more information on how to apply these changes to your campaigns.

### Set

The **New Total Budget** value that you enter is the exact value that’s used for the campaign’s total budget.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **= Set**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.

### Add

The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets added to the campaign’s existing total budget.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $50,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **+ Add**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.

### Split

The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets divided evenly across each of the campaigns you selected. Note that you must select more than one campaign for the **Split** open to appear.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You select four campaigns, enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field, and click **÷ Split**. Each of the four campaigns’ total budgets are $62,5000, which total $250,000 when combined.

## Locate additional dashboard resources

- [Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471810-generate-performance-and-insights-data-from-a-dashboard)

# Create or manage a dashboard

## Overview

> **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing data dashboards in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

You’ll use the dashboards you create in the Dashboard app to track your campaigns’ progress and performance. Create and manage customized dashboards that fit your needs and improve your reporting workflow.

You can also save time by adjusting certain campaign elements—like budgets and bid prices—directly from these dashboards. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for more information, and continue reading to learn how to customize your dashboards.

## Video tutorial: Create and manage a dashboard

## Customize a dashboard

Start by opening the Dashboard app from the homepage. You can customize a dashboard in the following ways:

- Limit data to a particular time zone or date range
- Customize a dashboard table
  - Add or remove a column
  - Sort by a column
  - Move a column
  - Filter or search
- Compare metrics
- Group by a metric

### Select a time zone and date range

The dashboard aggregates campaigns and related data based on your time zone and date range selections.

Follow these steps to choose the dates and times that you’d like for the dashboard to reflect:

1. Search or browse and select a time zone from the **Time Zone** menu.
2. Open the **Date Range** menu.
3. Either manually select your preferred date range or select a preset timeframe from the available options.
4. Click **Apply**.

### Customize a dashboard table

> **Reach metric notice:** The **Reach** metric is an aggregated value that’s updated daily. The value shown reflects the campaign’s reach through yesterday, and any changes you apply today will reflect on the dashboard tomorrow.

Choose which metrics appear in your dashboard’s table; define the order in which they appear; and sort, filter, or search to surface campaigns by their elements.

#### Add or remove a column

Follow these steps to choose which columns appear in your dashboard:

1. Open the **Columns** menu.
2. Click a metric to add it to the dashboard table.
3. Click a previously selected metric to remove it from the dashboard table.
4. If desired, use bulk operations to add or remove all columns.

#### Sort by a column

You can sort a dashboard table by any column’s dimensions or metrics.

Click a column’s title once to sort by that dimension or metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that dimension or metric in descending order.

#### Move a column

You can drag-and-drop a column to change the order in which your dashboard table’s dimensions and metrics appear.

Click and hold a column’s title. Drag the column’s title and hover it before or after another column’s title. When the vertical blue line appears, release your click to place the column in its new location.

#### Filter or search

Follow these steps to choose which insertion orders (IO) and campaigns populate in the table:

1. Select your preferred customizations from the row of filters.
   1. Refer to [Dashboard elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_6d2be3e27f) to learn more about each filter.
2. Use the **Search by** field to enter an IO, name, or status.

### Compare metrics and group by a metric

Use the data comparison panel to review data related to two metrics, and determine top performers by grouping by a particular dimension and metric.

### Compare metrics

1. If needed, select the arrow icon to expand the data comparison panel.
2. Browse and select the two metrics you’d like to compare from the menus.
   1. Note the colored circle next to each metric name to help you differentiate between them as you review the chart.
3. Hover your cursor over the chart area for metric details by date.

### Group by a metric

1. If needed, select the arrow icon to expand the data comparison panel.
2. Browse and select the dimension you’d like to group.
3. Browse and select the metric you’d like to review by the group you chose.
   1. For example, you might group by the **Creative** dimension and **Clicks** metric to uncover which creatives drove the most clicks during the date range you selected.
4. Review the bar graphs for performance details.

Note that the panel displays the top five items based on performance related to the metric you select; however, you can view full performance details in the dashboard table. Follow the steps outlined in Filter or search and Sort by a column to review performance by a particular campaign element and metric.

If no data was captured for this metric across the date range you select, **0** will appear next to each campaign element in the panel.

## Create a new dashboard

> **More on dashboard creation:** The **Dashboard** menu will only appear if you previously created and saved a dashboard. If this is your first dashboard, follow the steps outlined in Save dashboard settings instead.

Follow these steps to keep a record of each dashboard customization you apply:

1. Open the **Dashboard** menu.
2. Select **Create New Dashboard**.
3. Enter a name for the new dashboard.
4. Click **Create New Dashboard**.

## Save dashboard settings

Follow these steps to save changes to an existing dashboard:

1. Select **Save Dashboard**.
   1. If you’re saving changes to an existing dashboard, this will apply those changes.
   2. If you don’t have any saved dashboards, this will open the **Create Dashboard** pop-up window.
2. Enter a name for the new dashboard.
3. Click **Create**

You can return to the Dashboard app and Open a saved dashboard at any time to automatically apply each of your settings and filters.

## Open a saved dashboard

Open the **Dashboard** menu to browse and select an existing dashboard.

## Clear dashboard settings and filters

Follow these steps to discard a dashboard’s unsaved changes:

1. Select **Reset**. This will open the **Reset Dashboard** pop-up window.
2. Click **Reset** to confirm your selection.

If no changes were saved prior to resetting the dashboard, selecting **Reset** will restore the dashboard’s default settings and filters. Note that this action is permanent. You’ll need to manually apply each setting and filter if you’d like to create the same dashboard again.

## Locate additional dashboard resources

- [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview)
- [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard)
- [Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471810-generate-performance-and-insights-data-from-a-dashboard)

# Manage a campaign from a dashboard

## Campaign management overview

You’ll use the dashboards you create in the Dashboard app to track your campaigns’ progress and performance. You can also save time by adjusting certain campaign elements—like budgets and bid prices—directly from these dashboards.

Refer to [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview) for more information about each dashboard element, and continue reading to learn how to manage your campaigns from a dashboard.

## Video tutorial: Manage a campaign from a dashboard

## Run and review AI Insights from a dashboard

> **More on CampaignPulse:** Refer to [Dashboard overview: AI Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_68302a50c0) for more information on CampaignPulse, including which campaigns are eligible and which campaign-performance elements it checks.

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature automatically checks critical blockers to a running campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for [eligible campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_08d9acd6e9).

Follow these steps to access CampaignPulse and review its insights from a dashboard:

1. Open the **View by** filter and select **Campaigns**.
2. Locate the **AI Insights** column in the dashboard table.
3. Select **Run Now**.
4. Select the **AI Insights** icon next to the desired campaign. This will open the **AI Insights** panel.
   1. A number indicates that CampaignPulse identified risks to campaign delivery.
   2. An enabled **AI Insights** icon with number indicates that the campaign is currently eligible for CampaignPulse, but no critical underdelivery risks were identified.
   3. A disabled **AI Insights** icon indicates that the campaign is currently ineligible for CampaignPulse.
5. If desired, filter the insights by type.

## Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard

You can change your campaigns’ total and daily budgets from a dashboard. Note that budgets are editable for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

### Change a campaign’s total budget

> **Set**, **Add**, **or Split:** When you change a campaign’s total budget from a dashboard, you’ll choose whether to **Set**, **Add**, or **Split** the new value. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Set, add, split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_f2238b5d23) for more information on these options.

You can update total budgets individually or in bulk.

#### Change total budgets one by one

Follow these steps to update a campaign’s total budget:

1. Double-click the cell in the desired campaign’s **Total Budget** column.
2. Enter the new value.
3. Select the checkmark icon. This will open the **Set Total Budget** pop-up window.
4. Review the most recent total budget and the new total budget you’ve entered.
5. Click **Set** to apply your changes.

#### Change total budgets in bulk

Follow these steps to update the total budgets of multiple campaigns:

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
2. Click **Total Budget** from the **Set Budget** menu. This will open the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
3. Enter the new value in the **New Total Budget** field.
4. Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split**, depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
   1. You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
5. Select **Change** to apply your edits.

### Change a campaign’s daily budget

You can update daily budgets individually or in bulk.

#### Change daily budgets one by one

Follow these steps to update a campaign’s daily budget:

1. Double-click the cell in the desired campaign’s **Daily Budget** column.
2. Enter the new value.
3. Select the checkmark icon. This will open the **Set Daily Budget** pop-up window.
4. Review the most recent daily budget and the new daily budget you’ve entered.
5. Click **Set** to apply your changes.

#### Change daily budgets in bulk

Follow these steps to update the daily budgets of multiple campaigns:

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
2. Click **Daily Budget** from the **Set Budget** menu. This will open the **Change Daily Budget** pop-up window.
3. Enter the new value in the **New Daily Budget** field.
4. Select **Change** to apply your edits.

## Manage a campaign’s Max Bid Price and Min Bid Price from a dashboard

You can change campaigns’ Max Bid Prices and Min Bid Prices individually or in bulk.

### Change bid prices one by one

Follow these steps to update a campaign’s bid price:

1. Double-click the cell in the desired campaign’s **Max Bid Price** or **Min Bid Price** column.
2. Enter the new value.
3. Select the checkmark icon. This will open the **Set Max Bid Price** or **Set Min Bid Price** pop-up window, depending on the column you chose.
4. Review the most recent bid price and the new bid price you’ve entered.
5. Click **Set** to apply your changes.

### Change bid prices in bulk

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
2. Click **Max Bid Price** or **Min Bid Price** from the **Set Budget** menu. This will open the **Set Max Bid Price** or **Set Min Bid Price** pop-up window, depending on the bid-price type you chose.
3. Enter the new value in the **Max Bid** or **Min Bid** field.
4. Select **Set** to apply your edits.

## Change a campaign’s name from a dashboard

Follow these steps to edit an existing campaign’s name directly from a dashboard:

1. Double-click the cell in the desired campaign’s **Campaign Name** column.
2. Enter the new name.
3. Select the checkmark icon to apply your changes.

## Pause a campaign from a dashboard

Follow these steps to pause campaigns individually or in bulk:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign(s) you’d like to pause.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Click **Pause** to temporarily stop ad serving for the campaign(s).

## Edit a campaign from a dashboard

You can edit one campaign at a time. Follow these steps to edit a campaign:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign you’d like to update.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Click **Edit** from the **Actions** menu. This will redirect you to the **Edit Campaign** workflow in the Campaigns app, where you can apply and save any changes.

## Apply Bid Model settings to a campaign from a dashboard

You can adjust bids with Bid Modifiers, allocate budgets with Spend Ratios, and add/edit/shift priorities with Dimension Priorities to optimize performance across certain campaign dimensions.

Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-what-is-a-bid-modifier) for more information on which dimensions are supported, and how to apply Bid Model settings to them directly from the Dashboard app.

## Change a campaign’s end date from a dashboard

Follow these steps to change campaign end dates individually or in bulk:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign(s) you’d like to update.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Click **Set End Date** from the **Actions** menu. This will open the **Change End Date** pop-up window.
5. Choose a new end date for the campaign(s).
6. Click **Change** to save your edits.

## Duplicate a campaign from a dashboard

Follow these steps to duplicate campaigns individually or in bulk:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign you’d like to duplicate.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Click **Duplicate** from the **Actions** menu. This will open the **Duplicate Campaign** pop-up window.
5. Choose the campaign’s insertion order (IO).
6. Set the campaign’s start and end dates.

After you select **Duplicate,** your duplicated campaign gets added to the IO as a draft. You’ll still need to review and activate it in the Campaigns app, if desired.

## Delete a campaign from a dashboard

> **Campaign deletion notice:** Selecting **Delete** will permanently delete the campaign and all of its settings. Refer to [Create or manage a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard) if you’d like to simply remove a campaign from a particular dashboard view instead. The resource includes steps on how to change an existing dashboard’s filters and settings, or create a new dashboard.

Follow these steps to delete existing campaigns individually or in bulk:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign(s) you’d like to delete.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign(s).
4. Click **Delete** from the **Actions** menu. This will open the **Delete Campaign?** pop-up window.
5. Confirm your selection to permanently delete the campaign(s).

# Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard

## Performance and insights overview

Monitor your campaigns’ real-time performance at a glance, or generate detailed custom reports and Insights reports—all directly from the Dashboard app.

Review [Create or manage a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard) to learn how to apply your preferred filters before generating reports and insights from a dashboard, or [Dashboard metrics and definitions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_155ad385e2) to understand the data featured in a dashboard table or report.

## Video tutorial: Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard

## Generate reports and insights

> **Does certain data appear to be incorrect?:** The time zone and date range that you select limits all reporting data to the events that occurred during that timeframe. Refer to [Select a time zone and date range](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_988f22700a), and adjust your selection to review data across a wider or narrower reporting window.

You can complete the following reporting actions from a dashboard:

- Export data
- Generate a custom report
- Generate an Insights report

### Export data from a dashboard

You can download a dashboard table to your device as a CSV or XLSX file, or save a spreadsheet directly to your Google Drive. Either choice will include each column and row shown in your dashboard’s current view based on the filters you’ve selected.

Follow these steps to download a dashboard table:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to determine which details appear in the table.
3. Open the **Columns** menu to add or remove metrics to the table.
4. Select the download icon.
5. Click **Download CSV** or **Download XLSX,** depending on your preferred file format.

### Generate a custom report from a dashboard

Follow these steps to generate a custom report from a dashboard:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to determine which details appear in the table.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaign(s).
4. Click **Create Report** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Create New Report** page of the **Reports** app.

The new report will automatically include the **Campaign** row, and filter the row to include the campaign(s) you selected in the Dashboard app.

Refer to the instructions included in [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) for more support with customizing and running the report.

### Generate an Insights report from a dashboard

> **Insights report requirements:** Eligibility criteria varies by Insights report type. Refer to [“Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) for more information on the data included in each report and to review their individual eligibility requirements.

Follow these steps to generate an Insights report from a dashboard:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to determine which details appear in the table.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaign(s).
   1. Certain Insights reports support one campaign per report, while others support multiple campaigns. Refer to “[Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) to locate requirement resources for each report type.
4. Select an Insights report type from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the Insights app to finish creating the report.

## Apply dashboard data to a campaign

Now you have the performance details necessary to improve your campaigns. You can apply optimizations to them directly from a dashboard. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for more details.

## Locate additional dashboard resources

- [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview)
- [Create or manage a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard)

# "Reporting and analytics" collection overview

## Collection summary

Data and analytics are central to connecting ad spend to business results, and determining whether a campaign achieved the goals that you defined for it.

The “Reporting and analytics” collection is your guide to uncovering and interpreting the data that you’ll use to improve performance across each of your strategies. Refer to this article’s content catalog to discover each of the resources that are available in this collection, and review them to make the most of your data in the IQM platform.

## Custom reports

With custom reports, you can drag and drop dimensions and metrics to create fully customized reports. Generate the analytics that matter most to the business, and use them to inform current and future campaign optimizations.

### Primary app(s)

### All articles

Review these resources to learn more about custom report creation:

| --- | --- |
| [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) | Dive into custom reports concepts and requirements, and locate dedicated resources for each reporting metric and dimension. |
| [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) | Create a new custom report; run, download, duplicate, or delete one you’ve already created; and schedule one-time or recurring email delivery. |
| [Troubleshoot a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343903-troubleshoot-a-report) | Uncover solutions to custom report issues related to creating a new report or managing an existing one. |

Review these resources to learn more about custom report metrics and dimensions:

| [Video completion rate (VCR) reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343754-video-completion-rate-vcr-reporting-metrics-overview#h_0dbe207ac2) | Learn about the seven VCR metrics that you can use to measure whether your video creatives are engaging your intended audience. |
| [Cost reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343783-cost-reporting-metrics-overview#h_e1f356fadc) | Learn about the four cost metrics that you can use to measure advertising costs and increase margins on certain ad strategies. |
| [Spending reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview) | Learn about the six spending metrics that you can use to measure the costs incurred from data targeting, media buying, and insights reporting. |
| [Performance reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) | Learn about the seven performance metrics that you can use to measure the breadth and effectiveness of a campaign. |
| [Household Reach overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15656937-household-reach-overview) | Learn what the Household Reach metric represents and how it's calculated. |

| [Reporting dimensions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343842-reporting-dimensions-overview) | Learn about the eight dimensions that you can add to a custom report. |

## Insights reports

Insights reports include a pre-defined set of metrics and dimensions. They surface granular data without the need for manual customization. Each Insights report is expertly crafted to focus on a distinct area, whether it’s a campaign’s available impressions or an audience’s characteristics and behaviors, for example. Create one to quickly identify trends and apply precise adjustments that drive better results for your campaigns.

title: Manage pacing

blocks.text: Monitoring pacing helps ensure that your campaigns spend in full. You can review pacing metrics at both the campaign and insertion order (IO) levels in the Campaigns and Dashboard apps.

Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform) to learn how to interpret pacing metrics, or continue reading to locate pacing performance details for your campaigns and IOs.

sections.heading: Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics
heading_path: Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics

sections.heading: Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app
heading_path: Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics
Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to locate Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics in the Campaigns app:
Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
Filter or search your IOs to locate the one(s) for which you want to monitor pacing.
Locate the **IO Pacing** column.
You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.
Select the IO for which you’d like to review campaign pacing and daily pacing metrics.
Filter or search the IO’s campaigns, if desired, to narrow the table view to specific campaigns.
Locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.
You can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.

sections.heading: Locate pacing metrics in the Dashboard app
heading_path: Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics
Locate pacing metrics in the Dashboard app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to locate campaign pacing, IO pacing, and daily pacing metrics in the Dashboard app:
Open the Dashboard app.
Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
Open the **View by** menu and select **Insertion Orders** or **Campaigns**.
If you selected **Campaigns**, locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.
If you selected **Insertion Orders**, locate the **IO Pacing** column in the table.
You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.

Like in the Campaigns app, you can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.
Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing are reporting metrics—not settings. You can, however, respond to pacing performance by allocating budgets and optimizing campaigns.
When an IO is pacing behind, you have the opportunity to allocate resources to the right strategies that are pacing as expected.
Choose one of two methods to move budgets between campaigns that are assigned to the same IO:
From the Campaigns app
From the Dashboard app

sections.heading: Shift budgets from the Campaigns app
heading_path: Shift budgets from the Campaigns app

blocks.text: Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
Choose an IO, then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one(s) for which you want to manage budgets.
Select the checkbox next to the campaign(s).
Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Total Budget**. This will open the **Set Total Budget** pop-up window.
Enter the new value in the **New Total Budget** field.
Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split** depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
Select **Set** to apply your edits.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Set, Add, Split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_f2238b5d23) for more information on the ways you can apply a total budget to one or more campaigns.

sections.heading: Shift budgets from the Dashboard app
heading_path: Shift budgets from the Dashboard app

blocks.text: You can change your campaigns’ total budgets from a dashboard. Note that budgets are edible for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.
Refer to [Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_3589c432de) for step-by-step instructions.

When a campaign is pacing behind, you can adjust your campaign settings to get spending back on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for support.

You can also set a daily budget to influence how a campaign spends its budget. Daily budgets are distributed evenly throughout the day and include the media costs, data costs, and pre-bid targeting costs associated with the campaign.

# Manage pacing

## Pacing overview

Monitoring pacing helps ensure that your campaigns spend in full. You can review pacing metrics at both the campaign and insertion order (IO) levels in the Campaigns and Dashboard apps.

Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform) to learn how to interpret pacing metrics, or continue reading to locate pacing performance details for your campaigns and IOs.

## Video tutorial: Manage pacing

## Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics

### Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to locate Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Filter or search your IOs to locate the one(s) for which you want to monitor pacing.
3. Locate the **IO Pacing** column.
   1. You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.
4. Select the IO for which you’d like to review campaign pacing and daily pacing metrics.
5. Filter or search the IO’s campaigns, if desired, to narrow the table view to specific campaigns.
6. Locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
   1. You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.

You can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.

### Locate pacing metrics in the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to locate campaign pacing, IO pacing, and daily pacing metrics in the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
3. Open the **View by** menu and select **Insertion Orders** or **Campaigns**.
4. If you selected **Campaigns**, locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
   1. You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.
5. If you selected **Insertion Orders**, locate the **IO Pacing** column in the table.
   1. You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.

Like in the Campaigns app, you can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.

## Manage pacing

Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing are reporting metrics—not settings. You can, however, respond to pacing performance by allocating budgets and optimizing campaigns.

### Manage IO pacing performance

When an IO is pacing behind, you have the opportunity to allocate resources to the right strategies that are pacing as expected.

Choose one of two methods to move budgets between campaigns that are assigned to the same IO:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

#### Shift budgets from the Campaigns app

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an IO, then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one(s) for which you want to manage budgets.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Total Budget**. This will open the **Set Total Budget** pop-up window.
5. Enter the new value in the **New Total Budget** field.
6. Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split** depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
   1. You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
7. Select **Set** to apply your edits.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Set, Add, Split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_f2238b5d23) for more information on the ways you can apply a total budget to one or more campaigns.

#### Shift budgets from the Dashboard app

You can change your campaigns’ total budgets from a dashboard. Note that budgets are edible for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_3589c432de) for step-by-step instructions.

### Manage campaign pacing performance

When a campaign is pacing behind, you can adjust your campaign settings to get spending back on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for support.

### Set a daily budget

You can also set a daily budget to influence how a campaign spends its budget. Daily budgets are distributed evenly throughout the day and include the media costs, data costs, and pre-bid targeting costs associated with the campaign.

Since daily budgets cap the amount that a campaign can spend each day, limit them to campaigns that are [pacing on track or pacing ahead](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform#h_6b2774c8f9).

Choose one of two methods to define a daily budget for an existing campaign:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

#### Set a daily budget from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to add or change a daily budget from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an IO, then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one(s) for which you want to add a daily budget.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Daily Budget.** This will open the **Set Daily Budget** pop-up window.
5. Enter the desired daily budget in the **Daily Budget** field.
6. Select **Set** to confirm your changes.

#### Set a daily budget from the Dashboard app

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_3589c432de) for step-by-step instructions on setting a daily budget from the Dashboard app.

## Locate additional pacing resources

- [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform)
- [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind)

# Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind

## Troubleshoot pacing issues

Pacing determines if your strategies are on track to spend in full based on how much they’ve spent so far and how much time is remaining in the campaign or insertion order (IO).

Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform) for more information on your pacing options in the IQM platform. Return to this article to review the primary factors that influence a campaign’s pacing performance.

In most cases, a campaign paces behind when bid prices are too low to win in programmatic auctions, or when a campaign’s targeting rules are too restrictive. Follow the guidelines below to assess these factors and apply any necessary changes to help ensure your campaigns spend in full.

## Win rate

Win rate describes the percentage of impressions that you won in a programmatic auction, which is impacted most heavily by the bid price. Low win rates can cause your campaign to pace behind.

Check the campaign’s win rate, then consider optimizing its bidding to catch up on spending.

### Check a campaign’s win rate

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
3. Choose a time zone and date range for the dashboard’s data.
4. Apply filters to determine which insertion orders (IOs) or campaigns populate in the table.

Review the win-rate data to uncover the percentage of impressions that the campaign won. Note that win rates are ranges, and there’s no one ideal win rate. In general, you can consider a win rate of 50-80% to be good, 20-30% to be normal, and under 20% to signal an opportunity to improve your bidding strategy.

### Optimize bid prices - Max Bid Price

Your Max Bid Price may be limiting the impressions that the campaign can bid on.

You can adjust a Max Bid Price from the same dashboard table that you used to assess your Win Rate performance. Refer to the steps in [Change Max Bid Prices from the Max Bid Price column](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_0bda217a19) to increase a campaign’s Max Bid Price.

### Optimize bid prices - Bid Modifiers

There may be instances where your campaign is pacing behind, and you suspect that it’s due to your bidding strategy, but you only want to increase bids for certain dimensions.

Bid Modifiers allows you to take control of your campaign’s bidding strategy. You can choose to optimize your campaigns by bidding a higher or lower price for the individual creatives that are most or least important to them.

Bid Modifiers are especially useful when a certain targeting rule is non-negotiable. Since you can’t change the targeting rule, you can bid more for it instead to help keep the campaign’s pacing on track. These multipliers can be changed or removed at any time, as needed.

### Optimize bid prices - Bid Shading

Bid shading allows the platform to automatically optimize your campaign to achieve the best effective cost per mille (eCPM). It lowers your bid when you can win at auction for a lower price than the max bid price you specified for a campaign.

We enable bid shading by default across all campaigns to help you bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying. However, if a campaign is pacing behind, you might consider temporarily turning off the bid shading feature.

Click the **Bid Shading** toggle switch in the **Campaign Info** section to disable the feature. You’ll know that bid shading is turned off when the toggle switch moves to the left and changes in color from blue to gray.

Select **Save** to apply your updated bid shading settings.

## Bid rate

The bid rate metric helps you determine how often a campaign’s targeting criteria and other details matched available bid requests. Low bid rates can cause your campaigns to pace behind.

Your campaign’s targeting strategies are the main factors that determine bid rate. It can only pace properly if there are enough available impressions that you can bid on after your targeting is applied. Check the campaign’s bid rate, then consider optimizing its targeting rules to catch up on spending.

You can assess a campaign’s bid rate by generating a Campaign Bidding Insights report in the Insights app. The charts and figures included in the report highlight the following campaign details:

- What impact each targeting rule had on bid-request drop offs for a campaign
- How many bid requests remained and passed through each subsequent stage
- What final bid rate your campaign achieved after it honored each of the targeting rules you defined

Refer to [Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to assess a campaign’s bid rate, and pinpoint which targeting parameters are causing the biggest drop off in your campaign’s bid requests.

For example, if a campaign’s Location targeting settings are too restrictive, you can widen the targeted area to allow the campaign to serve more impressions.

Refer to [Apply Campaign Bidding Insights to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report#h_6145e7762a) to make adjustments that will allow the campaign to bid on more ad impression opportunities.

## Optimization & Delivery

> **AI Based Optimization notice:** When you choose an AI Based Optimization method, you forfeit certain manual-optimization features such as Advanced Modeling. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the differences between the Rule Based and AI Based Optimization methods.

Refer to [Frequency capping overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8480958-frequency-capping-overview) and [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) and for more details.

### Audiences

The size and cost of a campaign’s audience(s) can impact its ability to pace as intended.

If the campaign is pacing behind and you suspect that it’s due to audience targeting settings, check these two items for each of your audiences:

- **Cost:** Review the **Cost (CPM)** column and determine whether you can create a similar audience for a lower CPM.
- **Size:** Review the Reach column and determine whether you’ll need to create a less restrictive audience for your campaign to spend in full.

### Creatives

Choosing the right ad format helps ensure your message resonates with the intended audience, and affects how users engage with your ad. The size of your creatives also determines where your ad can get placed across digital inventory.

Check a campaign’s creative size(s) when it’s pacing behind. If your creative is a less common size, it can significantly reduce the number of impressions you can bid on. Consider adding more sizes in the same creative format (e.g., Image, Video, Native) to the campaign to win more bids.

Review [Creative formats overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview) for more details about the ad formats that are supported on the IQM platform, and refer to [Creative Ad Specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs) to check recommended sizes and requirements.

### Blocklists

Allowlists and Blocklists help ensure that every marketing dollar goes toward the strategies that are the most likely to reach your target audience—but they also limit the number of impressions that you can bid on. This can put your campaigns at risk of spending in full.

If the campaign is pacing behind, evaluate each of the campaign’s Blocklists and determine whether you can remove any of them. Review [Allowlist and Blocklist overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview) and [Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472023-manage-campaign-allowlists-and-blocklists) for more details.

## Proactive pacing tips

In the future, take a proactive approach to pacing. Forecasting metrics provide a sense of scale to help you determine whether you have the right targeting and blocking strategies in place to spend your campaign budget in full and achieve campaign objectives.

Before you run a new campaign, leverage forecasting tools in the Campaigns and Planner apps to help ensure your campaign can pace on track or pace ahead.

### Forecast in the Campaigns app

Each time you create a new campaign or edit an existing one, you can select **Run Campaign Estimations** to generate forecasts based on the targeting rules you add to the campaign. These include the approximate size of your targetable audience, estimated reach and impressions, and the number of impressions you can expect to win at different bid prices.

Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.

### Forecast in the Planner app

Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions as you layer each targeting parameter onto your campaigns. This process helps highlight which rules will limit your strategy’s scale the most. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full.

Unlike the Campaigns app, the Planner app creates your campaigns for you based on the rules you share when you create a proposal. You can review and tweak those campaigns, add your creatives, and run the campaigns in just a few clicks.

Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.

## Locate additional pacing resources

- [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform)
- [Manage pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471928-manage-pacing)

blocks.text: Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. These rules relate to various campaign elements (such as Locations, Device IDs, Audiences, and more. For example, you can choose which relevant audiences you’d like to show your ad to, and which ones you’d like to prevent from seeing the ad, by adding those audiences to an Allowlist or Blocklist. Note that you may see Allowlists referred to as “white lists” or “target lists” and Blocklists referred to as “black lists” in other DSPs.

While customizing a campaign with Allowlists and Blocklists is essential for tailoring a campaign, these elements should be reserved for only the non-negotiable rules you’d like to apply to the campaign. Refer to Impact on reach and impressions for more information on scale considerations.

You’ll apply targeting criteria to a campaign when you want to define who you're willing to serve the ad to based on a specific set of criteria. For example, you can choose to only advertise to users who are browsing on a particular device, located in a particular geographic region, and belonging to a particular audience.
Your targeting settings get added to an “Allowlist” for each relevant dimension category.

You’ll apply blocking criteria to a campaign when you want to avoid showing your ads to users based on a specific set of criteria. For example, if you’re building an awareness campaign, you might want to prevent users who previously converted on your website from seeing the ad by adding a Retargeting audience to a Blocklist. You can also choose which sites or apps you’d like to avoid in order to maintain the brand’s image or exclude irrelevant inventory.
Your blocking settings get added to a “Blocklist” for each relevant dimension category.

Note that a campaign’s Allowlists and Blocklists are assigned an “OR” relationship, meaning that they work independently for each dimension. Allowlists and Blocklists are specific to each campaign element such as Audience, Location, Inventory, and more. This means that you can, for example, exclude a certain audience and include a certain site domain.

With an “OR” relationship, a campaign won’t bid on an impression if it matches any one of the exclusion criteria included in a Blocklist. For example, you can’t block one user who is located in New York “AND” browsing a particular site domain. The campaign will block any user who is either located in New York “OR” browsing a particular site domain.

## Allowlist and Blocklist overview

Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. These rules relate to various campaign elements (such as Locations, Device IDs, Audiences, and more. For example, you can choose which relevant audiences you’d like to show your ad to, and which ones you’d like to prevent from seeing the ad, by adding those audiences to an Allowlist or Blocklist. Note that you may see Allowlists referred to as “white lists” or “target lists” and Blocklists referred to as “black lists” in other DSPs.

While customizing a campaign with Allowlists and Blocklists is essential for tailoring a campaign, these elements should be reserved for only the non-negotiable rules you’d like to apply to the campaign. Refer to Impact on reach and impressions for more information on scale considerations.

### Allowlists

You’ll apply targeting criteria to a campaign when you want to define who you're willing to serve the ad to based on a specific set of criteria. For example, you can choose to only advertise to users who are browsing on a particular device, located in a particular geographic region, and belonging to a particular audience.

Your targeting settings get added to an “Allowlist” for each relevant dimension category.

### Blocklists

You’ll apply blocking criteria to a campaign when you want to avoid showing your ads to users based on a specific set of criteria. For example, if you’re building an awareness campaign, you might want to prevent users who previously converted on your website from seeing the ad by adding a Retargeting audience to a Blocklist. You can also choose which sites or apps you’d like to avoid in order to maintain the brand’s image or exclude irrelevant inventory.

Your blocking settings get added to a “Blocklist” for each relevant dimension category.

### AND/OR relationships

Note that a campaign’s Allowlists and Blocklists are assigned an “OR” relationship, meaning that they work independently for each dimension. Allowlists and Blocklists are specific to each campaign element such as Audience, Location, Inventory, and more. This means that you can, for example, exclude a certain audience and include a certain site domain.

With an “OR” relationship, a campaign won’t bid on an impression if it matches any one of the exclusion criteria included in a Blocklist. For example, you can’t block one user who is located in New York “AND” browsing a particular site domain. The campaign will block any user who is either located in New York “OR” browsing a particular site domain.

Example Blocklist:

- New York
- Site Domain A

| **Impression details** | **Bid decision (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| Texas, **Site Domain A** | N - The impression matches a blocked Site Domain dimension. |
| **New York**, Site Domain C | N- The impression matches a blocked Location dimension. |
| California, **Site Domain A** | N - The impression matches a blocked Site Domain dimension. |
| California, Site Domain B | Y - The impression doesn’t match any blocked dimensions. |

Allowlists follow a similar logic, but will include rather than exclude the items you’ve specified. Using the same example, you can’t target one user who is located in New York “AND” browsing a particular site domain. The campaign will bid on an impression if it matches either one of these inclusion criteria.

Allowlist rules differ slightly from Blocklist rules. If you target certain campaign dimensions, then all other dimensions in the same dimension category are excluded. For example, if your campaign targets New York and California, it’ll only bid on New York impressions or California impressions. This means that all other Locations are effectively blocked from the campaign.

Example Allowlist:

- New York
- California
- Site Domain A

| **Impression details** | **Bid decision (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| **New York**, Site Domain B | N - If only **Site Domain A** is targeted, the campaign won’t serve ads on other site domains. |
| Texas, **Site Domain A** | N - If only **New York** and **California** are targeted, the campaign won’t serve ads to users in other locations**.** |
| **California**, **Site Domain A** | Y - The impression matches all Allowlist rules. |

> **Impressions that match targeted and blocked dimensions:** There may be instances when an available impression matches one targeted dimension and another blocked dimension. For example, the campaign is blocking the site domain and targeting the mobile operating system (OS). The campaign will only bid on impressions that meet every targeting requirement that you’ve defined. In the same way, it will never bid on an impression that matches any of your campaign’s blocked dimensions.

## Campaign elements to allow or block

You can create an Allowlist or Blocklist for each dimension category, or element, listed below.

| **Element** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Location | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which states, DMAs, counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses to include or exclude. |
| Audience | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which audiences to include or exclude based on your own user data, or segments from IQM or any of our data providers. These audiences are made up of groups of users who share common characteristics like age, gender, or home ownership status, for example. |
| Device | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which device IDs to include or exclude. In the **Bid Model** app, choose which device elements to include or exclude after they appear in the ad-serving data. These may include individual devices (TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile) or channels (app, web, connected TV [CTV], or over the top [OTT]). |
| Inventory* | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which Android packages, iOS Apple IDs, and/or site domains to include or exclude. In the **Inventory** app, assign inventory to a **Global Blocklist** to ensure that your ads are only displayed on high-quality websites that align with the brand image and target audience. The platform will immediately stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked. In the **Bid Model** app, choose which deal ID(s), Open Exchange inventory, and/or publisher categories that you want the campaign to include or exclude. |
| Advanced | In the **Campaigns** app, indicate which device ID(s) and/or internet protocol (IP) addresses that you want the campaign to include or exclude. |

* Refer to [What are Blocklisted Inventories?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6962891-what-are-blocklisted-inventories) for more information on inventory Blocklists.
