# Bid Model frequently asked questions (FAQ)

## FAQ overview

You’ll need to follow specific steps to successfully apply Bid Model settings to a campaign, and review certain concepts to understand how Bid Model components work individually and in tandem. If you encounter an error, are blocked from adding or managing Bid Model settings, or have questions related to how they work, refer to these resources first:

- [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview)
- [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview)
- [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview)
- [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

Return to this article to review additional questions that you may encounter related to Bid Modeling.

## General Bid Model FAQ

**Q: What is a Bid Model?**

**A:** A Bid Model is the set of rules that you apply to a campaign to optimize its performance. These rules allow you to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities for supported dimensions. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) to learn more about Bid Modeling, including eligibility requirements and supported dimensions.

**Q: What is a Bid Model component?**

**A:** Bid Model components include [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), [Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview), and [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview). While these granular adjustments are optional, they allow you to take greater control of your campaign’s optimizations and, ultimately, its performance.

**Q:** **What is the difference between a dimension category and a dimension value?**

**A:** Dimension values are the specific targeting parameters that you can adjust by applying one or more [Bid Model components](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f) to them. For example, you might choose for the campaign to prioritize spend for one creative over another, while still targeting both of them.

You can assign Bid Model settings to dimensions across the Creative, Location, Device, and Inventory categories. Refer to [Supported dimensions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177) for a list of all supported dimensions and dimension values.

**Q: Which Bid Model component (Priority, Spend Ratio, Bid Modifier) can I apply to the dimensions that my campaign is targeting?**

**A:** You can apply settings for any one Bid Model component or multiple components if both the campaign and its dimension values are eligible. Refer to these resources for more information on component-level eligibility requirements:

- [Spend Ratio eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_d2298002f2)
- [Priority eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview#h_3acf0c831f)
- [Bid Modifier eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview#h_c820e48631)

Note that certain Bid Modifier components are required when others are applied. For example, if you’ve applied a [strict Spend Ratio](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_0fc36087da), you won’t be able to apply a Priority to the same dimension value. However, you’re required to define a Priority when you apply a [flexible Spend Ratio](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_98b3a47af1) to a dimension value. Full details of these limitations and dependencies are available in the three resources linked above.

**Q: What does Others signify in each Bid Model table?**

**A:** The **Others** row functions as a bucket. When you apply Bid Model settings to only certain dimension values, the other dimension values that you’re targeting in the same dimension category and dimension are automatically aggregated in **Others**.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Others](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_d4328065fd) for more information.

**Q: How do I add the Others row to a Bid Model table?**

**A:** Follow the steps to apply a Bid Model to a Location, Creative, Device, or Inventory dimension:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

When you reach the step to choose the dimension values for which you’d like to apply Bid Model settings and **+ Add to Modeling**, the dimension values that you choose will display as individual rows in the table. All other dimension values within that category are captured in the **Others** category automatically.

**Q: What does Unknown signify in a Bid Model table?**

**A:** When bid requests pass through the IQM platform, it assesses key information about those requests to help ensure that they match a campaign’s targeting criteria. In certain instances, one or more details—such as Inventory or Location information—is unable to be gathered after the ad is served. These events are captured in the **Unknown** row.

The **Unknown** row may also signify that your campaign previously targeted an item that you have since blocked or removed from its targeting settings.

Note that you can only apply advanced modeling settings (Bid Modifiers, Spend Ratios, Priorities) to known dimension values.

**Q: Why am I unable to apply Bid Model settings to a Deal ID when this dimension is supported?**

**A:** This issue is likely due to one of the following three reasons:

1. The campaign is no longer targeting the Deal ID(s) or is blocking the Deal ID(s). Only targeted deals can be modeled.
2. The deal was duplicated from another deal that was originally created by you, a Workspace admin, or an IQM administrator. Only non-duplicated deals can be modeled.
3. You’re attempting to apply Bid Modifiers to the Deal ID(s). Bid Modifiers can only be applied to [supported dimensions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177).

**Q: What happens if I apply multiple Bid Model settings to the same dimension value?**

**A:** When you apply multiple components for the same dimension value, ad opportunities pass through a decision-making process. The Bid Model assesses whether serving is enabled for a dimension value at each stage based on the Bid Model components you defined and the campaign’s current performance. Refer to [Applying multiple Bid Model components](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_f9528b3c93) for more information on how this decision-making process works.

**Q: Why is the Bid Model app’s Model tab disabled?**

**A:** A campaign must target at least one dimension value from a given dimension for the app to enable that category’s **Model** tab. For example, you’ll need to target at least one state, city, or ZIP code in your campaign to apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension value.

Open the Campaigns app to review or update your campaign’s targeting settings, and refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) to confirm that the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling.

**Q: Why is the Advanced Modeling button disabled in the Campaigns app?**

**A:** A campaign must target at least one dimension value from a given dimension for the app to enable that category’s **Model** tab. For example, you’ll need to target at least one state, city, or ZIP code in your campaign to apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension value.

Review or update your campaign’s targeting settings, and refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) to confirm that the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling.

**Q: My campaign is set up and meets the requirements. Why is the Advanced Modeling button disabled in the Campaigns app?**

**A:** Confirm that you saved the campaign. This will create a campaign ID, which you’ll need in order to apply and manage Bid Model settings.

**Q: Why haven’t the changes that I applied in the Bid Model app been reflected in the Campaigns app?**

**A:** You’ll need to refresh the page in the Campaigns app to reflect any changes that you applied in the Bid Model app. While the changes typically appear within ten minutes, allow up to one hour before troubleshooting.

**Q: What does the page-and-eyeball icon signify next to a dimension value in the Bid Model table?**

**A:** After your campaign starts running, it might serve ads for dimension values in a dimension category that you didn’t include the campaign’s targeting parameters. These dimension values are identified from the campaign’s serving data over the past three months, captured in the Bid Model table, and labeled with an eyeball icon.

You can leave these items un-modelled, or apply a Bid Model setting to those dimension values directly in the Bid Model app. Note that the new dimension values that appeared in the serving data won’t appear in the campaign’s details in the Campaigns app.

**Q: What does the exclamation point icon signify next to a dimension value in the Bid Model table?**

**A:** When a dimension features the exclamation point icon, it signifies two things: The campaign previously targeted and served ads for that dimension, and the same dimension is no longer included in the campaign. In other words, the campaign previously targeted an item that you have since blocked or removed from its targeting settings.

**Q: What is a use case for applying Bid Model settings to dimension values that were identified from the campaign’s serving data?**

**A:** There may be instances where you’d like for a campaign to continue bidding on the dimension value, but not explicitly add it to the campaign’s targeting parameters. You can also apply Bid Model settings to dimension values that appear in the serving data to indirectly impact the Bid Model settings of targeted dimension values that share a parent/child relationship with the served dimension values.

For example, an advertiser’s campaign is targeting a set of cities, including **San Francisco**. The state of **California** appears in the campaign’s serving data and is listed in the Bid Model app. These dimension values have a parent/child relationship since **San Francisco** city is located in **California** state.

The advertiser can apply Bid Model settings to **State** dimensions to control the serving behavior in those states’ targeted child locations, and achieve the following outcomes:

- Apply a Spend Ratio setting to **California** state to put a cap on how much the campaign can spend on this state. Doing so would indirectly cap the campaign’s ability to serve in **San Francisco** city.
- Apply a Bid Modifier to **California** state to increase or decrease the bid price for **San Francisco** city.
- Apply a Priority to **California** to indirectly change the serving priority of **San Francisco**.

**Q: How long will it take for my new, changed, or removed Bid Model settings to apply to my campaign?**

**A:** In most cases, the campaign will reflect all Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifier settings within one hour.

**Q:** **Can I apply a Bid Model component (Bid Modifier, Spend Ratio, Priority) to a dimension value that’s not listed in the Bid Model app?**

**A:** No. You can add a dimension value to the Bid Model app by editing the campaign in the Campaigns app and adding the dimension value to its targeting rules. Keep in mind that the dimension value must also be included in the [supported dimension categories](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177) to be eligible for Bid Modeling.

**Q: How can I review a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings?**

**A:** Advertisers can review a campaign’s Bid Model settings directly in the Bid Model app, and workspace admins can view them in the Customers app.

**Q: How can I quickly determine which dimension values have Bid Model settings applied to them?**

**A:** Modeled [dimension values](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177) feature an icon in the **Bid Model** app, which indicates that modeling has been applied.

**Q: What are Dimension Bundles**?

**A:** A **Bundle** is a container or shell that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Instead of configuring their settings individually for each dimension value, you’ll apply them once at the **Bundle** level, and those settings automatically apply to everything inside.

You can add up to 1,000 dimension values to a single **Bundle**, and create up to 10 **Bundles** per campaign. [Refer to Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

**Q: Can I apply modeling settings to the child items that I added to a Bundle**?

**A:** No, Bid Model settings are applied at the **Bundle** level. Those settings are automatically applied to everything inside. This means you should reserve **Bundling** dimension values for instances when you’d like to apply the same Bid Model settings to more than one dimension value.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

**Q: How should I interpret a Bundle’s metrics?**

**A:** A **Bundle’s** title row displays the total metric data of its child items (individual dimension values).

**Q: Why are my Remove From Bundle or Save To Bundle options disabled?**

**A:** You likely have selected multiple dimension values, with some already assigned to a **Bundle** and others not yet assigned to one. To enable the **Remove From Bundle** option, all selected dimension values must already be included in the **Bundle**. In the same way, to enable the **Save To Bundle** option, all selected dimension values must not already be included in a **Bundle**.

**Q: What happens if I add a modeled dimension value to a Bundle?**

**A:** All of the dimension value’s existing Spend Ratio, Priority, and Bid Modifier settings will be replaced by the selected **Bundle’s** settings.

**Q: How do performance filters work for Bundled dimension values?**

**A:** Your performance filter settings will apply to both the **Bundle** and its individual child items via an “OR” relationship. This means that the table will display a dimension value and **Bundle** if either one meets the filter condition(s) you set.

## Spend Ratio FAQ

**Q:** **What is a Spend Ratio?**

**A:** A Spend Ratio is a Bid Model component that allows you to take control of your campaign’s spending pattern. You can specify how much of a campaign’s total budget you’d like to allocate to each Creative, Location, Device, or Inventory dimension that your campaign is targeting. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more information.

**Q: Can I repeat the same Spend Ratio for multiple dimension values within the same dimension category?**

**A:** Yes. While you can designate any percentage of your campaign’s budget to each dimension value, note that the sum of all percentages in a single dimension category must equal or exceed 100% for flexible Spend Ratios, and equal 100% exactly for strict Spend Ratios. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more details.

**Q: Can I remove a Spend Ratio from a campaign after it’s already started spending?**

**A:** Yes. You can add, edit, or delete a Spend Ratio from a campaign at any time. Note that you can only define Spend Ratios that equal or exceed the amount that the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to 21% or higher.

The sum of all percentages in a single dimension category must also equal or exceed 100% for flexible Spend Ratios, and equal 100% exactly for strict Spend Ratios. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more details.

**Q: Why can’t I change the Spend Ratio for my campaign?**

**A:** You can add, edit, or delete a Spend Ratio at any time; however, you’ll need to enter a Spend Ratio that’s greater than or equal to the percentage that the campaign has already spent on that dimension value.

**Q: Why can’t I apply a Spend Ratio to the dimension values that my campaign is targeting?**

**A:** There may be certain requirements that the campaign or its targeting dimensions don’t currently meet. For example, the campaign may be targeting only Publisher Categories, which would make it ineligible for Spend Ratio settings. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) to review a full list of eligibility criteria.

**Q: Why can’t I apply Spend Ratios to Publisher Categories?**

**A:** Spend Ratios aren’t supported for Publisher Categories because a single impression may belong to two or more Publisher Categories.

For example, an advertiser defines a total campaign budget of 1,000 impressions. The campaign serves 100 impressions, which happen to each belong to 10 different Publisher Categories. This scenario would cause the campaign to behave as if it served the full 1,000-impression budget (100 impressions x 10 Publisher Categories) rather than the actual 100 served impressions due to overlap.

**Q: What happens if I remove a Spend Ratio from only one dimension value in a dimension?**

**A:** If you’ve assigned a Spend Ratio percentage to one or more other dimension values in the same dimension, the dimension value will move to the **Others** category.

You may also need to adjust the Spend Ratios of the **Others** row, or the other dimension values in the dimension, to ensure that their percentages still equal or exceed 100% for flexible Spend Ratios, and equal 100% exactly for strict Spend Ratios. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more details.

**Q: How do I apply, change, or delete a Spend Ratio?**

**A:** The exact steps you’ll follow will differ based on the [dimension](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177). Refer to the dedicated resources linked below to learn how to add, edit, or remove a Spend Ratio or another Bid Model component based on the dimension category:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

**Q:** **Is there a limit to the amount of times I can change a Spend Ratio?**

**A:** There’s no limit. You can add, edit, or delete any Bid Model component as many times as you’d like if the campaign is still [eligible for Bid Modeling](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_29428f4f4b). Note that you can only define Spend Ratios that equal or exceed the amount that the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to 21% or higher.

The sum of all percentages in a single dimension category must also equal or exceed 100% for flexible Spend Ratios, and equal 100% exactly for strict Spend Ratios. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more details.

**Q:** How are Spend Ratios applied to Bundled dimension values?

**A:** A **Bundle**’s Spend Ratio can be either Strict or Flexible; however, all of the child items included in the **Bundle** are treated as having Flexible Spend Ratios in either circumstance until the assigned Spend Ratio is met (Strict), or met or exceeded (Flexible).

Refer to [Spend Ratios applied to Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_6138d8adf0) for more information and examples.

## Priority FAQ

**Q: What is a Priority?**

**A:** A Priority is a Bid Model component that allows you to take control of the way your campaign delivers impressions. You can specify the order in which a campaign should attempt to deliver impressions across the Creative, Location, or Inventory dimensions that your campaign is targeting. Refer to [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) for more information.

**Q: Why can’t I set a Priority when I’ve applied another Bid Model setting to the same dimension?**

**A:** You’ve likely already chosen a [strict Spend Ratio](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_0fc36087da) for the same dimension. You can apply a Priority to dimension values that are assigned a [flexible Spend Ratio](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_98b3a47af1). Refer to [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) for more information on the differences between flexible and strict Spend Ratios, and to review related requirements.

**Q: Can I review Priorities for an expired or deleted campaign?**

**A:** Yes. You can still view priorities if a campaign is expired or deleted; however, you won’t be able to add, change, or remove any Priorities that are assigned to expired or deleted campaigns.

If desired, you can update a campaign’s date range to restore an expired campaign.

**Q:** **Can I repeat the same Priority for multiple dimension values?**

**A:** Yes. You can assign the same priority to more than one dimension value. Any dimension values featuring the same priority will be treated equally during campaign execution. Refer to [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) for more information and examples.

**Q:** **How do I apply, change, or delete a Priority?**

**A:** The exact steps you’ll follow will differ based on the [dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177). Refer to the dedicated resources linked below to learn how to add, edit, or remove a Priority or another Bid Model component based on the dimension category:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

**Q:** **Is there a limit to the amount of times I can change a Priority?**

**A:** There’s no limit. You can add, edit, or delete any Bid Model component as many times as you’d like if the campaign is still [eligible for Bid Modeling](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_29428f4f4b).

**Q: How will I know when serving is enabled for a dimension value based on the latest performance check?**

**A:** You’ll know that serving is enabled for a dimension value when the circle next to it in the **Priority** column changes from gray to green. This indicates that ads are being targeted for that dimension value based on the latest pacing performance check. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Daily spend pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview#h_5bfddaa2d6) for more information.

**Q: When is my campaign’s next performance check?**

**A:** The frequency of pacing checks increases based on how soon the campaign is ending. Refer to [Daily spend pacing - Pacing-check schedule](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview#h_f173e27a17) for full pacing-check details based on a campaign’s remaining duration, or open the campaign in the Bid Model app. The **Modeled** tab will display the next performance check’s date and time toward the top of the page.

## Bid Modifier FAQ

**Q: What is a Bid Modifier?**

**A:** The Bid Modifier Bid Model component allows you to take control of your campaign’s bidding strategy. You can choose to bid a higher or lower price for the Creative, Location, Device, or Inventory targeting dimensions based on their importance to your campaign. Refer to [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) for more information.

**Q: Why can’t I apply a Bid Modifier to the dimension values that my campaign is targeting?**

**A:** Confirm that you defined a Base Bid Price and Max Bid Price for the campaign. The Bid Model multiplies the Base Bid Price by any Bid Modifiers you define for a dimension value while staying below the Max Bid Price.

If you’ve already defined a Base Bid Price and Max Bid Price, there may be other requirements that the campaign or its targeting dimensions don’t currently meet. For example, the campaign may be targeting Private Marketplace (PMP) deal IDs, which would make it ineligible for Bid Modifier settings. Refer to [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) to review a full list of eligibility criteria.

**Q: How are Bid Modifiers applied when a campaign is targeting both Open Exchange inventory and Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory?**

**A:** The bid request determines how Bid Modifiers are executed. Incoming bid requests from the Open Exchange will bid using the bid-modified Base Bid Price, while incoming traffic from the targeted Deal ID will instead bid the Max Bid Price. In other words, no Bid Modifier settings are applied to the Deal ID dimension.

Refer to [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) for more information.

**Q:** **What happens if I don’t add a Bid Modifier to a dimension value?**

**A:** Bid Modifiers are an optional optimization tool. The campaign will observe the same Max Bid Price for all of the dimension values that it’s targeting if no Bid Modifiers are applied. If you apply Bid Modifiers to only certain dimension values in a dimension, however, you will define a Base Bid Price, which the campaign will use to modify the bids of only those dimension values.

**Q: Can I review Bid Modifiers for an expired or deleted campaign?**

**A:** Yes. You can still view bid settings if a campaign is expired or deleted; however, you won’t be able to add, change, or remove any Bid Modifiers that are assigned to expired or deleted campaigns.

If desired, you can update a campaign’s date range to restore an expired campaign.

**Q: Can I repeat the same Bid Modifier for multiple dimension values in the same dimension category?**

**A:** Yes. The Bid Model will treat each Bid Modifier independently. Once the campaign confirms that an ad opportunity matches all campaign and Bid Model settings for that particular dimension value, it multiplies the dimension value’s Bid Modifier by the campaign’s Base Bid Price and places a bid in the programmatic auction.

**Q: What happens if I apply a Bid Modifier to multiple dimension categories (Locations, Creatives, Inventory, Device)?**

**A:** When an incoming ad requests matches dimension values across two or more dimensions categories, the campaign multiplies all applicable Bid Modifiers together, and multiplies the result by the Base Bid Price you defined for the campaign.

Refer to [Bid Modifier - Multiple dimension categories](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview#h_7d96d9311a) to review examples of how this process works.

**Q: What bid is placed when a dimension value’s modified bid exceeds the Max Bid Price I chose for the campaign?**

**A:** In instances when the Bid Modified value exceeds the Max Bid Price, the campaign will bid the Max Bid Price instead.

**Q: Why can I edit the Others row for Spend Ratios and Priorities, but not for Bid Modifiers?**

**A:** By definition, items included in **Others** have no Bid Modifiers applied to them. All dimension values included in the **Others** bucket are assigned a Bid Modifier of **1X**, meaning that the campaign should observe the Max Bid Price that you defined for the campaign.

If you want to change the Bid Modifiers of any items included in **Others**, you can do so by returning to the **All Creatives**, **All Inventory**, **All Devices**, or **All Locations** tab in the Bid Model app—depending on the dimension category—and managing each dimension value individually. Refer to the resources below for step-by-step instructions on applying a Bid Modifier to a dimension:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

**Q:** **How do I apply, change, or delete a Bid Modifier?**

**A:** The exact steps you’ll follow will differ based on the [dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177). Refer to the dedicated resources linked below to learn how to add, edit, or remove a Bid Modifier or another Bid Model component based on the dimension category:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension-category)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension#h_21205bd024)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

**Q:** **Is there a limit to the amount of times I can change a Bid Modifier?**

**A:** There’s no limit. You can add, edit, or delete any Bid Model component as many times as you’d like if the campaign is still eligible for Bid Modeling.

## Locate additional Bid Model resources

title: DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments

blocks.text: When you bid on an ad placement, verification partners like DoubleVerify (DV) determine whether or not it’s appropriate for the brand based on a predetermined set of criteria that you define. These predetermined rules can apply to several factors including fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement. Review [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information about these pre-bid categories, and refer to the IQM platform for each segment’s current pricing details.

DV identifies a range of IVT behaviors including fraud bots, non-human data center traffic, hijacked devices, and emulators. Target DV fraud and IVT segments to exclude sites or apps based on the percentage of fraud or IVT detected, ranging from insufficient data to 100% IVT. You can also exclude them based on the specific type of invalid traffic, such as sites with high fraud percentages or impressions with missing IP addresses.

blocks.text: DV brand suitability segments identify impressions for exclusion targeting based on a variety of brand suitability categories. Target these segments to exclude sites or apps based on their risk level, ranging from moderate to severe, age rating, or consumer-review rating. You can also exclude them based on whether the content is unknown or unrated, or related to copyright infringement or malware.
**Targeting Type**
**Segment Name**
**Segment Description**
Avoidance targeting of unknown inventory
Unknown Brand Suitability

DV has no classification information about the page (i.e., no avoidance or contextual categories) or the auction does not contain a web page URL or bundle ID/App ID that can be evaluated for brand suitability. This segment is made available to maximize the brand suitability protection for especially cautious bidders by allowing them to exclude impressions when brand suitability is unknown.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Aggregated: All Severe Content
Group of the most explicit and commonly-used DV avoidance categories.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Adult & Sexual - High Risk

Content involving adult and sexual topics that may be inappropriate for children including sexual themes, sexually suggestive images, nudity, and pornography. This segment includes pornography and the depiction of sexual acts and nudity; graphic description of sexual acts; discussion of adult themes and sexual acts in user-generated and/or unmoderated content; and irresponsible treatment of sexual harassment or sex crimes.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Alcohol - High Risk

Content that facilitates or discusses the consumption of alcohol including the promotion or irresponsible treatment of underage drinking, binge drinking, alcoholism, drunk driving, illegal sale/production of alcohol; and discussion of alcohol in user-generated content and/or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Aviation Disasters - High Risk

Content about catastrophic events involving aviation including both accidental and intentional acts such as hijackings and other attacks, runway accidents, or events that lead to downed aircrafts. This segment includes the irresponsible treatment of aviation disaster events (e.g., jokes about crashes) and discussion of aviation disasters in user-generated content and/or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Crime - High Risk

Content about actions that are illegal or harmful to the general public, and generally forbidden by law (not specific to a jurisdiction). This includes criminal actions and allegations.The segment includes promotion or irresponsible treatment of crime, discussions of serious violent crime in user-generated or unmoderated content, and guides and instructions on performing crimes. Financial and/or political crimes are not included within the category.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Death & Injuries - High Risk

Content that discusses or depicts all manners of death, severe injury, and medical emergencies. The category includes content related to specific instances of death and severe injury, as well as general discussion of these topics. This segment includes explicit, graphic depictions of death and severe injury; discussion of death and injury in user-generated or unmoderated content, and irresponsible treatment of instances of death and injury.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Drug Abuse - High Risk

Content about drug use including the use of illegal drugs and abuse of prescription/OTC drugs. This includes content about drugs, drug-related paraphernalia, and acts performed under the influence of drugs. This segment includes the discussion of illegal drugs in user-generated or unmoderated content, glorification or irresponsible treatment of drugs, and guides and explainers on how to use/acquire illegal drugs.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Extreme & Graphic

Content which includes extreme or highly graphic treatment of sensitive topic areas. This includes, but is not limited to, the following content: explicit depictions of sexual acts, highly graphic depictions of violence or harm, promotion of illegal activity, facilitation of purchase/consumption of illegal drugs, hate speech, promotion of terrorism, and the facilitation of underage consumption of tobacco or alcohol.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Hate Speech & Cyberbullying - High Risk

Content related to biased, derogatory, or offensive actions towards any individuals or groups. Content that may incite violence against individuals or groups within a protected class is also within the category.

The overall category is not limited to instances of harmful language or behavior. It also includes content about such language or behavior, such as news coverage about a hate crime or cyberbullying, as well as content about groups that are associated with such activities.

This segment includes content that includes hate speech or derogatory terms in a demeaning, harmful manner; discussion of hate crimes, hate groups, hate speech, discrimination, and cyberbullying in user-generated and/or unmoderated content; content that promotes or glorifies hate groups; and content that provides information on how to commit cyberbullying or hate crimes.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Human-made Disasters - High Risk

Content about human-made disaster events that are technological, sociological, or environmental with a human cause. Some topics include war, genocide, and industrial accidents. This segment includes the promotion or irresponsible treatment of human-made disasters, and discussion of human-made disasters in user-generated or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Incentivized/Malware/Clutter
Content associated with malicious online practices such as malware, viruses, spam, adware, ad clutter and incentivized traffic.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Inflammatory Politics & News

News and political content associated with or exhibiting inflammatory points of view; potentially fake, unreliable or unsubstantiated information; or significant political intolerance, hateful or threatening rhetoric, or other significantly controversial elements.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Natural Disasters - High Risk

Content about natural disasters, which are primarily earth- or disease-related harmful events. Topic examples include wildfires, famine, epidemics, and pandemics. This segment includes the irresponsible treatment of natural disaster events, and discussion of natural disasters in user-generated or unmoderated content. Only content about the negative aspects of COVID-19 are included.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Piracy/Copyright Infringement

Sites and apps presently or historically associated with access to copyrighted material (movies, music, books, etc.) without appropriate controls, licensing, or permission. Access methods include, but are not limited to, streaming, downloads, peer-to-peer and search. The Copyright Infringement category does not in any way characterize the site or app itself as being directly or indirectly engaged in illegal behavior. As used in this category definition, the term Copyright Infringement does not represent legal language as defined in various laws, statutes and ordinances or as conventionally used in courts or other legal proceedings, but rather a custom definition strictly for advertising classification purposes.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Profanity - High Risk
Content that contains or is about language considered vulgar, obscene, or inappropriate and content about the usage of profanity.

This segment includes any usage of obscene, vulgar, or profane terms in user generated or unmoderated content; and content that contains gratuitous or glamorized usage of obscene, vulgar or profane terms.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Terrorism - High Risk

Content related to acts of terrorism, terrorist attacks, terrorist organizations, and facilitation of terrorism. This segment includes the promotion or irresponsible treatment of terrorism, content that provides information on how to commit acts of terrorism or join terrorist organizations, and discussion of terrorism in user-generated or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Tobacco & eCigarettes - High Risk

Content about tobacco and tobacco products such as cigarettes, cigars, pipes, smokeless tobacco, and tobacco smoking simulators such as e-cigarettes. This includes any aspects of this topic, including health, business, politics, and lifestyle.

This segment includes discussion of how to use, make, or purchase tobacco and e-cigarettes; promotion or irresponsible content about smoking; and discussion of tobacco and e-cigarettes in user-generated or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content
Vehicle Disasters - High Risk

Content related to accidental or intentional vehicle disasters. This includes sea and land vehicles such as boats, buses, cars, and trains. This segment includes irresponsible treatment of vehicle disaster events, and discussion of vehicle disasters in user-generated or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of severe content

Content related to acts of physical harm and weapons that cause physical harm. The category includes content related to both legal and illegal violent subjects such as violent sports, firearms, shootings, violent crime, animal cruelty, and more.

This segment includes promotion or irresponsible treatment of violence and weapons; the offer of weapons for sale or guidance on where/how to purchase weapons; and discussion of violence and weapons in user-generated or unmoderated content.
Avoidance targeting of moderate content

This tier groups together the avoidance categories that are more selectively used by advertisers to customize their brand suitability profile.
Avoidance targeting of moderate content

Technology for serving ads online. Sites and apps to which this category is assigned rarely contain content.
Avoidance targeting of moderate content

Content that involves adult and sexual topics that may be inappropriate for children including content containing sexual themes, sexually suggestive images, nudity, and pornography. In addition to High Risk content, this segment also includes discussion of mature themes and sexual acts in news, dramatic depictions, or entertainment content; and depiction of individuals in lingerie or in sexually suggestive poses.
Avoidance targeting of moderate content

blocks.text: DV’s fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, and supply refinement segments use avoidance targeting. Avoidance targeting excludes the content or environments that aren’t aligned with the brand’s image or a campaign’s objectives. When you target these avoidance segments, you help ensure ads don’t show up in places that could harm the brand’s image or reach the wrong audience.

DV’s viewability segments use inclusion targeting. Inclusion targeting aims to include only the URLs and apps that have historically achieved specific viewability performance. When you target these inclusion segments, you help ensure ads have the opportunity to be seen by a user.

# DoubleVerify (DV) pre-bid segments

## DV pre-bid segments overview

When you bid on an ad placement, verification partners like DoubleVerify (DV) determine whether or not it’s appropriate for the brand based on a predetermined set of criteria that you define. These predetermined rules can apply to several factors including fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement. Review [Pre-bid targeting overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview) for more information about these pre-bid categories, and refer to the IQM platform for each segment’s current pricing details.

## DV pre-bid segments descriptions

### Fraud and invalid traffic (IVT) segments

DV identifies a range of IVT behaviors including fraud bots, non-human data center traffic, hijacked devices, and emulators. Target DV fraud and IVT segments to exclude sites or apps based on the percentage of fraud or IVT detected, ranging from insufficient data to 100% IVT. You can also exclude them based on the specific type of invalid traffic, such as sites with high fraud percentages or impressions with missing IP addresses.

| **Targeting Type** | **Segment Name** | **Segment Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with Insufficient Fraud & IVT Stats | Sites or Apps where DV does not have sufficient fraud and invalid traffic stats to classify. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 2% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 2% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 4% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 4% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 6% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 6% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 8% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 8% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 10% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 10% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 25% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 25% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 50% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 50% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Sites/Apps with >= 75% Fraud & IVT | Sites or Apps with greater than or equal to 75% traffic classified as fraud or invalid traffic. |
| Avoidance targeting by site/app | Fraudulent Sites/Apps (100% Invalid Traffic) | Sites or Apps presently or historically associated with ad impression fraud including, but not limited to, indications of impression laundering, hidden ads, nonhuman bot traffic, and Sites or Apps that don’t contain any ads. |

### Supply Refinement segments

DV identifies a range of Supply Refinement signals to proactively prevent low-value inventory like [Made For Advertising (MFA)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview#h_bfe466f8b4) and Low Quality [Generative AI (GenAI)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview#h_5fb64ee9d1) sites. Target DV Supply Refinement pre-bid segments to exclude low-value inventory intended for ad monetization rather than user experience and return on investment (ROI) for the brand.

This tier includes cases where only a section or a subdomain of a site demonstrates MFA characteristics. The tier also includes sites whose traffic relies not only on MFA content but rather a mix of MFA and non-MFA content. |
| Exclusion targeting | Made For Advertising - High & Medium Risk | For web inventory, avoids sites that exhibit a varying degree of MFA behavior. This tier includes sites indicating the presence of multiple MFA and traffic signals that indicate lower-than-average organic traffic sources. |
| Exclusion targeting | Made For Advertising - High Risk | For web inventory, avoids sites including MFA signals and non-organic traffic patterns of only the highest risk level. This tier includes sites with the highest number of MFA and traffic signals that indicate little-to-no organic traffic sources. The tier also includes sites where average ad intensity is significantly lower than the benchmark, suggesting a high level of MFA activity. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Avoidance (exclusion) targeting

DV’s fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, and supply refinement segments use avoidance targeting. Avoidance targeting excludes the content or environments that aren’t aligned with the brand’s image or a campaign’s objectives. When you target these avoidance segments, you help ensure ads don’t show up in places that could harm the brand’s image or reach the wrong audience.

### Inclusion targeting

DV’s viewability segments use inclusion targeting. Inclusion targeting aims to include only the URLs and apps that have historically achieved specific viewability performance. When you target these inclusion segments, you help ensure ads have the opportunity to be seen by a user.

title: Optimization & Delivery overview

blocks.text: A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively the campaign should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad.
Four elements comprise a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery:
Optimization
Bid Pacing
Budget Capping (budget caps and impression caps)
Frequency Capping

The way you manage these elements can impact the campaign’s performance, including its ability to pace on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for additional support.

When you create a campaign, you’ll choose whether you’d like to apply manual optimizations (Rule-Based Optimization) or let the IQM platform’s AI engine automatically apply optimizations that aim to achieve the campaign’s primary objective and goal (AI-Based Optimization).

The decision between Rule-Based Optimization and AI-Based Optimization depends on the individual campaign’s goal and your preference for managing performance. We recommend enabling AI-Based Optimization for campaigns that would otherwise require a significant time investment to complete the optimization cycle (optimize → serve → report → analyze → repeat).

Rule-Based Optimization gives you complete control over a campaign’s ability to achieve its performance targets. It involves monitoring real-time performance and steering the IQM platform’s manual optimization tools to refine your strategy–as needed–and ensure every dollar is spent efficiently.

The Advanced Modeling optimization feature is available for campaigns with the Rule-Based Optimization setting enabled.

Advanced Modeling is supported for the Creatives, Location, Inventory, and Device dimensions. It allows you to create a set of rules that are deployed as the campaign runs. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview), allocate budgets with [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), and define dimension value priorities with [Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-priority-overview) to optimize performance in real time.

In particular, Bid Modifiers are recommended to manage your campaign’s bidding strategy. You can optimize a campaign by bidding a higher or lower price for the individual dimensions that are most or least important to the campaign. These multipliers can be changed or removed at any time, as needed.
Refer to the [Advanced Modeling collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11511670-advanced-modeling) for more information
**AI-Based Optimization notice:** Note that Advanced Modeling is a manual optimization tool that’s available only for campaigns with Rule-Based Optimization settings enabled.

**Increase:**
Lift % = [(Post-learning-phase KPI) - (Pre-learning-phase KPI)] / (Post-learning-phase KPI)
**Reduction:**
Lift % = **-** [(Post-learning-phase KPI) **-** (Pre-learning-phase KPI)] / (Post-learning-phase KPI) * 100
**Actual KPI vs Target KPI**
Displays daily performance details related to the actual achieved daily average KPI (solid orange line) compared to the target KPI (dashed orange line).

Provides a complete list of the changes applied by the AI engine for the date selected in the **Actual KPI vs target KPI** chart. Each **AI Action** includes the specific dimension that was added or updated, along with that dimension’s new amount, percentage, or multiplier—all segmented by the time that the action took place.

blocks.text: **More on Bid Shading:** While Bid Shading helps your campaign bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying, we recommend temporarily disabling this feature if the campaign is pacing behind.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Bid Shading is enabled by default, regardless of whether AI-Based or Rule-Based Optimization is selected. It allows the platform to automatically optimize your campaign to achieve the best effective cost per mille (eCPM) by automatically reducing your bid when you can win at auction for a lower price than the Max Bid Price you specified for the campaign.

With the **Budget Capping** tool, you can define a **Maximum Daily** and/or **Maximum Total** spending limit once a certain cost is reached for impressions, clicks, and/or conversions. You can also set an impression cap to limit the number of impressions that you want to display per day.

Since impression and budget caps cause your campaign to stop spending once the daily limits are reached, we recommend reserving these settings for campaigns and IOs that are pacing on track (90%-100%) or pacing ahead (100%-120%). You might also consider increasing a budget cap to allow the campaign’s pacing to catch up. Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) for more information on how pacing performance is calculated, and how it differs for budget-based and impression-based campaigns.

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) for more information on how to enable or disable the **Budget Capping** feature and define impression, click, and/or conversion limits.

Bid Pacing helps ensure smooth and consistent bid distribution. When enabled, the **Bid Pacing** tool evenly distributes your bids throughout the campaign’s scheduled display times based on the daily budget you defined.

The decision to keep bid pacing turned on for a given campaign can depend on its pacing performance. For example, consider disabling the **Bid Pacing** tool if the campaign is pacing behind. This change will allow it to spend the daily budget as soon as possible without pacing restrictions in place.

Refer to [Manage Bid Pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_4fbc30de71) for more information on how to enable or disable the **Bid Pacing** feature.

Advertisers walk a fine line to drive brand awareness and earn conversions without over-serving ads. You can use frequency caps to strike this balance by limiting the number of impressions a user is served across their devices over a set timeframe.

While frequency caps are critical for creating a positive user experience, a campaign can begin to pace behind when the frequency cap you define is too restrictive. Campaigns are highly customized based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended frequency cap for optimal campaign performance.

If you suspect that your frequency cap settings are the cause of your campaign pacing behind, consider increasing its frequency gradually while monitoring both reach and performance. When user-level frequency caps are the cause of bid drop-offs, the campaign’s [Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview) will log these drop-offs under the **Optimization & Delivery** category and **Frequency Capping** sub-category.

Refer to [Frequency capping overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8480958-frequency-capping-overview) for more details on frequency capping, and review [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to set or change a campaign’s frequency-cap settings.
A maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign).

blocks.text: *The **Weeks** and **Months** durations are based on the calendar week and calendar month rather than today’s date. The **Weeks** duration takes place from Sunday at 12:00 AM through Saturday at 11:59 PM, and the **Months** duration takes place from the first day of every month at 12:00 AM through the last day 11:59 PM.
The campaign will apply an “AND” relationship to the rules you add. This means that a campaign can only target a user when every frequency rule is met.
For example, an advertiser adds the following two rules to a campaign:
**2** impressions every **1 Day**
**10** impressions every **1 Week**

By the last day of the week, a user was only served your ad a total of eight times. However, they saw your ad twice today. Since the first rule was already satisfied, the user will not be served more ads today to reach the total allowed **10** weekly impressions.

You can edit a campaign’s frequency settings throughout its duration. However, both the amount of time remaining in the campaign and the number of impressions already served to a given user can impact the way in which the campaign executes your settings.

For example, an advertiser sets a frequency cap of **100 impressions** for the **Campaign Duration**. After the campaign runs for one month, the advertiser changes the frequency cap to **20 impressions** for the **Campaign Duration**.

During its first month, the campaign served **50 impressions** each to 90% of users. Since this number is greater than the advertiser’s new frequency cap setting of **20 impressions**, the campaign will stop serving ads to those 90% of users who have already met the impression limit.
[Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings)
[Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12759402-optimization-delivery-frequently-asked-questions-faq)

# Optimization & Delivery overview

## Optimization & Delivery overview

A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively the campaign should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad.

Four elements comprise a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery:

- Optimization
- Bid Pacing
- Budget Capping (budget caps and impression caps)
- Frequency Capping

The way you manage these elements can impact the campaign’s performance, including its ability to pace on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for additional support.

## Optimization

When you create a campaign, you’ll choose whether you’d like to apply manual optimizations (Rule-Based Optimization) or let the IQM platform’s AI engine automatically apply optimizations that aim to achieve the campaign’s primary objective and goal (AI-Based Optimization).

The decision between Rule-Based Optimization and AI-Based Optimization depends on the individual campaign’s goal and your preference for managing performance. We recommend enabling AI-Based Optimization for campaigns that would otherwise require a significant time investment to complete the optimization cycle (optimize → serve → report → analyze → repeat).

### Rule-Based Optimization (Manual)

Rule-Based Optimization gives you complete control over a campaign’s ability to achieve its performance targets. It involves monitoring real-time performance and steering the IQM platform’s manual optimization tools to refine your strategy–as needed–and ensure every dollar is spent efficiently.

#### Rule-Based Optimization - Eligibility requirements

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| Advertiser Vertical | Healthcare Political Specialty |
| Estimated Impressions* | 10K+ |
| Campaign Type | Advanced |
| Creative Type | All |
| Dependencies** | Total Budget Daily Budget Max Bid Price |

***Estimated Impressions:** A campaign’s Estimated Impressions are determined by multiplying its **Total Budget** by 1,000 and dividing the result by the campaign’s **Total CPM** value.

****Dependencies:** These values must be added to the campaign before the Rule-Based Optimization option can be selected.

#### Rule-Based Optimization - Advanced Modeling

The Advanced Modeling optimization feature is available for campaigns with the Rule-Based Optimization setting enabled.

Advanced Modeling is supported for the Creatives, Location, Inventory, and Device dimensions. It allows you to create a set of rules that are deployed as the campaign runs. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview), allocate budgets with [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), and define dimension value priorities with [Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-priority-overview) to optimize performance in real time.

In particular, Bid Modifiers are recommended to manage your campaign’s bidding strategy. You can optimize a campaign by bidding a higher or lower price for the individual dimensions that are most or least important to the campaign. These multipliers can be changed or removed at any time, as needed.

Refer to the [Advanced Modeling collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11511670-advanced-modeling) for more information

### AI-Based Optimization (Automated)

> **AI-Based Optimization notice:** Note that Advanced Modeling is a manual optimization tool that’s available only for campaigns with Rule-Based Optimization settings enabled.

AI-Based Optimization helps you avoid KPI-chasing via manual tweaks throughout a campaign’s lifecycle. When enabled, this feature signals the platform’s AI engine to automatically optimize your campaign in an attempt to achieve the Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal that you define. It bases these optimizations on an initial pre-optimization learning phase, and later on ongoing KPI performance after AI-Based Optimizations are applied.

#### AI-Based Optimization - Eligibility requirements

A campaign must meet the following requirements at all times to be eligible for AI-Based Optimization settings.

If a campaign no longer meets the criteria after it starts serving, it automatically stops applying AI-Based Optimizations. You can adjust the campaign to again meet the criteria, which will resume optimizations and help avoid limiting overall spend and delivery.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| Advertiser Vertical | Healthcare Political Specialty |
| Estimated impressions* (impression-based campaign) | 10K+ estimated impressions |
| Monetary budget (budget-based campaign) | $100+ total budget |
| Campaign Type | Advanced |
| Campaign Duration | 3+ days |
| Creative Type | All - The Creative Type determines which Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal settings are available |
| Dependencies* | Total Budget Daily Budget Max Bid Price Creative Type Conversion*** |

***Estimated Impressions:** A campaign’s Estimated Impressions are determined by multiplying its **Total Budget** by 1,000 and dividing the result by the campaign’s **Total CPM** value.

****Dependencies:** These values must be added to the campaign before the AI-Based Optimization option can be selected.

*****Conversion:** You must add a Conversion to campaigns with a Conversion Campaign Goal.

#### AI-Based Optimization - Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal

Your Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal selections tell the IQM platform’s AI engine which optimizations it should prioritize to help achieve your desired goals.

We recommend also adding an optional Target KPI value. This will allow you to compare actual KPI performance against your target when you review KPI Performance Insights.

| **Campaign Objective** | **Campaign Goal*** | **Compatible Creative Type(s)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Awareness** | Increase Reach | All |
| **Awareness** | Increase CTR | All |
| **Awareness** | Reduce CPM | All |
| **Awareness** | Increase VCR | Video |
| **Awareness** | Increase ACR | Audio |
| **Consideration** | Reduce CPC | All |
| **Consideration** | Reduce CPCV | Video |
| **Consideration** | Increase CTR | All |
| **Consideration** | Increase VCR | Video |
| **Consideration** | Increase ACR | Audio |
| **Conversion** | Reduce CPA | All |
| **Conversion** | Increase Conversion Rate | All |
| **Conversion** | Increase ROAS | All |

***Campaign Goal:** Refer to the [Report dimensions and metrics collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11287049-report-dimensions-and-metrics) to learn more about a particular goal metric.

#### AI-Based Optimization - KPI Performance Insights

You can review the impact of AI-Based Optimization on your target KPI directly from the Campaigns app. Review the table below for more details, and refer to [Review KPI performance details](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_510488ac12) to learn how to locate KPI performance details for campaigns with AI-Based Optimizations applied.

| **Metric** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign Objective** | Displays the primary objective you selected for the campaign: **Awareness**, **Consideration**, or **Conversion**. |
| **Campaign Goal** | Displays the KPI increase or KPI reduction goal you selected for the campaign. |
| **Target KPI** | Displays the target KPI value you entered for the campaign (optional). |
| **Average (%, $)** | Depending on the **Campaign Goal**, displays the percentage or monetary average achieved for the KPI. |
| **Without AI based optimization** | Displays the percentage or monetary average KPI achieved during the pre-optimization learning phase. |
| **With AI based optimization** | Displays the percentage or monetary average KPI achieved after AI-Based optimizations were applied. |
| **Lift** | Displays the percentage change between the KPI value during the pre-optimization learning phase and the KPI value achieved after AI-Based optimizations were applied. In other words, this metric displays the percentage difference for KPI performance. Lift calculations differ based on whether the **Campaign Goal** is an Increase or Reduction goal: **Increase:** Lift % = [(Post-learning-phase KPI) - (Pre-learning-phase KPI)] / (Post-learning-phase KPI) **Reduction:** Lift % = **-** [(Post-learning-phase KPI) **-** (Pre-learning-phase KPI)] / (Post-learning-phase KPI) * 100 |
| **Actual KPI vs Target KPI** | Displays daily performance details related to the actual achieved daily average KPI (solid orange line) compared to the target KPI (dashed orange line). |
| **Action Log** | Provides a complete list of the changes applied by the AI engine for the date selected in the **Actual KPI vs target KPI** chart. Each **AI Action** includes the specific dimension that was added or updated, along with that dimension’s new amount, percentage, or multiplier—all segmented by the time that the action took place. **AI Actions** can be searched for the selected date, and all **Action Log** details can be downloaded as a CSV file for all dates. |

## Bid Shading

> **More on Bid Shading:** While Bid Shading helps your campaign bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying, we recommend temporarily disabling this feature if the campaign is pacing behind.

Bid Shading is enabled by default, regardless of whether AI-Based or Rule-Based Optimization is selected. It allows the platform to automatically optimize your campaign to achieve the best effective cost per mille (eCPM) by automatically reducing your bid when you can win at auction for a lower price than the Max Bid Price you specified for the campaign.

## Budget Capping

With the **Budget Capping** tool, you can define a **Maximum Daily** and/or **Maximum Total** spending limit once a certain cost is reached for impressions, clicks, and/or conversions. You can also set an impression cap to limit the number of impressions that you want to display per day.

Since impression and budget caps cause your campaign to stop spending once the daily limits are reached, we recommend reserving these settings for campaigns and IOs that are pacing on track (90%-100%) or pacing ahead (100%-120%). You might also consider increasing a budget cap to allow the campaign’s pacing to catch up. Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) for more information on how pacing performance is calculated, and how it differs for budget-based and impression-based campaigns.

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) for more information on how to enable or disable the **Budget Capping** feature and define impression, click, and/or conversion limits.

## Bid Pacing

Bid Pacing helps ensure smooth and consistent bid distribution. When enabled, the **Bid Pacing** tool evenly distributes your bids throughout the campaign’s scheduled display times based on the daily budget you defined.

The decision to keep bid pacing turned on for a given campaign can depend on its pacing performance. For example, consider disabling the **Bid Pacing** tool if the campaign is pacing behind. This change will allow it to spend the daily budget as soon as possible without pacing restrictions in place.

Refer to [Manage Bid Pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_4fbc30de71) for more information on how to enable or disable the **Bid Pacing** feature.

## Frequency Capping

Advertisers walk a fine line to drive brand awareness and earn conversions without over-serving ads. You can use frequency caps to strike this balance by limiting the number of impressions a user is served across their devices over a set timeframe.

While frequency caps are critical for creating a positive user experience, a campaign can begin to pace behind when the frequency cap you define is too restrictive. Campaigns are highly customized based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended frequency cap for optimal campaign performance.

If you suspect that your frequency cap settings are the cause of your campaign pacing behind, consider increasing its frequency gradually while monitoring both reach and performance. When user-level frequency caps are the cause of bid drop-offs, the campaign’s [Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview) will log these drop-offs under the **Optimization & Delivery** category and **Frequency Capping** sub-category.

Refer to [Frequency capping overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8480958-frequency-capping-overview) for more details on frequency capping, and review [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to set or change a campaign’s frequency-cap settings.

### Frequency values

A maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign).

| **Field** | **Accepted values** |
| --- | --- |
| Days | Whole numbers from 1 through 6 |
| Weeks* | Whole numbers from 1 through 4 |
| Months* | Whole numbers from 1 through 3 |
| Campaign Duration | Not applicable - The campaign’s duration information is prefilled |
| Impressions | Whole numbers from 1 through 999 |

*The **Weeks** and **Months** durations are based on the calendar week and calendar month rather than today’s date. The **Weeks** duration takes place from Sunday at 12:00 AM through Saturday at 11:59 PM, and the **Months** duration takes place from the first day of every month at 12:00 AM through the last day 11:59 PM.

### Frequency execution example

The campaign will apply an “AND” relationship to the rules you add. This means that a campaign can only target a user when every frequency rule is met.

For example, an advertiser adds the following two rules to a campaign:

- **2** impressions every **1 Day**
- **10** impressions every **1 Week**

By the last day of the week, a user was only served your ad a total of eight times. However, they saw your ad twice today. Since the first rule was already satisfied, the user will not be served more ads today to reach the total allowed **10** weekly impressions.

### Frequency changes example

You can edit a campaign’s frequency settings throughout its duration. However, both the amount of time remaining in the campaign and the number of impressions already served to a given user can impact the way in which the campaign executes your settings.

For example, an advertiser sets a frequency cap of **100 impressions** for the **Campaign Duration**. After the campaign runs for one month, the advertiser changes the frequency cap to **20 impressions** for the **Campaign Duration**.

During its first month, the campaign served **50 impressions** each to 90% of users. Since this number is greater than the advertiser’s new frequency cap setting of **20 impressions**, the campaign will stop serving ads to those 90% of users who have already met the impression limit.

## Locate additional Optimization & Delivery resources

- [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings)
- [Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12759402-optimization-delivery-frequently-asked-questions-faq)
