# Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)

## Impression-based IO overview

You decide between impression-based or budget-based settings when you create an insertion order (IO):

- **Budget-based IO:** Allocate a specific amount of money to the IO’s campaigns.
- **Impression-based IO:** Aim to deliver a specific number of impressions across the IO’s campaigns.

Review [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) for more information on their differences.

In this article, you’ll learn how to create an impression-based IO. Refer to [Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907165-create-or-manage-a-budget-based-insertion-order-io) to create a budget-based one instead.

## Create an impression-based IO

> **Budget Type notice:** When you create an IO, you’ll be prompted to choose a **Budget Type**: **Budget** for budget-based IOs, or **Impression** for impression-based IOs. The **Budget Type** setting that you select can’t be altered after the IO is created.

You can create an impression-based IO in the following ways:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboards app

### Create an impression-based IO from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to create an impression-based IO from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select **+ Create Insertion Order**. This will open the **Create Insertion Order** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name into the **Insertion Order Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this IO from others that you may create.
4. Open the **Start Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
5. Select a time zone from the **Timezone** menu.
6. Click **Impression** in the **Budget Type** section.
7. Select **Create** to finish creating the impression-based IO.

You’ll be redirected to the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app, where you can define an IO budget, manage the IO, and add campaigns to it.

### Create an impression-based IO from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to create an impression-based IO from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Select **Insertion Order** from the **Create New** menu. This will redirect you to the Campaigns app and automatically open the **Create Insertion Order** pop-up window.
3. Follow the steps outlined in Create an impression-based IO from the Campaigns app to specify the IO’s details and create it.

## Define an IO budget

> **More on IO-level budget settings:** The **Insertion Order Budget** will override campaign-level budget settings. For example, an IO with an **Insertion Order Budget** of 1MM impressions will stop spending once it reaches that amount, even if its campaigns feature budget settings of 800K and 500K impressions. However, neither campaign will exceed its individual impression budget, regardless of the overall **Insertion Order Budget**.

Follow these steps to choose an impression budget for an impression-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse and select the desired IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only impression-based campaigns. Select **Impression** to apply this filter.
3. Locate the **Insertion Order Budget** field and enter the desired impression budget.
   1. The combined served impressions of the campaigns that you add to this IO will not exceed the IO budget amount.
4. If desired, select the **Keep same as total campaign budget** checkbox.
   1. This setting fixes the budget to the individual total budgets of each of the IO’s campaigns. For example, an IO including two campaigns with individual budgets of 1MM impressions and 4MM impressions would equal an **Insertion Order Budget** of 5MM impressions.
   2. Since it’s fixed to the total campaign budget, the **Insertion Order Budget** can only be manually adjusted when this checkbox is unselected.
5. Select **Update Changes** to apply your settings to the budget-based IO.

## Manage an impression-based IO

You can manage an existing impression-based IO in the following ways:

- Edit
- Duplicate
- Delete

### Edit an impression-based IO

> **Editable fields for impression-based IOs:** Supported IO edits include changes to the IO’s name, time zone, impression budget, and/or end date. Note that end dates are optional, and all of an IO’s campaigns will stop serving once their IO’s end date is reached.

You can edit one IO at a time. Follow these steps to edit an impression-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate desired IO.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only impression-based campaigns. Select **Impression** to apply this filter.
3. Select the IO’s name. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
4. Locate and select the relevant field (**Insertion order name**, **Timezone**, **Start Date**, **End Date**, **Insertion Order Budget**) to edit that IO element.
   1. The option to change the **Insertion Order Budget** is available only when the **Keep same as total campaign budget** checkbox is unselected.
5. Select **Update Changes** to apply the new settings to the IO.

### Duplicate an impression-based IO

> **IO duplication notice:** Duplicated IOs will inherit the same **Budget Type** setting as the original IO: **Budget** or **Impression**. This setting can’t be changed once the duplicated IO is created.

You can duplicate one IO at a time. Follow these steps to duplicate an impression-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate the desired IO.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only impression-based campaigns. Select **Impression** to apply this filter.
3. Select the checkbox next to the IO.
4. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Duplicate**. This will open the **Duplicate Insertion Order** pop-up window.
5. Open the **IO Start Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
6. Open the **IO End Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**, if desired.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
7. Select a time zone from the **IO** **Timezone** menu.
8. Click **Campaigns** to search and select the ones that you’d like to add to the IO.
   1. The original IO’s campaigns are selected by default. Click those campaigns to deselect them, if desired.
   2. All selected campaigns will be added to the IO as **Draft** campaigns.
9. Select **Duplicate** to finish creating the duplicated impression-based IO.

### Delete an impression-based IO

You can delete IOs individually or in bulk. Follow these steps to delete an impression-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate the desired IO(s).
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only impression-based campaigns. Select **Impression** to apply this filter.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the IO(s).
4. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Delete**.
5. Review any warnings or disclaimers, and confirm your selection to delete the impression-based IO.

## Add campaigns to an impression-based IO

### Add new campaigns

> **Budget Type notice:** Note that campaigns inherit the same **Budget Type** settings as the IO they’re assigned to. This means that budget-based IOs can include only budget-based campaigns, and impression-based IOs can include only impression-based campaigns. These settings are unable to be altered after the IO or campaign(s) are created.

Refer to [Create a new campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-a-new-campaign) for more details on adding new campaigns to an IO.

### Add existing campaigns

Existing campaigns are tied to the IO that they’re associated with. You can, however, Duplicate an impression-based IO and select existing campaigns. These campaigns will be added to the IO as **Draft** campaigns, which you can edit and manage before running them.

Note that the original, existing campaigns will continue to be associated with their corresponding parent IO.

# Create or manage a budget-based insertion order (IO)

## Budget-based IO overview

You decide between budget-based or impression-based settings when you create an insertion order (IO):

- **Budget-based IO:** Allocate a specific amount of money to the IO’s campaigns.
- **Impression-based IO:** Aim to deliver a specific number of impressions across the IO’s campaigns.

Review [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) for more information on their differences.

In this article, you’ll learn how to create a budget-based IO. Refer to [Create or manage an impression-based insertion order (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io) to create an impression-based one instead.

## Create a budget-based IO

> **Budget Type notice:** When you create an IO, you’ll be prompted to choose a **Budget Type**: **Budget** for budget-based IOs, or **Impression** for impression-based IOs. The **Budget Type** setting that you select can’t be altered after the IO is created.

You can create a budget-based IO in the following ways:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboards app

### Create a budget-based IO from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to create a budget-based IO from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select **+ Create Insertion Order**. This will open the **Create Insertion Order** pop-up window.
3. Enter a name into the **Insertion Order Name** field.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this IO from others that you may create.
4. Open the **Start Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
5. Select a time zone from the **Timezone** menu.
6. Click **Budget** in the **Budget Type** section.
7. Select **Create** to finish creating the budget-based IO.

You’ll be redirected to the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app, where you can define an IO budget, manage the IO, and add campaigns to it.

### Create a budget-based IO from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to create a budget-based IO from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Select **Insertion Order** from the **Create New** menu. This will redirect you to the Campaigns app and automatically open the **Create Insertion Order** pop-up window.
3. Follow the steps outlined in Create a budget-based IO from the Campaigns app to specify the IO’s details and create it.

## Define an IO budget

> **More on IO-level budget settings:** The **Insertion Order Budget** will override campaign-level budget settings. For example, an IO with an **Insertion Order Budget** of $1MM will stop spending once it reaches that amount, even if its campaigns feature budget settings of $800K and $500K. However, neither campaign will exceed its individual budget, regardless of the overall **Insertion Order Budget**.

Follow these steps to choose a monetary budget for a budget-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse and select the desired IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only budget-based campaigns. Select **Budget** to apply this filter.
3. Locate the **Insertion Order Budget** field and enter the desired budget.
   1. The combined spend of the campaigns that you add to this IO will not exceed the IO budget amount.
4. If desired, select the **Keep same as total campaign budget** checkbox.
   1. This setting fixes the budget to the individual total budgets of each of the IO’s campaigns. For example, an IO including six campaigns with individual budgets of $5K would equal an **Insertion Order Budget** of $30K.
   2. Since it’s fixed to the total campaign budget, the **Insertion Order Budget** can only be manually adjusted when this checkbox is unselected.
5. Select **Update Changes** to apply your settings to the budget-based IO.

## Manage a budget-based IO

You can manage an existing budget-based IO in the following ways:

- Edit
- Duplicate
- Delete

### Edit a budget-based IO

> **Editable fields for budget-based IOs:** Supported IO edits include changes to the IO’s name, time zone, monetary budget, and/or end date. Note that end dates are optional, and all of an IO’s campaigns will stop serving once their IO’s end date is reached.

You can edit one IO at a time. Follow these steps to edit a budget-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate desired IO.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only budget-based campaigns. Select **Budget** to apply this filter.
3. Select the IO’s name. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page.
4. Locate and select the relevant field (**Insertion order name**, **Timezone**, **Start Date**, **End Date**, **Insertion Order Budget**) to edit that IO element.
   1. The option to change the **Insertion Order Budget** is available only when the **Keep same as total campaign budget** checkbox is unselected.
5. Select **Update Changes** to apply the new settings to the IO.

### Duplicate a budget-based IO

> **IO duplication notice:** Duplicated IOs will inherit the same **Budget Type** setting as the original IO: **Budget** or **Impression**. This setting can’t be changed once the duplicated IO is created.

You can duplicate one IO at a time. Follow these steps to duplicate a budget-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate the desired IO.
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only budget-based campaigns. Select **Budget** to apply this filter.
3. Select the checkbox next to the IO.
4. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Duplicate**. This will open the **Duplicate Insertion Order** pop-up window.
5. Open the **IO Start Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
6. Open the **IO End Date** menu to select a **Date**, **Hours**, and **Minutes**, if desired.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selections to the IO.
7. Select a time zone from the **IO** **Timezone** menu.
8. Click **Campaigns** to search and select the ones that you’d like to add to the IO.
   1. The original IO’s campaigns are selected by default. Click those campaigns to deselect them, if desired.
   2. All selected campaigns will be added to the IO as **Draft** campaigns.
9. Select **Duplicate** to finish creating the duplicated budget-based IO.

### Delete a budget-based IO

You can delete IOs individually or in bulk. Follow these steps to delete a budget-based IO:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse the **Insertion Orders** page to locate the desired IO(s).
   1. The **Filter** menu includes the option to display only budget-based campaigns. Select **Budget** to apply this filter.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the IO(s).
4. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Delete**.
5. Review any warnings or disclaimers, and confirm your selection to delete the budget-based IO.

## Add campaigns to a budget-based IO

### Add new campaigns

> **Budget Type notice:** Note that campaigns inherit the same **Budget Type** settings as the IO they’re assigned to. This means that budget-based IOs can include only budget-based campaigns, and impression-based IOs can include only impression-based campaigns. These settings are unable to be altered after the IO or campaign(s) are created.

Refer to [Create a new campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-a-new-campaign) for more details on adding new campaigns to an IO.

### Add existing campaigns

Existing campaigns are tied to the IO that they’re associated with. You can, however, Duplicate a budget-based IO and select existing campaigns. These campaigns will be added to the IO as **Draft** campaigns, which you can edit and manage before running them.

Note that the original, existing campaigns will continue to be associated with their corresponding parent IO.

## Locate additional budget-based and impression-based IO resources

- [Budget-based and impression-based IO overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview)
- [Create or manage an impression-based IO](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10907105-create-or-manage-an-impression-based-insertion-order-io)

title: Generate or manage a Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report

blocks.text: Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights are on-demand reports that include key details about prescribing behaviors and how they may be influenced by current and previous healthcare campaigns. Uncover pre-and post-campaign comparison data, prescription trends (Rx, TRx) for exposed and unexposed NPIs, and Rx and TRx volumes for competitor brands over the same time period.

You can generate SLS Insights reports if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on eligibility requirements, metrics, and costs.

sections.heading: Video tutorial: Generate an SLS Insights report
heading_path: Video tutorial: Generate an SLS Insights report

blocks.text: **Concept Group ID notice:** IQM will provide you with a Concept Group ID for your brand (all SLS reports) and the competitor brands of your choice (Competitive Analysis SLS reports). Contact your IQM account representative before creating your first SLS Insights report to ensure you have the appropriate Concept Group ID(s) for data generation.
You can generate an SLS Insights report in the following ways:
From the Insights app
From the Campaigns app
From the Dashboards app

sections.heading: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app
heading_path: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to access the **+ Generate New** workflow:
Open the **Insights** app.
Select **Script Lift Study**.
Click **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Script Lift Study** pop-up window.
Enter a name for the report.
Choose a unique one to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
If desired, select whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu, which will determine which campaigns are available in the **Campaign** menu.
Search and select the campaign(s) for which you want to generate insights.

Each campaign must belong to the same insertion order (IO) and be [eligible for SLS Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) report generation.
The **Campaign Duration** field will automatically populate once you select the report’s campaign(s).
If you selected more than one campaign, the **Campaign Duration** includes the selected campaigns’ earliest Start Date and latest End Date.
Choose a **Lookback Duration** of up to six months.
Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Lookback Duration](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_841b7f998e) for more information.
Select one or more **Report Types**.

Refer to [SLS Insights report metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_dd87d0b156) for more information on the insights available in each report, and to [SLS Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_46a38ac648) for cost details.

If you selected **Competitive Analysis**, enter the Concept Group IDs of up to three competitor brands in the available fields. Each ID must be unique, and must not match your brand’s Concept Group ID that you’ll enter in step 10.
Enter the prescription’s **Concept Group ID**.
Select **Next**.
Review your report settings, and a summary of the SLS Insights report’s chargeable impressions and the associated cost.
We calculate **SLS Cost** based on the number of impressions that your campaign(s) delivered during the specified date range at a CPM rate.
Select **Previous** to change any report settings, if desired.
Click **Generate** to create the SLS Insights report.

The **SLS Cost** will be deducted from your account’s available balance as soon as the report generates. Once generated, you can find generated reports on the **Insights** app’s **Script Lift Study** page. Review Manage an SLS Insights report for more details.

sections.heading: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Campaigns app
heading_path: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Campaigns app

blocks.text: You can begin SLS Insights report creation from the Campaigns app. Doing so will automatically populate certain fields such as the report’s campaigns, their statuses, and their date ranges.
Follow these steps to access the **Generate Script Lift Study** action from the Campaigns app:
Open the **Campaigns** app.
Select the insertion order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
Click the checkbox(es) next to each campaign for which you want to generate insights.
Select **Generate Script Lift Study** from the **More** menu.

Each selected campaign must meet the [SLS Insights eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) for the **Generate Script Lift Study** option to become enabled.
You’ll be redirected to the **Script Lift Study** page of the Insights app.
Follow steps 8 through 14 of the Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app section of this article to complete the workflow.

sections.heading: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Dashboard app
heading_path: Generate an SLS Insights report from the Dashboard app

blocks.text: Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to SLS Insights report creation from the Dashboard app:
Open the Dashboard app.
Filter or search the dashboard to locate the desired campaign(s).
Click the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).

Select **Generate Script Lift Study** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Script Lift Study** page of the Insights app and auto-populate details such as the campaign(s)’ name and date range.

Each selected campaign must meet the [SLS Insights eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) for the **Generate Script Lift Study** option to become enabled.
Follow steps 8 through 14 of the Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app section of this article to complete the workflow.

The **Script Lift Study** page displays each of your SLS Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. Use the **Actions** column to download or email an SLS report to your device or send it as an email attachment once it’s **Ready**.
Follow these steps to download an SLS Insights report:
Filter or search your SLS Insights reports to locate the one you want to download.
In the **Actions** column, open the **Download** menu.
Click **Download as PDF** or **Download as XLS**, depending on your preference.

**Email notice:** The email feature is disabled for certain reports if their file size is greater than 25 MB. This limitation is to comply with the file-size restrictions of most email inboxes. You can Download an SLS Insights report of any size.
Follow these steps to email an SLS Insights report:
Filter or search your SLS Insights reports to locate the one you want to email.
In the **Actions** column, select the envelope icon.
Click **Email as CSV** or **Email as XLSX**, depending on your preference. This will open an **Email Script Lift Study as XLSX/CSV** pop-up window.
Add up to 15 email aliases to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
Select **Send Email**.
We limit the ability to delete most SLS Insights reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights. You can, however, delete **Failed** reports.
Follow these steps to delete a **Failed** SLS Insights report from the **Script Lift Study** page:
Select the checkbox(es) next to the **Failed** report(s).
Click **Delete**.
Review any warnings or disclaimers and confirm your selection, if desired.

# Generate or manage a Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report

## SLS Insights report overview

Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights are on-demand reports that include key details about prescribing behaviors and how they may be influenced by current and previous healthcare campaigns. Uncover pre-and post-campaign comparison data, prescription trends (Rx, TRx) for exposed and unexposed NPIs, and Rx and TRx volumes for competitor brands over the same time period.

You can generate SLS Insights reports if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information on eligibility requirements, metrics, and costs.

## Video tutorial: Generate an SLS Insights report

## Generate an SLS Insights report

> **Concept Group ID notice:** IQM will provide you with a Concept Group ID for your brand (all SLS reports) and the competitor brands of your choice (Competitive Analysis SLS reports). Contact your IQM account representative before creating your first SLS Insights report to ensure you have the appropriate Concept Group ID(s) for data generation.

You can generate an SLS Insights report in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboards app

### Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to access the **+ Generate New** workflow:

1. Open the **Insights** app.
2. Select **Script Lift Study**.
3. Click **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Script Lift Study** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the report.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
5. If desired, select whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu, which will determine which campaigns are available in the **Campaign** menu.
6. Search and select the campaign(s) for which you want to generate insights.
   1. Each campaign must belong to the same insertion order (IO) and be [eligible for SLS Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) report generation.
7. The **Campaign Duration** field will automatically populate once you select the report’s campaign(s).
   1. If you selected more than one campaign, the **Campaign Duration** includes the selected campaigns’ earliest Start Date and latest End Date.
8. Choose a **Lookback Duration** of up to six months.
   1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Lookback Duration](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_841b7f998e) for more information.
9. Select one or more **Report Types**.
   1. Refer to [SLS Insights report metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_dd87d0b156) for more information on the insights available in each report, and to [SLS Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_46a38ac648) for cost details.
   2. If you selected **Competitive Analysis**, enter the Concept Group IDs of up to three competitor brands in the available fields. Each ID must be unique, and must not match your brand’s Concept Group ID that you’ll enter in step 10.
10. Enter the prescription’s **Concept Group ID**.
11. Select **Next**.
12. Review your report settings, and a summary of the SLS Insights report’s chargeable impressions and the associated cost.
    1. We calculate **SLS Cost** based on the number of impressions that your campaign(s) delivered during the specified date range at a CPM rate.
13. Select **Previous** to change any report settings, if desired.
14. Click **Generate** to create the SLS Insights report.

The **SLS Cost** will be deducted from your account’s available balance as soon as the report generates. Once generated, you can find generated reports on the **Insights** app’s **Script Lift Study** page. Review Manage an SLS Insights report for more details.

### Generate an SLS Insights report from the Campaigns app

You can begin SLS Insights report creation from the Campaigns app. Doing so will automatically populate certain fields such as the report’s campaigns, their statuses, and their date ranges.

Follow these steps to access the **Generate Script Lift Study** action from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app.
2. Select the insertion order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Click the checkbox(es) next to each campaign for which you want to generate insights.
4. Select **Generate Script Lift Study** from the **More** menu.
   1. Each selected campaign must meet the [SLS Insights eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) for the **Generate Script Lift Study** option to become enabled.
5. You’ll be redirected to the **Script Lift Study** page of the Insights app.
6. Follow steps 8 through 14 of the Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app section of this article to complete the workflow.

### Generate an SLS Insights report from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to access take a shortcut to SLS Insights report creation from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter or search the dashboard to locate the desired campaign(s).
3. Click the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Select **Generate Script Lift Study** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Script Lift Study** page of the Insights app and auto-populate details such as the campaign(s)’ name and date range.
   1. Each selected campaign must meet the [SLS Insights eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) for the **Generate Script Lift Study** option to become enabled.
5. Follow steps 8 through 14 of the Generate an SLS Insights report from the Insights app section of this article to complete the workflow.

## Manage an SLS Insights report

The **Script Lift Study** page displays each of your SLS Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. Use the **Actions** column to download or email an SLS report to your device or send it as an email attachment once it’s **Ready**.

### Download an SLS Insights report

Follow these steps to download an SLS Insights report:

1. Filter or search your SLS Insights reports to locate the one you want to download.
2. In the **Actions** column, open the **Download** menu.
3. Click **Download as PDF** or **Download as XLS**, depending on your preference.

### Email an SLS Insights report

> **Email notice:** The email feature is disabled for certain reports if their file size is greater than 25 MB. This limitation is to comply with the file-size restrictions of most email inboxes. You can Download an SLS Insights report of any size.

Follow these steps to email an SLS Insights report:

1. Filter or search your SLS Insights reports to locate the one you want to email.
2. In the **Actions** column, select the envelope icon.
3. Click **Email as CSV** or **Email as XLSX**, depending on your preference. This will open an **Email Script Lift Study as XLSX/CSV** pop-up window.
4. Add up to 15 email aliases to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
5. Select **Send Email**.

### Delete an SLS Insights report

We limit the ability to delete most SLS Insights reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights. You can, however, delete **Failed** reports.

Follow these steps to delete a **Failed** SLS Insights report from the **Script Lift Study** page:

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the **Failed** report(s).
2. Click **Delete**.
3. Review any warnings or disclaimers and confirm your selection, if desired.

## Review past SLS Insights report spend

You can review past SLS Insights report spend in the following ways:

- From the Dashboard app
- From the Reports app

### Review past SLS Insights report spend from the Dashboard app

Follow these steps to review the total amount spent on SLS Insights report generation from the Dashboard app:

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open the **View By** menu and click **Campaigns**, **Insertion Orders**, or **Advertiser**, depending on your preference.
   1. Workspace admins also have the option to select **Workspace**.
3. Select **SLS Cost** from the **Columns** menu.
   1. The **SLS Cost** column will populate in the table.
   2. Workspace admins also have the option to select **Workspace SLS Insights Earning**.
4. Adjust the dashboard’s **Time Zone** and **Date Range** details to view the amount spent on SLS Insights report generation within a specific time frame, if desired.

### Review past SLS Insights report spend from the Reports app

Follow these steps to review the total amount spent on SLS Insights report generation from the Reports app:

1. Open the **Reports** app.
2. Click **+ Create Report**. This will open the **Create New Report** page.
3. Locate and expand the **Spending** category.
4. Drag the **SLS Cost** metric into the **Columns** field.
5. Complete other required and optional fields, as needed.
   1. Note that your report’s **Rows** must include at least one of the following dimensions: **Campaign ID**, **Campaign**, **Insertion Order ID**, or **Insertion Order**. You can locate these dimensions in the **Insertion Order Specifics** or **Campaign Specifics** categories.
6. Select **Execute Report**.
7. Click **Save Report**.

Workspace admins also have the option to add the **Workspace SLS Insights Earnings** metric to a report. This metric is located in the **Earnings** category.

Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) for additional support related to creating a new custom report.

### Cannot locate Insights app on homepage

Your IQM homepage includes all apps that your workspace administrator has enabled you to access. Contact yours to request appropriate permissions to access the **Insights** app.

The workflow to generate an SLS report ends with a **Generate** button that you’ll use to create your report. If your account’s available balance is less than the **SLS Cost**, this button will prompt you to add funds to your account instead.

You can also add funds from the **Dashboard** app. Refer to the steps outlined in [Adding Funds](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5734663-adding-funds) for further details.

### Campaign(s) missing from list

Keep in mind that each selected campaign must also belong to the same insertion order (IO).
2. Check the campaigns’ current statuses. You can generate SLS Insights reports for eligible campaigns that feature a **Pending**, **Running**, or **Expired** status.

If the selected campaign(s) meets all eligibility criteria but the button remains disabled, note that, while you can generate insights for an unlimited number of campaigns, you can generate only one SLS Insights report at a time for each campaign. Campaigns that are currently **Running** will also reflect an End Date of today’s date minus 14 days.

### Lookback Duration field is disabled

We’ll automatically enable the **Lookback Duration** field after you use the **Campaigns** field to search and select one or more campaigns.

## SLS Insights report results troubleshooting

### Cannot delete a report

We limit the ability to delete SLS Insights reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights.

The **Script Lift Study** page of the **Insights** app displays each of your SLS Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can delete any **Failed** SLS Insights reports either individually or in bulk.

### Cannot email a report

The email feature may be disabled for one of the following reasons:

1. The report’s status is **Processing** or **Failed**.
   The **Script Lift Study** page of the **Insights** app displays each of your SLS Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can email any **Ready** SLS Insights reports.
2. The report's size is too large.
   You can email a report when its file size is less than 25 MB. This limitation is to comply with the file-size restrictions of most email inboxes. You can [Download an SLS Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10964623-generate-or-manage-a-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report#h_defd8460d3) of any size.
3. The **Send Email** button is disabled.
   If you can access the **Email Script Lift Study** widget, but the **Send Email** button is not enabled, note that you must complete each field to send the report to the recipients you specified.
   If you completed all fields but the button is still disabled, you likely only added one email alias. You’ll need to click anywhere within the **Email Script Lift Study** window, and outside of the **Email ID** field, for it to register. This will enable the **Send Email** button automatically.

### Cannot download a report

The **Script Lift Study** page of the **Insights** app displays each of your SLS Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can download any **Ready** SLS Insights reports by following the steps outlined in [Download an SLS Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10964623-generate-or-manage-a-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report#h_defd8460d3).

### Cannot edit or duplicate a report

The SLS Insights report doesn’t support edits or duplication. You can, however, create a new report with additional campaigns, a longer or shorter [Lookback Duration](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_841b7f998e), and/or different [Report Types](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_41f2165f77). Refer to [SLS Insights report pricing](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_46a38ac648) for cost details.

### SLS Insights report generation failed

You either encountered a technical error during report generation, or the campaign you selected is no longer eligible for SLS Insights reporting. For example, the campaign may have included an NPI-based Matched audience, but you removed the audience from the campaign while the report was generating. Try again in a few minutes to rule out a technical error, and refer to [SLS Insights report eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview#h_94b3e7a35d) to confirm that you didn't apply any changes that would make the campaign ineligible while report generation was in progress.

Note that, if an SLS Insights report features a **Failed** status, no **SLS Cost** will be deducted from the advertiser's account balance.

## Locate additional SLS Insights report resources

- [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview)
- [Generate or manage a Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10964623-generate-or-manage-a-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report)

# "Campaign delivery and optimization" collection overview

## Collection summary

The way you approach campaign delivery and optimization is central to achieving unique campaign-level performance goals, maximizing revenue, and realizing the desired business outcomes.

The “Campaign delivery and optimization” collection is your guide to effective campaign management to achieve better performance. Refer to this article’s content catalog to discover each of the resources that are available in this collection.

## Advanced modeling

Advanced modeling is the IQM platform’s most powerful optimization tool. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with Bid Modifiers, allocate budgets with Spend Ratios, and shift ad-serving priorities with Priorities to enhance campaign performance in real time.

### Primary app(s)

### All articles

## Allowlists and Blocklists

Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. You’ll target an Allowlist when you want to define who you're willing to serve the ad to based on a specific set of criteria. On the other hand, you’ll target a Blocklist when you want to avoid showing your ads to users based on a specific set of criteria.

### Primary app(s)

### All articles

Review these resources to learn how campaigns treat impression opportunities when they target an Allowlist or Blocklist, and follow steps to add Allowlists and Blocklists to campaigns.

| **Article** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| [Allowlist and Blocklist overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview) | Dive into Allowlist and Blocklist concepts, including which campaign dimensions you can include or exclude. |
| [Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472023-manage-campaign-allowlists-and-blocklists) | Block or enable ad serving for individual campaign dimensions. |

## Pacing

Pacing determines if your strategies are on track to spend in full based on two factors: how much they’ve spent so far and how much time is remaining in the campaign or insertion order (IO). Taking an active approach to pacing helps ensure you gather enough trend details to inform your optimization decisions and drive spend performance.

### Primary app(s)

### All articles

## Optimization & Delivery

Budget or impression capping, bid pacing, and frequency capping are the three tools that form a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings. How you manage them can impact a campaign’s ability to pace on track and achieve its performance goals.

title: Campaigns overview

blocks.text: Campaigns are the individual marketing strategies that define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. They contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify. You’ll set these parameters at the start of a campaign and adjust them throughout its flight to optimize performance.
Note that, as naming conventions for campaigns can differ across demand-side platforms (DSPs), you may also see campaigns referred to as flights, ad groups, or line items.

While campaigns include individual strategies, IOs function as an organizational framework. They’re the parent hierarchy that houses a set of campaigns, which you can oversee and manage individually or as a group.

The majority of your parameters and settings are defined at the campaign level. Certain settings–such as scheduling and budgets–can be set at the IO level. We also recommend reporting at the IO level to gain a comprehensive view of the performance and costs associated with each of the campaigns within the IO. This consolidated approach simplifies the process of tracking and assessing the effectiveness of your marketing strategies.
Refer to the table below for more information on the individual functions that can be managed at the campaign level and/or IO level:
**Setting**
**Insertion Order (IO)**
**Campaign**
**Scheduling**
IO dates define the timeframe during which the IO’s campaigns can run.
Each campaign can feature varying flights that take place during the dates defined at the IO level.
**Budget**
IO budgets set the cumulative spend or cumulative impressions across the IO’s campaigns.

Campaign budgets allocate the IO budget across individual campaigns. The campaigns will stop serving once that campaign’s budget is reached or the IO budget has been reached–whichever takes place first.
**Targeting**
N/A - Set at campaign level
When you define the campaign’s targeting strategy, you choose which campaign targeting elements to apply in order to strike the balance between scale, efficiency, and performance.
**Optimization & Delivery**
N/A - Set at campaign level

A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad.
**Creatives**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Select one creative format per campaign, and add one creative or multiple creative versions.
**Inventory**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Specify where ads should be placed by targeting Open Exchange inventory, Contextual inventory, or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals.
**Optimization**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Adjust individual campaign strategies such as bid amounts, creative rotation, and targeting criteria for different target-audience segments to improve performance.
**Conversions**
N/A - Set at campaign level
Implement and test conversion and postback pixels to measure how ad exposure impacts how your target audience interacts with your brand or its products and services.
**Reporting**
Report at the IO level to consolidate each of its strategies and gain an overall view of cost and performance.
Report at the campaign level to track the performance of specific targeting strategies and inform optimization decisions for current and future campaigns.

blocks.text: Each campaign includes a set of required and optional campaign targeting elements. The ones you’ll apply and customize will differ by campaign depending on aspects such as your ad’s creative format, your target audience, and your marketing objectives, for example.

Review the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for more information on each required and optional campaign targeting element, and refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) when you’re ready to apply these parameters and settings to a new or existing campaign.

When you create a new campaign, we’ll prompt you to choose whether it’s an **Advanced** or **Programmatic Guaranteed (PG)** campaign. The option you’ll select depends on the type of inventory that the campaign will target.

Choose **Advanced** if your campaign will target Open Exchange inventory or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. Select **PG** instead if you’ll purchase inventory directly from a specific publisher.

Note that certain features are supported for **Advanced** campaigns only. Selecting **PG** will reduce your campaign-targeting options as you instead agree to commit a set budget for a fixed number of impressions, and at a guaranteed price.

Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information on Open Exchange, Private Marketplace (PMP), and Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory groups and the differences between these inventory sources.
Data and analytics are central to connecting ad spend to business results, and determining whether a campaign achieved the goals that you defined for it.

The “Reporting and analytics” collection is your guide to uncovering and interpreting the data that you’ll use to improve performance across each of your strategies. This is made possible through IQM-platform features such as custom reports, insights reports, data dashboards, and more. Refer to [“Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) for a full list of this collection’s resources.

**More on campaign optimization:** You can enable AI Based Optimization in your campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings. This feature signals the platform’s AI engine to automatically optimize your campaign in an attempt to achieve the Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal that you define. It bases these optimizations on an initial pre-optimization learning phase, and later on ongoing KPI performance after AI Based Optimizations are applied.
Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on AI Based Optimization and requirements.

blocks.text: When you optimize a campaign, you apply data-driven decisions to it based on key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics such as conversions, cost per conversion, return on investment (ROI), and more. This process typically involves analyzing data, testing different approaches, and making adjustments to campaigns based on the results.

The “Campaign delivery and optimization” collection is your guide to each of the tools and features you can leverage to inform your optimization decisions and manage the overall performance of your existing campaigns. For example, you might apply advanced modeling to certain campaign dimensions, set up Allowlists and Blocklists, and optimize the campaign’s pacing performance. Refer to [“Campaign delivery and optimization” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11320980-campaign-delivery-and-optimization-collection-overview) to get started.
**Campaign template notice:** Items included in the **Campaign Info** section, such as budget, bid price, and date details, are excluded from campaign templates.

blocks.text: Streamline your campaign-creation operations by templatizing the [campaign targeting settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) that you plan to reuse in future campaigns.
Each time you create a new campaign, you’ll have the option to start from scratch or from a template. These templates can be created from either new or existing campaigns.

Campaign Templates are supported for both Advanced and PG campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) to get started with Campaign Templates.
AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical or high-risk blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for eligible campaigns. This diagnostic tool lets you know which issues are putting your campaign at the greatest risk, and what actions to take to address them.

Note that CampaignPulse is designed to help you detect and address significant risks to campaign delivery. For other campaign-optimization tools and strategies, refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview).

Review [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) to get started with CampaignPulse.
All advertisers are eligible to run CampaignPulse for eligible campaigns. Refer to the table below for campaign-eligibility criteria.
**Requirement type**

Specialty

blocks.text: Note that certain checks (IAB size checks for creatives, scheduling checks, and targeting checks) are triggered when CampaignPulse observes critical daily pacing on eligible campaigns. Refer to CampaignPulse delivery insights for more information on checked categories and their descriptions.
CampaignPulse checks for human errors, conflicting campaign settings, and account issues that could put your campaigns at medium or high risk.

This feature continuously monitors campaign health to discover issues that could limit or stop ad delivery. It highlights actionable insights across account readiness, campaign setup, targeting, budgeting, delivery settings, and more to help keep campaigns running smoothly.

Refer to the table below for more information on what CampaignPulse monitors, and always review all CampaignPulse delivery insights closely for instructions on how to address the issues that can put your campaigns at risk.
**Category**
**Description**
**Balance**
Monitors the Organization and Workspace’s account balance.
**Insertion Order (IO)**
Tracks each campaign’s IO to catch expired campaigns and conflicts between the campaign and IO end dates before serving is interrupted.
**Budget**

Confirms each campaign includes at least one Ready creative, and that the creatives’ sizes match the IAB’s standard format recommendations needed to access inventory at scale.

| **Optimization & Delivery** | N/A - Set at campaign level | A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine whether optimizations will be automatically or manually applied, how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. |
| **Creatives** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Select one creative format per campaign, and add one creative or multiple creative versions. |
| **Inventory** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Specify where ads should be placed by targeting Open Exchange inventory, Contextual inventory, or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. |
| **Optimization** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Adjust individual campaign strategies such as bid amounts, creative rotation, and targeting criteria for different target-audience segments to improve performance. |
| **Conversions** | N/A - Set at campaign level | Implement and test conversion and postback pixels to measure how ad exposure impacts how your target audience interacts with your brand or its products and services. |
| **Reporting** | Report at the IO level to consolidate each of its strategies and gain an overall view of cost and performance. | Report at the campaign level to track the performance of specific targeting strategies and inform optimization decisions for current and future campaigns. |

## Campaign targeting elements

Each campaign includes a set of required and optional campaign targeting elements. The ones you’ll apply and customize will differ by campaign depending on aspects such as your ad’s creative format, your target audience, and your marketing objectives, for example.

Review the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for more information on each required and optional campaign targeting element, and refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) when you’re ready to apply these parameters and settings to a new or existing campaign.

## Key terms and concepts

### Advanced and Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) campaigns

When you create a new campaign, we’ll prompt you to choose whether it’s an **Advanced** or **Programmatic Guaranteed (PG)** campaign. The option you’ll select depends on the type of inventory that the campaign will target.

Choose **Advanced** if your campaign will target Open Exchange inventory or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. Select **PG** instead if you’ll purchase inventory directly from a specific publisher.

Note that certain features are supported for **Advanced** campaigns only. Selecting **PG** will reduce your campaign-targeting options as you instead agree to commit a set budget for a fixed number of impressions, and at a guaranteed price.

Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more information on Open Exchange, Private Marketplace (PMP), and Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory groups and the differences between these inventory sources.

### Campaign measurement

Data and analytics are central to connecting ad spend to business results, and determining whether a campaign achieved the goals that you defined for it.

The “Reporting and analytics” collection is your guide to uncovering and interpreting the data that you’ll use to improve performance across each of your strategies. This is made possible through IQM-platform features such as custom reports, insights reports, data dashboards, and more. Refer to [“Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) for a full list of this collection’s resources.

### Campaign optimization

> **More on campaign optimization:** You can enable AI Based Optimization in your campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings. This feature signals the platform’s AI engine to automatically optimize your campaign in an attempt to achieve the Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal that you define. It bases these optimizations on an initial pre-optimization learning phase, and later on ongoing KPI performance after AI Based Optimizations are applied. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on AI Based Optimization and requirements.

When you optimize a campaign, you apply data-driven decisions to it based on key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics such as conversions, cost per conversion, return on investment (ROI), and more. This process typically involves analyzing data, testing different approaches, and making adjustments to campaigns based on the results.

The “Campaign delivery and optimization” collection is your guide to each of the tools and features you can leverage to inform your optimization decisions and manage the overall performance of your existing campaigns. For example, you might apply advanced modeling to certain campaign dimensions, set up Allowlists and Blocklists, and optimize the campaign’s pacing performance. Refer to [“Campaign delivery and optimization” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11320980-campaign-delivery-and-optimization-collection-overview) to get started.

### Campaign Templates

> **Campaign template notice:** Items included in the **Campaign Info** section, such as budget, bid price, and date details, are excluded from campaign templates.

Streamline your campaign-creation operations by templatizing the [campaign targeting settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) that you plan to reuse in future campaigns.

Each time you create a new campaign, you’ll have the option to start from scratch or from a template. These templates can be created from either new or existing campaigns.

Campaign Templates are supported for both Advanced and PG campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) to get started with Campaign Templates.

### AI Insights

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical or high-risk blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for eligible campaigns. This diagnostic tool lets you know which issues are putting your campaign at the greatest risk, and what actions to take to address them.

Note that CampaignPulse is designed to help you detect and address significant risks to campaign delivery. For other campaign-optimization tools and strategies, refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview).

Review [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) to get started with CampaignPulse.

#### CampaignPulse eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to run CampaignPulse for eligible campaigns. Refer to the table below for campaign-eligibility criteria.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| Vertical | Specialty Political Healthcare |
| Campaign type | Advanced |
| Campaign status | Running, with a Start Date in the past |

Note that certain checks (IAB size checks for creatives, scheduling checks, and targeting checks) are triggered when CampaignPulse observes critical daily pacing on eligible campaigns. Refer to CampaignPulse delivery insights for more information on checked categories and their descriptions.

#### CampaignPulse delivery insights

CampaignPulse checks for human errors, conflicting campaign settings, and account issues that could put your campaigns at medium or high risk.

This feature continuously monitors campaign health to discover issues that could limit or stop ad delivery. It highlights actionable insights across account readiness, campaign setup, targeting, budgeting, delivery settings, and more to help keep campaigns running smoothly.

Refer to the table below for more information on what CampaignPulse monitors, and always review all CampaignPulse delivery insights closely for instructions on how to address the issues that can put your campaigns at risk.

| **Category** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Balance** | Monitors the Organization and Workspace’s account balance. |
| **Insertion Order (IO)** | Tracks each campaign’s IO to catch expired campaigns and conflicts between the campaign and IO end dates before serving is interrupted. |
| **Budget** | Surfaces IO-level budget constraints that can prevent otherwise eligible campaigns from serving. |
| **Creative** | Confirms each campaign includes at least one Ready creative, and that the creatives’ sizes match the IAB’s standard format recommendations needed to access inventory at scale. |
| **Audience** | Surfaces audience readiness issues that can prevent the targeting selections from being used. |
| **Scheduling** | Surfaces when dayparting is limiting available delivery time for an under-pacing campaign. |
| **Targeting** | Highlights when the creative format, device, and traffic configuration may be limiting eligible inventory for an under-pacing campaign. |

title: Campaign targeting guide

blocks.text: Campaign targeting elements are the building blocks of your campaign. When you define the campaign’s targeting strategy, you choose which of these elements to apply in order to strike the balance between scale, efficiency, and performance.

This guide outlines each of the elements that are listed when you create a new campaign or edit an existing campaign in the Campaigns app. The ones you’ll apply and customize will differ by campaign depending on aspects such as your ad’s creative format, your target audience, and your marketing objectives, for example. Review each required and optional campaign targeting element, and apply the settings that make the most sense for your campaign.

Campaign targeting rules help ensure that every marketing dollar goes toward the strategies that are the most likely to reach your target audience—but they also limit the number of impressions that you can bid on. This can put your campaigns at risk of spending in full.

Forecasting and reporting metrics provide a sense of scale to help you determine whether you can spend your campaign budget in full and achieve campaign objectives. Leverage your preferred tools in the Campaigns, Planner, Reports, and Insights apps to help right-size your campaigns’ Allowlist and Blocklist strategies:

**Campaigns app:** Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.

**Planner app:** Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.

**Reports app:** Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) to get started with [Performance reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) in custom reports.

**Insights app:** Refer to [Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to pinpoint the campaign elements that are causing the biggest drop-off in available bid requests.

**Apply Bid Model settings:** Because Allowlists and Blocklists limit a campaign’s scale, it’s important to reserve them for when you only want to bid on certain dimensions, or never want to bid on certain dimensions. If your campaign’s targeting parameters are flexible, consider applying Bid Model components to apply optimizations throughout the campaign. You can stop bidding on the campaign dimensions that aren’t performing well, bid more precisely based on how valuable an impression is to the campaign, and choose which dimensions the campaign should prioritize over others. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details.

blocks.text: The campaign’s top-most section–Campaign Info–is where you’ll specify the campaign’s overall settings. The budget and bid price amounts you enter will determine when the campaign will stop serving impressions, and which impressions it’s eligible to bid on based solely on their price. You’ll also enter a name for the campaign and choose its flight dates.

sections.heading: Campaign info key terms and concepts
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

sections.heading: Total Budget
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: Total Budget represents the full amount that the campaign can spend in total including any applicable data, media, and pre-bid expenses. You can set this budget at the campaign level, or distribute a single total budget across multiple campaigns.
Total Budget can be either a monetary value or impression value depending on whether a budget-based or impression-based insertion order was selected for the campaign.

sections.heading: Daily Budget
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: You can set a daily monetary or impression budget to influence how a campaign spends its budget or serves impressions. Daily budgets are distributed evenly throughout the day and include the media costs, data costs, and pre-bid targeting costs associated with the campaign.

Since daily budgets cap the amount that a campaign can spend each day, limit them to campaigns that are [pacing on track or pacing ahead](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform#h_6b2774c8f9).

sections.heading: Min Bid Price
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: **Min Bid Price notice:** Your Workspace admin may configure a Min Bid Price that will apply to campaigns that you create after this minimum is set. You can choose a Min Bid Price equal to or greater than that value. Contact your Workspace admin directly if you have questions or concerns related to this minimum requirement.
If your Workspace admin has not configured a Min Bid Price, the campaign’s default Min Bid Price is $0 unless you choose to update the value.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: A campaign’s Min Bid Price is the lowest price you’re willing to pay for 1,000 impressions. While optional, the Min Bid Price helps safeguard impressions from being delivered on sub-standard inventory as the campaign won’t bid on inventory priced below this amount.

Min Bid Price also acts as a lower cut off for the bids that would otherwise come in lower due to [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview). We ensure that no bids are placed below the Min Bid Price.
Note that the campaign’s Min Bid Price must be lower than its Max Bid Price.

sections.heading: Min Bid Price execution logic
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: The IQM platform will execute your campaign’s Min Bid Price settings based on four values: the effective Min Bid Price, the incoming floor price, the predicted CPM, and the effective max floor price.
Refer to the table below for examples of scenarios when the campaign would choose to bid or not bid on a given impression based on each of these values.

**Effective Min Bid Price**

blocks.text: In summary, the campaign will reject impressions if the floor is less than the effective Min Bid Price.

sections.heading: Max Bid Price
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: Max bid price represents the highest bid amount that we can place for your ad at auction. You specify this amount during campaign setup, or adjust it while the campaign is running. Like Min Bid Price, this amount is on a CPM basis.

Max Bid Price also acts as an upper cut off for the bids that would otherwise come in higher due to [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview). We ensure that no bids are placed above the Max Bid Price.
Note that the campaign’s Max Bid Price must be higher than its Min Bid Price.

sections.heading: Total CPM
heading_path: Campaign info key terms and concepts

blocks.text: Total CPM represents the cumulative maximum cost per mille based on the various cost components you include in the campaign. This value updates dynamically as you add parameters to your campaign that have costs associated with them. Since this value is the maximum possible price per 1,000 impressions, the actual purchase price is typically lower than this value.
The breakdown of Total CPM includes the following metrics:
[Max Bid Price](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343824-budget-reporting-metrics-overview#h_b1d212d790): Applies to the Total CPM when a Max Bid Price is defined for the campaign.
[Data Cost](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview#h_dac673c724): Applies when paid audience segments are included.
[Pre-bid Cost](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview#h_4eac063528): Applies when paid pre-bid segments are used.
[Ad Serving Cost](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview#h_a18e8d19cc): Applies when a hosted creative is added.

Refer to [Spending reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview) for more information on the metrics that are included in the [Total CPM](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343795-spending-reporting-metrics-overview#h_736a52fa8f) calculation.

Creatives are central to ensuring your message resonates with its intended audiences, and affects how users engage with your ad. Each campaign must include at least one creative, but many advertisers add multiple creatives to compare performance and adjust accordingly as the campaign progresses.

In a campaign’s **Creatives** section, you’ll select only one creative format, then choose creatives that you’ve previously added in the **Creatives** app, and/or upload new ones directly from the campaign. Refer to [Assign a creative to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10552784-assign-a-creative-to-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions on how to complete either process for both new and existing campaigns.

If you’re still building your creatives or haven’t added them to the Campaigns app, first refer to [“Creatives and specifications” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10553413-creatives-and-specifications-collection-overview) for more resources on preparing, adding, and managing creatives.

[Add one or more ungrouped or grouped creatives](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10552784-assign-a-creative-to-a-campaign) to the campaign. These creatives were previously added in the Creatives app.

Add a creative to the campaign that hasn’t been previously added in the Creatives app. Note that adding a creative via **+ New Creative** will not save it to the Creatives app for future use. If you plan to add the same creative to a future campaign, refer to [Add creatives](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11684680-add-creatives) for more information on how to add new creatives to your creative library.

Advanced modeling refers to the Bid Model optimization tool. Apply Bid Model settings to the campaign’s creative(s) to adjust bids with [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview), allocate budgets with [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), and define priorities with [Dimension Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview). Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more information on how these Bid Model components work individually and in tandem.

The **TV Ad Buying** option signals that you plan to run your campaign on the connected TV (CTV) and over-the-top (OTT) channels. Note that you must select the **TV Ad Buying** toggle in the **Creatives** section to enable the CTV and OTT **TV Traffic Type** options in the **Device** section**.**

Five advanced-targeting settings are available for video campaigns: Placement Type, Roll Position, Player Size, Skippability, and Playback Method. Refer to their descriptions below for more information.
**Placement Type**: Defines where the ad is placed in the requested page content.
**In-Stream:** The ad plays in a video player either before, after, or in the middle of a featured video.
**Out-Stream:** The ad plays within non-video content. For example, in-article videos, in-feed videos, and interstitial ads are all considered out-stream placements.
**Roll Position**: Defines where the ad can play in the requested video content.
**Pre-Roll:** The ad plays before the requested video content.
**Mid-Roll:** The ad plays after part of the requested video content has played.
**Post-Roll:** The ad plays after the requested video content has finished playing.
**Player Size**: Defines the size of the player in which the ad plays.
**Medium & Big:** The ad plays in a video player that is equal to or bigger than 300x400.
**Small:** The ad plays in a video player that is smaller than 300x400 pixels.
**Skippability:** Defines whether the viewer is allowed to skip the ad after watching the first few seconds of it.
**Skippable:** The ad plays in an environment in which a viewer can skip the ad after watching the first few seconds of it.
**Non-Skippable:** The ad plays in an environment in which the viewer is unable to skip the ad. In other words, the viewer must watch the entire ad.
**Playback Method:** Defines whether the video’s sound is enabled or disabled when the ad plays.
**Sound On:** The ad plays with its sound on.
**Mute:** The ad plays with its sound off.

Each advanced-targeting setting for video campaigns includes the Unknown setting. Not all exchanges provide information about video Placement Type, Roll Position, Player Size, Skippability, or Playback Method. Selecting **Unknown** will allow the campaign to target ad placements that do not specify these items. We recommend including this option in your campaign if you have scale concerns.
One advanced-targeting setting is available for audio campaigns: Roll Position. Refer to its description below for more information.
**Roll Position**: Defines where the ad can play in the requested audio content.
**Pre-Roll:** Signals the ad to play before the requested audio content.
**Mid-Roll:** Signals the ad to play after part of the requested audio content has played.
**Post-Roll:** Signals the ad to play after the requested audio content has finished playing.

**Unknown:** Allows targeting ad placements where the Roll Position is not declared in the bid request. We recommend enabling this option if you have scale concerns for your campaign as not all exchanges provide information about Roll Position for audio.

**Looking for pre-bid audiences?:** Pre-bid audiences are included in their own dedicated section of each campaign. Refer to Pre-bid audience below for more information on this campaign targeting element.
