# IQM platform overview

## IQM platform overview

The IQM platform is a next-generation demand-side platform (DSP) with integrated data management platform (DMP) features. It’s designed around a modular, app-based experience.

Each app within the platform is purpose-built to lead you through every stage of the digital advertising lifecycle. From data onboarding, to media buying and planning, to real-time performance reporting and campaign optimization, the platform will guide you to complete fundamental processes and make smarter decisions at every touchpoint.

Continue reading to learn more about the apps you’ll use to manage your account details and ad strategies.

> **Access and permissions notice:** This article outlines all IQM platform apps; however, not every advertiser will have access to each app. Access and permissions for individual apps depend on how your organization’s Workspace is configured. Contact your Workspace admin to request access to a specific app, as needed.

## Audiences app

Bring your own first-party data and leverage IQM’s data-management platform (DMP) to build audiences that perform.

### Primary Audiences app use cases:

- Generate audiences through first-party data uploads, pre-existing partner segment selections, and IQM’s proprietary audience capabilities.
- Locate and review key audience information such as uniques and cost.
- Depending on the audience type, populate key insights across genders, age groups, devices, and geographies to craft strategies based on the audience’s key characteristics.
- Assign audiences to campaigns directly from the app.

### More Audiences app resources:

- [Audience targeting and data management](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1387061-audience-targeting-and-data-management) collection

## Bid Model app

Add and manage advanced campaign modeling settings through the Bid Model app: the IQM platform’s most powerful optimization tool.

### Primary Bid Model app use cases:

- Review detailed performance across Creative, Location, Inventory, and Device campaign dimensions.
- Enhance campaign performance in real time by adjusting bids with Bid Modifiers, allocating budgets with Spend Ratios, and shifting ad-serving priorities with Dimension Priorities.
- Adjust your optimization strategy based on daily spend performance checks.
- Apply real-time optimizations through campaigns via tactics like blocking inventory, turning off creatives, and more.
- Download detailed reports for complete performance transparency.

### More Bid Model app resources:

- [Campaign delivery and optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/3156335-campaign-delivery-and-optimization) collection

## Campaigns app

Define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. You can control these strategies on a campaign-by-campaign basis, or at the insertion order (IO) level to manage them as a group.

### Primary Campaigns app use cases:

- Build and access insertion orders (IOs) and campaigns from a dedicated campaign-management hub.
- Set data, targeting, creative, and inventory parameters to launch high-performing campaigns.
- Forecast a campaign’s Reach, Impressions, and Audience Size based on your targeting rules.
- Take control of the way your IO’s individual campaigns deliver their impressions via campaign priority settings.
- Add campaign scheduling (dayparting) settings to spend more effectively and engage your audience when they are most likely to be consuming digital media.

### More Campaigns app resources:

- [Media planning and campaign setup](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1962110-media-planning-and-campaign-setup) collection
- [Campaign delivery and optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/3156335-campaign-delivery-and-optimization) collection

## Conversion app

Create and manage tags to attribute and measure user activity.

### Primary Conversion app use cases:

- Create Pixel conversion tags to measure user actions such as page visits, purchases, or signups.
- Add Postback conversion tags to allow for server-to-server communication with measurement partners, which you can use to measure and optimize your mobile ad campaigns more effectively.
- Create Universal Pixel conversion tags to track site-wide events and conversions with a single JavaScript tag. Unlike traditional pixels that are installed only on conversion pages, a Universal Pixel fires on all pages and supports multiple events (e.g., signup started and purchase completed).
- Test tags that you previously installed to ensure they’re firing as expected.
- Associate Pixel, Postback, or Universal Pixel tags with your campaign to assign credit for conversions.

### More Conversion app resources:

- [Conversions and tracking](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/3219750-choose-your-conversion) collection

## Creatives app

Add your creative assets to a library for streamlined creative management and targeting.

### Primary Creatives app use cases:

- Upload image, HTML, video, native, and audio creatives one by one or in bulk.
- Save time on managing your creative assets by grouping them together.
- Preview creatives to ensure they render as expected.
- Set and change click-through URLs to support creative performance measurement.
- Assign creatives to campaigns directly from the app.

### More Creatives app resources:

- [Creatives and specifications](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1387054-creatives-and-specifications) collection

## Customers app

Manage customer accounts, approvals, and finance details by customer.

### Primary Customers app use cases:

- Invite new customers and add their operational details.
- Review an existing customer’s details, such as their vertical and status.
- Review and approve pending campaigns, creatives, audiences, and inventory deals.
- Manage payments and invoices for a customer.
- Review customer balances and add payments.
- Add an absolute or percentage markup on top of the platform rate for certain platform features.

## Dashboard app

Monitor your campaigns’ real-time performance at a glance and make ad-hoc adjustments to them in the Dashboard app. You can create customized dashboards that fit your needs and track progress over time.

### Primary Dashboard app use cases:

- Customize your dashboard view to surface the metrics that are most important to you every time you log in.
- Adjust certain campaign elements—like budgets and bid prices—directly from a dashboard.
- Create custom reports and [Insights reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview#h_71f232030c) from a dashboard.
- Generate campaign reporting data in real time.
- Visualize performance reporting.
- Review comparison data related to two metrics, and determine top performers by grouping insights by a particular dimension and metric.

### More Dashboard app resources:

- [Data dashboards](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11510700-data-dashboards) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection

## Insights app

Surface granular data without the need for manual customization. Each Insights report includes a pre-defined set of metrics and is expertly crafted to focus on a distinct area, whether it’s a campaign’s available impressions or an audience’s characteristics and behaviors, for example.

### Primary Insights app use cases:

- Quickly identify trends to drive better campaign performance.
- Depending on the report type, gain a holistic and in-depth view of target user or campaign attributes to craft highly personalized campaigns.
- Customize reports with your own logo.
- Download and share the report’s data and visualizations.

### More Insights app resources:

- [Audience Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/6001105-audience-insights-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection
- [Campaign Bidding Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/10888147-campaign-bidding-insights-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection
- [Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12010878-provider-level-data-pld-insights-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection
- [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12083517-script-lift-study-sls-insights-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection
- [Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/10358580-voter-level-data-vld-insights-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection

## Inventory app

Secure coveted or premium inventory, drive inventory cost and reach performance, and target ad placements based on specific criteria such as ad format, placement type, or other relevant attributes.

### Primary Inventory app use cases:

- Explore all inventory that’s targetable via the IQM platform from the Open Exchange, PMP Deals, or custom contextually built site lists.
- Create inventory groups to target or block the same set of inventory across multiple campaigns and streamline your operations.
- Apply search terms and filters to narrow a list of inventory by the criteria of your choice.
- Find and target unique connected TV (CTV) and sports deals to enhance your campaigns.
- Add inventory to a Global Blocklist to stop ad serving on those sites or apps across all of your campaigns.
- Assign inventory groups to campaigns directly from the app.

### More Inventory app resources:

- [Ad inventory and placements](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/2908807-ad-inventory-and-placements) collection

## My Profile app

Add and manage account-level details and review your account’s seat assignments.

### Primary My Profile app use cases:

- Manage your profile name, account email address, and profile picture.
- Reset your account password.
- Search, sort, and manage all seats available to your account’s users.
- Review which Workspaces and Advertiser accounts are associated with an Organization.
- Review which integrations are associated with your account, and disconnect any of those integrations as needed.

### More My Profile app resources:

- [Account setup and management collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/14628352-account-setup-and-management)

## Organization app

Oversee and define user and account management details for your organization.

### Primary Organization app use cases:

- Invite additional users within your organization to the platform.
- Manage app-level access by user.
- Track payments.
- Set a default margin to be applied to all advertiser accounts.
- Add funds to your account.
- Review Activity Log details by user.

### More Organization app resources:

- [Account setup and management collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/14628352-account-setup-and-management)

## Planner app

Generate data-driven media plans based on your campaign targeting criteria. Use these plans to pre-optimize your audience and targeting details without allocating resources to test-and-learn campaigns.

### Primary Planner app use cases:

- Craft customized media plans tailored to your campaign’s objectives and targeting requirements.
- Define a single, unified plan across devices and channels to maximize campaign reach and impact.
- Segment a plan’s campaigns by elements such as audience, device type, and inventory for more control.
- Gain insights into a plan’s potential reach and impressions to optimize your campaigns before they begin serving.
- Easily transition from planning to execution with campaign management tools that automatically sync with your media plans.

### More Planner app resources:

- [Media planning and campaign setup](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1962110-media-planning-and-campaign-setup) collection

## Reports app

Drag and drop the dimensions and metrics that matter most to your business into streamlined reports. With this data, you can connect ad spend to business results, and determine whether a campaign achieved the goals that you defined for it.

### Primary Reports app use cases:

- Create custom reports from a number of available dimensions and metrics.
- Save your preferred combinations of dimensions and metrics for future analysis.
- Schedule reports to generate automatically.
- Download PDF or XLSX files containing your performance data.

### More Reports app resources:

- [Custom reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11287040-custom-reports) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection
- [Report dimensions and metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11287049-report-dimensions-and-metrics) subcollection of the [Reporting and analytics](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) collection

## Vera app

Meet Vera: Your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.

IQM’s rigorous privacy, compliance, and regulatory safeguards apply whether you partner with Vera or prefer to work manually.

### Primary Vera app use cases:

- Prompt Vera to create campaigns that reflect your strategy and requirements.
- Let Vera create ready-to-target Segmented audiences and Matched audiences.
- Tell Vera the dimensions and metrics that matter most to your business to build custom reports.
- Describe your performance-monitoring preferences to Vera to create data dashboards.
- Streamline your campaign operations by moving from idea to execution faster with Vera.

### More Vera app resources:

- ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview)

# Account types and entities overview

## Account types and entities overview

This article outlines the relationships between a Workspace, Workspace User, and Organization/Advertiser. These entities determine the types of information you can access for your own and others’ accounts, and the actions you can perform across the IQM platform.

## Workspaces

Workspaces are one of the core entities of IQM’s organizational hierarchy. With Workspace access, you can manage multiple accounts within an agency on the IQM platform, including:

- Manage the permissions and credentials of assigned Organizations/Advertisers–known as “Customers” in this relationship–so they can access data related to key platform features such as reports and audiences.
- Perform financial operations related to margins, costs, invoices, and credits.
- Access real-time data and reporting across all assigned Customers in one place.

## Organizations/Advertisers

A Workspace User may have access to multiple Organizations/Advertisers, but may only have access to certain apps as determined by the Workspace.

Once assigned to a Workspace User, Organizations/Advertisers can run ad campaigns in the IQM platform. In other words, insertion orders (IOs) and campaigns are created at the Advertiser level. These Organizations/Advertisers also manage their own balances.

## Entity descriptions and relationships

Refer to the details below for more information on the relationship between the Workspaces and Organizations/Advertisers entities described in this article.

### Entity definitions

| **Entity type** | **Entity description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Workspace** | An agency account that defines permissions and credentials for Customers. |
| **Workspace User** | An individual who uses the IQM platform in a Workspace. A Workspace User has Advertisers assigned as their Customers. |
| **Organization/Advertiser** | A company that places ads and is assigned to a Workspace User. When invited as a Customer, an Organization is created with details including its name, website, and location information. User-level access and permissions for individual apps depends on how the Organization’s Workspace is configured. |

### Entity relationships

Workspaces and advertisers have a parent-child relationship.

### Entity management

Organizations, Workspaces, and Users are primarily managed in the Organization app. Refer to [Organization Profile overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003037-organization-profile-overview) for more information.

## Locate additional resources

- [IQM platform overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002765-iqm-platform-overview)

# Organization Profile overview

## Organization Profile overview

All agencies with Workspace-level ownership can access the Organization app and use it to manage an Organization Profile. The **Profile** tab of the Organization app is where you’ll add your company’s details; and manage Organization-wide settings such as white label, invoice, and margin settings.

Refer to [Manage an Organization Profile](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003211-manage-an-organization-profile) to get started.

### Organization Profile settings

Review the table below for more information on the elements you can locate or manage in the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.

| **Tab title** | **Settings description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Organization Profile** | Review and manage company details such as its contact information and tax ID, areas of expertise, and the Seat ID associated with your Organization. |
| **Advertiser Profile Settings** | Provide Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA)-required advertiser information. It will be used to disclose details on the webpage linked to the Ad Icon & Ad Marker that’s associated with your ads. |
| **White Label Settings** | Manage visual and link settings including banner images, login page tabs, Fav Icons, and more.; Change your Workspace URL.; Enable URL white labeling, connect your domain, and verify the connection.; Enable Tracking (Pixel) Domain URL white labeling, connect your domain, and verify the connection. |
| **Invoice Template Settings** | Customize your invoice template with a custom header and details such as tax rate, available payment methods, payment term, other terms and conditions, and more. |
| **Margin Settings** | Set or change a default Gross Margin for new advertisers. |
| **Security Settings** | Choose which users must verify their identity by entering their password and a one-time verification code each time they log in (Multi-Factor Authentication). |
| **Feature Settings** | Review legal terms and opt-in to feature testing at the Workspace level.; Enable Workspace-level access to individual features.; Review the current development phase of each feature. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Political Advertiser Profiles

All political advertisers are required to provide a Federal Election Commission Identifier (FEC ID) or a state equivalent in their Advertiser Profile.

An FEC ID is assigned to a registered political candidate, Political Action Committee (PAC), or a US political party. This ID can be obtained in the Federal Election Commission Database.

Acceptable state equivalents for an FEC ID are registration numbers of state candidates or committees, or the regulatory IDs that states maintain for state-level political campaigns.

Refer to [Manage Advertiser Profile settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003211-manage-an-organization-profile#h_61ab908c44) to add an FEC ID or state equivalent to an Advertiser Profile.

## Locate additional Organization Profile resources

- [Manage an Organization Profile](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003211-manage-an-organization-profile)

title: Manage an Organization Profile

blocks.text: All agencies with workspace-level ownership can access the Organization app and use it to manage an Organization Profile. The **Profile** tab of the Organization app is where you’ll add your company’s details; manage Organization-wide settings such as white label, invoice, and margin settings; and manage account security settings for individual users.

Your Organization Profile includes key company details such as its contact information and tax ID, areas of expertise, and the Seat ID associated with your organization.
Follow these steps to add company details to an Organization Profile:
Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
Click **Organization Profile**.
Locate the **Company Profile** section and complete each field.

Check that each field pertains to the Organization. For example, in the **Organization Email** section, provide the official email address associated with your organization rather than the contact information of a specific individual.
If desired, hover your cursor over the logo field and select it to upload a profile image.
Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.
Follow these steps to add your company’s industry, size, ID, and other details to your Organization Profile:
Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
Click **Organization Profile**.
Scroll to the **Company Details** section and complete each field.
Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.
You have the option to include additional information in your Organization Profile related to the organization and its area of expertise. Other organizations can review this information.
Follow these steps to select an Organization Expertise for your Organization Profile:
Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
Click **Organization Profile**.
Scroll to the **Organization Expertise** section and complete one or both fields, if desired.
Enter 50 to 250 words describing your Organization.
Open the **Expertise** menu and choose one or more competencies from the provided list.
Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.
A Seat ID is a unique identifier that can be used for data sharing and integrations with external data partners.
Follow these steps to locate and obtain your organization’s Seat ID:
Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
Click **Organization Profile**.
Scroll to the **Seat ID** section.
Select the page icon next to the ID to copy it to your device’s clipboard.

**Political Advertiser Profile notice:** All political advertisers are required to provide a Federal Election Commission Identifier (FEC ID) or a state equivalent in their Advertiser Profile. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Political Advertiser Profiles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003037-organization-profile-overview#h_8f0cee354a) for more information.

Provide advertiser details that will be used to disclose details on the webpage linked to the Ad Icon & Ad Marker associated with your campaign’s ads. This disclosure is required by the Digital Advertising Alliance’s (DAA) creative guidelines.

Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.

# Manage an Organization Profile

## Organization Profile overview

All agencies with workspace-level ownership can access the Organization app and use it to manage an Organization Profile. The **Profile** tab of the Organization app is where you’ll add your company’s details; manage Organization-wide settings such as white label, invoice, and margin settings; and manage account security settings for individual users.

Refer to [Organization profile overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003037-organization-profile-overview) for more information.

## Manage an Organization Profile

Your Organization Profile includes key company details such as its contact information and tax ID, areas of expertise, and the Seat ID associated with your organization.

### Add Company Profile

Follow these steps to add company details to an Organization Profile:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Organization Profile**.
3. Locate the **Company Profile** section and complete each field.
4. Check that each field pertains to the Organization. For example, in the **Organization Email** section, provide the official email address associated with your organization rather than the contact information of a specific individual.
5. If desired, hover your cursor over the logo field and select it to upload a profile image.
6. Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.

### Add Company Details

Follow these steps to add your company’s industry, size, ID, and other details to your Organization Profile:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Organization Profile**.
3. Scroll to the **Company Details** section and complete each field.
4. Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.

### Select an Organization Expertise

You have the option to include additional information in your Organization Profile related to the organization and its area of expertise. Other organizations can review this information.

Follow these steps to select an Organization Expertise for your Organization Profile:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Organization Profile**.
3. Scroll to the **Organization Expertise** section and complete one or both fields, if desired.
   1. Enter 50 to 250 words describing your Organization.
   2. Open the **Expertise** menu and choose one or more competencies from the provided list.
4. Click **Save Changes** to apply your updates to the company profile.

### Locate an Organization Seat ID

A Seat ID is a unique identifier that can be used for data sharing and integrations with external data partners.

Follow these steps to locate and obtain your organization’s Seat ID:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Organization Profile**.
3. Scroll to the **Seat ID** section.
4. Select the page icon next to the ID to copy it to your device’s clipboard.

## Manage Advertiser Profile settings

> **Political Advertiser Profile notice:** All political advertisers are required to provide a Federal Election Commission Identifier (FEC ID) or a state equivalent in their Advertiser Profile. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Political Advertiser Profiles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003037-organization-profile-overview#h_8f0cee354a) for more information.

### Add a new Advertiser Profile

Provide advertiser details that will be used to disclose details on the webpage linked to the Ad Icon & Ad Marker associated with your campaign’s ads. This disclosure is required by the Digital Advertising Alliance’s (DAA) creative guidelines.

Follow these steps to add a new Advertiser Profile:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Advertiser Profile Settings**.
3. Select **+ Add Profile**.
4. Complete each provided field with the advertiser’s details, such as the **Website**, **Physical Address**, and for political advertisers, the **FEC ID or State Equivalent**.
   1. Enter **NA** into the **FEC ID or State Equivalent** field if neither are applicable.
5. Select **Add** to create the new Advertiser Profile.
6. Complete steps 3 through 5 for each additional Advertiser Profile you’d like to add.

### Edit or delete an existing Advertiser Profile

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Advertiser Profile Settings**.
3. In the **Actions** column of the desired Advertiser Profile, select the pencil icon to apply changes or the trashcan icon to delete.

## Manage White Label Settings for an Organization

If your Organization is white labeling the IQM platform, you can manage your brand’s visual settings in the Organization app.

   1. Select up to three payment types in the **Select Payment Type** menu.
   2. For each applicable payment type, enter the details.

   1. Choose the **Payment Term**.
   2. Enter a **Net** payment term. For example, a **Net** payment term of “30” indicates that invoice balances are to be paid within 30 days from the date of the invoice.
8. Add any **Terms & Conditions** to include in each invoice.
9. Enter an invoice footer.
10. Click **Preview & Apply Changes**. This will open the **Save This Invoice Template?** pop-up window, where you can review and save the template’s updated settings.

## Manage Margin Settings for an Organization

### Set a default Gross Margin for new advertisers

Follow these steps to set a default margin that will be applied to all new advertiser accounts:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Margin Settings**.
3. Enter the desired gross margin percentage into the **Default Margin** field.
   1. Whole-number percentages between 1 and 99 are supported.

### Set a default 3rd Party Cost for new advertisers

> **More on 3rd Party Cost:** The Organization app process outlined below allows you to add a default 3rd Party Cost for all new advertisers onboarded under the Workspace. You can also define a 3rd Party Cost for individual advertisers by following the steps outlined in [Add or manage a margin](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13902110-add-or-manage-a-margin).

Follow these steps to set a default 3rd Party Cost that will be applied to all new advertiser accounts:

2. Click **Margin Settings**.
3. Select the toggle switch to enable **3rd Party Cost**.
4. Enter the desired CPM cost.

## Manage security settings for an Organization’s users

The IQM platform supports Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to add an extra layer of security to the account-login process. When enabled, this feature requires users to verify their identity by entering their password and a one-time verification code sent to their email.

Workspace Owners and Advertiser Owners can manage MFA security settings for users linked to their accounts in the Organization app.

Refer to [Manage a user’s account security settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12933376-manage-a-user-s-account-security-settings) for step-by-step instructions.

You can opt-in to testing features before their release, and grant individual feature access at the Workspace level.

# Invite and manage users

## Invite and manage users overview

The Organization app is where you’ll invite users to your Organization’s Workspace. You can also manage app-level access for these users and assign customers to them.

## Invite users to your Organization

### Invite a new user

Follow these steps to invite new users to your Organization’s Workspace individually or in bulk:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **+ Invite**. This will open the **Invite Users** pop-up window.
3. If desired, upload, drag-and-drop, or import a CSV file to add multiple new users’ invitation details in bulk.
4. Enter a user’s email ID and full name into the provided fields.
   1. For each additional user, click **+ Add New**.
5. Select **Send Invite**.

All newly invited users will appear in the **Users** list and feature an **Invited** status until they accept the invitation.

### Resend an invite

Follow these steps to resend an invitation to a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Locate and select the user whose profile features an **Invited** status.
3. Click **Resend Invitation**.

## Remove users from your Organization

Follow these steps to suspend or delete a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click the ellipses menu next to the desired user’s name.
3. Select **Suspend User** or **Delete User**.
   1. **Suspend User** will temporarily suspend the user’s access to your Organization’s Workspace and prevent them from using any apps in the Organization. You won’t be able to retrieve the data associated with the user while their account is on hold.
   2. **Delete User** will dissociate the relationship between the user’s account and your Organization’s Workspace. You can add the same user again at any time by following the steps outlined in Invite users to your Organization.
4. Review and confirm your selection.

The user’s status will immediately reflect your changes.

## Manage a user’s app access

> **Default app access notice:** Upon creation, each new user is granted access to all platform apps by default. You can Revoke access to an app at any time. Note, however, that the user won’t have access to the Organization app, and the list of available apps is dependent upon how the Organization’s Workspace is configured.

### Assign access to an app

Follow these steps to grant app access to a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Locate and select the desired user.
3. Select the **App Access** tab.
4. Click **+ Assign App**. This will open the **Assign Applications** pop-up window.
5. Select the checkbox(es) next to the app(s) you’d like to allow the user to access.
   1. The list includes only the apps that the user can’t currently access.
6. Click **Assign** to apply the app-access settings to the user’s account.

### Revoke access to an app

Follow these steps to remove app access from a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Locate and select the desired user.
3. Select the **App Access** tab.
4. Select **Revoke Access** from the **Actions** tab for each desired app. This will open the **Revoke Application Access** pop-up window, where you can review and confirm your selection.

## Assign customers to a user

### Assign a customer to a user

> **More on Customer Management Access:** Customer Management Access is automatically enabled when Login Access is enabled for a customer. As a result, Customer Management Access can only be disabled when Login Access is also disabled.

Follow these steps to assign one or more customers to a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Locate and select the desired user.
3. Click the **Assigned Customers** tab.
4. Select **+ Assign Customer**. This will open the **Assign Customer** pop-up window.
5. Open the **Customers** menu to select additional customers.
6. If desired, enable **Default login for new customers**.
7. If desired, enable **Auto-assign new customers**.
8. To manage **Login Access** and **Customer Management Access** individually, use the toggles in the row of the applicable customer.
9. To manage **Login Access** and **Customer Management Access** in bulk, select the checkbox in the row of the applicable customer and select the desired action at the top of the table.
10. Click the checkbox(es) next to the customer(s).
11. Select **Assign** to confirm the customer assignments.

### Unassign a customer from a user

Follow these steps to unassign a customer from a user:

1. Select the **Users** tab of the Organization app.
2. Locate and select the desired user.
3. Click the **Assigned Customers** tab.
4. Select **Unassign Customer** from the **Actions** tab for each desired customer.

title: Optimization overview

blocks.text: Campaign optimization is the process of making data-driven decisions to improve a campaign’s performance. These decisions are based on metrics such as Conversions, Cost Per Conversion (CPC), Return on Investment (ROI), and other Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), depending on your marketing objectives.
Optimization isn’t a set-it-and-forget-it process. Instead, it involves analyzing data, testing various approaches, and making small, informed adjustments to the campaign based on the results.

Before you can optimize a campaign, you’ll first need to uncover and interpret data and insights related to that campaign. Your essential tools for reporting and analytics are data dashboards, custom reports, and Insights reports.
Your first step to optimization is understanding your campaign’s starting point: monitoring performance in real time, analyzing and comparing key metrics, and identifying trends.

You can monitor the campaign’s real-time performance at a glance and make ad-hoc adjustments to it in the Dashboard app. You can create customized dashboards that fit your needs and track progress over time.

After you begin applying optimizations, you can return to your dashboard to compare whether key metrics are performing better (% increase) or worse (% decrease) than they were during the previous reporting window.

Refer to [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview) for more information, including instructions on how to customize your dashboard, and information about each metric and dimension that you can measure there.

With the Reports app, you can drag and drop dimensions and metrics to create fully customized reports. Generate the insights that matter most to the business, and use them to inform current and future campaign optimizations.
All reports must include at least one dimension and metric.
**Metrics:** The numeric values—whether a number, percentage, or dollar amount—that can be measured. These values are listed as individual rows in the report.

**Dimensions:** The campaign elements, IO details, or campaign details that are the subject of the numeric values that you generate and assess. These attributes are listed as individual columns in the report and are used to segment the data.
For example, you might create a report to assess the number of Impressions (metric) related to a particular campaign (dimension).
Refer to [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) to get started with custom reports.

Insights reports include a pre-defined set of metrics and dimensions. They surface granular data without the need for manual customization. Each Insights report is expertly crafted to focus on a distinct area, whether it’s a campaign’s available impressions or an audience’s characteristics and behaviors, for example. Create one to quickly identify trends and determine the precise adjustments that could drive better results for your campaigns.
Refer to these resources to get started with Insights reports:
[Campaign Bidding Insights reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/10888147-campaign-bidding-insights-reports): Assess which targeting rules are limiting a campaign’s number of bid requests.

[Audience Insights reports:](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/6001105-audience-insights-reports) Assess key characteristics about your campaign’s audience, including interests, behaviors, and other user attributes.
[Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights reports:](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/10358580-voter-level-data-vld-insights-reports) Assess demographic and ad-exposure data by voter.

[Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports:](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12010878-provider-level-data-pld-insights-reports) Assess ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your healthcare campaigns.

[Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports:](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12083517-script-lift-study-sls-insights-reports) Assess the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx/TRx) volumes and competitors’ prescription patterns.

The ["Reporting and analytics” Help center collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1361396-reporting-and-analytics) is your primary resource for campaign measurement and insights. Review the [Reporting and analytics collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) guide for more information on each of this collection’s resources.
Your data deep dive uncovered an underperforming metric that you’d like to improve. Now you can improve campaign delivery and performance by applying informed optimizations to the campaign.

It’s important to note that you should apply one or few changes to the campaign at a time. Depending on how soon your campaign is ending, we recommend waiting 24 hours so you can reassess performance based on the optimization(s) you’ve made. Otherwise, it’s difficult to determine which changes are having the most impact.

Your essential tools for campaign delivery and optimization are AI Insights, advanced modeling, allowlists and blocklists, pacing management features, and Optimization & Delivery features. If you’re just getting started with campaign optimization, begin with advanced modeling: the IQM platform’s more powerful optimization tool.
AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for [eligible campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55). This diagnostic tool lets you know which issues are putting your campaign at the greatest risk, and what actions to take to address them.

Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) and [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview) for more information on getting started with CampaignPulse and to review campaign eligibility details.

No two campaigns are the same. Monitoring real-time performance and continually refining your strategy are crucial to ensure every dollar is spent efficiently—but this presents a challenge when you’re managing several campaigns simultaneously.

A Bid Model is a high-performance machine that you can steer to optimize your campaigns. You create a set of rules that the Bid Model deploys as the campaign runs. With intuitive controls, you can adjust bids with [Bid Modifiers](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview), allocate budgets with [Spend Ratios](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview), and define priorities with [Dimension Priorities](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview) to optimize performance in real time, and all in one place. While you have full control of this tool, its built-in functionalities help ensure your optimization settings are applied intelligently. For example, daily spend performance checks determine how your campaign’s Dimension Priorities are executed.

Refer to [Advanced modeling](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11511670-advanced-modeling) to get started with the Bid Model app and learn more about the Bid Model settings that you can apply to supported campaign dimensions.

Pacing determines if your strategies are on track to spend in full based on how much they’ve spent so far and how much time is remaining in the campaign or insertion order (IO). Taking an active approach to pacing helps ensure you gather enough trend details to inform your optimization decisions. You’ll decide whether to shift budgets to different strategies in real time based on market changes, or adjust other elements such as frequency caps to drive spend performance.
Review [Pacing](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11511672-pacing) to learn about pacing metrics (IO Pacing, Campaign Pacing, Daily Pacing) and where you can manage them throughout the platform.

Note that, while optimizing certain metrics is straightforward, the factors that can influence a campaign’s pacing performance are vast. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) to uncover the primary factors that can influence pacing performance and optimization recommendations to address them.

Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. These rules relate to various [campaign elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview#h_1ee82b6de6) such as Locations, Device IDs, Audiences, and more.
Refer to [Allowlists and Blocklists](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/11511753-allowlists-and-blocklists) to define which ad impressions your campaign is eligible to bid on.

**AI Based Optimization notice:** When you choose an AI Based Optimization method, you forfeit certain manual-optimization features such as Advanced Modeling. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the differences between the Rule Based and AI Based Optimization methods.

# Share an inventory group with a customer

## Shared inventory group overview

Workspace admins can [prepare inventory groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) and share them with their customers individually or in bulk. While your customers can target these groups, note that only the Workspace admin can apply changes to them.

## Share an inventory group with a customer

Follow these steps to share an existing inventory group with a customer:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **Groups** tab.
3. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory group(s).
4. Select **Assign to Customer**. This will open the **Assign To Customer** pop-up window.
5. From the **Customers** menu, select each customer that you’d like to have access to the selected shared inventory group(s).
6. Click **Assign** to confirm your selections.

All shared inventory groups will feature a folder icon next to their name, so your customers can differentiate between their own inventory groups and the one(s) you’ve shared with them.

## Review assigned customers

Follow these steps to share the customers that can currently access a shared inventory group:

1. Follow steps 1 through 2 of the Share an inventory group with a customer workflow.
2. Select the digit from the desired group’s **Customers** column. This will open the **Assign To Customer** pop-up window, where you can review and manage current customer assignments.
   1. Inventory groups featuring a **-** symbol in place of a digit haven’t been shared with any customers.

## Stop sharing an inventory group with a customer

Follow these steps to remove a customer’s access to an inventory group that you previously shared with them:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Share an inventory group with a customer workflow.
2. Review the table to review all customers associated with the selected inventory group(s).
3. From the **Actions** column, select the trashcan icon next to a customer to revoke their access to the selected inventory group(s).
   1. You can only stop sharing an inventory group with a customer when none of their campaigns are currently targeting that group.

## Apply changes to a shared inventory group

> **Inventory removal notice:** Any campaigns targeting an inventory group will be impacted by the changes you apply to that group in the Inventory app. Keep this in mind when adding inventory to, or removing inventory from, an inventory group that is shared with multiple customers. We also recommend notifying those customers of any changes so they can monitor campaign performance accordingly.

Follow the steps outlined in [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) to apply changes to an existing, shared inventory group. Unlike with traditional inventory groups, shared ones can only be managed by the Workspace admin that created them.

## Locate additional inventory group resources

- [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview)
- [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group)
- [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign#h_078f0c870c)

title: Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category

blocks.text: A Bid Model is an optimization tool that you can control to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities to optimize campaign performance.

Certain factors, such as eligibility requirements, differ based on the individual [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f) that you define for a campaign. Refer to these resources before beginning the process of applying a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension:
[Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview)
[Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview)
[Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview)
[Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview)

In this article, you’ll learn how to apply a Bid Model setting (Spend Ratio, Priority, Bid Modifier) to a Device dimension. You can also add Bid Model settings to Creative, Location, and Inventory dimensions. Refer to these resources for more details:
[Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension) category
[Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension) category
[Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300567-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-an-inventory-dimension) category

blocks.text: **Dimension category notice:** For certain dimension categories, Bid Modeling settings can be applied to only one dimension type at a time. For example, you can apply Bid Model settings to either States, Cities, or ZIP Codes for Location dimensions—not a combination of them.
An exception is the Device dimension category: you can apply Bid Model settings to Device Types or Traffic Types, or a combination of these two dimensions.

sections.heading: Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app
heading_path: Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

blocks.text: Open the Bid Model app.
Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
Search and select the campaign for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
Expand the **Device** menu.
Choose **Traffic Type** or **Device Type**, depending on the dimensions for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
In the **All Traffic Type** or **All Device Type** tab, click the checkbox(ex) next to the desired dimension value(s).
Select **+ Add to Modeling**.
Select the **Modeled Traffic Type** or **Modeled Device Type** tab, depending on the dimension values you selected.
To apply a Spend Ratio to these Device dimensions:
Locate the **Spend Ratio Method** column and choose **Flexible** or **Strict.**
Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options.
Note that Priorities are required for any items featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each dimension value.
The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
To apply a Priority to these Device dimension values:
Locate the **Priority** column.
Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each dimension value, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
Refer to steps 9a-9b to apply Spend Ratios to these dimension values. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimension values that are assigned a Priority.
Select **Update Changes**.
To apply a Bid Modifier to these Traffic Type or Device Type dimension values:
Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired dimension.

1X indicates that you want the Device dimension to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than its Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
Select **Update Changes**.
The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

**Bulk operations:** Steps 9, 10, and 11 share how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

blocks.text: You can follow the steps outlined in Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app to configure these settings for a **Bundle**. blocks.text: **Modeling removal notice: Remove From Bundle** and **Remove Modeling** are two different actions.

If you have applied Bid Model settings to the **Others** category, then the dimension value(s) will inherit those settings.

   1. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
4. Expand the **Device** menu.
5. Choose **Traffic Type** or **Device Type**, depending on the dimensions for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
6. In the **All Traffic Type** or **All Device Type** tab, click the checkbox(ex) next to the desired dimension value(s).
7. Select **+ Add to Modeling**.
8. Select the **Modeled Traffic Type** or **Modeled Device Type** tab, depending on the dimension values you selected.
9. To apply a Spend Ratio to these Device dimensions:
   1. Locate the **Spend Ratio Method** column and choose **Flexible** or **Strict.**
      1. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options.
      2. Note that Priorities are required for any items featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
   2. Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each dimension value.
      1. The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
   3. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
10. To apply a Priority to these Device dimension values:
    1. Locate the **Priority** column.
    2. Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each dimension value, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
    3. Refer to steps 9a-9b to apply Spend Ratios to these dimension values. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimension values that are assigned a Priority.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.
11. To apply a Bid Modifier to these Traffic Type or Device Type dimension values:
    1. Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
    2. Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
    3. Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired dimension.
       1. 1X indicates that you want the Device dimension to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than its Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.

The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Bulk operations:** Steps 9, 10, and 11 share how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Campaigns app

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the desired campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate and expand the **Device** section.
4. Select **Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Advanced Modeling** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Dashboard app

You can choose to optimize a campaign via Bid Model settings from the Dashboard app. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app and preload key details such as the campaign’s name and status.

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Filter the dashboard to determine which campaigns populate in the table.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign you’d like to optimize..
4. Select **Optimize Campaign** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
   1. **Optimize Campaign** is enabled when the campaign is eligible for Bid Modeling. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more details on campaign eligibility requirements.
5. Follow steps 4 through 11 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Block or unblock serving for a Device dimension

Follow these steps to block or unblock ad serving for a Device dimension:

1. Select the checkbox next to the Device dimension value(s) that you’d like to manage.
2. Select **Block** to stop ad serving or **Unblock** to enable ad serving.

## Manage Dimension Bundles

> **More on Bundles:** A **Bundle** is a feature that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Note that all dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Dimension Bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911) for more information.

### Save dimension values to a Bundle

Follow these steps to save one or more dimension values to a new or existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Traffic Type** or **All Device Type** tab, or the **Modeled Traffic Type** or **Modeled Device Type** tab.
2. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
3. Select **Save To Bundle**. This will open the **Bundle Devices** or **Bundle Traffic Types** pop-up window, depending on the type of dimension value(s) you chose.
4. To add the dimension values to a new bundle:
   1. Click **New Bundle**.
   2. Enter a unique name for the **Bundle** to differentiate it from others that you may create.
5. To add the dimension values to an existing **Bundle**:
   1. Click **Existing Bundle**.
   2. Open the **Bundle Name** menu and select the desired **Bundle**.
6. Select **Save**.

The **Bundle** “shell” will feature a dedicated row in the Bid Model table, with each bundled dimension value nested below it.

### Remove dimension values from a Bundle

Follow these steps to remove one or more dimension values from an existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Traffic Type** or **All Device Type** tab, or the **Modeled Traffic Type** or **Modeled Device Type** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the dimension value(s) you’d like to remove.
4. Select **Remove From Bundle**. This will separate the dimension values out from the **Bundle** and list it as its own standalone item in the Bid Model table.

### Delete a Bundle

A **Bundle** is automatically deleted when all dimension values associated with it are removed from the **Bundle**. Refer to the steps outlined in Remove dimension values from a Bundle for more details.

### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier to a Bundle

You can follow the steps outlined in Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app to configure these settings for a **Bundle**. Instead of in individual dimension values’ rows, however, you’ll apply each of your settings in the **Bundle’s** top-most row. All dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level.

### Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle

> **Modeling removal notice: Remove From Bundle** and **Remove Modeling** are two different actions. When you **Remove From Bundle**, the dimension value is separated from the Bundle and is modeled as an independent dimension. However, when you **Remove Modeling**, the dimension value moves to the **Others** category. If you have applied Bid Model settings to the **Others** category, then the dimension value(s) will inherit those settings.

Follow these steps to remove Bid Model settings from a **Bundle** or a **Bundled** dimension:

1. Select the **Modeled Device Type** or **Modeled Traffic Type** tab.
2. Locate and expand the desired **Bundle**.
3. Select the checkbox next to the **Bundle’s** name to select every dimension value within it, or click the checkbox(es) next to individual **Bundled** dimension values.
4. Select **Remove Modeling**.

## Manage an existing Bid Model

There’s no limit to the number of times you can add, change, or remove a running campaign’s Bid Model components.

### Review Bid Model settings

You can review a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Activity Log

### Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Open the Bid Model app.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to review Bid Model settings.
4. Expand the **Device** menu.
5. Choose **Traffic Type** or **Device Type**, depending on the dimensions for which you want to review Bid Model settings.
6. Select the **Modeled Traffic Type** or **Modeled Device Type** tab, depending on the dimensions you selected.
7. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.
8. Select the magnifying glass icon to search for individual dimension values, and click **Advanced Search** to search up to 50 of them.
   1. Type the desired dimension values individually into the available field.
   2. Select **Upload** to add a CSV file containing the desired dimension values. We recommend starting with the provided sample file to ensure your keywords follow formatting and other guidelines.
   3. Click **Search** to apply the search criteria to the listed dimension values.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate and expand the **Device** section.
4. Select **View Advanced Modeling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
5. Follow steps 4 through 7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Activity Log

The Activity Log records when a user adds or edits a dimension rule across any [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f).

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more details on the types of activities recorded in an Activity Log, and [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log) for instructions on how to monitor or filter one.

### Edit Bid Model settings

You can edit a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

> **Spend Ratio notice:** When you change an existing Spend Ratio, you must define a Spend Ratio exceeding the amount the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to a value of 21% or higher. For **Bundled** dimension values, the **Bundle’s** Spend Ratio must equal or exceed the total amount the campaign has already spent on its dimension values. Refer to in-platform descriptions for further assistance.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1 through 7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one dimension value’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, or **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one dimension value’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those items. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio**, or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Edit Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one dimension value’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, or **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one dimension’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those Device dimension values. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio**, or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of **Bundled** dimension values–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings from Device dimensions

> **Targeting notice:** There may be certain instances when you’d like for a campaign to stop targeting dimension values that you’ve modeled. You’ll need to delete all Bid Model settings from a dimension value before you can remove it from your campaign.

You can remove a Device dimension value’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1 through 7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Device dimension value(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Refer to Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle to complete this process for **Bundled** dimension values, if applicable.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Delete Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled Device dimension(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Device dimension values by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All (Traffic Type, Device Type)** tab, or select the **Modeled (Traffic Type, Device Type)** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

title: Healthcare Professional (HCP) Planner overview

blocks.text: When defining your ad strategy, it’s vital to craft a plan that meets your client’s requirements while achieving healthcare campaign goals and objectives. Healthcare Professional (HCP) media plans created in the Planner app give you powerful insights into your strategy’s potential reach and impressions once those parameters are layered onto your campaigns. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full—all without allocating resources to test-and-learn budgets. This includes segmenting HCPs based on factors such as medical specialty, geographic location, and more; and determining budgets and targeting criteria for each campaign.

The plans you create will automatically sync with campaign management tools. This means you can easily transition from planning to execution once you gain client buy-in. Simply convert an HCP Planner plan into healthcare campaigns in one click, add your creatives, and launch your pre-optimized campaigns.
Healthcare advertisers are eligible to generate HCP plans in the Planner app at no additional cost.

Note that there is a cost associated with each data partner selection you make while creating in-plan audiences. However, their CPMs only apply when you convert the plan into an IO and campaigns, and those campaigns begin serving impressions against those audiences.

You can locate a data partner’s CPM in the **Data Cost** section. Refer to [Create or manage a Healthcare Professional (HCP) Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12238868-create-or-manage-a-healthcare-professional-hcp-planner-plan) to get started, or continue reading for more information on HCP plans.
You’ll define the following required items for each plan, and apply targeting parameters across three optional categories, if desired.
**Section**
**Type**
**Description**
**Basic Details**
Required
Specify the plan’s name, time zone, date range, and [frequency cap](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_a623e383be) settings.
**Plan Settings**
Required
Choose either a [monetary budget or an impression budget](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) for the plan’s campaigns.
**User Types and Audience Methods**
Required
Select a user type (HCP, Nurse) and choose up to four Audience Methods for adding your target audience to the plan.
**Creative Types**

Confirm whether the plan’s campaigns will target image, HTML, video, and/or audio creatives. All Creative Types are selected by default, and at least one is required per plan.
**Device Types**
Required
Select one or more device types including TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile. All Device Types are selected by default, and at least one is required per plan.
**Channel Types**
Required
Select one or more channels including app, web, connected TV (CTV), and over the top (OTT). All Channel Types are selected by default, and at least one is required per plan.
**Location**

Choose one or more states, cities, or ZIP codes. Note that Location targeting settings are available while completing the Filter Based and Upload NPI List. audience-creation workflows

**Split Strategy**
Required/Optional

Every plan’s campaigns are segmented by Creative Type (required), NPI Type (required), and (Data) Partner (optional) by default. If desired, you can also segment your plan’s campaigns by the Device Type and/or Audience Type dimensions.

blocks.text: ***Impacted fields:** Changing an editable campaign value impacts other fields, or in certain cases, the entire HCP plan. This column describes which values will change when you update an editable field in a generated plan.

In addition to customized campaigns, HCP plans return forecasting metrics that help you evaluate the potential reach of your campaigns before launching them. You can review these estimates while you build the plan and after you create it, and at the plan level and individual campaign level.

**Forecasting notice:** Provided forecasts represent estimates that are based on the last seven days of data across the IQM bid landscape. The bid landscape is variable based on changes in available impressions, market seasonality, and other dynamic factors.

blocks.text: **Forecast metric or graph**
**Description**
**Reach**
A metric representing the estimated number of unique NPIs that are available for targeting.
**Impressions**
A metric representing the estimated number of times the ad will be served to the audience.
**Total Plan Budget**

The estimated total dollar amount that the plan’s campaigns can spend, which is calculated by using a formula of (impressions/1,000)*CPM. This value is based on the plan’s **Incremental Reach**, which includes only unique NPIs from each selected data partner based on the priorities you assigned. The budget will be calculated considering the Reach and data cost (CPM) at the partner level.
**NPI Type**
An interactive graph illustrating the estimated total NPIs available for an audience when no additional targeting rules are added, and what percentage of those NPIs are HCPs or Nurses.
**Specialties**
An interactive graph illustrating the estimated total reachable NPIs by each selected specialty.
**Accounts**
An interactive graph illustrating the estimated total reachable NPIs by each selected account type.
**Device Type**
An interactive graph illustrating the estimated percentage of impressions that will come from each device that the plan’s campaigns will target.
**Channel Type**
An interactive graph illustrating the estimated percentage of impressions that will come from each channel that the plan’s campaigns will target.
**Creative Type**

An interactive graph illustrating how different bid prices (CPM) might impact the potential number of impressions that you can win. This data is segmented based on the creative formats that you choose for the plan.
