cleaned_markdown:
# Create or manage a Political Planner plan

## Political Planner overview

Political Planner proposals provide powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions once you layer targeting parameters onto your campaigns. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each political campaign spends in full—all without spending resources on test-and-learn budgets.

Review [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview) to learn more, or refer to the instructions below to get started.

## Create a plan and generate strategies

Follow these steps to create a new Political Planner plan:

1. Open the Planner app.
2. Select **+ Create Plan**. This will redirect you to the **New Plan** page.
3. Complete the following plan sections:
   1. Plan Information - Required
   2. Custom Voter audience - Optional
   3. Basic Details - Required
   4. Locations - Optional
   5. Demographics - Optional
   6. Audience - Optional
   7. Pre-bid Audience - Optional
   8. 3rd Party Data Segments - Optional
   9. Creatives - Optional
   10. Device - Optional
   11. Inventory - Optional
   12. Advanced - Optional

Note that only certain sections are applicable and available for plans with a **Voter TV+** objective (Plan Information, Basic Details, Locations, Demographics, Audience).

### Plan information - Required

Follow these steps to complete the plan’s required **Plan Information** section:

1. Enter a name for the plan.
2. Choose a plan objective based on the information you’re bringing to the plan (e.g., budget or targeting rules) and what information you’d like to explore.
   1. If you selected **Reach Forecasting** as your objective, enter the total monetary budget for all of the plan’s strategies.
3. Click **Next**.

### Custom Voter audience - Optional

> **Custom Voter audience notice:** Custom Voter audiences help ensure your political campaigns reach the right users. These audiences are built using voter segments, and are customized based on locations, districts, demographics, party registration, and more. Refer to [Custom Voter audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview) for more information. Note that creating a new Custom Voter audience from a Political Planner plan is optional. If you’d like to skip this step, refer to Skip Custom Voter audience creation for step-by-step instructions.

You can create a Custom Voter audience directly from the plan, and in the following ways:

- Create with voter segments
- Create with AI assist

#### Create with voter segments

1. Follow steps 1 through 12 of the [Create with voter segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_7f8710f69d) workflow.
2. Click **Next**.

#### Create with AI assist

1. Follow steps 1 through 6 of the [Create with AI assist](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_45cde562d7) workflow.
2. Click **Next**.

#### Skip Custom Voter audience creation

Follow these steps to create a plan without generating a new Custom Voter audience:

1. Select **Skip & Next**. This will open the **Skip Custom Voter Audience** pop-up window.
2. Click **Skip** to confirm your selection.

### Basic Details - Required

Follow these steps to complete the plan’s required **Basic Details** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Basic Details** section.
2. Choose the plan’s start and end dates.
   1. Click **Apply** to add your selection to the applicable field.
3. Select the plan’s time zone.
4. Set a daily frequency cap, which limits the maximum number of times per day the same user should see your ads.
   1. Select **–** to decrease the **Frequency** number.
   2. Select **+** to increase the **Frequency** number.
   3. Frequency settings are supported for plans with a **Reach Forecasting** or **Budget Estimation** objective.

Note that plans with a **Voter TV+** also require a **Total Plan Budget**.

### Locations - Optional

Political Planner plans support location targeting within the United States. Follow these steps to add optional location targeting settings to the plan’s **Locations** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Locations** section.
2. Enter the desired location into the search field, or skip this step and browse the list of locations.
3. If desired, filter the results by location type.
4. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired location(s).
5. Click the **Zip Codes** tab to search and select locations by ZIP code, if desired.
6. Review and manage your selections in the **Targeted Locations** panel.
   1. Expand a section to review all locations by that location type.
   2. If desired, select the toggle to move a targeted location from the plan’s Allowlist to its Blocklist.

### Demographics - Optional

Use the available menus to select the plan’s target age group(s), gender(s), income range(s), and/or ethnicities.

Note that party affiliation selections (**Democratic**, **Republican**, **Unknown**) are also available for applicable plans with a **Voter TV+** objective.

### Audience - Optional

The plan automatically populates the **Audiences** section with the new Custom Voter audience you created during plan setup. Follow these steps to review and, if desired, add additional audiences to plan:

1. Locate and expand the **Audience** section.
2. Select the desired audience type(s).
3. Click **Select Audience**. This will open the **Select Existing Audience** pop-up window.
4. Search or browse and select audiences that you previously created in the Audiences app.
5. Select **Submit**.
6. If desired, select the toggle to move a targeted audience from the plan’s Allowlist to its Blocklist.

### Pre-bid Audience - Optional

Follow these steps to add optional Pre-bid targeting to the plan’s **Pre-bid Audience** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Pre-bid Audience** section.
2. Search or browse and select the Pre-bid audiences that you previously created in the Audiences app.
3. If desired, select **+ Add Pre-bid Segments** to search and add individual pre-bid segments instead.
4. Select the trashcan icon next to any segments that you’d like to remove. Note that doing so will only remove the segment from this particular plan–not from the original Pre-bid audience.

### 3rd Party Data Segments - Optional

Follow these steps to add optional data segments to the plan’s **3rd Party Data Segments** section:

1. Locate and expand the **3rd Party Data Segments** section.
2. Enter search terms, separated by commas, to search for specific audience characteristics.
3. All selected segments will appear in the **Select segments** list, along with their reach and cost details.
   1. Note that all segments added to this [Segment Group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_31da47f45c) are assigned an “OR” relationship.

### Creatives - Optional

> **More on creatives:** You won’t need to add your creatives until after you convert a generated proposal into an insertion order (IO) and campaigns. But we recommend reviewing [Creative ad specs and requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements) to ensure the creative(s) you plan to target in your plan’s campaigns will render and scale as expected.

Follow these steps to add a required creative-type selection to the plan’s **Creatives** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Creatives** section.
2. Select one or more creative formats.
3. If you plan to run on connected TV (CTV) or over-the-top (OTT) devices:
   1. Select the **Video** creative format.
   2. Click the **TV Ad Buying** toggle.

If no individual selections are made, the plan will consider all creative types in the strategies it generates.

### Device - Optional

Follow these steps to add optional device-targeting settings to the plan’s **Device** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Device** section.
2. Select one or more device types.
3. Select one or more channels.
4. Note that the **CTV** and **OTT** channel options only become enabled when the **TV Ad Buying** toggle switch is enabled in the plan’s **Creatives** section. Refer to Creatives - Optional for more details.

### Inventory - Optional

You can choose one of the following inventory-targeting options for your plan:

- **Open Exchange:** Public inventory sources made available via real-time bidding auctions. This option includes targeting individual IAB categories and/or exchanges.
- **Inventory Groups:** The eligible Open Exchange or Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups previously created in the Inventory app. Note that Open Exchange and CTV inventory groups created purely for blocking and groups with zero or unknown Reach aren’t eligible. Private Marketplace (PMP), Programmatic Guaranteed (PG), and Contextual inventory groups also aren’t eligible at any time.

#### Open Exchange inventory type

Follow these steps to add optional Open Exchange inventory targeting to the plan’s **Inventory** section:

1. Locate and expand the **Inventory** section.
2. Select **Open Exchange**.
3. To target IAB categories, which are the IAB Tech Lab’s page content categories:
   1. Open the **IAB Categories** menu.
   2. Search or browse and select all desired categories, or **Select All**.
4. To target specific exchanges:
   1. Open the **Select Exchange** menu.
   2. Search or browse and select all desired exchanges, or **Select All**.

#### Inventory Groups inventory type

Follow these steps to add optional Open Exchange or Connected TV (CTV) inventory group targeting to the plan’s **Inventory** section:

1. Select **Inventory Groups**.
2. Search or browse the list of Open Exchange and Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups.
3. If desired, filter the groups by group type.
4. Review key details about each inventory group:
   1. **Icon:** A circle icon next to the group name represents that the group is an Open Exchange inventory group, while the internet-connected TV icon represents that it’s a CTV inventory group.
   2. **Creative Type:** All supported creative format types are listed next to each inventory group’s name.
   3. **Count:** The total number of ad placements (**Inventories** or **Apps**) that match the search criteria you applied when you created the inventory group.
   4. **Device Breakdown:** The breakout of devices for each inventory group.
5. Click the checkbox(es) next to the inventory group(s) you wish to target.

### Advanced - Optional

> **Maximum campaign limit notice:** While a plan’s advanced split strategy allows you to create more precise campaigns, too many selections may cause you to exceed the plan’s maximum limit of 250 campaigns. If you receive an error related to exceeding this limit, we recommend changing your **Manual Campaigns** selection to reduce the plan’s campaign count.

You can segment the plan’s campaigns in the following ways:

- **AI Campaigns:** Let AI automatically segment the plan’s campaigns by supported dimensions.
- **Manual Campaigns:** Manually segment the plan’s campaigns by the supported dimensions of your choice (Location, Audience, Device Types, Inventory).

#### Segment with AI (AI Campaigns)

Follow these steps to automatically split the plan’s campaigns:

1. Locate and expand the **Advanced** section.
2. Select **AI Campaigns**.

#### Segment manually (Manual Campaigns)

Follow these steps to manually split the plan’s campaigns:

1. Locate and expand the **Advanced** section.
2. Select **Manual Campaigns**.
3. Click the checkbox next to a targeting dimension to segment your campaigns by that dimension.
   1. Open the dimension’s menu to select individual parameters, if desired.
4. Repeat step 3 for each selected dimension.
5. Review the number of campaigns that the plan will include.
   1. More detailed **Advanced** plan settings typically result in a higher number of campaigns.

### Generate Strategies

Follow these steps to generate media strategies from a plan:

1. Click **Generate Strategies** only when you are ready to activate the plan. In other words, check that you’ve completed desired plan inputs.
   1. Note that the **Generate Plan** button is clickable only after all required sections have been completed.
2. If you’re not ready to generate strategies from the plan, select **Save As Draft** to come back later.

Plans with a **Voter TV+** objective will include a **Next** button in place of the **Generate Strategies**. This redirects you to cross-screen planning settings and insights. Refer to Voter TV+ for step-by-step instructions.

### Voter TV+

Follow these steps to manage cross-screen planning settings and insights for plans with a **Voter TV+** objective:

1. Enter the linear TV baseline details (**Linear TV CPM**, **GRP (Linear TV)**.
2. Enter the CTV pricing and frequency details (**CTV CPM**, **Total Campaign Frequency (CTV)**).
3. Manage the plan’s **Budget Allocation Split** settings to define how you’d like to model the plan’s **Audience Overlap** data.
   1. Move the slider to allocate more budget to Linear TV or CTV.
   1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Reach Distribution Settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_760bf98811) for more details.
4. Review reach forecasting metrics based on the plan’s **Reach Distribution Settings**.
   1. Note that **Audience Overlap** metrics are calculated against the selected voter universe.
   2. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Audience Overlap](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_b008e37f2d) for more details.
5. Select **Generate Proposal**.

The proposal will begin generating immediately.

## Review or add strategies and generate a proposal

> **Strategy notice:** Reviewing and adding strategies is applicable for plans with a **Reach Forecasting** or **Budget Estimation** objective.

### Review strategies

Depending on your plan inputs, a single plan may include up to five strategies. You’ll arrive at this page automatically when you select **Generate Strategies** from the plan creation workflow.

Refer to [Plan outputs - Strategies](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_b9e75d8d8d) for more information each row.

### Edit strategies

Strategies can’t be directly edited. You can however, make adjustments to the plan itself by selecting **Edit Plan**.

After you apply your desired changes, refer to Generate Strategies to restart the strategy generation process and return to the **Strategies** page.

### Edit a plan - Voter TV+

For plans with a **Voter TV+** objective, you have the option to edit the plan’s [Reach Distribution Settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_760bf98811).

Follow these steps to edit an existing plan’s Reach Distribution Settings:

1. Select the **Plans** tab.
2. Click the pencil icon in the **Actions** column of the desired plan.
3. Select **Next** until you reach the **3 out of 3 Steps** page of the plan.
4. Enter the linear TV baseline details (**Linear TV CPM**, **GRP (Linear TV)**.
5. Enter the CTV pricing and frequency details (**CTV CPM**, **Total Campaign Frequency (CTV)**).
6. Manage the plan’s **Budget Allocation Split** settings to define how you’d like to model the plan’s **Audience Overlap** data.
   1. Move the slider to allocate more budget to Linear TV or CTV.
   2. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Reach Distribution Settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_760bf98811) for more details.
7. Click **Save Plan** to apply the changes.

### Add a strategy

You can add a new strategy in one of two ways:

- From scratch
- From an existing strategy

#### Add a strategy from scratch

Follow these steps to manually enter all inputs for a new strategy:

1. Select **+ Add Strategy**. This will open the **Add Strategy** pop-up window.
2. Enter a name for the strategy.
3. Choose the **From Existing Strategy** creation method.
4. Click **Add**. This will open a plan creation form, with the existing strategy’s details prefilled.
5. Follow the steps outlined in Create a plan and generate strategies to update the plan elements of your choice. Note that only the following elements can be added:
   1. Frequency
   2. Pre-bid Audience
   3. 3rd Party Data Segments
   4. Inventory
   Other sections’ edits are limited to removing existing inputs.
6. Select **Generate Strategy** to create the new strategy.

#### Add a strategy from an existing strategy

Follow these steps to create a new strategy starting from an existing strategy’s pre-filled details:

1. Select **+ Add Strategy**. This will open the **Add Strategy** pop-up window.
2. Enter a name for the strategy.
3. Choose the **From Existing Strategy** creation method.
4. Open the **Strategy** menu and choose an existing strategy to start from.
5. Click **Add**. This will open a plan creation form, with the existing strategy’s details prefilled.
6. Follow the steps outlined in Create a plan and generate strategies to update the plan elements of your choice. Note that only the following elements can be added:
   1. Frequency
   2. Pre-bid Audience
   3. 3rd Party Data Segments
   4. Inventory
   Other sections’ edits are limited to removing existing inputs.
7. Select **Generate Strategy** to create the new strategy.

### Generate a proposal

> **Voter TV+ notice:** Follow the steps outlined in Voter TV+ instead to generate a proposal for a plan with a **Voter TV+** objective.

To generate a proposal, select **Generate Proposal** in the desired strategy’s column.

The proposal will begin generating immediately. You can open and adjust the proposal by following the steps outlined in Review and manage a generated proposal.

## Review and manage a generated proposal

### Review a proposal

Proposals featuring a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Converted** status can be reviewed. You can review proposals in the following ways:

- From the **Strategies** page of a plan
- From the **Proposals** tab

#### Review a proposal from the Strategies page

Follow these steps to review a proposal from the plan’s **Strategies** page:

1. Select the number of proposals listed next to **Generated Proposals**. This will open the **Generated Proposals** pop-up window.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Proposal Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.

#### Review a proposal from the Proposals tab

Follow these steps to review a proposal from the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.

### Edit a proposal

#### Edit proposals with a Reach Forecasting or Budget Estimation objective

You can change a generated proposal’s name and start date, and the names of each of the proposal’s campaigns.

Follow these steps to apply changes to a generated proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Located the desired proposal elements.
4. Click **Update Changes**.

#### Edit proposals with a Voter TV+ objective

You can change a generated proposal’s **CTV Budget** and/or **Linear TV** budget and the names of each of the proposal’s campaigns. If you added location targeting settings during plan creation, you can also split the proposal’s campaigns by location.

Follow these steps to apply changes to a generated proposal:

1. Follow steps 1 through 2 of Edit proposals with a Reach Forecasting or Budget Estimation objective.
2. Apply the desired changes to the proposal.
   1. Edit the **CTV Budget**, if applicable.
   2. Edit the **Linear TV Budget**, if applicable.
   3. Split the proposal’s campaigns by the location dimension.
   4. Select the **Campaign Name** field to change a campaign’s name.
3. Click **Edit Plan**.

### Download a proposal

Proposals featuring a **Ready**, **Processing**, **Converted**, **Failed**, or **Processing** status can be downloaded. You can download proposals in the following ways:

- From within a proposal
- From the **Proposals** tab

#### Download a proposal from within a proposal

Follow these steps to download a proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Open the **Download** menu.
4. Choose **Download as CSV** or **Download as XLSX**, depending on your preference.
   1. Proposals generated from plans with a **Voter TV+** objective can be downloaded as a PDF or XLSX file.

#### Download a proposal from the Proposals tab

Follow these steps to download a proposal from the Proposals tab of the Planner app:

1. Click the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the download icon in the desired proposal’s **Actions** column.
3. Choose **Download as CSV** or **Download as XLSX**, depending on your preference.
   1. Proposals generated from plans with a **Voter TV+** objective can be downloaded as a PDF or XLSX file.

### Duplicate a proposal

Proposals featuring a **Ready**, **Processing**, **Converted**, **Failed**, or **Processing** status can be duplicated. You can duplicate proposals in the following ways:

- From within a proposal
- From the **Plans** tab

#### Duplicate a proposal from within a proposal

Follow these steps to duplicate a proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Click the page icon. This will open the **Duplicate Plan** pop-up window.
4. Enter the plan’s name.
5. Choose the plan’s start and end dates.
6. Select **Duplicate**.
7. Follow the steps outlined in Create a plan to choose the plan’s inputs and generate strategies. The existing plan’s details are pre-filled.

#### Duplicate a proposal from the Plans tab

Follow these steps to duplicate a proposal from the **Plans** tab of the Planner app:

1. Select the **Plans** tab.
2. Click the page icon from the desired plan’s **Actions** column. This will open the **Duplicate Plan** pop-up window.
3. Enter the plan’s name.
4. Choose the plan’s start and end dates.
5. Select **Duplicate**.
6. Follow the steps outlined in Create a plan to choose the plan’s inputs and generate strategies. The existing plan’s details are pre-filled.

### Delete a proposal

Proposals featuring a **Ready**, **Failed**, or **Expired** status can be deleted. You can delete proposals in the following ways:

- From within a proposal
- From the **Proposals** tab

#### Delete a proposal from within a proposal

Follow these steps to delete a proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Select the trashcan icon.

#### Delete a proposal from the Proposals tab

Follow these steps to delete a proposal from the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app:

1. Click the **Proposals** tab.
2. Open the ellipses menu from the desired proposal’s **Actions** column.
3. Select **Delete**.

### Restore an expired proposal

Follow these steps to restore an expired proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Click the checkbox next to the expired proposal that you’d like to restore.
3. Select **Restore**. This will open the **Restore Proposal** pop-up window.
4. Choose a new start date for the proposal.
5. Click **Restore**.

### Edit a proposal’s campaigns

You can edit one element of a proposal’s campaigns: their names.

Follow the steps outlined in Edit a proposal to change a campaign’s name.

### Delete a proposal’s campaigns

> **Deletion notice:** Note that deleted campaigns are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating a proposal before deleting any campaigns from it.

Follow these steps to delete campaigns from a generated proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Locate the **Campaigns** section.
4. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s) you’d like to delete.
5. Click **Delete**.

## Generate campaigns from a proposal

Once a proposal features a **Ready** status, you can generate its campaigns. This will convert a proposal into an insertion order (IO) and campaigns. Refer to [Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266003-generate-campaigns-from-a-political-planner-proposal) for step-by-step instructions.

## Locate additional Political Planner resources

- [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview)
- [Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266003-generate-campaigns-from-a-political-planner-proposal)
- [Troubleshoot a Political Planner plan, proposal, or campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266007-troubleshoot-a-political-planner-plan-proposal-or-campaign)

cleaned_markdown:
# Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal

## Campaign generation overview

The proposals you create in Political Planner define a single, unified media plan across channels and devices to maximize the reach and impact of your political campaigns. You can easily transition from planning to execution by generating campaigns from your proposals.

Refer to [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview) for more information.

## Generate campaigns from a proposal

> **Campaign generation notice:** All of a proposal’s campaigns will attempt to generate when you select **Generate Campaigns**. You can exclude campaigns by deleting them from the proposal. Follow the steps outlined in [Delete a proposal's campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan#h_cf6b75f5d6) for step-by-step instructions.

You can generate a proposal’s campaigns in the following ways:

- From the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app
- From within a proposal

### Generate campaigns from the Proposals tab

Follow these steps to generate campaigns from the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app:

1. Open the Planner app.
2. Select the **Proposals** tab.
3. Click **Generate Campaigns** from the desired proposal’s **Actions** column.

The proposal’s status will change from **Ready** to **Processing** while we work on generating the campaigns, then from **Processing** to **Converted** when the process is complete. You can view and manage generated campaigns once they reach a **Converted** status.

### Generate campaigns from within a proposal

Follow these steps to generate campaigns from within a proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal’s name from the **Name** column. This redirects you to the proposal’s details.
3. Locate the **Campaigns** table and review each campaign.
4. Click **Generate Campaigns**.

The proposal’s status will change from **Ready** to **Processing** while we work on generating the campaigns, then from **Processing** to **Converted** when the process is complete. You can view and manage generated campaigns once they reach a **Converted** status.

## Manage generated campaigns

You’ll need to add your creative(s) to your campaigns before you can run them. You can review or manage campaigns that you generated from a Political Planner proposal in the following ways:

- From the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app
- From within a proposal

> **Save time with bulk actions:** If you plan to apply the same creative to multiple campaigns, assign it from the Creatives app instead. Simply follow the steps outlined in [Assign a creative to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10552784-assign-a-creative-to-a-campaign). Return to the Campaigns app when you’re ready to run the campaigns.

### Manage generated campaigns from the Proposals tab

Follow these steps to manage generated campaigns from the **Proposals** tab of the Planner app:

1. Open the Planner app.
2. Select the **Proposals** tab.
3. Locate the desired proposal, which must feature a **Converted** status.
4. Click **View Campaigns** in the desired proposal’s **Actions** column. This will redirect you to the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app.
5. Select a campaign from the **Campaign Name** column to open its detail page.
6. Locate and expand the Creative section. The creative formats you chose in your HCP Planner plan are pre-selected.
7. Click **+ Select Creatives** to add a creative you’ve already uploaded to the **Creatives** app, or **+ New Creative** to add a new one.
8. The remaining sections of the campaign automatically include each of the inputs you specified in your plan. You can review and update these items or any other section of the campaign, if desired.
   1. Any changes applied to the campaign will impact the values previously forecasted in your HCP Planner plan.
9. Select **Run** to run the campaign.

### Manage generated campaigns from within a proposal

Follow these steps to manage generated campaigns from within a generated proposal:

1. Select the **Proposals** tab.
2. Select the desired proposal from the **Name** column. This will open the proposal and its details.
3. Click **View Campaigns**. This will redirect you to the **Insertion Order Info** page of the Campaigns app.
4. Follow steps 5 through 9 of the Manage generated campaigns from the Proposals tab workflow.

## Locate additional Political Planner resources

- [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview)
- [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan)
- [Troubleshoot a Political Planner plan, proposal, or campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266007-troubleshoot-a-political-planner-plan-proposal-or-campaign)

title: Troubleshoot a Political Planner plan, proposal, or campaign

blocks.text: You’ll need to follow specific steps to successfully create a Planner proposal and generate campaigns from it. If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating or managing plans, proposals, and/or campaigns, refer to these resources first:
[Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview)
[Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan)
[Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266003-generate-campaigns-from-a-political-planner-proposal)
Return to this article to address and resolve other factors that may block your workflow.

sections.heading: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

sections.heading: Maximum campaign limit exceeded
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

blocks.text: You’ll receive a “This proposal draft exceeds the maximum limit of 250 campaigns” error when your current plan-form entries will produce too many campaigns.

You likely used the plan’s **Advanced** section to segment your campaigns by individual targeting categories and subcategories. This segmentation allows you to create more precise campaigns, but too many selections can cause you to exceed the maximum limit of 250 campaigns.
Follow these steps to address the issue:
If possible, change the selection from **Manual Campaigns** to **AI Campaigns**.
If **Manual Campaigns** is still selected, deselect certain Locations, Audiences, Device Types, and/or Inventory until the number of campaigns fall below the maximum limit.
If you haven’t made **Advanced** selections but are still exceeding the maximum 250-campaign limit, we recommend adjusting your plan’s targeting rules.

sections.heading: Minimum reach not met
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

blocks.text: A plan’s reach is the estimated number of individual users who will be exposed to your ad at least once during the campaign. Plans require a minimum reach of 1K users.

You’ll need to adjust your plan’s targeting criteria to expand the universe of users you can reach with your strategies. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - IQM Universe](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_be1b77ebf8) for more information.

sections.heading: Proposal is processing
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

blocks.text: When you generate a proposal by selecting **Generate Campaigns**, we sync it with IQM’s campaign management tools to ensure that all of your targeting rules are applied. This process typically takes approximately one hour to complete.
Contact your IQM account representative if your proposal fails to move from **Processing** to **Converted**.

sections.heading: Unable to select past dates
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

blocks.text: As Political Planner generates forward-looking strategies tailored to your upcoming campaigns’ objectives and targeting rules, you can select only future dates when creating a plan.
If you’d like to generate and review performance data for past campaigns instead, visit the Reports app and Insights app.

sections.heading: Targetable locations limited to United States
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting
Targetable locations limited to United States

blocks.text: Plans target the United States by default. You can add more granular targeting by selecting options such as states, Designated Market Areas (DMA), counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses.
Non-US targeting is not currently supported.

sections.heading: Targetable locations limited to “OR” relationship
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

blocks.text: Plans apply an “OR” relationship to your location targeting settings by default. This means the campaign will target a user if they’re located in any of the locations you chose, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

sections.heading: Certain data segments aren’t clickable
heading_path: Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

# Troubleshoot a Political Planner plan, proposal, or campaign

## Political Planner troubleshooting overview

You’ll need to follow specific steps to successfully create a Planner proposal and generate campaigns from it. If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating or managing plans, proposals, and/or campaigns, refer to these resources first:

- [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview)
- [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan)
- [Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266003-generate-campaigns-from-a-political-planner-proposal)

Return to this article to address and resolve other factors that may block your workflow.

## Political Planner plan and proposal troubleshooting

### Maximum campaign limit exceeded

You’ll receive a “This proposal draft exceeds the maximum limit of 250 campaigns” error when your current plan-form entries will produce too many campaigns.

You likely used the plan’s **Advanced** section to segment your campaigns by individual targeting categories and subcategories. This segmentation allows you to create more precise campaigns, but too many selections can cause you to exceed the maximum limit of 250 campaigns.

Follow these steps to address the issue:

1. If possible, change the selection from **Manual Campaigns** to **AI Campaigns**.
2. If **Manual Campaigns** is still selected, deselect certain Locations, Audiences, Device Types, and/or Inventory until the number of campaigns fall below the maximum limit.
3. If you haven’t made **Advanced** selections but are still exceeding the maximum 250-campaign limit, we recommend adjusting your plan’s targeting rules.

### Minimum reach not met

A plan’s reach is the estimated number of individual users who will be exposed to your ad at least once during the campaign. Plans require a minimum reach of 1K users.

You’ll need to adjust your plan’s targeting criteria to expand the universe of users you can reach with your strategies. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - IQM Universe](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview#h_be1b77ebf8) for more information.

### Proposal is processing

When you generate a proposal by selecting **Generate Campaigns**, we sync it with IQM’s campaign management tools to ensure that all of your targeting rules are applied. This process typically takes approximately one hour to complete.

Contact your IQM account representative if your proposal fails to move from **Processing** to **Converted**.

### Unable to select past dates

As Political Planner generates forward-looking strategies tailored to your upcoming campaigns’ objectives and targeting rules, you can select only future dates when creating a plan.

If you’d like to generate and review performance data for past campaigns instead, visit the Reports app and Insights app.

### Targetable locations limited to United States

Plans target the United States by default. You can add more granular targeting by selecting options such as states, Designated Market Areas (DMA), counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses.

Non-US targeting is not currently supported.

### Targetable locations limited to “OR” relationship

Plans apply an “OR” relationship to your location targeting settings by default. This means the campaign will target a user if they’re located in any of the locations you chose, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

### Certain data segments aren’t clickable

You can choose up to 100 audience segments. If you’ve reached this limit but want to select a different segment, then you’ll first need to remove a selected one.

### Certain targeting categories are missing

Note that only certain sections are applicable and available for plans with a **Voter TV+** objective (Plan Information, Basic Details, Locations, Demographics, Audience).

Refer to [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan#h_4bf5438655) for a complete list of targeting categories available for plans with a **Reach Forecasting** or **Budget Estimation** objective.

### No Inventory Groups are shown

You’ll need to create an inventory group in the Inventory app before you can add it to your proposal. That inventory group must also have a known Reach greater than zero. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for step-by-step instructions.

If you’ve already created an inventory group but it’s not populating in the plan-creation form, note that only Open Exchange and Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups are supported.

Refer to [Inventory - Open Exchange inventory type](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan#h_5e8d4e0a7c) if you’d like to choose individual IAB categories and/or exchanges to target instead.

### Contextual Inventory Groups or PMP Inventory Groups are missing

Only Open Exchange and Connected TV (CTV) inventory group types are supported in Political Planner proposals. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more information on creating inventory groups in the Inventory app.

### CTV and/or OTT devices aren’t clickable

You can target CV and OTT devices if you selected **Video** in the plan’s **Creatives** section and selected the **TV Ad Buying** toggle switch. These selections will enable the **CTV** and **OTT** buttons in the **Devices** section.

### Unable to add a strategy

The **+ Add Strategy** button becomes enabled only when four or fewer strategies are shown on the **Strategies** page.

### Strategies section is missing

The strategy review and creation workflow is only applicable for plans with a **Reach Forecasting** or **Budget Estimation** objective.

Refer to [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan#h_4bf5438655) to learn how to generate a proposal from a plan with a **Voter TV+** objective.

### Unable to edit, duplicate, download, or delete a plan or proposal

The ability to manage a plan or generated proposal depends on its current status.

Refer to [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan) for more information on supported actions by status.

### Generated proposal is missing Linear TV campaigns

Linear TV data is a reference baseline that’s included to model incremental CTV reach. No Linear TV campaigns are created or activated during the media-planning process in Political Planner.

## Political Planner campaign troubleshooting

### Time zone isn't editable

Generated campaigns use the same time zone as the location where the proposal was initially generated. While you can’t edit this setting, you can edit start and end dates directly in a plan’s draft.

### Campaign generation failed

In certain cases, campaigns may fail to generate after you select **Generate Campaigns**. This error is typically related to a technical issue. For example, your IQM login or device’s browser may have timed out.

Refresh your browser and select **Generate Campaigns** again to retry. Contact your IQM representative if the issue persists.

### Unable to choose which campaigns to generate

All of a proposal’s campaigns will generate when you select **Generate Campaigns**. You’ll need to delete any campaigns that you’d like to exclude. Note that deleted campaigns are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent.

Refer to [Delete a proposal's campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan#h_cf6b75f5d6) for additional information.

## Locate additional Political Planner resources

- [Political Planner overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265995-political-planner-overview)
- [Create or manage a Political Planner plan](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15265999-create-or-manage-a-political-planner-plan)
- [Generate campaigns from a Political Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15266003-generate-campaigns-from-a-political-planner-proposal)

# Vera overview

## Vera overview

Meet Vera: Your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.

You can work on multiple tasks in a single chat. For example, create a campaign, then build an audience and generate a report for it, without starting a new conversation. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

IQM’s rigorous privacy, compliance, and regulatory safeguards apply whether you partner with Vera or prefer to work manually.

## Vera eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to manage campaign operations in the Vera app. Note that access and permissions for individual apps and features depend on how your organization’s Workspace is configured. Contact your Workspace admin to request access, as needed.

Requirements and best practices are the same whether you manually manage your campaigns in dedicated apps (e.g., Audiences, Dashboards, Campaigns, Reports) or with AI assistance in the Vera app. Refer to the resources listed below to review those requirements and best practices.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Vertical** | Specialty Political Healthcare |
| **Audiences*** | [Matched audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview) [Segmented audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview) [Contextual audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview) |
| **Data dashboards** | [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview) |
| **Campaigns** | [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) |
| **Custom reports** | [Reports overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview) |

***Audiences:** Vera currently supports creating Matched, Segmented, Contextual, and Geofarmed audiences with AI assistance.

## Vera features

Partner with Vera to complete the following workflows:

- Create campaigns that reflect your strategy and requirements.
- Build ready-to-target Matched, Segmented, Contextual, and Geofarmed audiences.
- Craft custom reports that include the dimensions and metrics that matter most to your business and its stakeholders.
- Create detailed data dashboards based on your performance-monitoring preferences.
- Work across multiple workflows in one chat, and pick up any workflow where you left off.
- Track each workflow’s progress in the summary panel and Workflow history.
- Ask product questions without leaving your current workflow.
- Save your preferences and campaign setup playbooks as memories, so Vera applies them in future workflows for that advertiser.
- Streamline your campaign operations by moving from idea to execution faster.

Refer to the ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to start creating audiences, campaigns, data dashboards, and custom reports with Vera.

## Vera Quick start shortcuts

Not sure where to begin? Select a Quick start shortcut below the input box (**Campaign**, **Dashboard**, **Audience**, or **Reports**) to fill the input box with a ready-made prompt. Use the prompt as-is, edit it, or enter your own request from scratch instead.

## Key terms and concepts

### Summary panel

The summary panel on the right side of a chat shows the workflow you’re working on now, such as **Campaign Creation**, and how many of its details you’ve provided. Each detail is checked off as you provide it. Once you create the item, the panel shows its name and a **View** button.

### Workflow history

Workflow history, below the summary panel, groups the workflows in a chat into two lists: **Pending** for workflows that still need a next step from you, and **Done** for workflows where your part is finished. Items in **Done** also show their current status in the IQM platform. For example, a campaign you sent for approval appears in **Done** with a **Pending** status until it’s approved.

### Memories

Memories are preferences you teach Vera for a specific advertiser, such as a maximum bid or a naming convention. Vera applies them in future workflows for that advertiser and tells you which memories Vera used. Your memories are private to you, and you can view and manage them under **Settings** › **Memories** in the left panel. Refer to [Create or manage memories with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17631283-create-or-manage-memories-with-vera) for more information.

## Get started with Vera

Refer to the ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to start creating audiences, campaigns, data dashboards, and custom reports with Vera.

# Locate or manage an existing chat with Vera

## Vera overview

Vera is a sophisticated AI-driven assistant. Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) to get started with Vera.

## Locate existing chats

Access your recent conversations with Vera or browse your complete chat history at any time. You can review the chat details or jump back in to pick up where you left off.

### Locate pinned and recent chats

Follow these steps to open a pinned or recent conversation with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Locate the **Pinned** or **Recents** list in the left panel.
3. Select the desired chat.

### Locate all chats

Follow these steps to browse your complete chat history with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Select **View all conversations** in the left panel. This will open the **All Conversations** page.
3. To search for a specific chat, enter its name in the **Search chats and tasks** field and select the chat.
4. To filter your chats by status, select the filter icon and choose **Read** or **Unread**.
5. To browse your chats by the most recent interaction, review the list and select the desired chat. The **Last Edited** column shows when each chat was last updated.
6. Select **New chat** in the left panel if you’d like to start a new conversation with Vera instead.

### Search for a chat

Follow these steps to search across all of your conversations with Vera:

1. Select **Search** in the left panel.
2. Enter a keyword from the chat’s name or content, and select the desired chat from the results.

## Rename a chat

Follow these steps to rename a conversation with Vera:

1. Locate the chat in the **Pinned** or **Recents** list, or on the **All Conversations** page.
2. Hover your cursor over the desired chat and click the vertical ellipses.
3. Select **Rename**. This will open the **Rename Chat** pop-up window, where you can enter the desired name and apply your changes.

## Pin or unpin a chat

Pinned chats appear in the **Pinned** list at the top of the left panel, so you can return to them quickly.

Follow these steps to pin or unpin a conversation with Vera:

1. Locate the chat in the **Pinned** or **Recents** list, or on the **All Conversations** page.
2. Hover your cursor over the desired chat and click the vertical ellipses.
3. Select **Pin**, or select **Unpin** to remove a chat from the **Pinned** list.

## Mark a chat as read or unread

Mark a chat as unread to flag it for follow-up, or as read once you’ve reviewed it. You can filter the **All Conversations** page by **Read** or **Unread**.

Follow these steps to mark a chat as read or unread:

1. Locate the chat in the **Pinned** or **Recents** list, or on the **All Conversations** page.
2. Hover your cursor over the desired chat and click the vertical ellipses.
3. Select **Mark as unread** or **Mark as read**.

## Delete a chat

Follow these steps to delete a conversation with Vera:

1. Locate the chat in the **Pinned** or **Recents** list, or on the **All Conversations** page.
2. Hover your cursor over the desired chat and click the vertical ellipses.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Confirm the deletion in the pop-up window.

# Create a data dashboard with Vera

## Vera overview

Vera is a sophisticated AI-driven assistant. Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) to get started with Vera.

## Data dashboards overview

You can partner with Vera to create customized dashboards that fit your needs and track progress over time. Dashboards allow you to monitor campaigns’ real-time performance at a glance and make ad-hoc adjustments to them.

Refer to [Dashboard overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview) for more details.

## Create a data dashboard with Vera

> **More on dimensions and metrics:** Refer to [“Reporting and analytics collection” overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview#h_b2581d2fe8) to find resources related to the dimensions and metrics you can include in your data dashboards and custom reports.

Follow these steps to create a new dashboard with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Select **Dashboard** below the input box to start from a ready-made prompt, or type your own request.
3. If desired, use the chat box instead to ask Vera to create a new dashboard.
   1. Describe the dashboard’s details such as which campaigns and metrics it should include, and which dates it should cover.
   2. No need to include everything–Vera will prompt you to enter your preferences if you’ve missed any details.
4. Click the submit button. This will redirect you to a new conversation with Vera.
5. Review the dashboard’s settings summary and, if desired, use each dropdown menu to apply any changes.
   1. You can also use the chat box to specify your changes.
6. Select **Generate Dashboard**.

Vera will immediately begin processing your request and generating the dashboard’s data based on your requirements.

> **Create a dashboard in an existing chat:** You can also create a dashboard in a chat you’re already using, for example, to track a campaign you just created. Use the chat box to ask Vera for the dashboard, then follow steps 5 through 6 above. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

## Save a data dashboard you created with Vera

Follow these steps to save a data dashboard that you previously created with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Select **Save**.
   1. You can also use the chat box to tell Vera that you’d like to save the dashboard.
3. Enter a name for the dashboard.

## Review and manage a data dashboard with Vera

Follow these steps to review and manage a data dashboard that you previously created with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. If desired, filter and search the dashboard to further refine the data that populates.
   1. You can also use the chat box to tell Vera the changes that you’d like to apply.
   2. The dashboard shown in Vera behaves in the same way as the dashboards you access in the Dashboard app. Refer to the steps outlined in [Customize a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_31768e7adb) for additional support.
   3. Note that downloaded files will reflect your dashboard customizations.

## Download data from a data dashboard with Vera

Follow these steps to download data from an existing data dashboard:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Select **Download**.
   1. You can also use the chat box to tell Vera that you’d like to download the dashboard.
3. Choose your preferred file format.

## Manually create or manage a dashboard

You can manually create or adjust data dashboards at any time. Follow the steps outlined in [Create or manage a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for step-by-step instructions.

# Create or manage a Matched audience with Vera

## Vera overview

Vera is your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) for more information about Vera’s capabilities.

## Matched audience overview

Matched audiences are made up of users from your first-party data such as Customer Relationship Management (CRM) data for specialty campaigns, NPI lists for Healthcare campaigns, or past voters for Political campaigns, for example.

While the audience is generating, it recognizes consumers across channels and devices through IQM’s privacy-compliant [Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph), which unifies offline and online identifiers to a single profile. Targeting this segment allows you to reach these offline users through digital channels.

The following Matched audience types are supported:

- Specialty
- Political (Voter IDs)
- Healthcare (Healthcare Professional [HCP], Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, Patient, Generic)

Refer to [Matched audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility criteria.

## Create a Matched audience with Vera

Follow these steps to create a new Matched audience with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Select **Audience** below the input box to start from a ready-made prompt, or type your own request.
3. If desired, use the chat box instead to ask Vera to create a new Matched audience.
   1. Describe the audience’s details such as the type of source data you’ll provide (e.g., voter IDs for a Political audience or NPIs for a Healthcare audience).
   2. No need to include everything–Vera will prompt you to enter your preferences if you’ve missed any details.
4. Click the submit button. This will redirect you to a new conversation with Vera.
5. Add an XLSX or CSV file containing your first-party data.
   1. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files and you’d like to upload it, click Upload File and select it.
   2. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files and you’d like to drag and drop it, select the desired file and drag it into any area of the dashed rectangle.
   3. If the desired file is stored in an external account such as Google Drive or Dropbox, select the corresponding company’s icon.
      1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired file from the online drive.
6. Enter a name for the audience.
7. Open the **Primary Matching Criteria** menu and select the system field(s) contained in your file that will be used for audience matching.
8. Complete the required **System Fields** and **Uploaded File Columns** in the table.
9. Click **+ Add Field** to add additional fields to the table, if desired.
   1. Only one row is required; however, completing more will help increase the chances of a high Match Rate.
10. Depending on the Matched audience subtype (e.g., Specialty, Political, Healthcare [HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, Patient, Generic]), Vera will prompt you to provide additional details and requirements. This may include choosing a data partner or reviewing and agreeing to additional terms, for example.
11. Select **Generate Audience**.

> **Create an audience in an existing chat:** You can also create a Matched audience in a chat you’re already using, for example, right after you create a campaign. Use the chat box to ask Vera to create the audience, then follow steps 5 through 11 above. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

## Review a Matched audience with Vera

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Select **View Audience**. This will open a pop-up window featuring audience details such as its creation date, match rate, reach, status, and more.
3. Click **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to your conversation with Vera.

## Assign a Matched audience to a campaign with Vera

Follow these steps to assign a Matched audience to a campaign with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Select **Attach To Campaign**.
   1. You can also use the chat box to tell Vera that you’d like to assign it.
   2. Vera will ask a series of follow-up questions to capture the desired campaign(s) and any required details.

Refer to [Create or manage memories with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17631283-create-or-manage-memories-with-vera) for more information.

## Campaigns overview

Campaigns are the individual marketing strategies that define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. They contain a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify.

Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more details.

## Create a campaign with Vera

> **More on generating campaigns:** Note that a campaign doesn’t immediately begin spending and serving when you choose to generate it. First, the campaign will undergo a review process to confirm that it meets certain requirements. Refer to Send a campaign for approval with Vera to begin this review process. You’ll know when a campaign is approved when its status changes from **Pending** to **Running**. We’ll also notify you via email.

Follow these steps to create a campaign with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Select **Campaign** below the input box to start from a ready-made prompt, or type your own request.
3. If desired, use the chat box instead to let Vera know you’d like to create a new campaign.
   1. No need to include everything–Vera will prompt you to enter your settings and preferences if you’ve missed any details.
4. Click the submit button. This will redirect you to a new conversation with Vera.
5. Choose an insertion order (IO).
   1. Open the **Select Insertion Order** menu, or use the chat box, to choose an existing IO.
   2. Select **+ Create New IO**, or use the chat box, to create a new IO for the campaign instead.
   3. Note that you’ll need to choose a budget-based IO if the campaign will have a monetary budget, or an impression-based IO if the campaign will have an impression budget. Refer to [Budget-based and impression-based insertion orders (IO)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) for additional support.
6. Vera will guide you through adding the campaign's settings (e.g., budget and dates), creatives, and optional targeting settings one at a time.
   1. Feel free to skip any optional fields that Vera asks you to complete.
   2. Refer to the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) to review each required and optional campaign targeting element.
7. Your settings and requirements will appear in the summary panel, where each detail is checked off as you provide it, as you build out the campaign.
8. If desired, click **Modify Details** or use the chat box to ask Vera to apply any additions or changes to the campaign draft.
9. Click **Generate Campaign**.

Once the campaign finishes generating, you can review it and send it for approval.

> **Keep working in the same chat:** After you generate the campaign, you can create an audience, report, or dashboard in the same chat. Vera can use the campaign’s details, for example, to scope a report to it. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

## Manage a campaign with Vera

### Edit a campaign

Follow these steps to edit an existing campaign with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Review the campaign’s existing settings by selecting **View** in the conversation or its summary panel.
3. Use the chat box to let Vera know you’d like to change the campaign’s details.
   1. Specify the items you’d like to adjust directly in the chat box, or wait for Vera to prompt you.

Vera will prompt you to input the desired changes and confirm your selection. Refer to the [Campaign targeting guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for additional support with each required and optional campaign targeting element.

### Duplicate a campaign

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing campaign with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Use the chat box to let Vera know you’d like to duplicate the campaign. This will create a new draft campaign based on the original campaign.
3. Review the campaign’s existing settings by selecting **View** in the conversation or its summary panel.
4. Follow the steps outlined in Create a campaign with Vera to specify the campaign’s settings and targeting parameters.

### Restore an expired campaign

> **More on restoring expired campaigns:** You can restore an expired campaign by extending its End Date. This will reactivate the campaign, which will resume serving ads as long as its budget hasn’t been depleted. Note that an insertion order’s (IO) status outweighs the status of its individual campaigns. Like with campaigns, an expired IO can be restored by extending its End Date.

Follow these steps to restore an expired campaign with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Use the chat box to let Vera know you’d like to change the campaign’s End Date.

Vera will prompt you to share the desired End Date and confirm your selection.

## Send a campaign for approval with Vera

Follow these steps to begin the campaign-review process to confirm that it meets certain requirements:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Review the campaign by selecting **View** in the summary panel to ensure your campaign is ready to send for approval.
3. Select **Send For Approval**.

You’ll know when a campaign is approved when its status changes from **Pending** to **Running**. We’ll also notify you via email.

Once you send the campaign for approval, it moves to the **Done** list in Workflow history with a **Pending** status. You can continue in the same chat to create an audience, report, or dashboard.

## Manually create or manage a campaign

You can manually create or manage campaigns at any time. Follow the steps outlined in [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions.

# Manage an Organization's Feature Settings

## Feature Settings overview

The **Feature Settings** section of the Organization app allows Workspaces to unlock early access to powerful new features before their general release. You’ll be among the first to try and benefit from new product capabilities. Workspace admins can browse individual beta offerings and manage access at the Workspace level.

We recommend participating in our beta programs when your Workspace is interested in influencing the product roadmap. You shape what ships–features in beta may evolve based on user feedback and usage trends.

## Feature Settings eligibility criteria

Any user with access to the Organization app is eligible to opt a Workspace into feature testing and enable access to individual features at the Workspace level.

Super Admins are IQM representatives who manage access details for Workspaces. A Super Admin must first grant access to an unreleased feature before you can Enable Workspace-level access for it. You can review those features at any time in the **Profile** tab of the Organization app, where the **Feature Settings** section is located.

## Activate beta program

Follow these steps to review legal terms and opt-in to feature testing at the Workspace level:

1. Open the Organization app.
2. Select the **Profile** tab.
3. Click **Feature Settings**.
4. Select **Activate Program**. This will open the **Activate Beta Program** pop-up window, which includes terms and conditions for participating in feature testing.
5. Once you have reviewed and agreed to the listed terms and conditions, click **Agree & Activate**.

## Review signed consent

You can review your consent documents at any time by selecting **View signed consent** in the **Feature Settings** section.

## Enable Workspace-level access to individual features

> **Feature access notice:** Once you enable a feature, all users within the Workspace will be able to access the feature indefinitely. Revoking access isn’t supported.

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Activate beta program workflow to navigate to the **Feature Settings** page.
2. Review feature details such as the **Name**, **Description**, and **Feature Stage**.
   1. Refer to Key terms and concepts: Feature Stage for feature-stage descriptions.
3. Select the toggle switch in the feature’s **Action** column to enable access to the feature for all users in the Workspace.

## Disable Workspace-level access to individual features

Once you enable a feature, all users within the Workspace will be able to access the feature indefinitely. Revoking access isn’t supported.

## Key terms and concepts

### Feature Stage

The **Feature Stage** column of the **Feature Settings** section describes the current state of the listed feature. Refer to the table below for feature-stage descriptions.

| **Feature stage** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- |
| **Alpha** | Internal testing for IQM employees to validate core UI stability and functionality. |
| **Beta** | Early access for carefully selected customers to validate the feature and provide qualitative feedback. |
| **GA Beta** | Wide opt-in beta access via in-platform feature flags for eligible customers to validate high-volume performance and scalability. |
| **GA** | Fully supported release that’s broadly available for adoption by all eligible customers. |

## Frequently asked questions

**Q:** Who is eligible to test IQM features before their general release?

**A:** Any user with access to the Organization app is eligible to opt a Workspace into feature testing and enable access to individual features at the Workspace level. Refer to Feature Settings eligibility criteria for more information.

**Q:** What legal terms do I need to agree to prior to participating in the program?

**A:** You can review all program terms and conditions by following the steps outlined in Activate beta program.

**Q:** Do I need to accept legal terms each time I enable feature testing for my Workspace?

**A:** No. Accepting legal terms takes place at the program level rather than at the individual-feature level.

**Q:** Does each user in the Workspace need to accept legal terms to participate in feature testing?

**A:** No. Accepting legal terms takes place at the Workspace level rather than the individual-user level.

**Q:** Why should my Workspace test a feature before its general release?

**A:** We recommend participating in our beta programs if you’d like to be among the first to try and benefit from new product capabilities. You should also participate when your Workspace is interested in influencing the product roadmap. You shape what ships–features in beta may evolve based on user feedback and usage trends.

**Q:** How do I revoke my Workspace’s access to a feature that I previously enabled?

**A:** Revoking access isn’t supported. Once you enable a feature, all users within the Workspace will be able to access the feature indefinitely.

**Q:** Can I manage beta-feature access at the user level?

**A:** No. You can enable access at the Workspace level rather than the individual-user level.

blocks.text: **Household Reach notice:** This article covers the Household Reach metric in campaign reporting. Political Matched audiences also display an audience-level Household Reach metric, which is calculated differently. Refer to [Matched audience overview - Household Reach (Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf) for more information.

blocks.text: The Household Reach metric represents the number of unique households reached by a campaign. A household is identified by a shared IP address or a device-graph connection. In other words, Household Reach describes the number of distinct household IDs identified across all served impressions.
Decisions within a household are often shared. Grouping individuals by their home address is a critical step for reliable impact and attribution measurement and gauging household-level influence.

Household Reach is one of several Performance reporting metrics that you can add to custom reports in the Reports app. Refer to [Performance reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) for more ways to measure the breadth and effectiveness of a campaign.
IQM takes four steps to calculate Household Reach for your campaigns:

**Assign an IQM ID.** The IQM Identity Graph covers the US, with a scale of 250M+ US individuals (~75% of US population) and 102M+ US households (~78% of US households). It also covers ~70M US voters. Each user is assigned an [IQM ID](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview?q=custom+report#h_f6e9ec243c), which is paired with demographic, geographic, and behavioral data, which includes their full residential address. Refer to [IQM Identity Graph overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview) for more information on our identity-linking methodology and other ID graph use cases.

**Group addresses into Household IDs.** Users who share the same house number, street, city, and state are assigned a single, shared Household ID. While individual IQM IDs remain distinct, the Household ID acts as a common link between members of the same household.

**Match served impressions back to IQM IDs.** When a campaign targeting a Matched audience serves an impression, the exact IQM ID is logged. After delivery, we look up the Household ID associated with each served IQM ID in the [IQM Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview).
**Count unique household IDs as Household Reach.** The number of distinct Household IDs across all served impressions is calculated to determine the Household Reach for a given campaign.

Household Reach is a vital metric for Political advertisers. Understanding Household Reach performance can help prevent campaigns from oversaturating the same voters, optimize limited budgets, and measure actual voter reach at the household level rather than across individual devices.

The IQM Identity Graph covers ~70M US voters. Because IQM's data partners provide comprehensive address information for political and voter data, you can trust that Household IDs are resolved and assigned with a high degree of accuracy.
**Q: Which apps support Household Reach reporting?**
**A:** You can add the Household Reach metric to the [custom reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) you build in the Reports app.
**Q: Which audiences support Household Reach reporting?**
**A:** Household Reach reporting is currently available for campaigns targeting [Matched audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview).
**Q: What happens if my campaign targets multiple audience types?**

**A:** Household Reach reporting is currently available for campaigns targeting [Matched audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). If your campaign targets multiple audience types (e.g., 20% Matched audience and 80% Contextual audience), the report's overall Reach will reflect all impressions, while Household Reach will account only for the Matched audience portion. For this reason, the two numbers aren't directly comparable in this scenario.
**Q: Why is my campaign's Household Reach lower than its Reach?**

**A:** Reach is at the user level, while Household Reach is at the household level. Multiple individuals in the same household share a single Household ID. For this reason, Reach will always exceed or equal Household Reach.
**Q: Does Household Reach apply to frequency and recency calculations?**

**A:** No, Household Reach doesn’t apply to frequency and recency calculations. Frequency and recency are calculated at the [IQM ID](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview?q=custom+report#h_f6e9ec243c) level rather than the Household ID level. Household Reach is a separate, reach-only metric.
**Q: What happens if two users at the same address are included in different Matched audiences?**

**A:** If both users are served an impression, then they will contribute only one Household ID to the overall Household Reach count for the campaign. This is true regardless of how many individual IQM IDs are associated with the same household.
[Performance reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview)
