# Household Reach overview

## Household Reach overview

> **Household Reach notice:** This article covers the Household Reach metric in campaign reporting. Political Matched audiences also display an audience-level Household Reach metric, which is calculated differently. Refer to [Matched audience overview - Household Reach (Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf) for more information.

The Household Reach metric represents the number of unique households reached by a campaign. A household is identified by a shared IP address or a device-graph connection. In other words, Household Reach describes the number of distinct household IDs identified across all served impressions.

Decisions within a household are often shared. Grouping individuals by their home address is a critical step for reliable impact and attribution measurement and gauging household-level influence.

Household Reach is one of several Performance reporting metrics that you can add to custom reports in the Reports app. Refer to [Performance reporting metrics overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) for more ways to measure the breadth and effectiveness of a campaign.

## Household Reach calculation

IQM takes four steps to calculate Household Reach for your campaigns:

1. **Assign an IQM ID.** The IQM Identity Graph covers the US, with a scale of 250M+ US individuals (~75% of US population) and 102M+ US households (~78% of US households). It also covers ~70M US voters. Each user is assigned an [IQM ID](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview?q=custom+report#h_f6e9ec243c), which is paired with demographic, geographic, and behavioral data, which includes their full residential address. Refer to [IQM Identity Graph overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview) for more information on our identity-linking methodology and other ID graph use cases.
2. **Group addresses into Household IDs.** Users who share the same house number, street, city, and state are assigned a single, shared Household ID. While individual IQM IDs remain distinct, the Household ID acts as a common link between members of the same household.
3. **Match served impressions back to IQM IDs.** When a campaign targeting a Matched audience serves an impression, the exact IQM ID is logged. After delivery, we look up the Household ID associated with each served IQM ID in the [IQM Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview).
4. **Count unique household IDs as Household Reach.** The number of distinct Household IDs across all served impressions is calculated to determine the Household Reach for a given campaign.

## Household Reach for Political advertisers

Household Reach is a vital metric for Political advertisers. Understanding Household Reach performance can help prevent campaigns from oversaturating the same voters, optimize limited budgets, and measure actual voter reach at the household level rather than across individual devices.

The IQM Identity Graph covers ~70M US voters. Because IQM's data partners provide comprehensive address information for political and voter data, you can trust that Household IDs are resolved and assigned with a high degree of accuracy.

## Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

**Q: Which apps support Household Reach reporting?**

**A:** You can add the Household Reach metric to the [custom reports](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) you build in the Reports app.

**Q: Which audiences support Household Reach reporting?**

**A:** Household Reach reporting is currently available for campaigns targeting [Matched audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview).

**Q: What happens if my campaign targets multiple audience types?**

**A:** Household Reach reporting is currently available for campaigns targeting [Matched audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview). If your campaign targets multiple audience types (e.g., 20% Matched audience and 80% Contextual audience), the report's overall Reach will reflect all impressions, while Household Reach will account only for the Matched audience portion. For this reason, the two numbers aren't directly comparable in this scenario.

**Q: Why is my campaign's Household Reach lower than its Reach?**

**A:** Reach is at the user level, while Household Reach is at the household level. Multiple individuals in the same household share a single Household ID. For this reason, Reach will always exceed or equal Household Reach.

**Q: Does Household Reach apply to frequency and recency calculations?**

**A:** No, Household Reach doesn’t apply to frequency and recency calculations. Frequency and recency are calculated at the [IQM ID](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph-overview?q=custom+report#h_f6e9ec243c) level rather than the Household ID level. Household Reach is a separate, reach-only metric.

**Q: What happens if two users at the same address are included in different Matched audiences?**

**A:** If both users are served an impression, then they will contribute only one Household ID to the overall Household Reach count for the campaign. This is true regardless of how many individual IQM IDs are associated with the same household.

# Power Segment Insights report overview

## Power Segment Insights report overview

Power Segment Insights reports offer transparency into the composition of political audience data segments before you target them. Analyze political personalities’ immediate connections and broader social orbits to understand exactly who a segment can reach based on demographic, geographic, network, interest, turnout, and other insights.

Refer to [Generate or manage a Power Segment Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/16396946-generate-or-manage-a-power-segment-insights-report) to get started.

## Power Segment Insights report eligibility requirements

All political advertisers with access to the [Insights app](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002765-iqm-platform-overview#h_79a4cefd6e) are eligible to generate, download, and share Power Segment Insights.

## Power Segment Insights report metrics

> **More on “what the data shows”:** All sections of the report are followed by a “what the data shows” callout, which summarizes findings and trends. Review these callouts to better understand and apply the insights.

Sphere insight and Orbit insight Power Segment Insights reports include a series of metrics and values related to who’s reachable by targeting a particular political Power Segment. These insights are downloadable in PDF format and allow you to home in on details of each political decision maker’s most relevant, targeted connections.

### Profile

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Profile Overview | Learn the policymaker’s party affiliation, current position, and state location. |
| Audience Reach Overview | Review the number of unique individuals, targetable devices, and state coverage; and data-quality details including a confidence score and last-updated date. |

### Seed Network

> **Data-privacy notice:** Note that political, professional, and personal seed-network details are presented as aggregated, segment-level metrics–such as demographic mix, state heat maps, and turnout history–rather than exposing individual-level personally identifiable information (PII). Certain connections are named when they’re derived from publicly available information, such as donors and staffers.

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Seed Network Overview | Review a summary of the individual’s primary circle of influence. |
| Political Seed Network | Learn the individual’s primary supporters, allies, donors, and advisors reachable through the Power Segment. |
| Professional Seed Network | Learn the individual’s primary associates, staff, and counsel; and Chief of Staff; reachable through the Power Segment. |
| Personal Seed Network | Learn the individual’s primary neighbors, mentors, friends, and family reachable through the Power Segment. |

### Geography

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| States by Sphere/Orbit Members | Reference a heat map reflecting the sphere’s state concentration based on each individual’s last observed location in the IQM ID Graph. |
| State Breakdown | Review how many of the sphere’s individuals were most recently seen based on their last observed location in the IQM ID Graph. |

### Demographics

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Age Distribution | Learn the sphere’s age distribution and total number of individuals. |
| Gender Split | Learn the sphere’s gender distribution. |
| Summary Metrics | Review the sphere’s median age band and whether it leans more male or female. |

### Political Composition

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Party Affiliation | Learn the sphere’s party-affiliation distribution based on registered voter records. |
| Summary Metrics | Review the point gap between the sphere’s two largest parties. |

### Income & Affluence

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Household Income Distribution | Learn about the income distribution of the sphere to understand the audience’s economic profile. |
| Summary Metrics | Review additional income insights such as the sphere’s primary household-income bands and its median band. |

### Home & Household

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Marital Status | Reference what percentage of the sphere is married or single. |
| Home Ownership | Review whether the sphere is primarily homeowners or renters, and learn additional insights such as the sphere’s median home value and the percentage of households with children. |
| Estimated Home Value | Learn the distribution of estimated home values across the sphere. |

### Voter Engagement

| **Metric or insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Election Turnout | Understand voter turnout across recent general elections and presidential primaries, drawn from public voter-file records. |
| Voter Engagement Insights | Check additional insights such as the percentage of voters who participated in multiple general elections or primaries, and the percentage of voters who disengaged. |

## Power Segment Insights report statuses

Unlike other insights report types, a Power Segment Insights report’s status is indicated by the actions you can take. Refer to the table below for more details.

| **Status** | **Visual** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ready to generate** | A **Generate** button is shown and is clickable. | The insight hasn’t been requested yet. Click **Generate** to request it. |
| **Processing** | A **Generate** button is shown but isn’t clickable. | The insight has already been requested and is being processed. No action is needed. |
| **Generated** | A downward arrow and envelope icon are shown in place of a **Generate** button. | The insight has been generated and is ready to access and review. Use the downward arrow icon to download the insight or the envelope icon to send it. |

## Key terms and concepts

### Sphere insights and Orbit insights

Power Segment Insights reports relate to the “PowerSphere” and “PowerOrbit” data segments that are available for targeting when you [create Segmented audiences from Power Segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_c53e5ac090). Power Segment Insights reports offer transparency into the composition of these political audience data segments before you target them.

Power Segments and Power Segment Insights reports both separate a political personality's inner circle ("Sphere") from their extended reach ("Orbit"). The core differences between these two connection types is their network depth and purpose.

| **Connection type** | **Definition** | **Network depth** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Sphere** | Inner-circle connections | Primary (1st-degree) reach | High-precision targeting of the most direct associates and supporters of the political personality |
| **Orbit** | Extended-network connections | Broader (2nd/3rd-degree) reach | Scaling reach to secondary audiences who may influence or by influenced by the political personality |

## Power Segment Insights report overview

## Generate a Power Segment Insights report

> **More on generating a report:** There may be instances when the **Sphere insight** or **Orbit insight** shows a **Generate** button, but it’s not clickable. This means the report is currently processing. Once completed, you can Download or Send the report. Refer to [Power Segment Insights report statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/16396898-power-segment-insights-report-overview#h_8af09aaa55) for additional support.

Follow these steps to generate a Power Segment Insights report:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Click **Power Segment Insights**.
3. Locate the desired political personality in the table’s **Member names** table.
   1. Search by a name.
   2. Filter by category such as **Governor** or **Mayor**.
4. Select **Generate** in the **Sphere insight** column and/or **Orbit insight** column, depending on the insight type you’d like to generate.
   1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Sphere insights and Orbit insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/16396898-power-segment-insights-report-overview#h_ed926aa3a3) for more information on the differences between insight types.

The insights will immediately begin generating, and are typically ready within two business days. We’ll notify you via email when they’re ready.

## Download a Power Segment Insights report

Follow these steps to download a Power Segment Insights report:

1. Locate the desired political personality in the table’s **Member names** table.
2. Select the download icon from the **Sphere insight** column or **Orbit insight** column, depending on the insight you’d like to download.

The insights report will immediately download to your device as a PDF file.

## Send a Power Segment Insights report

> **Email notice:** We’ll let you know if the report’s file size is greater than 25 MB, which means you’ll need to Download the insights instead of emailing them. This limitation is to comply with the file-size restrictions of most email inboxes.

Follow these steps to send a Power Segment Insights report to up to 15 recipients:

1. Locate the desired political personality in the table’s **Member names** table.
2. Select the envelope icon from the **Sphere insight** column or **Orbit insight** column, depending on the insight you’d like to send. This will open the **Email Power Segment Insight as PDF** pop-up window.
3. Add each email alias to the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
4. Click **Send Email**.

The insights report will immediately be sent to the recipients you entered.

title: IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP) overview

blocks.text: Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and services. With MCP, an AI assistant can access capabilities made available by an MCP server, then use those capabilities to retrieve information or perform supported action.

IQM MCP extends this approach to the IQM platform. It brings specific platform capabilities into an AI-assisted workflow to offer an alternative method for managing your campaign workflow. This approach minimizes the need to toggle between apps to perform supported platform operations. Instead, you can perform supported tasks directly via Claude’s or ChatGPT’s chat interface.
**More on third-party eligibility requirements:** IQM MCP is supported via Claude and ChatGPT. You can sign up for a free account directly with either AI-assistant provider.

blocks.table_reason: boxed note: one text cell, or a bold label cell plus a text cell

blocks.text: Access to IQM platform apps and capabilities depends on how your organization’s Workspace is configured. IQM MCP connects directly to your account’s existing account-and-permission structure. This means you can consider IQM MCP access as an additional interface rather than a separate permission system.
If you can access an app or complete an action in the IQM platform–and it’s an IQM MCP supported platform operation–then you are eligible to complete those same tasks via IQM MCP.
Supported actions are the specific platform operations that you can complete using IQM MCP. These can include activities such as:
Retrieving information from IQM.
Generating or accessing reporting data.
Moving budgets from one campaign to another.
Supporting campaign creation, management, and performance analysis.
Returning information that can be used for deeper review or decision-making.
Performing other supported platform operations across apps and functions.

The table below outlines these supported platform operations and actions. Refer to [Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17238636-set-up-and-run-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp) to get started with your first prompt.
**Element**

**Details**
**Asset**
Manage creative-asset records and files.
Upload creative files.
Manage (list, fetch, update, delete) previously added asset records and files.

# IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP) overview

## IQM MCP overview

Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and services. With MCP, an AI assistant can access capabilities made available by an MCP server, then use those capabilities to retrieve information or perform supported action.

IQM MCP extends this approach to the IQM platform. It brings specific platform capabilities into an AI-assisted workflow to offer an alternative method for managing your campaign workflow. This approach minimizes the need to toggle between apps to perform supported platform operations. Instead, you can perform supported tasks directly via Claude’s or ChatGPT’s chat interface.

## IQM MCP eligibility requirements

> **More on third-party eligibility requirements:** IQM MCP is supported via Claude and ChatGPT. You can sign up for a free account directly with either AI-assistant provider.

Access to IQM platform apps and capabilities depends on how your organization’s Workspace is configured. IQM MCP connects directly to your account’s existing account-and-permission structure. This means you can consider IQM MCP access as an additional interface rather than a separate permission system.

If you can access an app or complete an action in the IQM platform–and it’s an IQM MCP supported platform operation–then you are eligible to complete those same tasks via IQM MCP.

## IQM MCP supported actions

Supported actions are the specific platform operations that you can complete using IQM MCP. These can include activities such as:

- Retrieving information from IQM.
- Generating or accessing reporting data.
- Moving budgets from one campaign to another.
- Supporting campaign creation, management, and performance analysis.
- Returning information that can be used for deeper review or decision-making.
- Performing other supported platform operations across apps and functions.

The table below outlines these supported platform operations and actions. Refer to [Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17238636-set-up-and-run-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp) to get started with your first prompt.

| **Element** | **Description** | **Details** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Asset** | Manage creative-asset records and files. | Upload creative files.; Manage (list, fetch, update, delete) previously added asset records and files. |
| **Audience** | Create, activate, and manage audiences. | Create new audiences ([Segmented](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview), [Retargeted](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview), [Lookalike](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview), [Pre-bid](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698600-pre-bid-targeting-overview), [Contextual](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview), [Geofarmed](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview), [Campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview), [Custom Voter](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview)); Manage existing audiences (search, [Re-Match](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf), generate insights, activate) |
| **Bid Model** | Apply rule-based optimizations to campaigns. | Set inclusion and exclusion rules for [supported dimensions](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_7889c31177) that your campaign is targeting.; Create and manage [dimension bundles](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_c35492f911). |
| **Campaign** | Create and manage campaigns and insertion orders (IOs). | Create new IOs and [Advanced or Programmatic Guaranteed (PG)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002251-programmatic-guaranteed-pg-inventory-overview#h_f3d42be8ed) campaigns.; Manage (edit, duplicate, delete, change status, change budget) existing IOs and campaigns. |
| **Creative** | Add and manage creatives. | Add or upload new creatives.; Check an existing creative’s status or details.; Target a creative or group of creatives. |
| **Customer** | Manage customers and approvals. | Obtain customers’ details and manage customers.; Review and approve submitted items (campaigns, creatives, audiences). |
| **Dashboard** | Gain visibility into delivery details. | Review the impact of [AI-Based Optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_4753688f6d) on your target KPI.; Group performance by IO, campaign, exchange, advertiser, or Workspace.; Compare a set of metrics over the same timeframe.; Access previously created data dashboards.; Diagnose why a campaign isn’t serving or is underdelivering with [AI Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_b80f13a4bb). |
| **Inventory** | Identify, group, and target inventory and deals. | Create or manage [inventory groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) (Open Exchange, Connected TV [CTV], Private Marketplace [PMP], Contextual).; Add PMP or Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deals.; Manage blocked-inventory lists. |
| **Master*** | Pull Master API details. | Look up reference data across: Location (time zones, geographies); Segments (demographics); Channels and traffic (devices, carriers, networks, traffic types, channels, exchanges, deal curation, ad categories, real-time bidding [RTB] types); Creatives (creative sizes, video parameters) |
| **Report** | Generate and manage custom reports. | Review [supported dimensions and metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343665-reports-overview#h_c4776c776c).; Generate a new report.; Manage (save, list, execute) and existing report. |

*** Master API:** IQM MCP can connect to the [Master API](https://developers.iqm.com/guidelines/master-api/). The Master API serves as a central source for shared reference data across IQM. It provides the standardized values and lookups required by other IQM APIs.

## IQM MCP use cases

In general, IQM MCP supports a range of AI-assisted workflows across the IQM platform, with its primary use cases including:

- **Reducing context switching:** Access supported actions from an MCP-compatible AI application instead of manually moving between tools to complete every task.
- **Enabling conversation-based operations:** Ask questions in natural language and allow the AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT) to run various platform tasks across the campaign lifecycle in real time.
- **Uncovering and interpreting data and insights:** Generate custom reports and summarize campaign-performance data and other insights to apply them to your workflow.
- **Managing tasks in bulk and across the campaign lifecycle:** Create and manage insertion orders (IOs) and campaigns along with individual targeting elements such as audiences, inventory, and creatives, then report on and optimize those campaigns, all from a single chat.

We recommend referencing [Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17238636-set-up-and-run-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp) and following its prompt examples to get familiar with IQM MCP and understand its capabilities.

## IQM MCP setup and getting started

You can set up IQM MCP via custom connectors (Claude) or custom plugins (ChatGPT via developer mode).

Refer to [Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17238636-set-up-and-run-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp) for setup guides, example prompts, and tutorials.

## Key terms and concepts

### MCP terms

Refer to the table below for MCP terms and their definitions.

| **Term** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol, a standardized way for AI applications to interact with external tools and services. |
| **IQM MCP** | The approach used to bring specific, supported platform capabilities into an AI-assisted workflow. It offers an alternative method for managing your campaign tasks, where AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT) take real-time action based on the tasks you request via a chat interface. |
| **MCP client** | The AI application that connects to an MCP server. In the IQM MCP ecosystem, external clients can include an AI assistant or agent such as Claude or ChatGPT, custom applications, and developer tools. |
| **MCP server** | The service that exposes tools and capabilities through MCP. In the IQM MCP ecosystem, MCP servers–or apps–include the **Dashboard App MCP Server**, **Report App MCP Server**, and **Bid Model App MCP Server**, and more. |
| **MCP action** | The specific operations that can be requested and performed through an MCP server. Refer to IQM MCP supported actions for more details. |
| **AI application** | The application that uses MCP capabilities to respond to your requests and perform supported tasks. |
| **Prompt** | The request you share via chat with an AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT) that signals that agent to perform an action. |

### AI-assisted decision making

For advertising workflows, IQM MCP can help surface information, compare performance, identify opportunities, and execute supported IQM platform actions. Organizations should continue to apply their existing review, approval, compliance, and governance processes when using any AI-assisted workflows, which includes using IQM MCP.

### IQM MCP and Vera AI

IQM MCP and Vera AI offer different use cases. IQM MCP provides a convenient alternative method to manage campaign tasks directly within third-party chat interfaces like Claude and ChatGPT. Vera is IQM’s proprietary, dedicated AI agent designed to deliver a highly integrated, platform-native experience.

IQM MCP is a fantastic option for performing quick, chat-based supported actions in external tools, but Vera serves as a central companion built directly into the IQM ecosystem. It provides a visually supportive interface for building audiences, creating and submitting campaigns, customizing rich performance dashboards, and more.

For users who want a seamless, unified workspace without toggling between systems, partnering with Vera offers the ultimate combination of conversational intelligence and platform capabilities. Refer to the [“Vera - IQM’s artificial intelligence (AI) agent” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) for more information.

## Locate additional IQM MCP resources:

- [Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17238636-set-up-and-run-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp)

blocks.text: Follow these steps to connect IQM MCP to your Claude account:
Visit [https://claude.ai/new](https://claude.ai/new) to navigate to Claude and open a new chat.

Hover over **Connectors**.
Click **Manage connectors** from the **Connectors** menu. This will open the **Connectors** pop-up window.
Open the **+ Add** menu.
Select **Add custom connector**. This will open the **Add custom connector** pop-up window.

Enter **IQM MCP** in the **Name** field.
Enter **[https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp](https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp)** in the **MCP server URL** field.
Click **Continue**.

Select **Connect**. This will redirect you to a page that confirms whether you’d like to grant Claude access to IQM MCP.

Enter your IQM platform login credentials.
Select **Login**. This will authenticate your account and redirect you to the **Your connectors** page, where IQM MCP now appears connected.
Confirm that setup was successful.

# Set up and run IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP)

## IQM MCP overview

Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and services. With MCP, an AI assistant can access capabilities made available by an MCP server, then use those capabilities to retrieve information or perform supported action.

IQM MCP extends this approach to the IQM platform. It brings specific platform capabilities into an AI-assisted workflow to offer an alternative method for managing your campaign workflow. This approach minimizes the need to toggle between apps to perform supported platform operations. Instead, you can perform [supported tasks](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17233458-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp-overview#h_b2ba4c3952) directly via Claude’s or ChatGPT’s chat interface.

Refer to [IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17233458-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp-overview) for more information, including supported actions and eligibility details.

## IQM MCP setup

> **More on third-party eligibility requirements:** IQM MCP is supported via Claude and ChatGPT. You can sign up for a free account directly with either AI-assistant provider.

You can set up IQM MCP via custom connectors (Claude) or custom plugins (ChatGPT via developer mode).

### Connect to Claude - Video tutorial

> **More on the MCP server URL:** This video tutorial includes a step to add the **MCP server URL** during setup. Refer to step 8 of Connect to Claude - Written instructions to copy the URL to your clipboard.

### Connect to Claude - Written instructions

Follow these steps to connect IQM MCP to your Claude account:

1. Visit [https://claude.ai/new](https://claude.ai/new) to navigate to Claude and open a new chat.
2. Select **+** to open the options menu.
3. Hover over **Connectors**.
4. Click **Manage connectors** from the **Connectors** menu. This will open the **Connectors** pop-up window.
5. Open the **+ Add** menu.
6. Select **Add custom connector**. This will open the **Add custom connector** pop-up window.
   1. If your Claude account is a corporate organization account, you may need to ask an organization owner to add this capability for your team.
7. Enter **IQM MCP** in the **Name** field.
8. Enter **[https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp](https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp)** in the **MCP server URL** field.
9. Click **Continue**.
10. In the **Authentication** section, select **Sign in now**.
11. In the **OAuth client** section, select **Use Claude’s published identity**.
12. Click **Add**. This will close the **Add custom connector** pop-up window.
13. Select **Connect**. This will redirect you to a page that confirms whether you’d like to grant Claude access to IQM MCP.
14. Click **Allow access** to confirm your selection. This will redirect you to the **IQM MCP Server** page.
15. Enter your IQM platform login credentials.
16. Select **Login**. This will authenticate your account and redirect you to the **Your connectors** page, where IQM MCP now appears connected.
17. Confirm that setup was successful.
    1. Open a new chat.
    2. Select **+** to open the options menu.
    3. Hover over **Connectors**.
    4. Locate **IQM MCP** and check that the toggle switch is turned on.

### Connect to ChatGPT - Written instructions

Follow these steps to connect IQM MCP to your ChatGPT account:

1. Visit [https://chatgpt.com/](https://chatgpt.com/) to navigate to ChatGPT and open a new chat.
2. Click your profile name or initials.
3. Select **Settings**. This will open the **General** pop-up window.
4. Click **Security and login** from the left-side panel.
5. Scroll to the **Developer mode** section and enable **Developer mode**.
   1. If your ChatGPT account is a corporate organization account (e.g., Business, Enterprise), you may need to ask an organization owner to add this capability for your team.
6. Select **Plugins**. This will redirect you to the **Plugins** page.
7. Click **+**. This will open the **New Plugin** pop-up window.
8. Enter **IQM MCP** in the **Name** field.
9. Enter **[https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp](https://mcp.iqm.com/v1/iqm/mcp)** in the **Connection** field.
10. Review any warnings and disclaimers, then select the **I understand and want to continue** checkbox to agree.
11. Click **Create**.
12. Select **Connect** from the **IQM MCP** page. This will open the **Add IQM MCP to ChatGPT** pop-up window.
13. Click **Sign in with IQM MCP**. This will redirect you to a page that confirms whether you’d like to grant ChatGPT access to IQM MCP.
14. Click **Allow access** to confirm your selection. This will redirect you to the **IQM MCP Server** page.
15. Enter your IQM platform login credentials.
16. Select **Login**. This will authenticate your account and redirect you to the **Your connectors** page, where IQM MCP now appears connected.

## Run IQM MCP

Refer to the example text prompts and tutorial videos below to get started with IQM MCP, and review [IQM Model Context Protocol (MCP) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17233458-iqm-model-context-protocol-mcp-overview) to reference all actions that are supported via IQM MCP.

### Example text prompts

#### Optimization (Bid Model)

> **More on Bid Modeling:** A Bid Model is the set of rules that you apply to a campaign to optimize its performance. These rules allow you to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities for supported dimensions. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) to learn more about Bid Modeling, including eligibility requirements, components (Spend Ratio, Priority, Bid Modifier) and supported dimensions.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Creates a table of modeled items for a specified campaign and dimension | “Show me the modeled items for Campaign [Campaign ID] and [dimension name(s)], with the details in a table format.” | “Show me the modeled items for Campaign 123 and the creative dimensions with the details in a table format.” |
| Creates a table of supported Bid Model dimensions, with descriptions and targeting examples | “Show me a list of Bid Model dimensions.” | “Show me a list of Bid Model dimensions.” |
| Removes modeling from the specified item | “Remove modeling from the [dimension details] [dimension].” | “Remove modeling from the “barcelona-skyline” creative.” |
| Sets new modeling rules for the specified item | “Set or update modeling for [dimension details] [dimension]: [bid model settings].” | “Set modeling for the “barcelona-skyline” creative: Spend Ratio 10, Priority 4.” |
| Reallocates budget based on pacing performance and cost efficiency | “Pull every running campaign in [IO name or advertiser] for the last 7 days with spend, pacing %, daily budget, total budget, max bid, and CPM. Move $[amount] of total budget from campaigns pacing under [percentage]% to campaigns pacing over [percentage]% with CPM under $[price]. Split in proportion to their spend. Show me the before-and-after table and wait for my approval before changing anything.” | “Pull every running campaign in IO 4921 for the last 7 days with spend, pacing %, daily budget, total budget, max bid, and CPM. Show me the full list before creating anything, then give me the new campaign IDs.” | “I've attached campaigns.xlsx. Keep them as drafts. List each new campaign ID next to its source, and flag anything that still needs budget, creatives, deals, or conversions before launch.” |

Leave all other audiences on those campaigns untouched. Show the before and after audience list per campaign and wait for my approval.” |

Show me the deal to campaign changes first and wait for my approval.” | “Assign PMP deals 4445 and 4446 to every running CTV campaign for Advertiser ABC and remove deal 4444 from them. #### Analysis (Reports)

# Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera

## Multi-context chats overview

Vera can handle several workflows in a single chat. For example, you can create a campaign, build an audience for it, generate a report, and ask a product question without starting a new conversation. Vera keeps each workflow’s details separate, so you can move between them and pick up where you left off.

The following workflows are supported in a multi-context chat:

- Campaigns
- Audiences (Matched, Segmented, Contextual, Geofarmed)
- Custom reports
- Data dashboards
- Product questions

Vera keeps track of your workflows for the duration of your chat session.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) for more information about Vera’s capabilities.

## Start another workflow in the same chat

Follow these steps to start a new workflow in a chat you’re already using:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be), or continue in your current chat.
2. Use the input box to tell Vera what you’d like to do next, such as “Now help me create an audience.”
   1. When you finish a workflow, Vera marks it **Task completed** and suggests next steps you can select instead.
3. Follow Vera’s prompts to complete the new workflow.

Vera adds the new workflow to the summary panel and keeps your earlier workflows in Workflow history. Refer to Track your work for more information.

> **Build on earlier work:** Vera can use details from earlier in the chat. For example, after you create a campaign, you can ask for a report and Vera will scope it to that campaign.

## Switch between or resume workflows

You can move between workflows at any time without losing your progress. Use the input box to tell Vera which workflow you’d like to work on.

- **Refer to a workflow by name.** For example, “Now continue the Pfizer campaign.”
- **Resume where you left off.** For example, “Continue where we left off.”

If your request could apply to more than one workflow, Vera will ask which one you mean before continuing.

You can also select any workflow in Workflow history to resume it. Refer to Resume a workflow from Workflow history for step-by-step instructions.

## Ask a product question during a workflow

You can ask Vera a product question at any point in a chat, such as how a feature works or what a setting means. Vera searches the Help Center and answers in the same chat, and your workflows stay as you left them.

## Track your work

The summary panel on the right side of the chat shows the workflow you’re working on now, and Workflow history lists the other workflows in the chat.

### Track the active workflow in the summary panel

The top of the summary panel shows the workflow that’s active now and how many of its details you’ve provided, for example, **Campaign Creation**, **Active**, and “3 of 8 details collected.” Each detail is checked off as you provide it.

Once you create the item, such as a campaign, the summary panel shows its name and a **View** button you can select to review it.

### Resume a workflow from Workflow history

**Workflow history** groups the workflows in a chat into two lists:

- **Pending:** Workflows that still need a next step from you.
- **Done:** Workflows where your part is finished. Each item also shows its current status in the IQM platform. For example, a campaign you sent for approval appears in **Done** with a **Pending** status until it’s approved.

Follow these steps to resume a workflow from Workflow history:

1. Open the **Pending** or **Done** list below the summary panel.
2. Locate the desired workflow.
   1. Search by name or ID.
   2. Browse the groups: **Campaigns**, **Audience**, **Reports**, and **Dashboard**.
3. Select the workflow to resume it and pick up where you left off.

## Locate additional Vera resources

- [“Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview)
- [Locate or manage an existing chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera)

title: Create or manage a Contextual audience with Vera

blocks.text: Vera is your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.
Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) for more information about Vera’s capabilities.

Contextual audiences group users based on their online activity. You’ll provide keywords and/or URLs, and users are added to the audience when they visit sites that feature them during the data collection period and at the frequency you choose.
Vera can recommend related keywords for you to review, so you can start with a short description of your audience instead of a complete keyword list.
The following Contextual audience types are supported:
Specialty
Political
Healthcare (Healthcare Professional [HCP], Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, Generic)
Refer to [Contextual audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility criteria.

sections.heading: Create a Contextual audience with Vera
heading_path: Create a Contextual audience with Vera

blocks.text: Follow these steps to create a new Contextual audience with Vera:
Open the Vera app.
Select **Audience** below the input box to start from a ready-made prompt, or type your own request to create a new Contextual audience. This will redirect you to a new conversation with Vera.
If desired, describe the audience, such as “Create a contextual audience for diabetes.”
No need to include everything–Vera will prompt you to enter your preferences if you’ve missed any details.
If not already provided, add the **Audience Details**.
Select **Contextual**.
Click **Apply**.
If you’re creating a Healthcare audience, choose the audience type when Vera prompts you: **Generic**, **NPI Type** (**HCP**, **Nurse**), or **Non-NPI Type** (**Non-NPI Nurse**).
Add the keywords and/or URLs that define the audience.
To add keywords manually, add or describe keywords in the input box.
To add URLs manually, paste the URLs you’d like to include.
To upload a file containing a set of keywords or URLs, click **+** and select the file.
If any items can’t be added, Vera lets you know and offers a downloadable list of the errors.
Review your keywords and URLs in the **Select Keywords** card.
Your keywords and URLs appear under **Captured & Selected Keywords**. Click the **x** on any item to remove it.
Add individual keywords from the **Recommended** list, or click **Select all**. Recommendations are ranked by confidence score (High, Medium, Low).
Type in the input box to get more relevant keywords and links.
Click **Next Step**.
Choose a data collection method in the **Data Collection Method** card.
**Static:** Enter a **Date Range** and **Frequency** to capture a fixed snapshot of users.
**Dynamic:** Enter a **Timeframe** (the number of days before the current date) and **Frequency** to capture a rolling audience that refreshes daily.

Refer to [Contextual audience overview: Data Collection Period](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_62268aaadb) for more information on Static and Dynamic settings.
Select **Generate Audience**.
Vera will confirm once the audience is generated and saved. The audience appears in the Audiences app with a **Processing** status.

For HCP and Nurse audiences, Vera first gathers reach data across data partners. Choose your preferred partner in the **Data Partner** pop-up and click **Select Data Partner** to finish generating the audience.

**Keep working in the same chat:** After you create the audience, you can ask Vera to attach it to a campaign, or start another task such as a report or dashboard, in the same chat. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

# Create or manage a Contextual audience with Vera

## Vera overview

Vera is your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) for more information about Vera’s capabilities.

## Contextual audience overview

Contextual audiences group users based on their online activity. You’ll provide keywords and/or URLs, and users are added to the audience when they visit sites that feature them during the data collection period and at the frequency you choose.

Vera can recommend related keywords for you to review, so you can start with a short description of your audience instead of a complete keyword list.

The following Contextual audience types are supported:

- Specialty
- Political
- Healthcare (Healthcare Professional [HCP], Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, Generic)

Refer to [Contextual audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility criteria.

## Create a Contextual audience with Vera

Follow these steps to create a new Contextual audience with Vera:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Select **Audience** below the input box to start from a ready-made prompt, or type your own request to create a new Contextual audience. This will redirect you to a new conversation with Vera.
   1. If desired, describe the audience, such as “Create a contextual audience for diabetes.”
   2. No need to include everything–Vera will prompt you to enter your preferences if you’ve missed any details.
3. If not already provided, add the **Audience Details**.
   1. Select **Contextual**.
   2. Click **Apply**.
4. If you’re creating a Healthcare audience, choose the audience type when Vera prompts you: **Generic**, **NPI Type** (**HCP**, **Nurse**), or **Non-NPI Type** (**Non-NPI Nurse**).
5. Add the keywords and/or URLs that define the audience.
   1. To add keywords manually, add or describe keywords in the input box.
   2. To add URLs manually, paste the URLs you’d like to include.
   3. To upload a file containing a set of keywords or URLs, click **+** and select the file.
   4. If any items can’t be added, Vera lets you know and offers a downloadable list of the errors.
6. Review your keywords and URLs in the **Select Keywords** card.
   1. Your keywords and URLs appear under **Captured & Selected Keywords**. Click the **x** on any item to remove it.
   2. Add individual keywords from the **Recommended** list, or click **Select all**. Recommendations are ranked by confidence score (High, Medium, Low).
   3. Type in the input box to get more relevant keywords and links.
   4. Click **Next Step**.
7. Choose a data collection method in the **Data Collection Method** card.
   1. **Static:** Enter a **Date Range** and **Frequency** to capture a fixed snapshot of users.
   2. **Dynamic:** Enter a **Timeframe** (the number of days before the current date) and **Frequency** to capture a rolling audience that refreshes daily.
   3. Refer to [Contextual audience overview: Data Collection Period](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview#h_62268aaadb) for more information on Static and Dynamic settings.
8. Select **Generate Audience**.

Vera will confirm once the audience is generated and saved. The audience appears in the Audiences app with a **Processing** status.

For HCP and Nurse audiences, Vera first gathers reach data across data partners. Choose your preferred partner in the **Data Partner** pop-up and click **Select Data Partner** to finish generating the audience.

> **Keep working in the same chat:** After you create the audience, you can ask Vera to attach it to a campaign, or start another task such as a report or dashboard, in the same chat. Refer to [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera) for more information.

### Create a Contextual audience while creating a campaign

You can also create a Contextual audience while you create a campaign with Vera. When Vera asks which audience the campaign should target, ask Vera to create a new Contextual audience. Vera will guide you through steps 3 through 8 above, then add the new audience to the campaign.

Refer to [Create or manage a campaign with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15496973-create-or-manage-a-campaign-with-vera) for more information.

## Review a Contextual audience with Vera

Follow these steps to review a Contextual audience with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Select **View** on the audience card. This will open a pop-up window featuring audience details such as its keywords and URLs, reach, status, and more.
3. Close the pop-up window to return to your conversation with Vera.

## Assign a Contextual audience to a campaign with Vera

Follow these steps to assign a Contextual audience to a campaign with Vera:

1. [Locate an existing chat](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492472-locate-or-manage-an-existing-chat-with-vera#h_3c2d8326be).
2. Open the **Assign to Campaign** menu.
3. Click **Assign to Existing Campaign** or **Assign to New Campaign**.
   1. You can also use the input box to tell Vera that you’d like to assign it.
   2. Vera will ask a series of follow-up questions to capture the desired campaign(s) and any required details.

## Manually review, manage, or assign an audience

You can manually create or manage Contextual audiences at any time. Follow the steps outlined in [Create or manage a Contextual audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7018329-create-or-manage-a-contextual-audience) for step-by-step instructions.

# Create or manage memories with Vera

## Vera overview

Vera is your AI-powered campaign operations partner. Vera can assist you with workflows spanning campaign strategy, execution, and reporting. Simply start a conversation with Vera to transform ideas and requirements into actionable marketing workflows in minutes instead of hours.

Refer to [Vera overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15492134-vera-overview) for more information about Vera’s capabilities.

## Memories overview

Memories are preferences that you teach Vera to apply them the next time you work on that advertiser's workflows. For example, you can save a maximum bid, a frequency cap, or a naming convention once, instead of repeating it in every campaign. You can also paste a full campaign setup playbook, and Vera will save each rule as its own memory.

Memories are scoped to you and to the advertiser you’re working on. A memory saved for one advertiser isn’t applied to your other advertisers, and other users can’t see or use your memories.

Memories can include conditions, such as “Max bid $20 – when creative is Image” or “Frequency cap 3 – for CTV.” Vera only applies a conditional memory when its condition is met.

You can save memories for the following workflows:

- Campaign creation
- Matched, Segmented, Contextual, and Geofarmed audiences
- Report creation
- Dashboard creation

### How Vera applies memories

When you start a workflow, such as creating a campaign, Vera applies the memories that match your advertiser and workflow, and tells you which ones Vera used. For example, “I applied your saved max bid and naming convention.”

- **Priority:** Instructions you give in the current chat take priority over your saved memories, and your saved memories take priority over Vera’s default settings.
- **Conflicts:** If more than one memory could apply and Vera can’t tell which one you want, Vera asks before continuing.
- **One-time changes:** To use a different value for the current workflow only, change the field or tell Vera. For example, “Use a frequency cap of 5 for this campaign.” Your saved memory doesn’t change.

To change a memory permanently, edit it on the **Memories** page. Refer to Edit a memory for step-by-step instructions.

## Create a memory on the Memories page

> **More on Vera Memories:** Vera never saves a memory without your confirmation. Using a value in a single workflow doesn’t save it as a memory.

Follow these steps to create one or more memories on the **Memories** page:

1. Open the Vera app.
2. Open the **Settings** menu in the left panel.
3. Select **Memories**.
4. Describe a preference or paste your playbook in the input box.
   1. If desired, select a suggestion chip to start from a ready-made prompt.
   2. Include any conditions, such as “for CTV” or “when the creative is Image.”
   3. To save several preferences at once, paste them together, such as a list from your campaign setup playbook.
5. Click the submit button.

Vera identifies each preference in your text so you can review them before anything is saved.

### Review and save identified preferences

Follow these steps to review the preferences Vera identified and save them as memories:

1. If any new preferences conflict with your saved memories or with each other when you Create a memory, the **Resolve conflicts** window opens.
   1. For each conflict, select **Save** to save the new preference, or **Don’t save** to keep your existing memory.
   2. Click **Next**.
2. Review the preferences in the **Preferences identified** window.
   1. Clear the checkbox next to any preference you don’t want to save.
   2. Preferences you’ve already saved appear dimmed.
   3. If some of your text doesn’t match a setting Vera can apply, Vera won’t save it. Select **Download (.CSV)** to review those items.
3. Click **Save**.

Vera confirms how many preferences were added, and your new memories appear on the **Memories** page.

## Create a memory in a chat with Vera

You can also tell Vera to remember a preference in any chat, including in the middle of a workflow such as creating a campaign.

Follow these steps to create a memory in a chat with Vera:

1. Use the input box to describe a lasting preference for the advertiser, such as “For ACME, always use a max bid of $20 for Image creatives and a frequency cap of 3 for CTV.”
2. Review the **Preferences identified** card. Clear the checkbox next to any preference you don’t want to save.
3. Click **Save**.

Vera confirms that your memories are saved. To review them, select **Manage your saved memories** in the suggested next steps.

## Manage your memories

### Locate your memories

Follow these steps to locate your saved memories:

1. Open the **Settings** menu in the left panel.
2. Select **Memories**.
3. In the table, review the preferences you’ve saved as memories.
   1. The **Workflow** column shows where each memory applies.
   2. The **Last Updated** column shows when each memory was last changed.
4. Locate a specific memory.
   1. To search, enter a keyword in the **Search your memories** field.
   2. To filter by workflow, select the filter icon and choose a workflow.

### Turn a memory on or off

Turn a memory off to stop Vera from applying it without deleting it. Turned-off memories stay on the **Memories** page so you can turn them back on later.

Follow these steps to turn a memory on or off:

1. Follow steps 1 through 2 of the Locate your memories workflow.
2. Select the toggle next to the desired memory to turn it on or off.

### Edit a memory

Follow these steps to edit a saved memory:

1. Follow steps 1 through 2 of the Locate your memories workflow.
2. Click the edit icon in the **Action** column next to the desired memory. The memory appears in the input box.
3. Describe the change in the chat box.
4. Click the submit button.
5. Review the update when Vera asks you to confirm it.
   1. If the change conflicts with another memory, Vera flags it so you can choose which one to keep.

### Delete a memory

> **More on deleting memories:** Deleting a memory only affects what Vera applies going forward. Campaigns and other items you’ve already created don’t change.

Follow these steps to delete a saved memory:

1. Follow steps 1 through 2 of the Locate your memories workflow.
2. Click the delete icon in the **Action** column next to the desired memory. This will prompt you to review any disclaimers and confirm your selection.

## Locate additional Vera resources

- [Work on multiple tasks in one chat with Vera](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/17605856-work-on-multiple-tasks-in-one-chat-with-vera)
